Neo4j is a leader in graph databases and analytics, helping companies quickly and easily uncover hidden patterns and relationships across billions of data connections.

As a pioneer in graph database technology, Neo4j developed the property graph model, which represents data as nodes and relationships rather than traditional rows and columns. This uncovers complex connections within data, delivering deeper insights and enhanced analytical capabilities that go far beyond conventional database structures. The Neo4j model preserves context and relationships—making data smarter and easier to work with.

Real-time flexibility for evolving data needs

Neo4j provides exceptional schema flexibility, setting it apart from traditional databases that require a fixed schema with predefined data formats. Unlike these rigid systems, Neo4j allows schema modifications on-the-fly, empowering companies to adapt to their evolving data needs without incurring downtime. This capability is especially valuable in scenarios like fraud detection, where new patterns and relationships must be analyzed in real time to surface hidden risks. In contrast, conventional databases may require significant refactoring or downtime to implement schema changes, making Neo4j a more agile and efficient choice for dynamic, data-rich environments.

Empowering businesses to seamlessly represent all their data in graph form, Neo4j helps uncover critical insights with a suite of more than 65 algorithms. This helps their customers to efficiently detect financial anomalies for fraud prevention, resolve supply chain disruptions, identify key customer sets, and track materials with laser precision.

Accelerating adoption, driving growth

When combined with Microsoft Fabric and Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service, Neo4j helps organizations to integrate both structured and unstructured data effortlessly. This powerful integration helps to accelerate Azure OpenAI adoption.

By optimizing analytics using Neo4j’s property graph modeling, organizations can build AI applications that not only define data points but also establish their relationships and contextual significance. This creates more intelligent and efficient decision-making.

Expanding its operations to connect with more potential customers required significant resources, making it difficult for Neo4j to scale efficiently. Seeking a more streamlined path to global reach, Neo4j turned to the Microsoft marketplace.

“For us, the relationship between data points creates the magic,” said Sudhir Hasbe, Chief Product Officer at Neo4j. “Through our relationship with Microsoft and the marketplace, we can now make this magic accessible to more customers than ever before.”

A marketplace-first approach: Scaling with Microsoft Azure

Neo4j found that offering their solution through the Microsoft marketplace offered scale. The marketplace helps customers adopt their solution within a few clicks—with simplified deployment to their Azure environment.

Neo4j recognized that cloud marketplaces would play a dominant role in the future of IT transactions and adopted a marketplace-first approach as a core part of its growth strategy. By prioritizing marketplace distribution, Neo4j could accelerate deal closures, simplify adoption, and significantly expand its reach. As Hasbe noted, “We knew the marketplace could shorten our sales cycle by 33-40% because the testing, procurement, and deployment cycles would become much easier.”

Using the marketplace, Neo4j could easily scale without the significant upfront costs and infrastructure challenges typically associated with expansion, delivering faster growth and broader accessibility for customers worldwide.

Accelerated customer adoption and streamlined sales

Selling through the Microsoft marketplace has optimized Neo4j’s sales cycles and improved their operational efficiency. “We always want to close deals through marketplace, because it just streamlines everything for us—as well as our customers,” remarked Hasbe. The collaboration with Microsoft has also addressed a common challenge in enterprise technology adoption: the multi-layered internal approval process.

Traditionally, each team within an organization must individually perform multiple evaluations and follow a series of procurement steps to gain authorization to adopt a new solution. The marketplace model removes common friction points from the purchasing process.

Once Neo4j receives organizational-level approval, individual teams can immediately begin applying the technology for their specific use cases. All terms and conditions are managed by Microsoft, allowing customers to bypass lengthy legal reviews or custom contract discussions. Supporting the seamless transition from purchase to implementation, this approach not only accelerates time to value for customers, but also reduces downtime and administrative overhead, getting Neo4j customers to ROI much faster. “Nearly half of our self-service business now comes from this channel because it removes the usual barriers to adoption,” said Hasbe.

Developers can deploy the professional edition of the Neo4j database with a single click—locating the desired version, launching it directly from the marketplace, and immediately putting the technology to work, speeding up development cycles. In addition to streamlining technical implementation, the marketplace also supports Neo4j customers in meeting their MACC. Customers apply their existing MACC funds toward Neo4j solutions, just as they would with Microsoft-native services, eliminating the need for additional procurement processes or contract negotiations, making it faster and more convenient for customers to acquire and deploy the technology. According to Hasbe, “Since we have introduced our graph database and analytic solution in the Microsoft marketplace, our revenue from that channel over the last 18 months has grown 600%.”

New technology is making job hunting and hiring processes easier. Geographic Solutions, a leading provider of online employment software, is embracing the AI capabilities of Microsoft Azure to connect job seekers with meaningful career opportunities and to empower employers to find candidates who fit their needs. With Virtual OneStop (VOS) Sapphire AI, Geographic Solutions equips state government workforce development agencies to help constituents find gainful, long-term employment.

Empowering job seekers and employers with generative AI 

Employees at Geographic Solutions are passionate about helping people find jobs. The company’s VOS Sapphire software gives employment agencies in more than 40 US states and territories a customizable solution for connecting over 200 million job seekers with open positions.  

Paul Toomey, President and CEO of Geographic Solutions, understands the stresses associated with unemployment and views technology as a crucial tool in streamlining the process of helping people find jobs. “The commonality of everything we do with our software is finding someone a good-paying, well-matched job,” says Toomey.  

Geographic Solutions knew that generative AI offers an unprecedented opportunity for people on both sides of the hiring process to find the right job and the right hire. “We wanted to use AI to help with the areas that we know job seekers, employers, and staff struggle with the most,” says Toomey. “Building a quality resume can be a daunting task, so that was an ideal use case for AI. From the employer side, we focused on using AI to quickly produce better-quality job descriptions.”

Streamlining employment processes in two weeks or less

For Geographic Solutions, Azure OpenAI stood out for its use of cutting-edge AI models. “We looked at other technology, but we’re very happy with Azure OpenAI Service,” says Toomey. “Our monitoring shows that Azure OpenAI Service is consistent and reliable across all of our use cases. Microsoft’s dedicated support team has also been a key factor in integrating AI functionality into our software solutions.” The company collaborated closely with Microsoft Support teams to create VOS Sapphire AI, which supplements its existing VOS Sapphire solution with generative AI capabilities.

VOS Sapphire AI helps job seekers create and tailor resumes and cover letters for specific job openings within minutes, potentially saving these individuals hours of work. Employers can quickly generate high-quality job descriptions for multiple openings and customize interview questions based on applicant resumes.

State employment agencies, for example, can harness AI to create accurate case-management notes on prospective candidates. For states already using VOS Sapphire, these AI capabilities can be deployed in two weeks or less, an astonishingly short timeline. “We built the system to be flexible and easy to customize,” says Melina Tabares, Project Architect at Geographic Solutions. “It takes two weeks or less for us to configure VOS Sapphire AI, create the endpoints, and connect to Azure OpenAI Service.”

Boosting resume creation by 70% with generative AI

Geographic Solutions has seen a rapid acceleration of AI use by job seekers and state agencies. Internal data indicates a rising trend of AI use for resume creation for job seekers. These metrics also show that AI-generated resumes generally achieve higher quality scores than those crafted manually.

The Georgia Department of Labor deployed VOS Sapphire AI in December 2024, and the State of Texas followed in March 2025. The number of resumes created with generative AI has increased by 70% since December 2024, with a 74% increase in the number of resumes improved using generative AI. In April 2025, VOS Sapphire AI generated more than 2,300 new resumes and enhanced 3,100 others for both staff members and job seekers in Texas.

VOS Sapphire AI is also enhancing productivity for staff at these agencies. The number of records created with generative AI has increased by 65%, and state agency staff members are excited about the impact on their jobs. “AI integration has delivered a measurable impact across our workforce programs in Georgia,” says Damon Weller, Assistant Commissioner at WorkSource Georgia. “Since implementation in early December 2024, over 11,000 resumes have been generated utilizing AI Assist, with nearly 2,000 customized to job postings—enhancing job seeker competitiveness. These advancements will drive stronger outcomes and are elevating service delivery. We are encouraged to see the continuation of the AI learning development and prompt engineering that will better refine the overall results and enhance the user’s experience.” 

Geographic Solutions hopes to expand VOS Sapphire AI to more states and to help job seekers quickly find new opportunities. Toomey is excited to collaborate with Microsoft to create AI solutions that will recommend courses and training opportunities for individuals. 

“We believe in what we’re doing to help people, and we appreciate Microsoft’s willingness to work with us,” says Toomey. “Microsoft has worked closely with our team and really helped us out in this new area.”

Elanco is a global leader in animal health products for farmers, veterinarians, and pet owners. The company’s offerings help keep animals and the people around them healthy and safe. In 2018, Elanco began an effort to modernize its cloud architecture, boost security, and promote ongoing innovation.

Elanco began a cloud transformation, migrating some of its on-premises infrastructure to Microsoft Azure and adopting solutions including Microsoft Defender for Cloud to enhance security and operational efficiency. Thus, it has built a strong foundation ready to nimbly develop new business opportunities. Elanco’s collaborative culture has also positioned the company to continue innovating in animal health.

Rebuilding IT infrastructure in 18 months while enhancing security with Microsoft Defender Experts for XDR

Elanco is one of the largest independent animal health companies in the world. Its central focus on research and development leads the way to improve the health of animals, people, and the planet by discovering important medicines and treatments in more than 90 countries. “Animal health is connected in so many ways, both in terms of pets—which enrich our lives through companionship—and raising healthy farm animals to meet growing demand for protein and quality nutrition,” says Matthew Bull, Chief Technology and Information Security Officer at Elanco.

Elanco needed a reliable technology foundation for its crucial in-house drug discovery work, which helps it treat and prevent diseases worldwide. The company’s portfolio spans six core species and is balanced across farm animal and pet health products. “Innovation is at the core of Elanco, and we recognize that technology and data are going to be the force multipliers of the future,” says Bull.

Elanco had previously used on-premises datacenters, workloads, and many disparate tools. It also used a third-party security provider for its infrastructure. When it separated from its parent company in 2018, Elanco saw an opportunity to streamline its architecture. “We were a 70-year-old business exiting from a 150-year-old business,” says Bull. “Legacy architecture can result in technical debt and inertia, which can be a bit of an anchor as it relates to innovation.” To modernize its operations, the company rebuilt its IT infrastructure in 18 months with Microsoft.

Elanco decided to migrate some of its infrastructure to Microsoft solutions to create an environment that would strengthen security, accelerate development, and improve resiliency. The company was already using Microsoft 365, and it began its transformation by upgrading to the Microsoft 365 E5 enterprise plan. Elanco’s engineers wanted to promote operational efficiency, so the team modernized its systems as it migrated them. “We wanted to make sure that we seized this opportunity with both hands,” says Bull. “We see our technology ecosystem as a differentiator, one that will ultimately lead to a competitive advantage.”

Next, the team replaced its previous third-party security service with Microsoft Defender Experts for XDR, which provides managed extended detection and response around the clock, saving Elanco more than $300,000 annually. Now, the team can better help protect its entire cloud environment at scale using Microsoft offerings. “We can make improvements to efficiency and response time because everything is designed to work together on Microsoft technology, and the people who support it are also Microsoft experts,” says Brad Klotzsche, Senior Adviser for Cyber Detect and Respond at Elanco. “That’s why we invest across the entire security stack, from endpoint security to identity and cloud management.”

Streamlining infrastructure and reducing response times by approximately 50%

Elanco’s approach to using Microsoft offerings has enhanced its security posture and operational efficiency. “We’re very much leaning into Microsoft solutions, not just from a technology standpoint, but also from the expertise that its resources can bring as part of a managed service offering,” says Bull.

To advance this transformation, Elanco offered training and professional development to its IT team and recruited talent to bring in fresh perspectives. “People and processes are at the forefront of how you drive transformation, with technology being the foundation,” says Bull.

Elanco migrated about 90% of its workloads to the cloud, running some of them on Azure and implementing conditional access policies in Microsoft Defender for Cloud to manage their use. “Having the single platform from Microsoft has helped us to turn up our security posture in a way that is fairly easy,” says Mike Chilvers, Deputy Chief Information Security Officer at Elanco. “Using identity and endpoint security and privacy in an all-in-one package using Microsoft solutions is incredibly powerful.”

Elanco uses Microsoft Sentinel for security analytics and Microsoft Security Copilot for AI assistance. The company has shortened the time it takes to detect and respond to security issues by approximately 50% using unified management tools and automations. And it can configure security controls to meet its exact needs. “Microsoft Defender for Cloud uses Copilot for remediation action plans, and as they get escalated to our team, we also use Copilot for assistance with queries on Sentinel or other Microsoft products,” says Klotzsche. “Using the same technology creates efficiencies to get us where we need to get faster.”

The company also uses Azure OpenAI Service to incorporate AI into its workloads and unlock further efficiency gains. “We have thousands of users, every single day, using all the Azure OpenAI models—both the foundational models that are available and some of the new reasoning models that have a tremendous opportunity to influence and shape how we run our business going forward,” says Bull.

Engineers also have a better development experience. Because the Microsoft solutions that Elanco uses are designed to work together, the company can iterate on its internal workflows without worrying that the changes will affect efficiency or security. Furthermore, the company deploys all apps within its security boundary, so that engineers can focus on building features instead of managing security. Thus, Elanco can develop new ideas in days instead of months. “We can focus on being effective and efficient with our resource allocation and prioritize the research and development work that drives innovation in our animal health products,” says Bull.

Improving the lives of animals and the people who care for them with Microsoft technology

Elanco created a secure and resilient environment that supports its ambitious goals and promotes innovation, adding features such as predictive cyberthreat detection and customizable controls. Now, the company is exploring additional AI use cases and implementing sensitivity labels from Microsoft Purview Information Protection to help categorize and further protect its data.

At the heart of Elanco’s mission is a deep dedication to improving the lives of animals and the people who care for them. This mission drives every decision, from adopting a cloud-first approach to adding robust security measures.

“With Microsoft technology, you can go from nothing to something very quickly,” says Bull. “That spirit of discovery is powered by technology and helps us deliver the animal health solutions that really matter. It’s exciting to witness its benefits across the business.”

EchoStar delivers entertainment, communication, and connection to millions of businesses and consumers around the world through leading satellite-powered brands, including Hughes Network Systems, DISH, Sling, and Boost Mobile. The company aims to provide these services reliably and expand on its mission to offer satellite coverage in hard-to-reach rural areas. That’s why EchoStar and its brands take a technology-forward approach to solving complicated operational, productivity, and customer experience inefficiencies.  

An avid and early AI adopter, Hughes Network Systems understood the power of generative AI to address challenges in speech, vision, text, and structured data for a wide range of work productivity challenges. It needed a way to relieve sales call auditors from listening to hours of conversations to ensure quality communications, a priority customer experience objective at Hughes. The company knew it was an area in which it could significantly improve cost, productivity, and ROI by using the right technology.

Tapping the power of advanced analytics and speech-to-text AI


“We chose Microsoft Azure AI Foundry because of our longstanding partnership with the company and its deep technical knowledge. We rely on Microsoft’s approach to responsible AI and its data privacy, security, and governance options,” says Rupinder Bir, Senior Director for Software Delivery at Hughes Network Systems. This decision initiated an exciting journey toward automation and enhanced insights. 

Using Microsoft Azure AI Foundry products, including Azure AI Speech and Azure OpenAI Service, Hughes has offloaded manual sales agent audit calls with an AI-driven, automated speech-to-text system. This new system delivers higher-value interactions and produces advanced call insights and agent directives across the entire call, exponentially boosting productivity.

Amarender Singh, Director of AI at Hughes Network Systems, adds, “Working with Microsoft, we have the flexibility to use open-source models and create speech-to-text and text-to-speech avatars, helping us process thousands of call center calls, driving substantial ROI gains for Hughes. Our sales agents can now act on advanced analytics we didn’t have access to before, freeing them up to create more innovative customer service experiences.”

Establishing a grounded, trusted LLM operations framework 

Hughes also trusted Azure AI Foundry to help it successfully create a solid large language model (LLM) operations framework. “Generative AI comes with risks to security, privacy, and intellectual property with potential legal ramifications, so we wanted to be sure we were building and evaluating responsibly,” explains Singh. 

To ensure high standards, Hughes used automated evaluation tools in Azure AI Foundry to systematically measure the quality and safety of AI-generated outputs. “The robust evaluation tools in Azure AI Foundry help our developers continuously assess the performance and accuracy of our AI models, including meeting standards for coherence, fluency, and groundedness,” says Singh. “This advantage helps us get from pilot to production more quickly and with confidence.”

Saving time and money

Hughes has implemented multiple AI applications that enhance employee efficiency and elevate customer service. Using AI to summarize all calls to the contact center, the company has saved more than 30,000 hours annually. In field services, AI-driven process automation such as virtual assistants for field technicians, site auditing, and analysis of technical support calls has streamlined operations, saving more than 8,000 hours. By replacing human auditors in sales call audits, Hughes has saved thousands of dollars and significantly increased efficiency.

Hughes has also adopted AI for generating and annotating images faster, to train traditional computer vision models, significantly reducing training times and improving model accuracy. The ability to search knowledge bases using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has enhanced information accessibility for employees and installers in the field, ensuring quick and accurate responses. 

In quality assurance, AI helps Hughes better understand the reasons behind customer churn by analyzing the customer journey through surveys, calls, and case data. Collectively, these AI initiatives have boosted overall productivity by up to 25%, including automated sales call audit reductions of 90%, from $26 per hour for each call to just $2.

Looking to the future


Hughes is preparing to deploy further innovations. It currently has 12 applications in production, with many more in development. “We want to deploy agentic AI across various company verticals, and we’ve already gauged its potential with Azure AI Foundry and Microsoft Copilot Studio. We view Microsoft as a long-term collaborator for AI innovation, even beyond the success we’ve already had,” says Singh.

By embracing AI across multiple facets of the organization, including customer service, field services, and quality assurance, Hughes is signaling its continuing commitment to improving operational efficiency and delivering superior customer experiences.

The landscape of enterprise technology is ever-evolving, and few companies are rising to meet the challenge of AI transformation. One company that has taken the lead in this revolution is WinWire. At the heart of WinWire’s mission is a bold and complex challenge to help organizations understand what AI transformation means for them. As AI becomes central to IT strategy, many businesses are at a tipping point, unsure how to begin or where to invest. “Some of the biggest challenges our customers face today,” says Tony Guidi, Senior Executive at WinWire, “is really trying to understand what AI transformation is going to mean for them. Everybody needs a strategy for how they're going to adopt AI.”

WinWire meets this challenge head-on by focusing on real business problems, helping clients identify use cases, and guiding them through a journey that is as strategic as it is technical.

Central to WinWire’s success is its partnership with Microsoft. As Guidi states, “Without Microsoft, what we do today doesn't exist.” WinWire collaborates closely with Microsoft’s field teams, account executives, and specialist groups to ensure a unified approach to every customer engagement. Azure provides the foundation for the AI transformation journey, delivering scalable infrastructure, powerful AI services, and industry-leading innovation.

Microsoft Azure stood out to WinWire for several key reasons:

Comprehensive Platform: Azure offers a full-stack solution that spans AI, application, and data platforms supported by secure and scalable cloud infrastructure.

Generative AI Leadership: Microsoft’s investments in generative AI through Azure OpenAI and tools like Microsoft Copilot Studio give WinWire powerful tools to build intelligent, context-aware solutions.

Industry Expertise: Azure’s adaptability across industries, especially healthcare and high-tech ISVs, empowers WinWire to deliver tailored, high-impact solutions.

Incentive Programs: Microsoft’s funding programs, such as Azure Innovate and Azure Migrate and Modernize, help WinWire accelerate customer adoption while reducing financial barriers.

AI-powered modernization

Over the past two years, WinWire’s AI engagements have evolved from educational initiatives into fully realized, production-ready solutions. WinWire starts by helping customers understand the capabilities within Microsoft Cloud, whether that’s Azure OpenAI, Microsoft Copilot Studio, or custom agent development. WinWire then maps those capabilities to specific business use cases in an approach that includes data platform modernization—migrating legacy infrastructure to Azure for a secure, scalable foundation; AI-infused applications—building apps that integrate custom Copilots and large language models to improve decision-making and automation; cloud migrations—helping companies move from competitive platforms like AWS and GCP to Azure, including migrations from Tableau to Power BI; industry-specific expertise—developing use cases tailored to healthcare sub-industries like pharma, medtech, and providers.

One example is WinWire’s work with a pharmaceutical company. By leveraging Azure OpenAI and large language models, WinWire helped build a platform that accelerates drug discovery using synthetic data and AI-powered decision-making to reduce time-to-market for new drugs.

Unsurprisingly, WinWire’s partnership with Microsoft has driven transformative outcomes across industries, leveraging Azure’s capabilities to accelerate innovation and efficiency. In pharmaceuticals, generative AI platforms built on Azure expedite drug discovery by using synthetic data to streamline research and development. Companies are also modernizing their IT landscapes, rapidly migrating from legacy systems and competitive clouds to Azure’s secure, scalable infrastructure. Additionally, AI-infused applications tailored to specific industries enhance business agility, enabling organizations to boost productivity and maintain a competitive edge in an increasingly digital world.

Most compelling, however, is WinWire’s commitment to meaningful impact. As Guidi notes, “These are solutions that can ultimately improve the quality of patient care in the healthcare community.”

Notable data points includes 2-plus years of focused investment in Azure OpenAI and AI design, significant momentum in Tableau to Power BI migrations, an increasing number of projects focused on healthcare and pharmaceutical AI solutions, and dedicated internal team to identify and secure Microsoft funding programs for clients.

Scaling the future together

The future for WinWire and Microsoft Azure is bright. With customer demand for AI transformation only increasing, WinWire plans to continue expanding its Azure capabilities, deepening its industry focus, and bringing even more holistic solutions to market. As Microsoft continues leading the way in cloud and AI innovation, WinWire is uniquely positioned to be the trusted guide for enterprises ready to embrace the next chapter of digital transformation. Together, WinWire and Microsoft Azure are not just solving technical problems, they’re shaping the future of entire industries.

Story Content:
In enterprise environments, information is everywhere—and nowhere. Knowledge lives across documents, emails, chat threads, PDFs, videos, and apps. But when employees need answers, traditional search falls short. Teams waste time digging, re-asking, or giving up altogether because context is missing, formats are fragmented, and silos block discovery.

Capacity, a support automation platform serving enterprise organizations, set out to fix that. Its Answer Engine® delivers precise, context-aware responses to natural language questions by retrieving information from across an enterprise’s unstructured knowledge. The goal: eliminate friction, empower users with instant answers, and unlock the full value of a company’s internal knowledge—no matter where it lives.

Transitioning to Microsoft Azure AI Foundry

To take its Answer Engine to the next level, Capacity re-architected its pipeline with generative AI at the core. The team needed a solution that could understand user intent, work across formats, and deliver fast, reliable answers at scale—without compromising on cost, security, or flexibility.

Capacity selected Microsoft Azure Phi small language models via Azure AI Foundry to power both real-time query handling and offline content enrichment. Phi delivered the low-latency performance and cost efficiency required to support dynamic user interactions. Its deployment flexibility, across Azure environments or air-gapped Kubernetes clusters, met enterprise-grade security demands.

Capacity also incorporated Azure tools for multilingual search, document enrichment, and semantic retrieval, allowing the system to handle everything from keyword tagging to video indexing. The result is a modern, scalable architecture that bridges the gap between unstructured content and meaningful answers.

“To deliver a superior experience, we needed to move from a natural language classifier to a generative AI solution,” says Steve Frederickson, Head of Product, Answer Engine at Capacity. “Knowledge management complexity requires a robust, scalable, flexible, and cost-effective approach.”

Improving retrieval relevance and accuracy

Capacity implemented Phi-4 and Phi-4-mini from Azure AI Foundry Models for its speed, cost-effectiveness, and deployment flexibility. Using both 4K and 128K variants with prompt engineering, adherence workflows, and structured indexing helped refine search accuracy and accelerate engine development.

The metadata tagging ability of Phi-4-mini also helped Capacity optimize search results, ultimately improving development speed and query processing efficiency. Phi models are able to run locally, which provided Capacity with a strong long-term strategy for its private cloud deployment, vectorization, and query routing activities. All proved to be advantages in helping customers search for hyper-specific responses and receive more precise, context-aware results.

“We work with a variety of companies in different industries, including consumer packaged goods. For example, a global condiment manufacturer used Answer Engine to find a research study on optimizing the viscosity of their product without adding sugar,” says Zach Meierhofer, Director of Customer Success at Capacity. “Another use case involved employee onboarding, where new team members ask the engine questions and get immediate answers, helping them learn about the organization faster to become productive more quickly.”

Defining optimal components for an enhanced Answer Engine

To deliver precise, multilingual, and secure answers at scale, Capacity redesigned its Answer Engine using a modular architecture built on Azure AI. Each component was selected for a specific role in the pipeline and optimized for speed, performance, and user experience.

At the heart of the solution is Azure AI Foundry, where Capacity deploys the Phi small language models. These lightweight models run without fine-tuning and support both offline enrichment—like title generation and keyword tagging—and real-time query refinement. To help ensure scalable, containerized deployment across secure environments, Capacity uses Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) to manage their Kubernetes clusters and support a range of compute needs—including backend services, file processing, and reporting—across both its cloud environment as well as in customer-hosted, air-gapped infrastructures. Capacity adopted Azure AI Foundry early, enabling it to validate model performance, security, and latency benchmarks ahead of broader implementation. The result is a low-latency, high-performance system that delivers the benefits of generative AI at a fraction of the cost of larger models. With flexible deployment options—including air-gapped Kubernetes clusters and customer-specific Azure environments—Capacity ensures security, scalability, and enterprise-grade reliability across industries.

To support multilingual search, the team layered in Azure AI Translator and Azure AI Language. Users can now ask questions and receive results in their preferred language, with support for up to 46 languages. Translation happens on the fly, and built-in language detection helps deliver a seamless experience across global teams.

For fast, relevant results, Capacity uses Azure AI Search to index the enriched content produced during preprocessing. Metadata and semantic structure are fully employed to return accurate, context-aware answers. Behind the scenes, Azure Database for PostgreSQL supports structured metadata management and content configuration, helping ensure the retrieval layer remains fast, consistent, and optimized for scale.

Finally, Azure AI Video Indexer expands the reach of Answer Engine to multimedia. By transcribing and tagging video and audio content—like webinars, podcasts, and training sessions—Capacity makes knowledge stored in rich media as searchable and discoverable as any document or deck.

Together, this Azure-powered architecture forms a modern retrieval system that’s accurate, multilingual, secure, and media-aware—designed to meet the complexity of enterprise content at scale.

“Security and privacy concerns come up every time,” says Meierhofer. “Our customers trust us to protect their sensitive content, and Azure helps us ensure their deployment data is private, individualized, safe, and secure.”

Frederickson agrees, “For customers needing higher security, we deploy models in their Azure environment to make sure data doesn’t leave their cloud.” He adds that Capacity can offer even more secure options through the deployment capabilities of Phi.

Scaling to grow datasets while avoiding prohibitive costs

“Unifying our datasets with the Phi-4-mini model was effortless,” says Frederickson. “We have found new opportunities in its speed, and the enriched customer experience of GenAI enables us to resolve customer issues far more effectively.”

Additionally, the model as a service (MaaS) offering from Azure AI Foundry provides developers the ability to interoperate with cutting-edge models across the landscape, addressing a wide range of customer use cases with enhanced efficacy. This, in turn, elevates the overall user experience. “Depending on the use case and timing, we deploy different models,” says Frederickson. “For example, we use small language models for title enrichment asynchronously, while more sophisticated models are used for high-touch tasks like document chat and focused research. This approach allows us to balance cost and effectiveness for our customers.”

Capacity appreciates that the models have rapidly increased in sophistication. Initially, its generative title capability was limited to a single source at a time, but additional infrastructure and model scalability can now be built into the pipeline for all approved use cases. The result is improved content and a better user experience with faster, more accurate results.

Maintaining fast response times without compromising accuracy: how Answer Engine works

For the user to feel confident in their search results, it’s important for Answer Engine to instantaneously present the full answer to a query in addition to the related answer content metadata. To accomplish this, Capacity engineered split tasks for Phi into preprocessing and real-time flows.

In preprocessing, Capacity generates metadata such as title summaries for answers, keyword tags for search, and other information to the index. This prework is done offline and ahead of time. Depending on the tagging task required for each answer and the customer’s generative AI preferences, Capacity routes the query to the appropriate Phi model.

At query time, Phi models preprocess the query to retrieve the most relevant content. The split tasks for Phi enabled repeatable performance, keeping the responsive query times that users expect while enhancing results with new functionality and increased retrieval relevance.

Paving the way for future customer successes

Using AI-driven search and retrieval, Answer Engine can be set up in minutes, delivering users instant, high-quality, and accurate answers in real time. The solution also improves trust and transparency with metadata tagging, providing context around responses, and enhancing confidence in search results within a highly secure environment.

“What truly impressed us about building this solution, in using the Azure AI Foundry stack, was its remarkable accuracy and the ease of deployment, even before customization,” says Frederickson. “Since then, we’ve been able to enhance both accuracy and reliability, all while maintaining the cost-effectiveness and scalability we valued from the start.”

Cognition is redefining the future of software engineering with a bold vision and groundbreaking technology. Founded in 2024 by Scott Wu, Walden Yan, and Steven Hao, this applied AI lab is on a mission to revolutionize how software is built. Leading the charge is "Devin," the world’s first autonomous AI software engineer, designed to work alongside human developers or operate independently. As Cognition continues to push the boundaries of innovation, its partnership with Microsoft Azure is key to scaling its transformative solutions across the enterprise landscape.

From the start, Cognition’s vision for Devin was ambitious: an AI agent capable of end-to-end engineering, from scoping and execution to testing and iteration. But delivering such a powerful tool to enterprise customers required more than advanced models and smart interfaces. Cognition needed a platform that could meet the demanding infrastructure needs of large-scale enterprises, support integration with the existing software development lifecycle, and open the door to joint go-to-market efforts.

Enter Microsoft Azure.

An empowering partnership with Microsoft Azure

Microsoft Azure's comprehensive cloud platform is known for its enterprise-grade infrastructure, powerful developer tools, and seamless integrations with Microsoft's broader ecosystem. For AI-focused companies like Cognition, Azure offers a scalable, secure, and developer-friendly environment to bring cutting-edge solutions to market. Cognition selected Azure as its cloud partner for two key reasons:

Enterprise-Ready Infrastructure: Azure’s robust environment made it easy to support complex infrastructure needs for customers like Visma—a 2 billion Euro fintech company based in Norway, undergoing large-scale app modernization and cloud migration efforts.

Go-to-Market Collaboration: Azure enabled deep sales and technical collaboration with Microsoft’s Sales and Black Belt teams, creating new opportunities to bring Devin into the enterprise fold through the Microsoft commercial marketplace distribution and joint outreach.

When Devin met Azure

"At Cognition we love working with partners like Visma and Microsoft who provide the expertise and tools to accelerate value from Devin. Devin only gets better when combined with great humans and access to tools like Copilot and Azure," explains David Morse, Cognition VP of Enterprise. Cognition’s integration with Azure goes far beyond basic cloud hosting. Devin works hand-in-hand with Microsoft’s ecosystem, including GitHub Copilot and Azure’s native developer tools like .NET migration utilities. Together, these solutions form a powerful triad for enterprise software modernization.

Take the case of Visma. Faced with the high costs and long timelines of migrating legacy .NET and PHP applications to the cloud, Visma turned to the combined power of GitHub Copilot, Azure utilities, and Devin. The result? A 50% reduction in project costs, faster delivery timelines, and a dramatic increase in developer productivity, up to 2x in some scenarios.

An impact felt across cost savings and market growth

The integration of Devin into enterprise workflows isn’t just about speeding up code. It’s a fundamental shift in how software gets built. Devin’s ability to operate autonomously and asynchronously allows engineering teams to scale their efforts exponentially. For Visma, this translated into:

50% reduction in engineering costs

2x increase in developer productivity

Up to 10x improvement on complex modernization projects

Faster time-to-market and improved customer satisfaction

Better software and API performance

Improved developer engagement (+16 eNPS)

These improvements are not theoretical. They are driving meaningful business results, from greater market share to more efficient R&D investments.

Scaling innovation together

Cognition and Microsoft Azure are only beginning to tap into the full potential of their partnership. With Devin already in use by engineers at Microsoft and enterprise customers worldwide, their collaboration is set to grow even stronger. Upcoming initiatives will focus on scaling their joint solution across additional industries, deepening integration with other Azure services, and unlocking new levels of productivity in software development.

Devin is more than just a tool; that much is clear. It marks a shift in how engineering teams operate. By enabling AI agents to execute thousands of tasks in parallel, Devin empowers human developers to concentrate on high-level innovation and system design. As Cognition continues to push the boundaries of what's possible, Microsoft Azure remains an essential partner in transforming that vision into an enterprise-ready, scalable reality. Together, they’re not just revolutionizing software development, they’re helping shape the future of work.

Accenture (NYSE: ACN) provides consulting, technology, and outsourcing services to 9,000 clients in in more than 120 countries, in fields as diverse as cloud computing, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, marketing, risk management, supply chain, commerce, digital engineering, strategic managed services, and technology transformation. Headquartered in Dublin, Ireland, the company’s more than 730,000 employees guide clients from making practical, operational improvements, one department at a time, all the way up to complete digital transformations.

Turning a challenge into a solution

Accenture’s strategic managed services for operations’ group contracts with companies and government entities to help optimize and transform business processes and enable reinvention. When the firm was retained to modernize a state agency’s customer relationship management (CRM) operations to reduce cost and streamline customer service, for example, Accenture knew that migration to the cloud with Dynamics 365 Customer Service and Dynamics 365 Contact Center would simplify the agency’s technology infrastructure and drastically reduce the costs associated with on-premises legacy tools.  

Accenture already operated and maintained software applications for the call center in addition to hiring and managing the center’s 300 employees. The call center staff relied on the agency’s legacy CRM application to handle approximately 150,000 calls per month relating to medical claims, provider enrollment, prior authorizations, claim status, payments, and various program benefits. 

In 2022, Accenture was asked to recommend ways the agency could reduce costs while maintaining excellent customer service for all constituents requesting information about medical coverage and financial reimbursement for patients across the state.

The legacy system was integrated with an on-premises phone response (IVR) system for call routing. This technology infrastructure was the department’s largest cost center. For this reason, it was a natural focus of Accenture’s reinvention. 

To modernize the agency’s solution and find efficiencies in technology and operations, Accenture recommended updating the application infrastructure and migrating to the cloud with Microsoft Dynamics 365. It integrates seamlessly not only with cloud call routing systems that could replace the legacy IVR software, but also with several of the agency’s other on-premises systems. Christine Adams, Service Delivery Manager for Contact Center, Accenture Operations—Health and Public Service says the “transition to Dynamics 365 has made it easier and faster to make changes and the integration with AWS allows us to listen to a call directly from the Dynamics 365 rather than manually search through a database.” 

The migration project would incur a one-time expense, but the cost effectiveness of a modern cloud solution would pay off in the long term with richer capabilities, reduced maintenance costs, enhanced user experience, and improved employee productivity.

A cloud-based call center launches

Dynamics 365 Contact Center and Customer Service modernized the call center experience with an improved case management system, enhanced chat bot functionality and call forwarding, and automated calls where possible to reduce volume for agents. As part of the migration, Accenture used Microsoft Entra ID for authentication and single sign-on, streamlining and simplifying the process for onsite and remote users and ensuring the latest security measures were in place. 

As a leading technology provider, Accenture always provides a robust training program to help workers feel confident and productive on day one and meet all procedural standards. The implementation team’s goal was a smooth cutover from the on-premises system to Dynamics 365 without any service disruption, including timely handling of thousands of calls and emails.

After going live with Dynamics 365, the responses from various Accenture Operation teams were positive; the new capabilities were making a noticeable impact. Some of the realized benefits to date are:

One application for most daily activities 

In the past, employees used multiple apps and tools in their daily workflow. Cases for Accenture Operations team members were created manually, which was time consuming. Now, users have a unified interface for all actions and tasks that makes it easier to better manage their work inventory. Accenture Technology Team also uses Power Automate flows and Server-Side Sync to automatically create Cases and assign them to the appropriate users.  

With context and notes displayed in a single interface, CRM users now have a better experience while using the system.

Single sign-on saves valuable time

With many call center employees working remotely, Dynamics 365 makes connecting to their work environment easy. The legacy system required separate authentication processes and credentials for different applications. Using the latest Microsoft Azure security tools, employees now sign in once to gain access to all the applications they need to do their jobs. “We moved away from managing service requests via emails to working directly within Dynamics 365. This allows us to manage our workload and reporting more efficiently,” explains Jeremy Floyd York, Portfolio & Delivery Management Associate Director, Accenture Operations – Health and Public Service. 

Enhanced reporting capabilities

Reports are the primary way for call center managers to understand how their team is performing. Creating legacy reports required specialized technical skills and manual labor, and the results offered limited formatting options. Now, the Accenture technology team uses Power BI to create insightful reports based on multiple data sources presented in a variety of ways which are more informative and help the operations team make critical decisions based on real time data. 

Robust email notifications avalable on demand 

Through an integration with Click Dimensions, agency enrollees receive approximately 500,000 emails every month which provide useful information and status updates about their enrollment application. Click Dimensions also can track and provide email statistics regarding when these emails are opened by the Providers, how many times these emails are clicked or if the emails bounced or failed to reach the intended recipients.

Enterprise case management solution for omnichannel experience     

With the intuitive user interface of Dynamics 365, seamless integrations and automations enable Call Center staff to create cases from incoming phone calls—roughly 150,000 per month—emails or Chat and Dynamics CRM sends notifications to clients or providers via Email, Phone or Text Messages (SMS). All cases created in the system are automatically assigned to a Call Center agent along with all relevant background information. The case management solution also creates cases from new channels like Emails, Chat Conversations and Excel files ensuring all service level agreements (SLA) are met.

Natural next steps for Accenture

Accenture is committed to progress and innovation as stewards of their clients’ business values. Moving to the cloud with Dynamics 365 positions the firm's clients to utilize Accenture’s expertise and stay agile, always ready to embrace what comes next. Accenture is already finding ways to build more efficiencies for its government call center clients with new AI-driven capabilities and Gen AI to automate case opening and resolution for simple requests answered by the IVR call routing system, provide real-time responses from organization-approved content sources to improve response accuracy and reduce agent effort, and use chat bots to answer common questions and forward customers to human agents when further support is needed.

Single application for most tasks vs. multiple tools improves processes. Automation and new workflows allow staff to handle more cases with less effort. Robust, easy-to-read reports built in Power BI are emailed to 500k providers monthly.

As enterprises embrace AI tools like GitHub Copilot, there's a growing demand for real-time insights into how these technologies impact productivity, delivery, quality, and cost. Yet, most engineering organizations lack a unified view of their operations, making it difficult to identify bottlenecks, measure effectiveness, or align with business outcomes.

Faros AI saw this gap. Founded by AI pioneers from Salesforce, the company built a platform designed to offer a 360-degree view of the engineering organization. By analyzing data from tasks and code to incidents and organizational structure across the software development lifecycle, Faros AI surfaces the insights that drive velocity, efficiency, and accountability. Ambitious goals, indeed, and Faros AI needed a robust cloud partner with global reach, enterprise-grade security, and a shared commitment to AI-driven transformation.

A partner for growth

Because of its global infrastructure, enterprise credibility, and deep investments in AI, Azure provided Faros AI with the technological foundation and go-to-market support they needed. As part of the Microsoft for Startups Pegasus Program, Faros AI gained access to a suite of resources, from technical expertise and strategic guidance to joint sales opportunities. Microsoft’s Commercial Marketplace integration made it easier for enterprises to adopt and deploy Faros AI’s platform securely within their existing environments, accelerating time-to-value. But the alignment runs deeper. Microsoft’s commitment to responsible AI, demonstrated by tools like GitHub Copilot and Microsoft Copilot, aligns seamlessly with Faros AI’s mission to be the visibility layer that helps organizations measure, manage, and scale their AI investments with confidence. "Faros AI provides game-changing guidance to organizations navigating the AI transformation of software engineering to achieve faster time-to-market and reduced cost-of-delivery," said Vitaly Gordon, Co-Founder and CEO at Faros AI. "Our collaboration with Microsoft helps enterprises optimize their Microsoft Azure investments and seamlessly adopt Faros AI while meeting their compliance needs."

The scalable, secure, and strategic Azure advantage

Faros AI capitalizes on several key strengths of Microsoft Azure to deliver value at scale. Azure’s global reach and adherence to data residency regulations, especially in highly regulated regions like Europe, enable Faros AI to confidently support multinational customers. Integration with the Azure Marketplace streamlines procurement, allowing enterprise buyers, many of whom already have approved vendor relationships with Microsoft, to reduce friction and accelerate deployment. Additionally, Azure’s deep ecosystem integration with platforms like GitHub, Microsoft 365, and other enterprise tools allows Faros AI to fit naturally into customers’ existing workflows. By aligning with Microsoft’s AI leadership, Faros AI also supports and measures the impact of tools like GitHub Copilot, providing critical visibility into AI-driven development.

"With software development at the core of digital transformation, engineering leaders need precise insights to guide investments in productivity, quality, collaboration, and security," said Phil Kim, Senior Director, Microsoft Corporate Business Development. "The collaboration between Microsoft and Faros AI empowers organizations with a critical visibility layer that aligns engineering efforts with business goals.”

Measurable results

The Faros AI and Microsoft Azure partnership is already delivering significant results for Faros AI's end customers, including some of the world’s most complex engineering organizations:

$50 million in revenue growth over two years through on-time product delivery

$21 million in annual cost savings via improved engineering efficiency

$10 million in first-year ROI from accelerated development velocity

95% improvement in lead times and 72% boost in code quality

23% faster code review cycles and 37% greater delivery predictability

These figures underscore a powerful truth that combining AI-powered insights with enterprise-grade cloud infrastructure drives real business value.

Scaling innovation together

Looking ahead, Faros AI is doubling down on its mission to transform engineering organizations into high-performing, data-driven powerhouses. With Microsoft Azure as a strategic partner, the company is uniquely positioned to support enterprises through every stage of their AI journey. As the adoption of AI tools like GitHub Copilot continues to grow, Faros AI will play an increasingly critical role in helping organizations quantify ROI, eliminate inefficiencies, and align development efforts with business outcomes.

Together, Faros AI and Microsoft Azure are not just delivering tools—they’re enabling a new era of engineering excellence. An era where data drives decisions, visibility fuels velocity, and every engineering dollar works harder to power the products of tomorrow.

Searching for a home online has been stuck in the filter-search paradigm for decades. “Our business is real estate data,” says Andy Florance, CEO of CoStar Group, which owns homes.com, apartments.com, and many other real estate marketplaces. “We provide proprietary data and insights—including market research and neighborhood details—across commercial and residential real estate. No other business can offer what we have. There aren’t enough filters in the traditional search matrix to capture the nuance we can offer a home buyer in their search.”

Seeking insightful, nuanced conversation

CoStar Group (CoStar) is rethinking the home search experience on its homes.com marketplace. It needs a solution that replicates the casual, nuanced conversations that buyers have with human real estate agents, to surface its vast amount of relevant data.

“When you talk to your human real estate agent, you don’t say, ‘Three bedroom, two bath, under $700,000, Wilmington area,’” notes Livia Sponseller, VP of Product Management at homes.com. “You have a conversation. There’s back-and-forth. Your real estate agent offers insights. It’s a richer, more nuanced and thoughtful experience. That’s what we want for our visitors to homes.com.” A conversational search experience helps home buyers be more specific about their priorities, yielding results that more closely align with their desires. This, in turn, means a home buyer is more likely to find the home that fits.

A real-time audio search experience seemed the perfect solution. But real-time audio presents latency issues, where the pause between the human speaking and the AI response is too long. CoStar knew the solution would have to be extremely fast to draw people in.

Prioritizing security and scalability

Two other considerations drove CoStar’s planning. First, the solution needs to offer a secure environment to help protect both the proprietary data owned by CoStar and consumer conversations. Second, the solution needs to scale as CoStar expands domestically and globally. Already, more than 100 million people come to homes.com to search for homes every month. With a premier search experience, that number is expected to grow. In addition, introducing a new technology to an existing website requires careful consideration to help ensure every visitor’s experience remains positive.

Succeeding with real-time audio AI

CoStar looked for a speech and audio API that would deliver low-latency performance, scalability, and reliability. The GPT-4o Realtime API audio models on Microsoft Azure OpenAI in Azure AI Foundry Models exceeded expectations. “The speed of the GPT-4o Realtime API is just incredible,” observes Andy Ventura, VP. “The ability to interrupt —it’s awesome.”

Sponseller agrees, adding, “Every time we interact with the voice tech, it feels magical. It’s exceeding our original expectations and vision, making the home buying process more engaging and efficient. The detail we can offer through this experience, from data on the heat index in a specific region to showing a view out the kitchen window, is mind-blowing.”

Discovering the right AI model

CoStar was able to experiment efficiently and cost-effectively with the generative AI models in Azure AI Foundry to find the most suitable fit for a real-time audio search solution for home buyers. Identifying the right model was crucial for addressing the requirement for a low-latency experience.

“One of the key advantages of choosing Microsoft was access to Azure AI Foundry Models. We were able to easily and affordably experiment with multiple models before deciding on the best low-latency model for our use case,” says Ventura. The ability to test and refine different models was instrumental in achieving the desired performance and efficiency.

CoStar chose Mistral 3B for natural language processing because it is optimized for low-latency, high-volume workloads. Since the company didn’t require a large model, Mistral 3B met the need with fewer parameters, making it faster to fine-tune and deploy. It also requires less computational power and memory, making it a strong choice for applications drawing on limited resources, such as mobile devices.

Because of these specifications, Mistral 3B uses significantly fewer tokens for each search query (for example, 100 tokens versus 4,000 with other models for an initial query such as “Show me homes in the Michigan area that are on a lake”). As a result, it’s faster and more cost-efficient. Despite its smaller size, Mistral 3B delivers the uptime, scale, and governance capabilities needed, thanks to its interoperability with Azure.

Seeing the whole picture

With the real-time search and navigation experience, a visitor to homes.com can say, “Show me homes within 25 miles of downtown Denver that are in the top school district.” Then they might ask, “Which of these have a big backyard?” and continue to refine until finally saying, “Show me the view out of the kitchen window on this one.” Home buyers can virtually step inside the home, thanks to CoStar’s recent acquisition of Matterport, the first 3D capture solution to deliver dimensionally accurate, photorealistic virtual tours or “digital twins” for any type of property. When they ask, “Can we fit a king-size bed in this room?” the combination of Matterport and the AI audio experience delivers an accurate, immediate response.

CoStar is unlocking access to insights that were previously undiscoverable. It’s doing this in a search experience that feels natural and intuitive with the combination of Mistral 3B and GPT-4o Realtime API audio models. Using Azure AI Foundry, the team can easily and seamlessly combine both Mistral and GPT-4o Realtime API audio models.

Meeting the need for security and scalability

A key reason that CoStar turned to Microsoft was for its robust security and compliance features. Azure AI Foundry provides advanced threat protection and regulatory compliance frameworks, helping ensure the highest standards of data protection and operational integrity. “Protecting our proprietary data is how we protect our business value. It’s no small thing that Microsoft is helping us achieve this,” says Florance.

Safeguarding customer conversations and maintaining compliance with data collection and disclosure laws is automatically managed with Azure AI Foundry.

Azure AI Foundry also offers autoscale features that automatically adjust resource limits based on real-time usage metrics. This helps guarantee that CoStar’s conversational AI solution can handle varying loads efficiently without manual intervention.

Preparing for what’s next

CoStar’s innovative real-time audio search sets it up for an exciting future. With the heavy lift of initial development complete, the company is poised to implement this solution across its other marketplaces domestically and globally. The success of the project is expected to drive more traffic to homes.com, ultimately increasing revenue.

Committing to exploration

CoStar aims to continue enhancing the buyer experience, making it even more personalized and intuitive. The foundational work done with Azure AI Foundry and the interoperability of advanced models like Mistral and Azure OpenAI GPT-4o Realtime API sets the stage for future innovations.

Florance concludes, “With Azure AI Foundry, we’re exploring the latest AI has to offer. Our data is highly secure, we can scale for millions of visitors, and in the end, we’re radically improving how people search for—and find—a place to call home."

Inflation, supply chain disruptions, and labor shortages have intensified pressure on already slim margins in the highly competitive retail industry. Facing intense competition, The ODP Corporation (NASDAQ: ODP), which includes Office Depot, ODP Business Solutions, and VEYER, needed more than incremental improvements to remain competitive. Protecting its market share became an urgent imperative. To address these pressures, The ODP Corporation strategically embraced generative AI—not simply to streamline workflows, but to accelerate innovation, increase agility, and strengthen its competitive edge without increasing costs.

Building on Azure for rapid AI development

To accelerate its AI journey, The ODP Corporation chose a unified development framework that combines Azure AI Foundry products such as Azure AI Search, Azure AI Document Intelligence, Azure OpenAI, and Azure AI Language. These became the foundation for building an enterprise AI environment at The ODP Corporation, supporting development of the ODP Personal Assistant and tailored assistants for HR, sales, and retail operations.

“Having the guarantee that our data would remain in our tenant and that models would not be trained on it was a big differentiator for us,” says Richard Coggins, Vice President and Distinguished Engineer at The ODP Corporation. These assurances were critical in securing leadership support and driving confidence in a company-wide rollout.

Azure AI Foundry connects key services into one pipeline, simplifying data prep, indexing, and model interaction. The ODP Corporation used Azure AI Document Intelligence to structure 10,000-plus documents, index them with Azure AI Search, and flag PII with Azure AI Language. Azure OpenAI powers the conversational interface, helping teams quickly move from idea to prototype without infrastructure complexity. “With Azure AI Foundry, we can move from concept to prototype in weeks,” says Carl Brisco, Chief Technology Officer and Senior Vice President at The ODP Corporation. Coggins agrees. “These tools worked together out of the box—we didn’t need to spend time wiring up infrastructure. With Azure AI Foundry, we can focus on building applications with real business impact.”

The ODP Corporation quickly formed a cross-functional team to deliver custom AI solutions that support productivity and address business challenges across departments.

Creating custom chatbots for retail, sales, and HR

In just six weeks, the team launched its foundational, internally developed ODP Personal Assistant, available for all associates. Building on that momentum, the team moved fast to deliver tailored solutions across the organization, including custom chatbots for retail, sales, and HR associates. Though each assistant addressed a different area of the business, all were built on the same architecture of Azure AI Foundry products to accelerate delivery and simplify management.

The ODP Corporation launched its first AI-powered assistant for retail, supporting over 12,000 retail associates across nearly 900 stores and delivering instant answers on handheld devices. It draws from documents processed by Azure AI Document Intelligence and indexed in Azure AI Search.

The HR assistant answers associates’ questions about PTO, leave, benefits, and training. Built on the Azure AI app platform—which includes AI, data, and app services—the HR assistant interprets prompts, retrieves HR info, and manages chat history. “We use Azure Cosmos DB to store HR data at the profile level,” says Mick Feller, Distinguished Engineer at The ODP Corporation. “It’s the glue between our back end and front end—everyone who logs in gets a profile, and the model reads and writes to it in real time to maintain context.”

The sales assistant helps reps generate quotes using natural language. Its SKU matching feature cross-references large product lists in minutes, versus days, and produces quote-ready summaries and tables.

From HR to sales to retail, The ODP Corporation’s chatbots are helping employees work faster, make better decisions, and support customers in real time.

Scaling and evolving the platform

With chatbots in place, The ODP Corporation shifted its focus to scaling the platform and extending its capabilities through agentic AI. The ODP Corporation containerized its platform on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), scaling compute on demand with a pay-as-you-go model that reduced costs and sped up rollout. “We’ve been running Kubernetes since 2017,” says Coggins. “AKS let us fast forward with a variable cost model. Instead of one or two services per VM, we could run 20 or 30 microservices.” That scalability supported multiple chatbots, faster testing, and lower infrastructure costs.

With the platform scaled and optimized, The ODP Corporation began exploring what agentic AI could unlock. The team is now building a multi-agent system with Azure AI Foundry, using AutoGen by Microsoft Research with Azure OpenAI and Azure AI Search for an agentic RAG solution. Early use cases include sales prospecting, deep research, and complex document search. “We’re building agents that can perform long-running processes and check back with humans when needed,” says Coggins. “We’re running AutoGen v0.4 on AKS, and the entire experience is hosted within Azure AI Foundry.”

These early systems are laying the groundwork for self-service intelligence, allowing teams to focus on strategy while an AI agent handles repetitive work. “The AI agent is a single pane of glass for many applications across the enterprise,” says Brisco. “Azure’s breadth and depth lets us create something that delivers real value across every part of our business.”

Adoption has spread beyond technical teams. The ODP Corporation launched its own AI Champions network and monthly AI Connect events to share updates, gather feedback, and spark innovation. More than 700 employees joined the initial sessions. “We started with just three of us,” says Patti Mooney, Director of Product and Technology at The ODP Corporation. “Now we have more than 50 AI champions and a huge appetite for what’s next.”

Delivering real-world impact and results

The ODP Corporation’s AI assistants now support more than 16,000 associates across departments, with more than 7,500 active users across Office Depot, ODP Business Solutions, and VEYER. These tools are saving time, increasing speed, and opening new revenue streams across the business.

The HR assistant has reduced routine ticket volume by instantly resolving questions about benefits, leave, and training. It now handles an average of 172 prompts per week, replacing a 24-hour turnaround with real-time answers.

In retail, associates using the ODP Personal Assistant on handheld devices resolve customer questions on the spot. Across the organization, prompt volume has grown 431% year over year, and users have logged over one million prompt interactions and more than 100,000 unique threads.

One ODP Business Solutions sales representative used the sales assistant to analyze 1,000 SKUs in under an hour—a process that previously required manual analyst support over multiple days. Another sales representative was able to respond to a pricing bid during a customer call. A third representative cross-referenced 4,000 competitor items, saving 25-plus hours and helping to drive $800,000 in net new annual business. With pricing bids now delivered in hours—which previously required one–two days—and tailored quotes saving reps five-eight hours a week, the sales assistant is driving 20% more sales opportunities each quarter.

These aren’t isolated gains. The ODP Corporation has reshaped work across sales, service, HR, and retail and plans to extend Azure AI Foundry to supply chain and procurement.

New agentic AI prototypes are also underway, designed to handle more complex, long-running tasks across teams. “This technology has changed how we work,” says Brisco. “And we’re just getting started.”

Leading online automotive retailer Carvana is known for changing the way people buy and sell cars. Carvana completely reimagined the car buying and selling process with the customer in mind. Its vertically integrated operations and purpose-built technology let customers browse, finance, purchase, and even trade in a car entirely online, putting the customer in control of a process that is fast, fun, and fair.

“Our goal has always been to make the car buying process the smoothest, easiest, and most transparent experience possible,” explains Alex Devkar, SVP of Engineering and Analytics at Carvana. “We put the customer in the driver’s seat,” he says. 

Prioritizing the customer experience

Carvana’s unique approach was designed to create fundamentally better customer experiences in automotive retail. The company uses technology to bring convenience and transparency to every step of the process, and has a strong culture of continuous improvement, always raising the bar and removing customer frictions.

In recent years, Carvana delivered high-quality customer support with Sebastian, an AI agent. Sebastian has deep insight and action-taking capabilities to help guide customers through every step of the buying and selling journey. To make both Sebastian and Carvana’s Customer Advocate team even more efficient and effective in working with customers, Carvana created CARE (Conversation Analysis Review Engine). This AI-powered platform pulls insight from every customer touchpoint to keep getting better.

Analyzing conversations with AI

CARE, Carvana’s quality review platform, works alongside Sebastian to analyze millions of customer conversations each month to ensure consistency in quality and identify opportunities for improvement. These insights allow Carvana to find and solve problems, provide high-quality feedback for its tools and teams, and refine its approach to customer support over time.

When it came to developing CARE, building with Microsoft was an easy choice, according to Michael Graf, Associate Director of Engineering at Carvana. “Microsoft was the obvious answer,” Graf says. “Pretty much all of our systems run on Microsoft Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) to scale and reliably provide all our services and for simplified management. We have a single place for all our stuff in the ecosystem that we could very easily scaffold up in a matter of minutes with just the click of a button. Having our infrastructure and AI foundation on Microsoft is a competitive advantage to Carvana. It puts us in a position to run fast, adapt to the market, and innovate with less complexity.” 

Efficient development for faster deployment

The development team at Carvana works with GitHub Copilot to automate repetitive tasks and enable faster, more efficient code writing. With GitHub Copilot handling routine coding tasks, engineers can focus on more complex and creative problems. Interoperability with the Microsoft ecosystem makes workflows seamless.

CARE uses Azure AI Speech within Azure AI Foundry for quick and accurate transcription. CARE data is stored in Azure Cosmos DB for scalability, security, and uptime. “We use Azure Cosmos DB for every step of our process with CARE,” Graf explains.

With the flexibility of Azure Cosmos DB, the Carvana team can move quickly and adapt to change on the fly. “My team is running really fast on complex projects, and we don’t know all the answers until we bump into them. So having flexibility with schema changes, with automatically scaling throughput and storage with Azure Cosmos DB, is key,” Graf says. Taken together, these benefits mean the development team can get product to market faster.

Ensuring a secure, compliant environment

Azure architecture delivers enterprise-grade reliability, security, speed, and scalability. This is critical to meet the demand for real-time answers in a live, high-pressure environment. Given that customer conversations may include sensitive information, security and compliance are nonnegotiable for Carvana. “Microsoft has been a great resource for making sure all of the data that Sebastian and CARE have access to is handled in a compliant, secure way,” Devkar says. 

Attaining 100% visibility

By moving from sampling a smaller number of customer interactions to 100% visibility into customer interactions, CARE enables continuous improvement across the board. Graf emphasizes, “The data has validated that our training efforts are paying off, and our advocates are all on the same page in how we’re servicing customers.”

AI-powered solutions at Carvana drive both customer satisfaction and operational efficiency. “As Sebastian gets better at supporting customers, driven by refinement through CARE, average calls per sale have decreased 45% over the past two years,” says Tacarra Brown, Associate Director of Customer Service at Carvana. This decrease in calls allows Carvana Customer Advocates to dedicate more time to personalized service and complex problem-solving. Brown notes, “Sebastian handles more standard scenarios, leaving more time and space for our Advocates to handle complex situations where it matters most.”

Maintaining the cutting edge

Building on the success of Sebastian and CARE, Carvana is road-testing Azure AI Foundry Agent Service to manage multiple agents with just a few lines of code. This forward-looking approach helps ensure that Carvana remains at the cutting edge of technology, continuously improving the customer experience and operational efficiency. 

“Microsoft has been a great collaborator, making sure we have access to the latest workflows, security, and models in Azure AI Foundry so we can provide enterprise-grade solutions for our customers,” Devkar says.
