Pixel Lab’s developer team is pushing the boundaries of digital storytelling, building an AI-powered remix experience that lets Coldplay fans generate personalized video creations. This fusion of artist visuals, music, and emotion transforms Coldplay’s “A Film For The Future” into something interactive. The resulting experience at afftf.coldplay.com allows fans to blend their own thoughts with ideas and imagery from the film, along with music from Coldplay’s latest album, MOON MUSiC. In this way, fans can create their own custom emotional narrative through the use of Microsoft 365 Copilot and the Azure AI stack.

By pairing open-source tools with Azure AI Foundry, the team created a dynamic remix engine based on emotion and visual resonance. Pixel Lab drew on the idea of a “mood ring,” where colors are associated with emotions to simplify the complex, creating something unique to how each fan engages with the band’s music.

“We‘re very proud of ‘A Film For The Future,’ which was created by 151 amazing artists from around the world,” says Coldplay. “The film is a glorious, kaleidoscopic patchwork quilt of individuality, and we love that Microsoft’s technology has helped everyone to make their own unique version of it.”

Pixel Lab developer Josh Wagoner highlights some of the Azure AI technologies used to process the imagery and ideas from “A Film For The Future,” including Azure AI Video Indexer and Azure AI Vision, and create the video playback experience, showcasing WebGL, Canvas, and the Web Audio API.

In this Q&A, Pixel Lab developers Robby Ingebretsen, Josh Wagoner, and Joel Fillmore take us behind the scenes. They share how they brought one of the most forward-thinking AI-powered music experiences to life—where fans, technology, and creativity all remix together.

How did you approach building an AI-driven creative platform from the ground up?

Robby Ingebretsen: We first set out to define what an AI-driven remix experience should feel like. We weren’t just building a tool—we were creating an artistic collaboration between Coldplay’s visuals, their music, and the fan’s own input. That meant designing AI to feel like a creative partner, not just an algorithm. Azure AI Foundry let us try out different models and evolve the interaction until it felt right.

Josh Wagoner: The key was mapping user inputs to the visuals in an organic way. The film is a collection of artist-submitted video clips, and we needed a method to match fan-generated text with the videos. Our “mood ring” system helped us match emotional tone to imagery. We connected color to emotion, and we then used Azure AI Foundry as a gateway to a wide variety of products, including Azure OpenAI APIs, Azure AI Vision, and Azure AI Video Indexer, to process the film and align fan-submitted text with specific clips to feel personal and real.

How did you use the Azure AI stack to analyze and categorize Coldplay’s artist-created visuals?

Josh Wagoner: We started by running the 151 video clips through Azure AI Video Indexer to segment scenes and identify transitions. We then fed those clips through Azure AI Vision to extract color, object recognition, and movement patterns. That gave us a rich set of attributes to work with. We combined those with GPT-generated summaries to turn the visuals into a format the AI could match to fan-submitted text.

Robby Ingebretsen: Once we had a structured dataset, the next step was making sure it aligned with fan inputs. We used the latest GPT-series model to generate textual descriptions of each video clip, essentially translating visual information into something our AI matching system could process. We built a framework where fan-submitted text could be analyzed, categorized, and matched to corresponding video moments in real time.

How did you build the AI system that matches text to video content organically?

Josh Wagoner: The system had to analyze user inputs, determine the sentiment and emotional tone, and find the best-matching video content. We used Azure OpenAI to classify text into predefined emotional categories. Then we developed a ranking system that scored potential video matches based on sentiment analysis, visual coherence, and overall thematic relevance.

Joel Fillmore: The AI pipeline involved multiple steps. First, user text was processed through sentiment analysis. Then, the system queried our database of video segments and compared them based on emotional similarity. Finally, the AI ranked the best-matching clips and dynamically assembled a remix experience for the user.

Robby Ingebretsen: One of the most rewarding aspects of this project was seeing how the AI-driven matching felt organic. We weren’t just throwing random video clips together—we were building a system that let fans cocreate something emotional and unique, within Coldplay’s world.

How did you ensure seamless synchronization, scalability, and security for a global audience?

Joel Fillmore: We wanted every user worldwide to see the same experience at the same moment. Each remix is synced to a global timeline, so fans can see when their personalized version will play in the continuously streaming song. We used Azure Front Door and Azure Content Delivery Network to deliver content quickly across geographies, and Static Web Apps made it possible to scale seamlessly based on demand.

Josh Wagoner: We designed the back end to handle traffic spikes by caching AI results and scaling compute dynamically. Using Azure Functions (Flex Consumption plan), we ensured back-end processes could handle thousands of simultaneous requests without breaking. And security was just as critical. We implemented encrypted user submissions, granular access controls, and protected endpoints through secure API gateways.

How did you build the user interface for the application?

Josh Wagoner: The remix plays on a video canvas rendered with WebGL, with real-time effects driven by the Web Audio API. When the audio plays, the outer ring pulses with the beat, using frequency analysis to animate color shifts and glow. We used Canvas and Three.js to apply a soft blur and animate the mask dynamically, giving the visuals a subtle, breathing quality. The whole interface is immersive, like the experience is reacting to the music in real time.

What advice would you give to developers looking to build AI-powered interactive experiences?

Robby Ingebretsen: AI is more accessible than many developers think. The most important thing is learning how to frame problems in a way that AI can help solve. You don’t need to be a machine learning expert to build something meaningful—you just need a clear vision and the right tools.

Josh Wagoner: Experimentation is key. AI doesn’t always behave predictably, so you need to iterate quickly and test different approaches. We spent a lot of time testing the system with real-world fan input and refining how matching worked over time.

Joel Fillmore: And finally, always design for scale. Even if it starts as an experiment, think through concurrency, caching, and how your services will respond under load. Azure gives you flexibility—but only if you plan for growth from the start.

Delivering AI-powered engagement for fans around the world, these developers used multiple Azure AI solutions to pave the way for a new kind of interactive storytelling. With Azure AI Foundry, Pixel Lab built a remix engine that’s scalable, customizable, and emotionally resonant, proving that with the right tools, developers can lead the next era of creative innovation.

With pressure mounting to meet rising client expectations, law firms are discovering that traditional tools, siloed systems, and manual workflows are no longer sufficient. Assembly Software is focused on developing software to support legal professionals, delivering scalable, secure, and configurable solutions that streamline legal workflows and unlock new levels of productivity.

“We know people in the legal sector often work long hours and face high stress,” says McKay Ferrell, SVP of Products at Assembly Software. “We’re committed to helping them be more efficient and productive through technology.”

Legal case management is particularly time-consuming and complex. Tasks include creating and maintaining client profiles, drafting legal communications, reviewing extensive documents, and tracking expenses. Firms also need to ensure privacy and compliance while adhering to strict deadlines. “We wanted to find more ways to ease the burden and give back time to attorneys and their staff so they can serve more clients,” explains Ferrell.

The Assembly Software team recognized that a generative AI solution could automate many of these legal tasks and deliver significant efficiency gains. The team envisioned a fully embedded generative AI solution to securely automate nearly every aspect of the legal workflow, from document receipt to data extraction and automated entry, all the way to document generation and performance reporting.

Establishing a foundation

“As a Microsoft shop that uses Azure, we trust Azure AI Foundry as a comprehensive platform for designing, customizing, and managing AI solutions. It was ideal for us because it’s scalable and provides the robust security and compliance the legal industry demands,” says James Garrett, CTO at Assembly Software.

With Azure AI Foundry, Assembly Software knew it could simplify AI development processes and workflows and create a solution to handle its customers’ critical needs. Requirements for the solution, called NeosAI, included capabilities for easy document generation. These abilities encompassed generating abstractive and extractive document summaries, intelligent data extraction, optical character recognition (OCR), and dynamic forms.

To prepare the team for a successful build, Assembly Software provided all its engineers with GitHub Copilot licenses. “GitHub Copilot significantly improved our productivity,” says Rick Cirigliano, CPO at Assembly Software. “Our developers can write and execute code more efficiently with real-time code suggestions and code structure completion in GitHub Copilot.” This helped accelerate project deployment, ensure adherence to best practices, and produce error-free code.

Building NeosAI

By using Azure DevOps, NeosAI developers can track code changes, build applications, and support a seamless deployment pipeline. The NeosAI user interface (UI), built with React, is hosted on Azure Content Delivery Network for quick loading and availability. The React UI communicates with back-end services via APIs written in .NET 8, hosted on Azure App Service and Azure Functions, enabling real-time responses and efficient workflow handling.

“NeosAI is designed to handle a high volume of transactions, achieving an impressive average response time of 67.2 milliseconds across 4.2 million transactions per hour,” says Garrett. “This performance is directly related to the effectiveness of the capabilities of Azure, including load balancing and failover strategies.” Cirigliano adds, “We do our own monitoring of the DTU (database transaction unit) and utilize Azure management APIs to upscale and downscale.”

Azure App Service helps NeosAI run web applications, mobile applications, and microservices. “Azure App Service helps our developers focus more on their application and less on the underlying infrastructure, enhancing productivity and efficiency,” explains Ferrell.

The back end consists of multiple Azure services, helping ensure high availability and scalability. According to Garrett, the team uses Azure SQL Database and Azure Cosmos DB for data management, optimizing performance and response times. Azure Cosmos DB is used for US-distributed cross-tenant data structures and rapid response times, specifically for components like Neos Activity Feed and Notifications. “The regional availability and multi-region read-and-write capabilities of Azure Cosmos DB help us ensure low latency and high availability, making it ideal for handling hot data,” Garrett says.

Efficiency through AI automation

Cirigliano says Azure AI services plays a pivotal role in supporting NeosAI. He explains, “We merged Azure AI Foundry into workflows, rather than introducing it as a separate module, making it a seamless part of the users’ experiences.” This supports users in easily creating tailored case communications. It also drives an interactive chat function that gives NeosAI the ability to provide interactive and intelligent responses to user queries on both document generation and interrogation.

“One of the most time-consuming tasks for our customers is searching through documents for critical information pertaining to their cases,” says Ferrell. “We used Azure AI Search for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to support contextual searches, ensuring NeosAI can easily retrieve relevant information from large datasets, saving firms a significant amount of time.”

Cirigliano adds that the average big law firm bills at rates ranging from $500 to $1,000 per hour. Therefore, the time savings provided by Azure AI Search can translate into substantial financial savings for these firms.

Assembly Software used Azure AI Document Intelligence to help NeosAI automate extraction of information from a variety of documents, including forms, photo IDs, invoices, and receipts. Azure AI Vision for OCR easily pulls text from images. This reduces the need for manual data entry and helps ensure that information is captured accurately. Ferrell adds that with Azure AI Speech, NeosAI will soon be able to transcribe and analyze spoken language for legal documents and communications, which further supports accuracy and speeds document processing.

Enhanced privacy and security

NeosAI prioritizes the privacy and security of user data, ensuring that firm data is not shared with other Assembly Software customers or Microsoft Azure services. Assembly Software also uses Microsoft Defender as part of its security suite. 

Named entity extraction and personal data extraction help identify and extract specific entities and personal data from documents, ensuring compliance with data privacy regulations. This is crucial for maintaining the integrity and confidentiality of sensitive information. In addition, says Cirigliano, “The AI models we use through Azure help ensure a zero data retention policy for data passed through NeosAI APIs.” Upon generating and sending back a response, the input data is immediately deleted.

Massive time savings, efficiency gains

Deployed in under six months, NeosAI simplifies legal workflows and saves firms time and resources. Features like document drafting automation, speedy document review, and efficient information retrieval help law firms reduce errors and inconsistencies. Documents are processed quickly and accurately, reducing manual data entry.

“By eliminating data entry, there are fewer accuracy issues. It’s improving expense tracking and optimizing firm performance,” says Ferrell. With their newfound efficiency, legal teams can spend more time on their clients.

Assembly Software customers report that NeosAI saves them up to 25 hours per case on manual data entry, document generation, and review. It has cut the time required to draft legal documents from 40 hours to mere minutes. 

Ferrell adds that NeosAI has, on average, given Assembly Software customers efficiency gains equivalent to approximately two full-time equivalents (FTEs) for a legal team with 20 users over the course of a year. The outcome translates to about a 10% gain. “This is significant for firms that are more interested in growth and productivity savings than cutting staff,” says Ferrell.

With the growing adoption of NeosAI by law firms in the United States, Assembly Software is exploring ways to expand NeosAI’s reach. Concludes Garrett, “Thanks to the solid foundation of Azure AI, databases, and apps, we have the ability to continually innovate and adapt the platform to meet the specific legal requirements of different regions around the world, paving the way for future AI advancements and global expansion.”

The AI revolution has fundamentally reshaped customer expectations. Beyond essential uptime and performance for business-critical operations, the seamless integration of intelligent AI features is now the new expected standard.

Writesonic is an AI-powered marketing and SEO platform that streamlines research, strategy, content creation, and optimization into a single interface. Its all-in-one approach features AI agents handling end-to-end SEO workflows, content creation, and generative engine optimization (GEO). As one of the first to pioneer GEO, Writesonic uniquely helps brands track their visibility in AI search engines, offering actionable recommendations to improve brand presence in AI-generated responses. Tailored for marketing teams, agencies, and businesses seeking automation and data-driven solutions, the company has evolved from its conversational AI agent Chatsonic into a suite of specialized, round-the-clock AI marketing agents.

The company emerged from a clear need: to accelerate content creation for marketing needs. Writesonic founder and CEO Samanyou “Sam” Garg turned a side project into a start-up business. Acceptance into a leading start-up accelerator program fed Garg’s energy and technical acumen, which resulted in achieving his vision of creating AI solutions to help marketers and other content creators write smarter and faster.

However, a critical challenge arose. As queries and requests from the company’s increasing user base surged, so did its cloud platform instability. Platform outages could last hours, and access to the newest AI models could take days or months. An unreliable cloud infrastructure affected customer satisfaction and the start-up’s ability to expand and attract more enterprise businesses.

“We were seeing scale in the number of queries we were processing. We were also seeing stability issues, especially AI models going down, which was inconvenient for our users, so we began looking for a stable, enterprise-grade AI-powered platform,” recalls Garg.

The Writesonic team wanted a solution that offered speed to help process its growing number of queries. It also sought access to enterprise-grade AI models to provide stability for its expanding platform. Because Writesonic aimed to attract more enterprise customers, security features and a brand with built-in trust would be critical.

Searching for a stable, AI-ready solution

Writesonic needed a scalable and fast solution to manage the requests that its AI products handle for the company’s users. Garg felt he could achieve the pace and stability needed to level up the Writesonic platform by using Microsoft products and services.

The company migrated its data estate to Microsoft Azure, an AI-ready cloud environment equipped with advanced features, and strengthened its foundation for continued innovation, while boosting the user experience. “Microsoft adds new capabilities regularly and moves at the speed of a start-up. This is important, because at Writesonic, we innovate for speed in our products,“ explains Garg. Today, all of Writesonic’s products run on the Azure platform.

Immediate access to leading AI models

Before migrating, accessing new models could be delayed, sometimes by months, and a potentially disruptive process. Now Writesonic can get AI models—typically the same day they’re available—from Azure AI Foundry Models. “The availability of enterprise-grade AI models was a decisive factor in our migration to Azure,” says Garg. “At Writesonic, we stay on the cutting edge of AI. The space moves very fast. Having near-immediate access to new AI models gives us a competitive advantage—the faster you move and the quicker you implement, the more steps ahead of your competitor you are.”

Currently, Writesonic is experimenting with o4-mini reasoning models in Azure OpenAI in Azure AI Foundry Models. “We like the intermediate report generation of the Azure OpenAI o4-mini and its favorable query response times,” explains Ashish Bedi, Sr. Staff Software Engineer and Cybersecurity Leader at Writesonic. The strong consolidation capabilities of the o4-mini reason through the AI agent’s initial plan, gather information from various knowledge sources, and quickly summarize results. The o4-mini also offers significant cost savings over a third-party model that Writesonic has also been using. “The final report is the most cost-contributing factor in our entire pipeline,” adds Bedi.

Addressing latency issues with Azure

The bulk of Writesonic’s users reside in the United States and Europe. One concern for Garg was latency caused by geographic separation of users, AI models, and databases. Users expect near-instant responses to queries. These latency gaps create dissatisfaction, and delays lead to drop-offs. “Minimal latency was the key driver for adopting Azure Database for PostgreSQL,” says Garg. Writesonic uses the service to perform business-critical transactional query patterns and critical data operations via rest APIs.

The company also set up the TimescaleDB extension on Azure Database for PostgreSQL to efficiently manage time-series queries and avoid the complexity and overhead of a dedicated data lake. “TimescaleDB directly addressed latency issues by streamlining query paths,” says Bedi.

Beyond that, Writesonic uses the built-in zoned redundancy in Azure Database for PostgreSQL to help ensure exceptional reliability. “We have experienced no downtime, achieving more than 99.999% availability,” adds Bedi. This availability rate surpasses the guaranteed service level agreement for Azure Database for PostgreSQL.

Writesonic uses Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) for cost-effective and flexible workload scalability and the graceful node shutdown feature in AKS pods. This helps prevent interruptions to customer requests during traffic bursts, autoscaling, application updates, or node maintenance. Graceful shutdowns protect work in progress for customers and help ensure that resources are deployed correctly. “With AKS, we can seamlessly scale up or down based on user demand, helping ensure consistent performance,” says Garg.

Data security and the trust factor

Protecting user data is a top priority for Writesonic and customers. The enterprise-grade data security built into Azure is a boon, especially for Writesonic’s European customers that require localized hosting to meet privacy protocols.

“Microsoft’s reputation is an asset, especially when discussing AI model training and data security,” Garg points out. “Users do not want their data used for training models. Writesonic’s multitenant hosting, combined with Azure data policies, reinforces data protection.”

In addition to platform reliability and innovative capabilities and services, Garg explains that the collaboration with Microsoft comes with a trust factor, especially for enterprise customers. “We can move forward faster with bigger agreements, averting the six months of back-and-forth discussion with security teams,” he adds.

Writesonic continues driving innovation

Writesonic turned to Azure to achieve better stability and performance. The platform has helped take the company from 100,000 users to 10 million in just four years to uphold its mission of innovation in support of business growth.

“Our vision is to create fully autonomous AI marketing agents that provide proactive assistance, similar to Jarvis from Iron Man,” says Bedi. “We’re already delivering this with our SEO AI Agent and Content AI Agent that work 24/7 to handle end-to-end marketing workflows. What’s exciting is how we’re pioneering generative engine optimization to ensure brands remain visible in AI search results from ChatGPT and similar.” Continues Bedi, “With the high availability and advanced AI models in Azure, we’re accelerating our innovation in data-driven marketing automation that integrates with marketing tools to deliver real-time insights and automated fixes for SEO issues. This is transforming how marketing teams operate, reducing what used to take weeks into minutes.”

Enterprise revenue has significantly increased, now accounting for 20% of Writesonic’s total revenue, up from 2% pre-migration, a tenfold increase. Writesonic is more confident in its focus on expanding enterprise partnerships.

“We have stability, reliability, and data privacy with Azure—all the elements that allow us to move faster and make sure we are giving the latest and best to our customers,” concludes Garg.

Global Travel Collection (GTC*) is a network of elite travel advisors focused on creating unique experiences for their corporate and high-net-worth clients. Whether handling the travel plans for a corporate meeting or creating the itinerary for a European luxury vacation, details are everything and, unfortunately, everywhere. In fact, to book the kind of complex trips that GTC advisors handle, they might access 10 or more airline, hotel, entertainment, and corporate travel information resources.

Planning and booking highly personalized trips often took six to eight hours—time spent navigating fragmented systems, not adding value. Although clients never saw that work, GTC advisors felt the inefficiencies daily. “When I came to Global Travel Collection, I noticed a serious disconnect across the systems our advisors use. It was clear we needed to unify the data behind a single interface,” says Casey Soto, who serves as Senior Director of Product Management at Global Travel Collection and Artificial Intelligence Center of Excellence Leader at Internova, GTC’s parent company.

Mapping out the solution

Determined to simplify advisor access to the mountains of data that GTC advisors rely on, Soto set out to design and deploy Atlas, a secure, scalable, and compliant AI-powered platform purpose-built to help luxury travel advisors accelerate trip planning without removing the human touch.

As Soto considered how his team might simplify access to information for GTC’s network of elite travel agents focused on corporate and luxury travel, he was certain that AI was the right technology for the job. “GenAI looked like the easiest way to combine all these data sources, pulling everything into one spot to give advisors the ability to search all of it,” he says.

At the same time, Soto recognized a broader shift in user expectations: advisors were increasingly accustomed to natural language search in their everyday lives. To meet those expectations—and move beyond rigid keyword-based systems—his team needed to create an AI-powered platform that could understand conversational queries and return actionable, context-rich results. “To allow advisors to access information in the way they’d become accustomed, we had to create that system,” Soto adds. 

He knew that solving this challenge meant more than adding AI. It meant delivering a modern, governed architecture that could scale across the entire Internova portfolio. Together with Microsoft, Soto and his team began work on developing Atlas to give advisors fast access to accurate, high-quality travel information.

A plan for rapid innovation

Soto selected Microsoft Azure AI Foundry for its simplicity, advanced security, and flexibility to scale AI innovation quickly. The team began building Atlas with Copilot Studio, capitalizing on its rapid prototyping capabilities and graphical interface. As development progressed, they incorporated Azure AI Foundry to deepen interoperability, provide centralized governance, and orchestrate back-end workflows—including prompt flow, Azure AI Search, and Azure OpenAI in Azure AI Foundry Models. Atlas also uses Azure Blob Storage to more securely host travel content, enabling efficient retrieval through AI Search. “Azure AI Foundry was key to orchestrating the AI Search flow and ensuring our data was properly indexed,” Soto explains.

Together, Azure AI Foundry and Copilot Studio gave GTC a full-stack generative AI architecture. Copilot Studio delivered a low-code interface for advisor interaction, while Azure AI Foundry enabled highly secure model orchestration, data indexing, and scalable deployment across services.

Streamlining the development process

Soto’s team used Azure AI Foundry as the experimentation platform to rapidly test and refine Atlas. The management center in Azure AI Foundry allows for centralized governance, version control, and more secure deployment of the generative AI stack, helping the team scale confidently and reduce development friction. Azure AI Foundry orchestrates the retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline behind Atlas. Using Azure AI Search, the platform retrieves relevant content from SharePoint and travel data sources, while Azure OpenAI generates grounded responses in real time. This approach gives advisors access to context-rich answers without manual lookup.

In development, Copilot Studio acted as the interface where AI solutions developed in Azure AI Foundry were tied into user-friendly applications, dashboards, and workflows. In day-to-day operation, Atlas runs on a GTC-built interface fueled by Copilot Studio on the back end. Copilot Studio handles intent recognition and manages back-end workflows, including calls to Azure App Service. Hosting the custom orchestration logic that connects AI Search and Azure OpenAI, App Service powers the administrative portal used to manage advisor tools, content, and system workflows. 

By building on a fully managed platform as a service (PaaS), GTC reduced the time and resources needed for infrastructure management, allowing the team to focus on developing new AI capabilities. App Service also helps ensure global scalability, high availability, and enterprise-grade security without additional overhead. Atlas uses Azure Cosmos DB to store advisor interaction history and session context. In doing so, it lays the groundwork for future personalization, knowledge graph development, and more intelligent advisor–client interactions over time.

Building with Azure AI Foundry in Copilot Studio, GTC was able to take Atlas from idea to inception quickly and safely, with built-in governance, enterprise-grade security, and compliance that let the company embrace AI with confidence. Mark Munley, SVP and CIO at Global Travel Collection, amplified the value of the safety and security that Azure delivers, explaining, “Security is paramount to us as a company dealing with traveler information globally and having to worry about GDPR and other regulations and security protocols, like PCI compliance. We know that Microsoft’s whole ecosystem is set up for protection, and the fact that we could do all this within our Azure tenant was very important.”

Munley adds that choosing Microsoft was not only about compliance, but also about clarity and continuity. “We didn’t feel driven by the technology—we had a clear need, and the Microsoft tools we already had in place made it easy to deliver,” he says. “With so much of our data already in OneDrive, SharePoint, and our tenant, it just made intuitive sense to build Atlas in Copilot Studio powered by Azure AI Foundry.”

Faster access to better information

Atlas is built for high-value, context-rich interactions, such as surfacing policies, vendor details, and booking logic in seconds. Copilot Studio powers the back-end orchestration, enabling a seamless, guided experience that advisors rely on to plan complex travel. By replacing manual searches with a single natural-language query, Atlas solves one of the travel industry’s most persistent challenges: inefficient, disconnected data access.

Longtime Global Travel Collection advisor David Waldes estimates that Atlas saves him 10 to 15 minutes per query. “Atlas spiders out through our systems and gives me a solid answer in seconds—what used to take me 10 to 15 minutes,” he says. “For something as simple as ‘What are the best hotels in Zurich,’ I’m instantly seeing six options, past client feedback, and booking context, without having to dig.”

Maintaining momentum

With Atlas reducing planning time by an average of three hours per trip, GTC’s 1,700 advisors, with most booking 300-plus trips per year, are projected to reclaim over 1.5 million hours annually. Vendors are also taking note, with airlines and hotel brands exploring opportunities to feature their services within Atlas—a potential new revenue stream for GTC.

As usage grows, GTC plans to expand Atlas across Internova’s full network of 150,000 advisors. Built with Copilot Studio and Azure AI Foundry services, the platform is designed to scale securely, serving as a blueprint for future generative AI applications across the business.

On a sunny day at the Miami Zoo, four-year-old Amelia fed giraffes, petted a sloth, and made friends with tortoises. She shadowed animal experts to provide behind-the-scenes care to some of her favorite species. A chimpanzee even fingerpainted a picture for her. The animal-filled adventure offered a welcome break from treatment for pediatric leukemia, which Amelia was diagnosed with at age three. Her local Make-A-Wish organized every aspect of Amelia’s day as a zookeeper so the girl could focus on fun—and recovery. As Amelia’s mom remembered, "Her wish inspired us to keep going.”  

Make-A-Wish turns a child’s imagination into a hope-giving reality for children diagnosed with a critical illness. The nonprofit works with families, medical providers, volunteers, and communities to grant wishes, from a tropical island vacation to a photo shoot with a unicorn. The anticipation, experience, and memories help them endure challenging therapies, explains Keith Goodwin, Chief Information Officer at Make-A-Wish. “We bring joy, hope, and strength to children with critical illnesses, their families, and their communities,” he adds. “Having something to look forward to makes a difference in their outcomes."

It takes a lot of steps to grant a wish, from fundraising and medical provider referrals to planning and executing the experience. With partner Redapt’s support, Make-A-Wish is optimizing its operations with Microsoft technology to ensure they can fulfill as many wishes as possible. “We’re a wall-to-wall Microsoft shop, and that has a direct impact on our mission,” Goodwin says.

With Microsoft 365 Copilot, Azure, Copilot Studio, the Microsoft Power Platform, Power BI, and other supporting technologies, Make-A-Wish is making more children’s wishes come true.

Increasing productivity with generative AI

Whether a child wishes for a celebrity meetup, a trip to a theme park, or a new puppy, that wish requires an all-hands-on-deck mentality. Make-A-Wish is rolling out Microsoft 365 Copilot to do that work more efficiently, creating more time and energy for mission-critical efforts. 

“There’s a direct correlation between leveraging AI and operating more effectively,” Goodwin says. Make-A-Wish staff direct Microsoft 365 Copilot to write first drafts of emails, blog posts, strategic plans, and more, then use their expertise to revise and refine materials. The AI assistant also takes notes during meetings, transcribes calls, and tracks follow-up actions. Tackling manual, repetitive, and time-intensive tasks through generative AI helps teams create more marketing materials, generate more revenue, and engage with the many people who make wishes happen. 

Make-A-Wish's IT staff also built Wish Helper, a generative AI chatbot built with Copilot Studio that enables self-service IT support. Users can ask questions, from how to reset a password to how to set up a new SharePoint folder. The chatbot helps users troubleshoot issues by either providing curated answers to common questions or using Azure AI Search to pull information from approved knowledge sources then generating conversational answers. It helps around the clock, an important expansion of support for staff working fundraising events or helping wish families on nights, weekends, and holidays. 

“We’re seeing a lot of demand for AI, in part because of the success of the chatbot,” explains Derek Johnson, Senior Director of Infrastructure, Security, and Operations at Make-A-Wish. Roughly two-thirds of the nonprofit's staff use the self-service chatbot on a given week. As the IT team continues to iterate on the tool, they anticipate improvements will further enable staff to solve their own IT challenges. With fewer tickets to tackle, the IT staff could redirect their energy to value-adding projects, such as expanding the chatbot’s scope to cover HR and finance questions. 

By streamlining everyday tasks, generative AI empowers Make-A-Wish staff, Goodwin says. “Copilot makes us faster so we can work to ensure we serve every eligible child.”

Unifying data for insights and action

To execute on its mission, Make-A-Wish's national and regional chapters needed an accurate, up-to-date understanding of the organization’s fundraising, engagement, wish granting pipelines, and more. Reporting used to be manual and time-consuming, leading to differing figures staff would spend hours reconciling. Now with a unified data platform in Azure and Microsoft Fabric, Make-A-Wish has a single source of truth to distill insights, direct planning, and support a nationwide effort to help children diagnosed with critical illnesses.

Data funnels into centralized storage in the Azure cloud, where it is aggregated and cleansed into data sets. National and regional chapters alike have access to this data, which leadership uses to improve business processes and navigate turbulent times in the nonprofit sector.

Consolidation of data in Azure warehouses empowers Make-A-Wish to utilize deep wells of information for analytics. “This allows Make-A-Wish to properly steer resources in the right direction for generating revenue, reducing donor churn, increasing engagement, and producing the most effective engagement strategies,” explains Joe Maurer, Senior Client Director for Tech for Social Impact at Redapt. “This enhances their ability to make predictions, increase donor value, and fulfill their mission of granting wishes to more children.”

For example, the nonprofit used Azure Machine Learning to create a predictive model for the fundraising team. The model scans donation transactions to identify supporters who are more likely to increase their giving to Make-A-Wish. This predictive capability helps the fundraising team to focus their efforts on building relationships with the greatest potential of generating the revenue needed to expand the nonprofit’s capacity to grant even more wishes. 

Power BI pulls data from Azure and Fabric to create dashboards for every Make-A-Wish chapter, which are like “real-time report cards,” Goodwin says. Now that Power BI operates under Fabric as a unified source, dashboards can connect to multiple data sources, take advantage of the Power BI automation capabilities, and better analyze chapter wish granting, revenue, budgeting, and more.

Many offices display these dashboards—such as ones depicting the status of in-process wishes or fundraising streams—so all staff can track important metrics such as average wait time for wish completion, the number of referrals, average wish cost, and more. They can compare their benchmarks to national averages and to nearby chapters.  

“A complete understanding of our data profoundly impacts the daily operation of everything we do,” Goodwin says. “We use dashboards every day to drive efficiency in financials and mission work.” For example, up-to-date revenue figures indicate how a chapter is performing against budgets and forecasts, enabling leadership to provide additional support or change tactics when needed. Dashboards also reveal bottlenecks or challenges, such as a spike in new wishes, so nearby chapters or national staff can quickly step in to help. 

Goodwin says, “Data visibility empowers our teams. We make sure our resources have the most impact for more wishes.”

Fulfilling more wishes on a budget

Generous supporters donate loyalty points and other in-kind gifts to Make-A-Wish to facilitate kids’ wishes. Given that travel tends to be the most costly aspect of wish fulfillment, these gifts enable the nonprofit to serve more families on a limited budget.  

Make-A-Wish had a web application to track these in-kind donations, called the Wish Bank. The organization recently upgraded the Wish Bank using Microsoft Power Platform to enhance security, refine the user interface, allow for ongoing modifications, and improve tracking capabilities. They began by migrating their on-premises SQL database to a newly established Azure SQL database, which includes comprehensive management of data, security, and database administration.  

The team also reconstructed the .NET application and its forms using Microsoft Power Apps and Power Automate. The Wish Bank now employs shared connectors to the SQL database for data updates, while a Microsoft 365 Outlook connector was used for automated email notifications. The tool links to Power BI for reporting purposes, enabling Make-A-Wish to track gifted points, which chapters have received points, and more. 

“Our collaboration on Wish Bank v2 allows non-technical users to manage donations easier and faster, without having to write complex code,” Mauer says.  

The Azure SQL database houses data of all the gifted points, organized by airline, hotel brand, and credit card company as well as other details, such as expiration date. This granular detail is vital to Make-A-Wish's reporting, which external partners require, and to ensure miles are used before they lapse.  

The secure, centralized inventory empowers staff to efficiently make the best use of donations. For example, the deep pool of points with a wide variety of carriers enables staff to choose one that offers a needed flight for less. The new, intuitive interface also streamlines the previously manual processes of requesting, approving, and distributing requests for points or miles. The visibility of the single solution also helps the team effectively and fairly distribute gifted points across chapters.   

With the former .NET application, a skilled developer had to make any needed modifications. Now the team can easily adjust the Wish Bank within the low- and no-code Microsoft Power Platform. This flexibility enables Make-A-Wish to refine the tool, for example adding different categories of in-kind donations to the Wish Bank.  

The improvements mean it will be easier for Make-A-Wish to distribute miles and other donations, reducing the cost of wish-associated travel—and freeing funds to make more wishes happen. "The new Wish Bank helps us distribute donations fairly among chapters,” Goodwin says.

Improving security to protect children’s data

To make children’s wishes come true, Make-A-Wish stewards families’ data, including sensitive information such as medical diagnoses. The nonprofit is dedicated to protecting children’s privacy through industry-leading technology safeguards. 

“As a nonprofit, the integrity of our brand is everything. To fulfill our mission, people must trust that we can protect their data,” Goodwin says. 

Microsoft security products and services shield Make-A-Wish's operations across the board. Microsoft Defender for Cloud uses advanced threat protection, detection, and response for the nonprofit’s cloud applications, storage, devices, identities, and more. Purview provides next-level data security as well as a holistic platform for data governance and compliance. Make-A-Wish sets up policies and procedures within Purview to ensure only approved staff can access beneficiary data, information is securely stewarded throughout its lifecycle, and that data is retained only as long as it is needed.

Make-A-Wish's digital infrastructure, platforms, and data are now safer behind the Microsoft Cloud’s defenses. Centralizing its apps and data on Azure diminished security vulnerabilities of on-premises servers while enabling the nonprofit to share information needed for collaboration. Securely communicating information with external partners brings in additional resources, such as in-kind donations, increasing the number of wishes granted. In addition, the nonprofit created and hosts several public-facing websites with Azure App Service, taking advantage of Azure’s built-in security and compliance features. 

Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio, and Azure also "close cyber risks,” Johnson says. “With Copilot, we have a central gen AI solution we control and that ties into our entire security framework,” he adds. With an approved and closed generative AI solution, Make-A-Wish steers staff away from external, open-source AI tools that may store and use inputs. 

Every improvement makes a difference for Make-A-Wish's mission, Goodwin explains. “While we grant over 16,000 wishes a year, for every wish we grant, there are still two children with critical illnesses whose wishes need financial support. Anytime we can save a dollar or time through technology, that means more wishes for more children. That’s how we can reach our vision to grant the wish of every eligible child.”

Intralox’s conveyance solutions have moved the world’s most critical products for more than 50 years. Its extensive portfolio of modular plastic conveyor belts can be found in food processing plants, industrial manufacturing facilities, and logistics and material handling applications worldwide. Its innovative product line isn’t the company’s only distinction, however. It also offers the industry’s most comprehensive customer support, thanks in large part to Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales, Customer Service, and Field Service. Now Intralox is empowering its support teams with AI-powered insights, efficiencies, and time savings with Microsoft 365 Copilot for Sales, Copilot in Dynamics 365 Customer Service, and Copilot in Dynamics 365 Field Service.

Innovation in constant motion
Like its conveyor systems, Intralox’s culture of innovation is in constant motion. The company successfully boosted its customer service effectiveness with Dynamics 365 Sales, Customer Service, and Field Service in 2019, 2020, and 2021, respectively, and was soon looking for ways to apply its new insights to its customers and the products they use to improve customer experiences. Copilot in Customer Service, Copilot in Field Service, and Copilot for Sales promised to improve access to information, reduce inefficiencies, and save time for both Intralox and its customers—and they delivered.

Copilot in Customer Service

Intralox products are highly specialized, so a deep understanding of customers’ applications is critical. And with nearly 40,000 service calls each year for everything from initial consultations and custom system design to installation, maintenance, and repairs, service center and field technicians don’t have a lot of time for research. Response time is key for a customer-centered company. At Intralox, the goal is optimizing, not reducing, call times, and case and conversation summaries generated by Copilot in Customer Service help technicians get up to speed quickly and efficiently.

Key customer interactions and requests are entered in Dynamics 365 Customer Service to capture customers’ continuous flow of information with the company. Copilot case summaries turn that abundant data into easily consumable information. “If we can introduce efficiencies into understanding our customers, that yields a more meaningful conversation and deepens our relationship with that customer,” says Jordan Farley, Product Owner for Customer Service.

Case summaries are a thorough and convenient reference for understanding an account and gaining insights on how to move the relationship forward. Better still, Microsoft’s soon to be released Customer Intent Agent in Dynamics 365 Contact Center will take that capability even further. Customer Intent Agent analyzes past interactions to create an intent library that helps service representatives quickly understand customer needs, guide conversations with follow-up questions, and offer tailored solutions in real time.

Copilot in Field Service

When a customer issue can’t be resolved remotely and is escalated to onsite service, the field service team members review the case in Field Service, including emails, notes, troubleshooting steps, and other details, along with service history and related cases. Intralox customers often have several cases open at a time, many with long timelines that would take considerable time to review. Case summaries allow the company’s 300 service team members to hit the ground running. Megan Hearen, Field Service Product Lead, says that Copilot “does a really good job of taking all that information and giving a quick summary, including people involved, tasks, requests, and recommendations.”

After a service call, Copilot in Field Service work order summaries offer a clear and comprehensive picture of the work done onsite, helping remote service representatives and technicians in real-time troubleshooting and optimizing the time they spend with each customer. “We really pride ourselves on what we call Level 4 Partnerships with our customers—fast, reliable, personalized service to work together to solve a problem,” says Hearen. Whether its account managers, customer service teams, or technicians, “we want to be able to get on a call and quickly have an understanding of the background without making our customer repeat it. Work order and case summaries help provide a seamless, personalized, high-quality service experience for our customers from onsite repair to call center.”

With customers in more than 100 countries, Intralox offers support in 18 languages—and so does Copilot in Field Service. Copilot summaries allow service teams to view and update cases in their native language.

Because customer complaints are entered as cases, product managers can search cases across multiple customers to quickly identify common issues and trends and drill down to pertinent records. The time they used to spend poring through long email chains and notes to research complaints can now be devoted to addressing customers’ concerns.

Intralox customers are also saving time with Copilot in Field Service, because all those gains in efficiency allow the company to be more proactive. When an issue is identified, support teams can quickly assess the scale of the problem and prepare resources accordingly. Often, it can be preempted entirely at other locations, preventing costly downtime.

Copilot for Sales

Implementing Copilot for Sales was another easy decision and productivity significantly improved as a result. Copilot for Sales summarizes customer emails, helping employees quickly grasp important information. It also saves them time when they’re ready to reply to a customer inquiry, by drafting an appropriate response that the employee can edit—also with Copilot’s help, if they like—or send as-is. Andrew Koehler, Commercial Systems and Operations Manager, says that Intralox salespeople like the flexibility of being able to get help with writing emails, adding, “Copilot [for Sales] enhances customer relationships and increases customer value by streamlining communication and making interactions more intuitive and meaningful.”

Many of Intralox’s account managers are multilingual and find Copilot for Sales helpful in bridging language gaps. They enjoy knowing that Copilot for Sales can draft emails that are clear and grammatically correct, allowing them to focus on their customers’ needs, not the readability of their emails. And Copilot email summaries in their native language save them time reviewing and translating long email threads.

If all Copilot for Sales did was draft and summarize emails, it would still boost sales teams’ productivity. The real game-changer is that it embeds access to Dynamics 365 Customer Service and Field Service in Outlook. Intralox employees can seamlessly add, view, share, and even update customer contact and other data in an email or calendar invite, without leaving Outlook. Concise summaries of cases, work orders, and opportunities are easily accessible, ready for employees to enrich their emails and meeting invitations with relevant information as they’re drafting them.

Copilot for Sales has been a big win for Intralox sales teams. “Copilot for Sales has made our team much more productive,” says Fernando Silva, Global Account Team Leader at Intralox. “For us, the number one asset is information, and Copilot for Sales supercharges our ability to access, analyze, and act on it.”

Looking ahead

While the company is enjoying its increase in productivity and finding new meaningful ways of connecting with its customers, Intralox is expert at keeping things moving, and isn’t about to stop its digital transformation now. The company remains focused on innovating its customer service and technical support processes even further. One look inside Intralox reveals a company that keeps new ideas moving down the belt.

The implementation of these solutions improved access to information, reduced inefficiencies, and saved time for both Intralox and its customers, leading to enhanced overall customer satisfaction.

Eye care and eyeglass provider Now Optics transformed its business operations with a unified enterprise resource planning (ERP) solution that is driving operational efficiency across its distribution center and more than 300 stores. Now Optics needed a scalable IT infrastructure to power its rapid business growth. The company turned to Microsoft partner Avantiico for a multiphase project that would ultimately incorporate Now Optics’s finance, inventory, and warehouse operations. The unified ERP solution is fueling productivity and helping the company offer a more personalized customer experience.

Expanding access to modern eye care with technological innovation

Now Optics, an eye care and eyeglasses retail operation, believes in modernizing the eye care experience and is a leader in telehealth eye exams that complement its over 300 corporate and franchise store locations. In 2024, Now Optics opened more than 30 new stores and expects to open at least 40 more in 2025.

This rapid business expansion strained the company’s existing IT infrastructure, which had been built piece by piece over the company’s history. Now Optics decided to transform and unify its point-of-sale, inventory, and finance systems. “We were running various systems, including a custom point-of-sale system and a financial system, and we didn’t have specific supply chain tracking for inventories and warehousing,” says Lakshmi Balusu, Chief Information Officer at Now Optics. “From an IT point of view, we wanted a platform that would help the company grow and not look backward. We don’t want the IT infrastructure to be a hindrance for company growth.”

With the company’s reputation as a leader in hybrid eye exams and eye care e-commerce, the company’s technology teams wanted to develop an omnichannel ERP system that would complement its online presence. Now Optics had already migrated some business operations to Microsoft Azure, and the company determined that Microsoft technology was a natural fit for additional modernization. “We analyzed how much Microsoft is investing in its cloud and technologies and decided it was the best option,” says Balusu.

Driving change across business operations in 18 months

Initially, Now Optics was focused on moving its finance operations to Microsoft Dynamics 365, which features AI-driven customer relationship management and ERP business applications. It turned to Microsoft partner Avantiico, which has extensive experience with Dynamics 365 and large-scale, complex projects involving finance and accounting systems. “We bring deep knowledge on the technical side of Dynamics 365,” says Dan McAllister, Solution Architect at Avantiico. “Complex, multinational, and multicurrency projects are in our wheelhouse with the use of our Advance Multi-Company Solution.”

While Now Optics worked with Avantiico, the eye care company decided that it wanted to go beyond modernizing its finance operations and make Dynamics 365 its supply chain and warehouse management system. To bring together data from multiple systems, Now Optics used data platform Microsoft Fabric. Avantiico collaborated with teams across multiple time zones to gain a deep understanding of Now Optics’s business needs. “Avantiico truly felt like a team member, not just a partner,” says Nicole Lord, Vice President of Merchandising at Now Optics.

Upgrading the company’s finance operations took only six months using Avantiico’s Advance Multi-Company Solution, which accelerated data migration and incorporated Now Optics’s payroll and expense management solutions. Now Optics adopted Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management, which helps companies streamline supply chain operations, and Microsoft Power BI to help the company uncover and visualize strategic business insights. The company was ready to pilot its unified ERP system 12 months later, a fairly quick turnaround for an international, multiphase project.

For one pilot, a small group from the senior leadership team, including the chief executive officer, went to a store location and personally tested the new solution over four days. “We wanted to make sure that the new system was developed with no training requirements,” says Balusu. “We wanted to see how the executives used the system with no training. We then took what we learned from that experience to improve the solution.”

Enhancing operational efficiency across more than 300 locations

As Now Optics refined its ERP system, it continued rolling out the solution to individual stores, then ramped up to four stores at a time. The ERP system is now fully operational at over 300 locations and the company distribution center. This solution is empowering individual franchises to enhance operational efficiency and provide customers with a more personalized experience.

The modernized infrastructure is also improving employee satisfaction, retention, and recruitment at Now Optics. The system is easier for developers to maintain, and they no longer spend time managing multiple programs. Employees benefit from single sign-on and do not have to track multiple logins to accomplish tasks, and automation is fueling productivity. “Employees can upload their invoices and automatically code the invoices to the vendor,” says Balusu. “The process to upload the invoice, code the invoice, send it for approval, and get it back for a payment is fully automated.”

With a unified data estate, Now Optics is positioned to gather strategic business insights with tools such as AI and machine learning. “We’re going to be able to remove ourselves from the day-to-day insight building and focus on using that information to develop strategy,” says Lord. “We will be able to focus on strategic planning and long-term growth opportunities.”

Transforming eye care for the era of AI

As Now Optics employees become more confident in the new ERP solution, the company is already looking for new ways to innovate and continue expanding access to eye healthcare. The company is eager to experiment with Microsoft 365 Copilot to streamline business operations. “We think with Copilot, we can automate our redundant processes and do more advanced data analysis,” says Balusu.

Now Optics’s close collaboration with Avantiico and the software vendor’s expertise with Microsoft technology fueled a complete digital transformation within the eye care company. “Understanding our business, as well as Avantiico really being in the trenches with us, challenged us to make the best decisions for our company,” says Lord.

Fulton County Schools (FCS) is the fourth largest school system in Georgia with more than 10,900 employees, serving nearly 87,000 students  across 104 schools.

FCS is known for its commitment to student achievement and continuous improvement, earning state and national recognition. With this commitment in mind, FCS found that traditional education models struggled to keep pace with rapid advancements in technology, leaving students underprepared for future careers. This gap was particularly evident in fields like computer science, where industry standards evolve faster than curricula can adapt.

But for FCS, AI isn’t just about keeping students competitive—it’s about challenging them to do more and empowering them to turn their ideas into reality. Students aren’t just learning how to use AI; they’re leveraging it to push past limitations, break down complex challenges, and bring ambitious projects to life.

"If you take traditional computer science, we were years behind the industry,” says Dr. Joe Phillips, Chief Information Officer with Fulton County Schools. “Now add AI, which is exploding into everything, and we knew we had to get in front of it. We want AI to be as familiar as a textbook or a laptop—an everyday tool that enhances teaching and learning. Students have to be skilled in how to use technology properly before they ever get to college."

To help students stay competitive in college and beyond, FCS realized that both students and staff needed proficiency and support in AI. Their goal: create more personalized, engaging learning experiences while reducing administrative workloads. The district also prioritized a structured and protective environment to ensure data security and trust in AI adoption.

FCS formed an AI task force to evaluate over 200 potential use cases for AI in education. After thorough evaluation, the district decided to join a preview for students 13 and older for Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat due to its security, reliability, and seamless integration within FCS’s existing Microsoft ecosystem.

Implementing a structured approach to AI

When Copilot Chat was introduced, the first step was equipping educators and staff with the knowledge to use it effectively. Training sessions were held to ensure educators felt confident integrating AI into their classrooms, not just as a tool, but as a thought partner for students.

“I always want to grow as an educator, and give my students more nuggets of knowledge,” says Dr . Steve Sweigart, Engineering Instructor at Fulton County Schools. “And Copilot Chat has allowed me to do that, securely and safely in the classroom. And it's making it a lot of fun in the process!”

With a solid foundation in place, the next challenge was weaving Copilot Chat into the curriculum. Educators aligned AI capabilities with learning objectives to tackle complex subjects, enhance problem-solving, and support personalized learning.

Throughout the process, data privacy and security remained a top priority. Safeguards were put in place to protect student information, ensuring that Copilot Chat could be used in a measured and responsible way.  

"Copilot Chat allowed us to explore AI within a safe environment,” explains Dr. Phillips. “We're able to make sure we have the guardrails in place for our students, our educators, and our staff. It’s not about automation; it’s about equity—giving every student the opportunity to learn in a way that works best for them.”

Bridging the gap between ideas and execution

FCS’ Johns Creek High School has a diverse student body of approximately 1,800. The school’s career tech department provides students with training they’ll need to thrive in the modern workplace.

“When the school rolled out Copilot Chat as our official AI tool for students, I thought it was really forward thinking,” says Jayson  Gonzalez, senior at Johns Creek High School. “Before, I had to limit my ideas to whatever I was sure I could do. Now I can push past those limitations, break down complex challenges step-by-step, and apply new concepts in a way that makes sense. It helps me bridge the gap between ideas and execution. It’s not just about helping me build something—it’s about expanding what I believe is possible.”

Gonzalez used Copilot Chat to design a smart mobility cane with IoT capabilities, explore new coding languages, troubleshoot design constraints, and even consider where to go for college.  

“Copilot Chat isn’t just about finding answers; it challenges me to think critically, explore multiple solutions to a problem, ask better questions, and refine my thought process. It’s helping me to be the best version of myself, both in my schoolwork and in my personal life,” says Gonzalez.

Empowering students to tackle complex challenges with confidence

Using AI responsibly is essential in education, ensuring students develop critical thinking and digital literacy while maintaining data security and fairness. FCS’s integration of Copilot Chat demonstrates this approach by providing students with a disciplined environment to explore AI while learning about responsible usage. By prioritizing thoughtful implementation, FCS fosters inclusivity and prepares students for an AI-driven future.  

“AI is evolving rapidly, and learning how to use it responsibly now will give me a huge advantage,” says Pragya Modgil, a junior at Johns Creek High School. “Our school’s approach is helping us build a strong foundation in ethical AI use, giving me a leg up in college and in how to use AI responsibly in my future career."

FCS students are using Copilot Chat to conduct research, create multimedia projects, such as podcasts on historical events, help with coding challenges, 3D modeling, design ideation, time management, academic planning, and accessible technology.

“We use Copilot Chat as a brainstorming partner to ideate, but not to actually do our work for us,” explains Modgil. “It helps us collaborate and expand our creativity to think of more ambitious ideas.”

Modgil used Copilot Chat in her computer science class to help build a system that connects a running accelerometer to a front-end user interface. “Copilot Chat allows me to integrate my passions into my classroom work,” Modgil says. “I run for my high school's cross country and track team. I thought it would be cool to bring this passion into my computer science class. And Copilot Chat helps me do just that!”

Johns Creek High School AP Computer Science teacher Dr. Raymond Schenk sees Copilot Chat as levelling the playing field in his classes, helping students new to coding feel more confident in their capabilities. “There can be some apprehension with coding until students realize that, yes, they really can do this!” says Schenk. “Then, all of a sudden, they light up! I have seen this happen again and again with Copilot Chat."

Modgil agrees. “When I first started coding, I felt intimidated, especially as one of the few girls in my class. I was sometimes nervous to ask for help, but now—with Copilot Chat—I really see potential for it to level the playing field in computer science—and in all subjects—providing another way for students to get help and feel empowered without worrying if they're being judged. Now, instead of waiting for help, I can troubleshoot on my own, which has made me more independent in my learning.”

Reducing workload, boosting learning, and empowering future leaders

Educators and administrators at FCS are also utilizing Copilot Chat for lesson planning, student reports, and action plans, as well as streamlining facility maintenance and capital planning. For example, FCS fed facility condition assessments for all of its buildings into Copilot Chat, with the tool helping staff to create a prioritization list for the district's long-term capital plan. Copilot Chat condensed a process that typically takes nine to 11 months into something taking only two or three days.  

“It is absolutely making my job easier,” says Dr. Schenk. “If a student doesn’t fully understand something, they can spend five minutes with Copilot Chat and have it explained to them. This allows me to spend my time teaching the bigger concepts, in a shorter amount of time. My students are accelerating their learning. They are gaining confidence. Copilot Chat is a force multiplier. And it meets every student exactly where they are.”

Dr. Sweigart also finds it easier to accomplish greater things in the classroom. “I challenge my students more now than ever because of Copilot Chat in the classroom,” he says. “They're able to come up with multiple solutions to problems and solve those problems faster, creating better projects in the same amount of time."

Leveraging AI to create inclusive, future-ready classrooms

FCS’ pilot of Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat has empowered educators by reducing administrative burdens so they can focus on what truly matters: engaging and inspiring students. For students, it acts as a thought partner, helping them tackle complex problems, explore new ideas, and turn ambitious projects into reality. Beyond just saving time, Copilot Chat helps students engage more deeply and maximize their potential, providing educators with renewed excitement. The result is a learning environment where curiosity thrives, creativity flourishes, and AI enhances, rather than replaces, human potential.

“I'm always trying to figure out what that future might look like,” says Dr. Schenk. “I want my students to harness the power of Copilot Chat to explore and become inventive programmers, so that—one day—they can own their own companies. How? Because they had the vision to apply computer science to a world that desperately needs it.”

In the fast-evolving world of artificial intelligence, enterprises need efficient ways to build and deploy agentic AI applications and AI models. Weights & Biases is on the front line of this challenge, providing an AI developer platform. With AI’s expanding role in industries like healthcare and autonomous driving, Weights & Biases customer requirements are many including the need to run AI workloads on Microsoft Azure. As a leader within the cloud space, Microsoft Azure has the infrastructure and services to supercharge AI development.

As the go-to platform for AI teams worldwide, many industries and enterprises look to Weights & Biases to accelerate agentic AI applications as well as deep learning use cases such as drug discovery and computer vision. 

According to Sasha Manuilova, Director of Partnerships at Weights & Biases, the company’s mission is to build the best tools for AI developers. Weights & Biases partnered with Microsoft Azure to seamlessly integrate into the AI development workflow and provide the computational power required for AI experimentation.

Their collaboration has led to exciting new developments, including:

Developers can automatically track fine-tuning jobs, as well as compare model versions and evaluate and trace large language model-powered applications.

Azure Marketplace Availability: The Weights & Biases platform is available for seamless procurement via Microsoft Commercial Marketplace, allowing enterprise teams to seamlessly adopt the platform while leveraging existing cloud budgets.

Weights & Biases’ seamless integration into the Azure ecosystem ensures that AI teams can connect their workflows to data sources, compute environments, and AI applications and models within Microsoft’s cloud infrastructure.

Innovation that powers solutions

Azure’s comprehensive cloud services provide developers with cutting-edge AI capabilities:

Scalability & Compute Power: Azure’s powerful GPU and CPU offerings support complex AI training workloads, ensuring that developers can experiment at scale.

Enterprise-Ready AI: Azure OpenAI’s balance of out-of-the-box defaults and customizable controls with access to Weights & Biases allows teams of all skill levels to optimize their AI models effectively.

Seamless Integration: By embedding Weights & Biases’ platform within Azure services, developers gain a frictionless experience, whether fine-tuning OpenAI models or deploying AI applications.

According to Sasha Manuilova, “We are integrated with Azure on every layer of the stack, ensuring that AI teams can build and scale AI projects with minimal friction.”

Advancing multiple industries with AI innovation

The collaboration between Weights & Biases and Microsoft Azure is already making a tangible impact across multiple industries:

Healthcare: Weights & Biases partnered with a large hospital system to build a natural language processing (NLP) model that scans doctors’ notes for missed follow-ups, ensuring patients receive timely care.

Autonomous Driving: Wayve, an AI-driven autonomous vehicle company, leverages Weights & Biases and Azure ML to train its computer vision systems—powering self-driving cars.

Consumer Packaged Goods: Weights & Biases partnered with a large CPG company to help build and monitor performance of their chatbots to ensure they follow the brand guidelines. 

Accelerated AI Development: Customers report that Weights & Biases significantly reduces the time from idea to production allowing for faster innovation cycles.

A future powered by AI and cloud innovation

As AI continues to transform industries, the partnership between Weights & Biases and Microsoft Azure is poised for further breakthroughs. With the introduction of Azure AI Foundry, Weights & Biases anticipates even smoother AI development experiences, helping enterprises push the boundaries of what’s possible with machine learning.

Looking ahead, Weights & Biases aims to expand its integrations within the Azure ecosystem, unlocking new capabilities for AI developers and ensuring that enterprises can build, train, and deploy AI models faster than ever before. “We are very excited about the joint announcements we’ve made this week at Microsoft Ignite,” says Manuilova. “The support from Microsoft—on the marketing, go-to-market, and product sides—has been phenomenal, and we look forward to deepening our partnership.”

Centro de la Familia de Utah is a nonprofit organization with a mission to promote lifelong educational success for children in underserved communities.

In 1991, the federal government selected Centro to implement the Head Start Program for Utah. Head Start provides comprehensive services to low-income children and families. Centro is one of approximately 1,600 Head Start grantees serving 800,000 children across the United States and its territories. Today, Centro operates 27 Head Start centers in Utah, Colorado, Nevada, and Montana.

Head Start actively encourages programs such as Centro’s to use data for continuous improvement, yet many Head Start grantees struggle with time-consuming reporting systems that limit their ability to make timely, data-informed decisions. What’s more, Centro was working with an external legacy system that limited access and control of their data.

A better system, for dramatically better results

To address the challenges of their legacy systems, Centro worked with its technology partner, JourneyTeam, to develop C-FIT—a Power Platform solution that integrates customizable reports and analytics. Built using Power BI and Power Apps, the solution represents a major upgrade and is making data analysis more accessible and actionable for Centro’s Head Start centers. 

With C-FIT’s user-friendly reporting tools, centers can:

Identify trends in child outcomes and make targeted interventions  

Streamline compliance and reporting to federal and state agencies  

Make real-time, data-driven decisions to enhance service quality  

Dataverse provides each Centro center with secure, role-based access and control of their own data, eliminating separate data access requests and exports that were required with the previous system. Power Platform also enabled Centro to customize the system, including new performance indicators. “With Power Platform, we were able to get the exact functionality we needed quickly and cost efficiently,” says Gonzalo Palza, CEO & Head Start Director at Centro.

The impact of the solution has been substantial. Notably, Centro has achieved a 5x reduction in time spent on administrative processes daily and a 54% reduction in costs compared to the previous solution. This transformation allows Centro de la Familia to shift their focus from paperwork to improving child and family outcomes, reinforcing their mission of promoting lifelong educational success for children in underserved communities.

The system drove another key benefit for Centro’s employees – recognition by their peers. With the new performance indicators in C-FIT, Centro was better able to demonstrate key progress metrics to the National Head Start Association. This led to Centro being certified as a program of excellence – just one of 4 programs across the country that earned the distinction last year.

Streamlining report generation with Copilot Studio 

Building on the success of C-FIT, Centro and JourneyTeam took the solution one step further – with an AI-powered agent built using Microsoft Copilot Studio. 

Currently, Family Service Specialists spend significant time summarizing and reviewing case notes to create applications for families in need of Head Start support. These reports would often go back and forth between the specialists and approval managers. 

To streamline the process, the new agent automates note summarization and data entry, dramatically reducing administrative burden. The agent is embedded in C-FIT using an iframe. When employees meet with families, the new agent prompts employees with questions and automatically creates a report or ‘narrative’ for submission. “Our agent in Copilot Studio has reduced the time to compile reports from hours to minutes – and that’s allowing us to spend more time engaging directly with families who need our help,” says Lorena Cervantes, Family Partnerships Specialist at Centro. 

Easy integration with the existing C-FIT system and data helped accelerate development. Additionally, all security features needed for the agent were already in place. “When developing on Power Platform, we have the peace of mind knowing that it's integrated with Microsoft security infrastructure. That’s a benefit that other AI development platforms simply can’t offer,” says Eric Beins, Chief Technology Officer at JourneyTeam.

As with the original C-FIT system, Power Platform has also made it easier to implement quick changes to the agent and drive a collaborative development process. “We knew that AI could help improve processes but, with Microsoft Copilot Studio, our developers built a truly customized AI tool that meets our specific needs,” says Euleta Christiansen, Senior Program & Behavior Specialist, Centro Headquarters. 

A platform built for the future

Looking ahead, Centro and JourneyTeam are excited to share their C-FIT solution with other Head Start programs across the country, empowering more organizations to enhance their efficiency and focus on their core missions.

In the meantime, JourneyTeam is working on a Copilot Studio training program and workshop that will help Centro employees develop, manage and deploy agents on their own. “Power Platform enabled us to develop a solution that Centro can build on quickly and cost effectively for the next 5-10 years,” says Beins. 

That kind of forward thinking excites employees at Centro. “I’m not a developer – but I can clearly see how Power Platform can empower our employees to be even more analytical and productive,” says Palza. “Tools like our agent in Copilot Studio are literally transforming the way we work and giving us more time to focus on serving our communities.”
