In today’s AI-driven world, businesses generate an unprecedented amount of data—often unstructured, complex, and difficult to manage. LlamaIndex has emerged as a game-changer, enabling enterprises to connect their data seamlessly with large language models (LLMs). By bridging the gap between raw data and AI-powered applications, LlamaIndex is revolutionizing industries like healthcare, insurance, and legal services. But as AI adoption grows, so do concerns about security, scalability, and efficiency.

To tackle these challenges, LlamaIndex partnered with Microsoft Azure to enhance data security, accelerate AI development, and unlock new capabilities. Their mission is to make AI more accessible by providing a framework connecting proprietary data with LLMs. However, there are customers in regulated industries that face significant challenges.

Many companies face data privacy and security challenges as they want to leverage AI but are hesitant to expose sensitive data to third-party cloud services. They need an AI solution that ensures data remains within their control. There are scalability challenges as small-scale AI applications are easy to build but managing millions of documents while maintaining accuracy is a significant hurdle. Lastly, AI accuracy and reliability challenges are significant as LLMs sometimes "hallucinate," generating inaccurate or irrelevant responses. LlamaIndex needed a way to enhance AI precision.

LlamaIndex’s search for a partner that could provide enterprise-grade security, seamless AI integration, and scalability led them to Microsoft Azure.

Partnering to power the future of AI

Microsoft Azure stood out as the ideal partner for LlamaIndex due to its robust AI infrastructure and commitment to security. Laurie Voss, VP of Developer Relations at LlamaIndex, highlighted Azure OpenAI Service as a key differentiator. Unlike other cloud-based AI solutions, Azure OpenAI allows enterprises to keep their data private, ensuring that sensitive information never leaves their network.

Additionally, Azure AI Search provided a critical solution for storing and retrieving vast amounts of unstructured data, enhancing LlamaIndex’s ability to deliver precise and relevant results.

"Our customers make a lot of use of Azure OpenAI. That’s the foundation of everything they do. And we're also increasingly using Azure AI Search as the vector store to store the data once it has been prepared for use by LLMs," stated Laurie Voss.

With Azure’s support, LlamaIndex implemented a cutting-edge AI solution to meet enterprise demands. Azure OpenAI Service ensures data privacy, allowing businesses to use powerful AI models without exposing sensitive data to third-party services. This is particularly crucial for industries handling confidential information. Azure AI Search provides a hybrid search solution, combining traditional keyword-based search with vector-based semantic search. This improves the accuracy of LlamaIndex’s AI-powered applications. Azure Managed Identity Services offers advanced security and identity management, reassuring enterprises that their data is being handled with the highest security standards.

Measuring the impact

LlamaIndex’s partnership with Microsoft Azure has resulted in substantial benefits for their customers. By leveraging AI-powered automation, enterprises can enhance efficiency using LlamaIndex save 10-20 hours per report, reducing a 40-hour manual task by nearly 50%. By minimizing hallucinations, Azure-powered AI applications improve AI accuracy by providing more relevant and precise answers, ensuring high-quality business insights. Lastly, enterprises have stronger data security and can now process AI queries within their network, eliminating risks associated with third-party data exposure.

What does the future hold?

LlamaIndex and Microsoft Azure are just getting started. Looking ahead, Azure AI Search will play an important role in LlamaIndex’s evolution. New hybrid search capabilities will further enhance their ability to connect businesses with their data more intelligently.

“We’re really excited about Azure AI Search. The additions that are coming, like hybrid search, are going to accelerate what we can do for our customers,” stated Laurie Voss.

With a deepening partnership and ongoing AI advancements, LlamaIndex and Microsoft Azure are set to redefine how enterprises harness AI for data-driven decision-making.

Enterprises struggle to rapidly access and interpret complex data, leading to delayed decisions and lost opportunities. Skilled users face steep learning curves, while less-technical users are often excluded entirely. Without the ability to quickly retrieve and analyze data to chart a strategic course, organizations risk falling behind the competition.

Spotfire has long been a name synonymous with innovation in visual data science. Combining visualizations and advanced analytics, Spotfire consistently pushes the boundaries of what‘s possible, helping organizations make sense of their data and gain actionable insights. To empower its users to stay agile and make better decisions faster, Spotfire has added layers of natural language capabilities to the rich features of its core platform. The combination enables Spotfire users, both novice and seasoned, to access advanced visual data science features through natural language prompts.

“Our customers are solving some incredible problems,” says Michael O’Connell, Chief Analytics Officer at Spotfire. “These large enterprises are inventing new therapeutics that save lives, manufacturing chips with resolution more than 30,000 times smaller than a human hair, and supplying energy to the world. At Spotfire, we are driven to help our customers rapidly identify insights in their data and take actions that generate extreme value for their business.”

Empowering rapid insights with Azure

Spotfire’s search for the right technology led to Microsoft Azure AI Foundry. The company selected Azure OpenAI Service within Azure AI Foundry to quickly implement an intuitive, conversational analytics platform extension. Employing the multimodal capabilities in Azure OpenAI Service, the Spotfire Copilot™ assistant helps users interact with data using natural language inside the Spotfire user experience, which drastically simplifies complex analytics tasks. Within days of close collaboration with Microsoft AI experts, Spotfire built a functional retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) prototype, transforming theoretical ideas into tangible innovation.

Making it faster and easier to analyze data through interactive AI, Spotfire Copilot was designed to help users quickly navigate the complexities of data analytics. Using Azure OpenAI Service, Spotfire Copilot provides fast insights, automates routine tasks, and enhances the overall user experience.

“Our goal has always been to empower our users with everything they need to make data-informed decisions, making our data visualization solution even easier to work with,” says Ahmad Fattahi, Senior Director of Data Science at Spotfire. “We want our product to be so intuitive that regardless of skill level, users can engage with Spotfire Copilot using natural language and focus on achieving their goals.”

With Spotfire Copilot, tasks previously taking days or weeks can now be completed within minutes. By automating routine data analysis tasks, users spend more time interpreting insights and driving strategic decisions, significantly increasing productivity and innovation across industries.

The following diagram shows the architecture of Spotfire Copilot, illustrating the products and solutions involved in creating the workflow for the new solution. These include content indexers, such as Azure AI Search, and language models, where Azure OpenAI Service plays a critical role.

Simplifying complex analytics across industries

Azure AI Foundry provides a centralized platform for managing AI resources. In implementing Azure OpenAI Service, Spotfire now offers its visual data science workflow capabilities via a convenient chat interface. This enables AI-assisted interactive visualizations, data science functions, data insights, explanations, and user assistance that use the rich set of Spotfire functionalities. The company can now better help customers discover meaningful connections between variables, surfacing visual insights from data and suggesting high-value business actions.

In addition, Azure AI Search was crucial for RAG use cases. It provides robust repositories and data services, so the AI model can access and retrieve specific information from large datasets.

Real-time analytics deliver immediate business impact

“With Azure OpenAI Service, we’re seeing a significant reduction in the time it takes to analyze data,” says Vaibhav Gedigeri, Lead Data Scientist at Spotfire. “Our users can now spend more time interpreting the results and less time looking for and working with the numbers.”

Key solution benefits include the following.

Instant data exploration and visualizations with AI: Azure OpenAI Service gives Spotfire Copilot users the ability to instantly query complex datasets using natural language, making data retrieval intuitive for all users. As a result, the learning curve for new users is reduced and existing user personas are more efficient, reducing analysis time from days to minutes and enabling the creation of visualizations with the click of a button.

Enterprise-ready AI at scale: With Azure AI Foundry and AI Search, ​​Spotfire Copilot can support thousands of users across global enterprises, ensuring seamless scaling while maintaining compliance with strict industry security standards.

Faster, smarter data discovery: Spotfire Copilot uses AI Search to surface the most relevant insights from vast datasets, helping users quickly identify trends and patterns without manual searching.

The following screenshot shows Spotfire Copilot in action, illustrating clear visual insights and natural language summaries. A chat panel on the right shows a prompt: Create a stacked bar chart of losses due to various factors over time. Graphs to the left show the outcome.

Yet another benefit from Azure OpenAI Service is its more secure and private data handling capabilities. Using the enterprise-grade security features in Azure, Spotfire can confidently address stringent regulatory demands from highly regulated sectors such as pharmaceuticals, manufacturing, finance, and insurance. Customers can manage their own Azure-protected environments, benefiting from Azure data privacy and protection capabilities without compromising on analytical capabilities.

“Security is paramount for our large enterprise customers, and our collaboration with Microsoft allays any concerns,” says Fattahi. “With Azure AI Foundry, we have the desired observability and control over our infrastructure and can deliver a highly secure environment to our customers.”

The company’s ability to make Spotfire Copilot available to its global user base in just a few months speaks to the platform’s scalability, ensuring that the Spotfire platform can expand as needed.

“Once the proof of concept using Azure was done, we went from a small pilot to a full-scale rollout in a matter of months,” says O’Connell. “The speed of deployment was incredible.”

Spotfire’s AI-driven success continues

“The architecture we developed working with Microsoft makes for easy application of new technologies as those emerge, including AI agents. This flexibility is crucial for staying ahead in the industry,” says Marcelo Gallardo, Principal Solutions Architect at Spotfire.

Spotfire Copilot is already delivering results, not just in operational efficiency but also in customer satisfaction and retention, including:
 

Improved user efficiency and job satisfaction: Instead of having to sit in days or weeks of training before using the tool and generating the first bit of value, customers can effectively navigate data in minutes.

Increased ability to innovate: Since users can automate many tasks and secure data insights more quickly, they can focus on the truly innovative part of their job, driving results for their organization.

Cost efficiency and operational gains: Spotfire has seen measurable cost savings in operational expenses due to reduced analysis times and the need for fewer support resources. A new user can generate value with data 90% faster, while an expert user can generate 50% more value. The scalability of Spotfire’s Microsoft-powered solution also means it can quickly adapt to growing demand without significant additional costs.

By developing, deploying, and managing Spotfire Copilot with Azure, Spotfire is well positioned to continue growing and improving user satisfaction, helping further transform data analytics.

“Our experience with Microsoft has been a true collaboration. The team is always looking to the future and working to anticipate what might be helpful to us,” says O’Connell. “It’s an important relationship that’s keeping Spotfire ahead of the competition and setting a new standard for our industry.”

Ramp is one of the fastest-growing startups in the U.S., landing consistently on top innovation lists for redefining how businesses manage spend. With a mission to help customers save their two most valuable resources–time and money–Ramp offers a modern suite of corporate cards, expense management and bill-pay solutions built for speed and simplicity. To fuel its rapid growth, deliver even better customer experiences and empower its workforce at scale, Ramp focused on time-consuming manual tasks that can quietly drain hours of the day, like tracking receipts or paying multi-line invoices.

“Nobody likes filing expense reports,” says Rahul Sengottuvelu, Head of Applied AI at Ramp. “And when you're paying lots of bills, especially long ones with dozens of line items, it can take up a lot of your time.”

Ramp set out to eliminate as much friction as possible.

Rahul adds: “We wanted it to be as simple as swiping a card and texting the receipt, with Ramp handling the rest.”

That forward-thinking vision called for a modern solution: one that could scale with Ramp’s ambitions and meet the expectations of enterprise-grade customers. Powered by Microsoft Azure AI services and Microsoft Azure AI Document Intelligence, Ramp built a custom OCR tool that lets users simply text or upload a receipt.

Behind the scenes, Azure’s AI services automatically extract, categorize and enrich the data, turning raw documents into structured, usable insights in seconds. This seamless automation empowers Ramp to deliver fast, accurate and secure finance workflows at scale.

Less manual, more automation

Ramp’s goal of a seamless experience became a reality at scale. With its custom-built OCR technology, Ramp now automates what used to be hours of repetitive admin work.

30,000 hours of manual work saved per month

400,000 invoices and 5 million receipts processed monthly

90%+ accuracy on OCR fields

“Time savings is the biggest feedback we get. Customers can finally focus on what matters, growing their business instead of chasing receipts,” says Colin Kennedy, Chief Business Officer at Ramp.

Each automated receipt saves up to a minute. Multiply that by millions, and it’s not just time–it’s momentum gained.

 "We run about 5 million reimbursements and receipts monthly. If each one saves even 15 seconds, that adds up fast,” explains Andrew Gu, Senior Software Engineer at Ramp.

Small team, right partner, big results

Ramp’s lean but highly skilled team built and deployed its custom OCR solution in under a week. Leveraging the power of Azure Document Intelligence, Azure AI services as the foundation, and using tools like Microsoft Visual Studio to accelerate development and deepen visibility into what’s happening under the hood.

Colin Kennedy shares the reason behind choosing Microsoft solutions. “We picked Azure because it’s best-in-class for AI-powered solutions. The reliability, low latency and cost benefits are unmatched.” 

Scalability and the responsiveness of the Microsoft team, who provided fast, informed support at every stage, were also key factors.

“Whenever we have questions, the Microsoft Unified team answers quickly and clearly, which makes it easier to keep growing fast,” continues Colin Kennedy.

“We love being able to move fast. With prebuilt Azure models in Document Intelligence, our teams stay unblocked and keep building,” adds Rahul Sengottuvelu.

Built for builders: empowering developers

Ramp’s culture is built on supporting both customers and employees–and that means giving internal teams the same seamless, high-performance tools they offer to their users.

Colin Kennedy explains: “Our job is to delight employees the same way we delight customers. That includes helping our finance teams close books faster and giving developers what they need to build faster.”      

Encouraged by the success of OCR, Ramp decided to expand its use of Azure, migrating DevOps processes to the platform to unlock greater speed and efficiency for its developers. With Azure as the foundation for DevOps and GitHub Copilot embedded in daily workflows, Ramp’s engineers are shipping code faster, with fewer blockers and more visibility.

The team also benefits from GitHub's hosted runners, which are flexible and scalable enough to reduce the need for managing internal CI infrastructure, saving valuable engineering resources. GitHub Actions allows Ramp to run continuous integration pipelines in parallel, speeding up testing and unblocking engineers. Logs and outputs are now centralized within GitHub’s interface, giving teams a complete view in one place and accelerating iteration cycles.

In just one month, Ramp developers logged:

2.7 million GitHub Actions minutes

965,000 GitHub Actions runs

“Almost every engineer uses GitHub Copilot, it’s part of how we build. You notice when it’s not there,” enthuses Rahul Sengottuvelu.

Expanding impact, sharing success

With the Microsoft foundation in place, the team is scaling even faster than before, serving new markets and launching more integrations.

“We’re not just a fast-growing startup–we’re also earning the trust of large enterprise customers. Microsoft has been a key partner in that journey,” Amanda Carroccio, Product Partnerships, AI and Strategic Tech at Ramp.

From Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations to Microsoft Entra, Ramp continues to expand its product integrations–powered by Azure and backed by Microsoft’s enterprise-grade security, performance and reliability.

Ramp is also committed to paying that success forward by sharing what they’ve learned. 

Colin Kennedy advises for other fast-scaling companies: “It is important to make sure your partner truly understands your space and the challenges companies like yours face”. 

He continues: “The quality of the people you work with makes all the difference. For Ramp, that’s definitely been the Microsoft team.”

Always-on ambition, always for the customer     

Ramp is growing fast, but it’s doing so with purpose. One thing drives every decision: customer experience. That commitment shows in Ramp’s top-tier Net Promoter Score (NPS), and it’s shaping where the organization goes next.

“The NPS of both the end user and the finance leader matters deeply to us,” confirms Colin Kennedy. “We want every part of the experience to be exceptional.”

Customer needs are guiding Ramp’s next moves: expanding into procurement, serving larger enterprises and continuing to support a growing community of finance professionals who want smarter, faster, more unified tools.

“We’re excited by what excites our customers. That means going broader, building a platform that solves everything connected to expense, travel and procurement,” he adds.     

Ramp also plans to explore more use cases with Azure, especially around specialized AI models and agents–with an eye on scale and impact.

“We pride ourselves on being the most reliable solution a finance team can use. That means partnering with the most dependable platforms–and for us, that certainly includes Microsoft Azure,” concludes Colin Kennedy.

When Industrialized Construction Group (ICG) spun off from a larger engineering firm, it had to quickly find its footing. A startup in the construction industry, ICG needed to establish a revenue stream while ramping up a slate of innovative solutions for clients.

ICG helps construction companies accelerate their transition to faster, safer, more efficient processes. This means moving from a construction mindset to a manufacturing mindset. Currently, most commercial construction happens on site. Trade workers, such as electricians, plumbers, and drywall installers, show up to a site and do their work in isolation. In contrast, ICG consults with companies to build offsite industrialized construction lines. For example, patient bathrooms for a hospital would be built more efficiently and safely offsite with a smaller footprint in a manufacturing facility, then delivered and installed on-site. 

From juggling to streamlining

The ICG team of five found themselves stretched thin, juggling administrative tasks, client engagement, and strategic planning. “Establishing our critical infrastructure, things like templates and proposal writing, and our marketing materials—it had to come from somewhere,” says Nick Masci, Principal and Cofounder of ICG. “We’re lean thinkers and systems thinkers. Our whole mission is to help our customers work more efficiently and with better results,” he continues. “We realized Microsoft 365 Copilot was right there, so we started experimenting.”

The team uses Copilot to supplement functions such as Marketing, Sales, HR and Accounting. “Copilot helped me streamline historical proposals into a new proposal with a template, so we don’t have to rewrite those for every customer,” says Sally Mizell, Principal and Cofounder of ICG. “Using a prebuilt agent in Copilot Studio for new hires, I was able to quickly onboard a new employee with the correct forms and payroll enrollment,” Mizell continues. To get a clear picture of profitability, the team also connected Microsoft 365 Copilot to financial data to produce visualizations. 

“Copilot is streamlining so many processes for us.” Nick agrees, adding “We thought we needed more people. But what we really needed was a smarter way to work."

Articulating a clear vision

“Copilot became a dynamic collaborator. It helped us polish language, define value propositions, and clarify communications,” Masci says. Melissa McEwen, Principal and Cofounder at ICG, notes, “As Copilot has helped us articulate our business value proposition more clearly, we’ve created alignment and clarity across the company. That’s no small thing.” 

Paving the way to profitability

With solid business infrastructure in place, the team turned to Copilot to chart their next steps. “As Microsoft 365 tools and capabilities have evolved, we’ve grown right along with it. Building agents in Copilot Studio will help us expand our offering to customers, which directly contributes to our profitability,” notes Masci. 

ICG conducts an Industrialized Construction Maturity Assessment (ICMA) for customers, which evaluates a company across six disciplines, 70 topics, and five levels of performance. “I’m working with Copilot to analyze correlations between different areas of construction maturity so when we report to our clients, we can show them what levers to pull to impact their business,” says Coleton Callender, Senior Product Manager at ICG. “We’ve never been able to do this before because there’s too much complexity in the assessment. A Copilot agent gives us this new capability.” 

Before ICG realized Copilot could help streamline the ICMA reporting and data gathering, it anticipated needing to hire a programmer to help build a custom solution. “We’ve saved ourselves probably $500,000 in programming services that we don’t need because we can use Copilot instead,” observes Mizell.

Redefining construction

ICG is poised to help redefine the construction industry. By tying predictive analytics into its ICMA tool, it aims to provide clients with actionable insights that drive efficiency, reduce costs, and improve quality. Already, Copilot has helped ICG reduce proposal response time by 80%, so the team can focus on customers instead of paperwork. Copilot has also contributed to a 20% increase in gross margins by helping the team implement value pricing and simplify billing.

As Masci puts it, “Copilot has allowed us to punch above our weight. It’s not just a tool; it’s a partner in our mission to transform construction.” 

Melissa McEwen, Principal and Cofounder at ICG, shares her perspective on transforming from within

I really do love the construction industry. I love the built environment. I'm kind of a geek about buildings and infrastructure and design. What really drives me is the people that build these things for us. They impact our communities. They create the things around us that enable us in life. I'm driven to use my technical skills to help people in construction apply what they know so we can all adapt to this moment.

We’re process thinkers, so we want to find the most efficient, smart way to get our work done. Copilot is an invaluable tool, streamlining processes and enhancing our capabilities in ways we never imagined. It helps us show up consistently across customer touchpoints with templates, and we create proposals in a fraction of the time we used to. Marketing materials, onboarding new employees, and a long list of administrative tasks—all handled by Copilot now. 

It is surprising how Copilot has helped with continued refinement of our vision, strategy, and value proposition. This has helped build a singular clear purpose. People apply this clarity to their work every day with each other and our customers.

I am incredibly proud of our team at ICG. Their dedication, creativity, and willingness to embrace new technologies have been instrumental in our success. These technologies are helping us empower the people in this industry that I love to do their absolute best to build a sustainable, more efficient approach to construction.

OneDigital is a strategic advisory firm that helps businesses and individuals with insurance, financial services, and human resources consulting. Focused on helping clients achieve health, success, and financial security, OneDigital also prioritizes building an internal environment where its talented team can do their best work. With a forward-looking approach to artificial intelligence and automation, OneDigital is enhancing internal workflows, improving productivity, and setting new standards for service delivery through smart technology.

With a bold goal to scale the consulting power of its people, OneDigital set out to transform how its teams prepare for and deliver high-impact client engagements. The vision was clear: empower consultants to spend more time on strategic thinking, human connection, and delivering value—while reducing the time spent on labor-intensive research and manual insight-building.

The challenge: Elevating consultant preparation and client engagement

The OneDigital benefits consulting team regularly faced the challenge of thoroughly preparing for strategic client meetings. Consultants spent hours or days conducting deep research on their clients' industries, benefits strategies, market trends, recent organizational developments, and individual client stakeholders. This manual, time-consuming process limited consultants' ability to consistently deliver tailored and strategic insights across a growing client base.

With an expanding number of engagements, the team needed a smarter way to quickly gather relevant, personalized information. The existing approach risked consultants entering meetings underprepared, with generic information that didn't clearly demonstrate OneDigital’s strategic advantage. To enhance service quality and client satisfaction, consultants required intelligent workflow automation that could rapidly synthesize comprehensive client insights—freeing their time to focus on relationship-building, strategic advisory, and personalized recommendations.

Collaboration and innovation through Microsoft Azure Innovate

OneDigital partnered with Microsoft to create a solution and find the right partner to meet their AI needs. By securing Microsoft funding through Azure Innovate, a Microsoft offer that enables AI-led transformation, OneDigital was able to offset the engagement cost and co-develop a custom large language model (LLM) with Data Science Dojo, an experienced Azure partner with AI expertise, tailored to their goals.

“Our initial connection with OneDigital came through [the account manager] at Microsoft, under the Azure Innovate [offer]. This streamlined approach—from easy nomination and prompt funding—allowed us to efficiently understand OneDigital’s needs and bring AI coworkers into production faster.” Arham Akheel, Senior Solutions Architect at Data Science Dojo, stated. Thanks to years of experience using the Microsoft Azure platform, OneDigital trusted its proven technology. They chose Azure because its generative AI solutions offered advantages. Azure provided a comprehensive suite of AI tools and services, including Azure OpenAI Service, which made AI development accessible with easy-to-use APIs allowing the OneDigital team to integrate advanced AI functionality into their existing environment.

“Through Azure Innovate, we co-developed a custom LLM agent platform with Data Science Dojo, revolutionizing our innovation. Their AI expertise and swift adaptation to our industry have unlocked new business capabilities. We look forward to continuing this partnership," Vinay Gidwaney, Chief Product Officer at OneDigital stated.

OneDigital identified Ejento AI, a no-code AI agent building platform powered by Azure, to build AI agents for knowledge workers. “Ejento AI agents ensure security, privacy, compliance, data governance, guardrails, evaluation and interoperability while drastically improving productivity of knowledge workers.” explained Raja Iqbal, Chief Data Scientist.

“We saw an opportunity to leverage Azure’s ecosystem to build AI agents to support OneDigital for a wide range of use cases like writing proposals, doing market research, responding to RFPs and providing assistance to employees,” Senior Solutions Architect at Data Science Dojo stated.

OneDigital leveraged Azure to deploy the AI agent building platform in their cloud tenant. This platform integrates key Azure services including Azure OpenAI Service, Azure AI Foundry, Azure Document Intelligence, Azure Service Bus, Azure Bot Service, Azure AI Search, App Services, Microsoft Entra, Azure Front Door, Azure Blob Storage, Azure Container Service, Azure Logic Apps, Azure Communication Service, Azure CDN, and Cosmos DB. To ensure security and performance, OneDigital relied on Azure Database for PostgreSQL, which offers built-in security, automated backups, and scalable infrastructure. This setup allowed OneDigital to maintain high availability and protect their cloud and AI investments.

Ejento AI is a licensed solution available on the Azure Marketplace as a SaaS product. With seamless deployment through the Azure Marketplace, users can set it up with a single click. The solution was designed to:

Handle a range of employee queries related to benefits such as health insurance, retirement plans and disability insurance

Consistently provide the most accurate and up-to-date information

Offer multilingual support

Provide simple and clear language, ensuring that all employees can easily access the information they needed regardless of their language or comprehension level

Productivity improvement

OneDigital partnered with Data Science Dojo to develop a team of AI Coworkers, specially trained chatbots equipped with proprietary data and customized instructions tailored to OneDigital and its clients. Among them is Ben, an AI benefits expert designed to support the consulting team. Ben quickly synthesizes extensive industry data, client background details, stakeholder insights, and strategic benefits recommendations.

Since its introduction, Ben has significantly boosted the productivity and effectiveness of OneDigital’s benefits specialists, delivering faster, smarter solutions for clients.

Consultants who previously spent hours or even days manually compiling research now receive comprehensive, personalized engagement briefs in minutes.

Azure’s secure, compliant cloud infrastructure ensures sensitive client information remains confidential, protected, and fully compliant with stringent data privacy regulations. Automated backups, security controls, and scalable cloud computing resources guarantee reliability, security, and continuous availability—especially crucial during peak client engagement periods or multiple simultaneous client meetings.

By automating this intensive research workload, OneDigital consultants reclaimed substantial amounts of valuable time—estimated at hundreds of person-hours per year. This newfound efficiency allowed consultants to focus deeply on client relationships, strategic advisory, and delivering more targeted, meaningful insights. As a result, client engagements became consistently personalized, high-impact, and strategically relevant, directly translating into stronger client satisfaction, improved retention, and enhanced competitive differentiation for OneDigital.

Ultimately, the deployment of Ben streamlined consulting operations, empowered the consulting team to engage strategically rather than tactically, and elevated the overall client experience—turning routine preparation tasks into opportunities for deeper human connection and strategic value.

Evolving relationships

OneDigital will continue to innovate with Microsoft Azure, using the power of AI and Machine Learning to remain at the forefront of improving employee benefits. Moving forward, OneDigital is exploring a Proposal Writer, which generates detailed proposals using past submissions and marketing materials—already a hit with the sales team.

“With so many stateroom options and packages, booking a cruise can be a complicated process, and once you’re booked, it’s not always easy to understand how to prepare for a cruise and add additional services,” says Scot Pettit, Sr. Director, E-commerce at Holland America Line.

To help customers through the process, Holland America Line already has an excellent website with access to live chat and call support. But this recognized leader in the cruise industry wanted to go further for Holland America guests and the valued travel advisors who assist them. Finding ways to simplify this complex customer journey around the globe became a focus for the company. As Pettit says, “We wanted to provide even faster, personalized, and more targeted customer support—without driving up call volumes.”

Adding a chatbot with round-the-clock support seemed to be the next logical step. But Holland America Line was very clear that it didn’t want a traditional chatbot with limited if-then responses. This is what led the company to Microsoft Copilot Studio and the development of a virtual “agent”—an advanced, natural language conversational experience that uses AI to support the guest’s digital journey. This agent acts as a digital concierge called “Anna,” which customers access from the company’s website.

An extensible development platform

The minimal viable product (MVP) operating today was built in just three months. As Pettit explains, “We have worked with a variety of chatbot development tools and processes. We like Microsoft Copilot Studio as it’s proving to be the fastest and easiest way to build complex, AI-driven agents. We also like the single interface, extensible connectors, and tight interoperability with the Power Platform ecosystem.”

In this first MVP release, Holland America Line’s Anna supports new and existing customers, including travel advisors, and was designed to support three core scenarios: booking new cruises, adding products and services to existing bookings, and responding to myriad general questions. “We get an incredibly diverse number of questions—from basic cruise and booking requests to travel documentation needed for specific routes, even what to wear on specific dates and destinations,” says Pettit. “Our goal was to create an agent that could address a wide range of customer questions and requests with natural language—just like a live agent, and with 24/7 availability.”

To inform both generative actions and knowledge, the agent is integrated with several back-end systems, including the company’s CRM system and cruise reservations and booking system. Interoperability with the company’s website content is driven through Bing Search APIs, including Bing Custom Search.

Working closely with Microsoft, Holland America Line pushed the boundaries of generative answers and actions in Copilot Studio and developed several significant custom improvements and enhancements to the agent.

Multi-intent detection: Ability to understand queries such as “Help me find a cruise to Alaska for 6 to 8 days from Seattle.”
Custom entity extraction: Ability to expand on predefined entities such as dates and add custom entities (i.e., “I want to go next summer” will generate a JSON object for the June–August summer season {"departurefromdate": "2025-06-01","departuretodate": "2025-08-01"})
Single-page reasoning: Ability to reason over a particular cruise itinerary page to answer questions like “Which day are we getting to the Bahamas and what are we seeing before that?”

Deep telemetry, strong response rates

To ensure a quality customer experience, the first-generation Anna was refined through a multi-wave, three-month rollout. First, it was made available as a tool for contact center agents to answer customer questions, and then it was tested internally with all employees. From there, it was launched on the external website, starting with making it available to 5% of customers, then 50%, and then 100% of all customers visiting the website. Holland America Line expects to ramp up engagement levels as it continues expanding Anna’s capabilities.

The accuracy and performance of the agent was monitored using multiple tools and data sources. “The built-in analytics tools in Microsoft Copilot Studio and connectivity to other analytics platforms enabled us to set up an effective feedback loop,” says Pettit. Interoperability with Dataverse delivers conversational logs and feedback from customers. Adobe Analytics provides custom business metrics, and Application Insights in Azure Monitor provides near real-time technical monitoring of the platform. 

Copilot Studio also made it easy to take this feedback and refine the agent. As Pettit explains, “With Microsoft Copilot Studio, we are able to quickly assess what was answered and not answered by Anna, then organize responses into clear topics and categories, so we know exactly where to focus our time on content updates.”

Using generative answers, along with a highly effective monitoring and training process, the agent has achieved strong  resolution rates  with early users and is currently handling thousands of conversations per week. The excellent response rates by Anna are helping deliver more of the information customers need faster, leading to a better overall experience.

This is reflected in the latest business results. “What we’re finding is that when customers engage with Anna, they are more likely to find the right cruise that fits their needs than if they do not engage at all,” says Pettit. At the same time, there are early indications that Anna will reduce the number of basic informational queries to contact center agents. 

Optimizing AI for customers

The team continues to expand Anna’s capabilities. This first MVP release of Anna is currently running in the United States, and she is set to go live in Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom, equipped with market-specific cruise and booking information. Anna will also soon be introduced in non-English markets.

Looking further ahead, Holland America Line is poised to advance the AI capabilities of its agent by integrating additional secondary flows, enabling customers to book excursions, spa services, drink packages, and other services, as well as find specific information about port and destination interests. 

These advancements will enhance the experience throughout a customer’s journey. As Pettit says, “With Microsoft Copilot Studio, we have an effective platform for delivering the benefits of generative AI to our customers, providing them with faster service and an even better overall cruise experience.”

Kacy Cole, CMO at Holland America Line, shares her perspective on how AI-powered agents are transforming marketing

An unexpected effect of implementing generative AI is that we’re gaining insights and understanding what’s changing in the cruise industry, what’s happening in our business, and better connecting with guests. These insights are going to transform how we continue to go to market. 

We’re able to localize our marketing using AI capabilities, and we’re able to get to market faster because AI helps us define audiences, product offerings, and media opportunities in a fraction of the time. The real opportunity is around the guest experience and deepening our relationship with them. With AI, we can have one-to-one conversations with guests, at scale. 

AI is also enriching my employees’ experience. 

What’s exciting about generative AI, as well as agents, is the ability to unleash imagination. I think marketing really starts to become a creative powerhouse limited only by our ability to dream.   

My team has started down this path, and we’re seeing a fundamental shift in our capabilities. Platforms like Microsoft Copilot Studio, which help us build AI-powered agents, are allowing us to think bigger, different, more expansively than before. What was once out of reach is now something we can pull a daily report about.

“Drug development, which underpins our mission to serve patients, is very much becoming an information capability. Finding, parsing, and processing information is a big part of how we get medicines to patients more quickly,” says Scott Skellenger, SVP and CIO at Amgen.

Amgen, a leading biotechnology company, is known for innovative approaches that harness biology and technology to discover new medicines. “Advances in machine learning and computing power applied to biology have the potential to supercharge our ability to uncover insights,” explains Sean Bruich, SVP of AI & Data at Amgen. “AI has the potential to dramatically reduce cycle time in medicine development.”

Identifying a need

Like many companies, Amgen struggled to make its vast corpus of knowledge and resources easily accessible to the teams that work together to develop new therapies. “A drug developer might search our intranet for past trial designs or resources about a specific molecule,” says Bryan Yee, Executive Director of R&D Knowledge and Learning at Amgen. “They’d get a set of links to hunt down and sort through—PowerPoints, PDFs, articles, reports, SharePoint folders. This can take hours, days, even. We wanted to make this a more intelligent, intuitive process, the same way you’d ask a colleague a question.” Yee smiles. “Yes, it’s complex. But we knew we needed to figure it out.”

Building a solution

Amgen is an early adopter of Microsoft 365 Copilot. This made Copilot Studio, a low-code platform that uses generative AI and agentic workflows to build intelligent agents, an obvious place to start. Working with the Amgen technology team, Yee and his knowledge management crew built an agent for the R&D team that could reason over large volumes of information. The entire process took about six weeks. The goal was to use AI to sort, surface, and analyze Amgen’s existing thoughtfully curated resources, with a natural language interface. This led to the development of Catalyst Copilot, an agent embedded with Catalyst, Amgen’s knowledge management platform.

“As with all AI systems, the most important step for us was first having a carefully curated collection of information,” Yee says. “Adding Copilot to that made our ever-growing body of knowledge instantly more accessible and is a key strategy in how we are advancing the way we learn in real-time.”

Accelerating the path to discovery

With Catalyst Copilot, drug developers are tapping into the collective intelligence of the organization faster than ever. They are shortening the cycle of discovery by more easily finding the information and people needed to answer key questions that advance potential new medicines forward. Catalyst Copilot is helping to remove barriers to information-gathering, including the age-old problem of not knowing the right question to ask. Catalyst Copilot’s ability to reason and infer from multiple fact sets enables faster, more accurate conclusions. The Q&A–style chat inputs also help the knowledge management team understand intent, so they more precisely curate content.

Advancing for the future

Having seen the benefits of custom agentic workflows, Amgen looks to incorporate more in other areas of the business. “With Copilot Studio, we have a common platform to rapidly deploy solutions from the low-code and no-code environments, and we can also extend with more complex configurations as needed,” says Skellenger. “We see a future where there’s a single user experience that’s routing people to the agents that they need.”

"One of the key metrics for measuring AI success at Amgen is enabling better science at scale. This includes automating parts of the scientific process and distilling data that leads researchers to deep insights,” says Bruich. “Since Microsoft is a trusted technology collaborator, we can experiment quickly to see where AI can have a big impact.”

Bryan Yee, Executive Director of R&D Knowledge and Learning, shares his perspective on how digital agents boost innovation

Every organization struggles with knowledge and resources scattered around digitally. In Research and Development, this could be a serious impediment to innovation.

Removing this impediment is my team’s job. We manage information architecture for R&D. How can I quickly and intuitively connect drug developers to information that leads to breakthrough insights? The time it takes someone to find the right information, the right person to talk to, the right resource, is white space. We needed to close those gaps to help get therapies to patients faster.

We used Copilot Studio to build an agent in just six weeks that’s embedded in our knowledge platform, Catalyst. We’d already done the critical hard work of curating and organizing our knowledge—lessons learned, articles, presentations, and the like. Now we added AI to help analyze, classify, and apply reason over that information. With our agent, Catalyst Copilot, any one of the many roles that work together to bring potential new medicines to patients can now ask a question in natural language and get an answer. It’s like asking the right colleague a question at the right time, when they have all the right information at their fingertips. This approach has the potential to fundamentally change how R&D approaches knowledge management and how we learn as an organization. Now instead of starting at “Where is the information I need?” our team can go straight to “What do we already know?”

Copilot is helping remove obstacles and is bringing to life new ways to tap into our collective intelligence across Research and Development. This is the future of how we learn. That’s innovation.

“How does an 80-year-old company compete with new, agile startups?” asks Raheel Khan, Senior Vice President, Foresight and Growth Intelligence at The Estée Lauder Companies (ELC). “By using our intelligence.”

With nearly 25 brands operating across 150 countries, ELC generates an immense amount of consumer, market, and industry information to support product innovation, marketing, and sales. This vast amount of data, spread across the company in different formats – PDFs, PowerPoints, spreadsheets – is dense with meaningful insights that employees can use to create products and campaigns that meet consumer needs.

“By synthesizing and providing a simple way to access information from multiple sources, we can quickly identify data-backed insights to inform consumer-centric decisions,” says Jennifer Lee, Director, Strategic Initiatives and Predictive Analytics at ELC.

In a global company with many brands, housing data in one centralized location helps bring visibility to ELC’s vast treasure trove of data. “The sheer scale of our consumer insights and complexity of our matrixed organization makes it unrealistic for any team to know everything that’s available, which can result in duplicative studies and delays in activating with our consumers,” Lee continues.

It was imperative that ELC harness its decades of intelligence, which is an industry advantage. In a TikTok world where beauty trends shift with a tap, being able to get product to market quickly is essential for staying competitive.

Instant insights, validated and secure

To address this challenge, ELC created ConsumerIQ, an agent built in Microsoft Copilot Studio. ConsumerIQ is a dynamic intelligence hub underpinned by Azure OpenAI Service, with a chat interface using natural language to provide actionable intelligence. “We chose Copilot Studio because it’s tied into our Azure environment, giving us the seamless integration with our data that we needed,” notes Jayesh Mehta, VP, Brand Technology Leader at ELC.

To pull it all together, the team first centralized their information in one place. Then, with Azure OpenAI, the platform was taught to read research like charts, graphs, and images. Using generative AI, ConsumerIQ analyzes the documents to identify trends, connecting disparate data sources and providing strategic recommendations. It brings together decades of ELC’s knowledge along with current trends and studies to provide high quality, data-driven insights.

Now a product marketer at Origins, Estée Lauder, or any of the other ELC brands can query ConsumerIQ, “What are the trends in night cream?” for example. They’ll immediately receive an insight that includes citations so they can track down the original source for validation or more specific information.

Intelligence at speed

By centralizing insights and applying a user-friendly interface, ELC has reduced the time required to gather data from weeks to minutes. ConsumerIQ allows employees to quickly identify consumer insights exactly when they need them – empowering them to make data-backed decisions and move faster in the ever-evolving beauty industry.

Automating tedious data-gathering tasks with ConsumerIQ frees up teams to focus on strategic initiatives. “Since we deployed our Copilot agent, teams can now elevate their skill sets and focus on creating compelling marketing strategies and innovative products,” says Lee.

“Having the right information at our fingertips through our Copilot agent gives us the speed and competitive edge we need to go up against small, nimble newcomers,” explains Mehta.

Beauty reimagined

Looking ahead, ELC plans to expand ConsumerIQ’s capabilities, integrating additional data sources and scaling its use across all brands and functions. “The low-code/no-code capabilities of Copilot Studio allowed us to build a scalable solution that can be expanded to other use cases in the business, like supply chain and manufacturing,” says Shilpa Niranjan, Director, IT Business Partner at ELC. “Microsoft is connecting the dots across Copilot Studio solutions,” notes Khan, “and helping us build an agentic world for ELC.”

“ConsumerIQ is helping us put generations of experience to work for everyone, ensuring we stay competitive in a fast-changing world,” concludes Khan. “Intelligence is a beautiful thing.”

Shilpa Niranjan, Director, IT Business Partner at ELC, shares her perspective on creating Copilot agents

When I got the chance to work on the Copilot Studio project, I jumped at it. I really wanted to go deeper into AI as an important step for my career, and also because I’m fascinated by AI. This was a perfect opportunity to step outside my current role in global supply chain and dive into something completely different—in the marketing domain. It was a stretch assignment, but that’s what made it so exciting.

The project was all about building ConsumerIQ, a generative AI tool that lets global marketing, insights and other brand teams ask questions like “What is the mascara trend with daily exercisers?” and instantly get summarized, actionable answers. No more digging through piles of documents or spending hours summarizing data. The architecture behind it is very complex, with Azure OpenAI Service and Azure Functions apps, but the idea was simple: speed to information.

What really got me hooked was the chance to build my own AI agent. Using Copilot Studio, I created a supply chain agent that pulls answers from specific documents I have access to. Training it felt surprisingly natural—like teaching a human assistant. This kind of intuitive AI agent builder tool can be scaled to broader business users, for domain specific or generic use cases.

Acute care clinicians are often overwhelmed by the demands of documentation, reducing the time they can spend with patients. Sayvant, a health technology start-up, is on a mission to change that. By providing AI-driven clinical documentation solutions for emergency and other acute care providers, Sayvant is harnessing the power of AI and large language models to enhance the quality of patient care and improve financial and operational efficiency.

Empowering clinicians to spend more time with patients

Delivering high-quality care in acute care settings is challenging. Clinicians are burdened with extensive documentation required for transitions of care, reimbursement, and quality measurement. Sayvant, codesigned and codeveloped with Vituity, one of the largest democratically physician-owned healthcare delivery organizations, recognized this pressing issue and wanted to make a difference. Such a nuanced workflow meant the team had to create a product specifically tailored for an acute care setting.

Between 2017 and 2021, denial rates by payors surged by 20%,1 and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services coding changes in 2023 have placed the burden on clinicians to provide extensive documentation regarding their medical decision-making.2 This unfortunately means less face-to-face time with patients and higher burnout rates, resulting in staffing shortages and inefficiencies across hospital systems. On average, emergency medicine clinicians spend over two hours per shift, or about 20% of their time, on charting alone.3 “Every patient going to the emergency room is having their worst day,” says Dr. Andrew Napier, Cofounder of Sayvant. “If you can make that slightly better, whether it’s a faster visit, a more efficient visit, or an improved care outcome, ultimately, that’s why we’ve built Sayvant.”

Sayvant envisioned a generative AI solution that would transcribe, summarize, and generate patient charts so that clinicians could have more face-to-face interactions while maintaining document quality. The company had an existing relationship with Microsoft and chose to build its solution on Microsoft Azure offering Azure OpenAI Service. “We can do everything from accessing pay-as-you-go services for Azure OpenAI models to renting graphics processing units (GPUs) to self-host our own models,” says Justin Mardjuki, CEO of Sayvant. “This allows us flexibility to customize and build quickly.”

Sayvant built a multitenant architecture to ensure scalability, security, and compliance to meet demanding regulatory requirements like SOC 2 and the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act. “We’re building the highest-performing, secure clinical documentation solution that meets the demands of acute care settings,” says Mardjuki. “Microsoft is the preferred cloud vendor for a healthcare enterprise leader, and choosing Azure for Sayvant was a natural decision.”

Transforming patient care by decreasing documentation burden in more than 30 languages

Collaboration with clinicians is at the heart of Sayvant’s research and development. The company built its solution based on extensive feedback from hundreds of clinicians working at sites ranging from rural urgent care centers to level 1 urban trauma centers. “Given the amount of protected health information we’d be handling in these institutions, we wanted to ensure that they felt comfortable with our choices regarding infrastructure, scalability, security, and privacy,” says Mardjuki. “We’ve been very happy with that decision.”

Sayvant transcribes conversations between clinicians and patients in near real time and in more than 30 languages. The solution then creates robust, clinically defensible charts for healthcare providers to review, along with personalized discharge instructions. “There’s a pretty radical transformation when clinicians walk into the room with Sayvant in their pocket,” says Mardjuki. “The doctor doesn’t have to worry about getting every word right because Sayvant helps them generate that chart. They can have a face-to-face conversation with the patient.”

Reducing discharge delays by 40%

Sayvant adoption has spread to nearly 70 sites since its private beta app launched in the summer of 2024. To date, more than 30,000 shifts have been completed using Sayvant, and charting time for emergency providers has been significantly reduced, from 10 minutes to less than 90 seconds per patient, saving an estimated 50,000 hours.

Extra one-on-one time with patients and clear discharge instructions has led to a 40% reduction in discharge delays at one site, reducing patient time in the waiting room and in the emergency room. “As labs and images are returned, clinicians can have ongoing conversations with Sayvant about diagnoses,” says Mardjuki. “This allows them to focus on the right next step of care for the patient instead of the right next step in documentation.”

Some clinicians now use Sayvant exclusively, an adoption rate 10 times higher than other solutions on the market. “I have been using Sayvant exclusively for the last three months and can never go back to the original ways of charting,” says Dr. Cameron Nouri, Medical Director of the Department of Emergency Medicine at the Community Hospital of San Bernardino in California. “I am able to quickly and efficiently see more patients and finish my charts before getting out on time.”

Expanding the impact of AI on healthcare

Sayvant is excited to partner with more healthcare providers and clinicians, and it plans to continue investment in its best-of-breed large language model infrastructure. “We’re building Sayvant with input from experts in the field so that we can really validate the impact that we are having,” says Mardjuki. “As we expand the number of sites, clinicians, and patients that we support every day, we’re excited about deepening our AI investments to ensure that we continue to improve the speed, accuracy, and quality of our acute care documentation output.”

For 100 years, Toastmasters International has helped people build confidence and expand their network through effective communication. Clubs in 150 countries welcome all people to practice preparing and giving speeches, responding to questions, and supporting other members. Online education programs empower members to develop skills at their own pace. “A lot of people join Toastmasters for a sense of community and an opportunity to make a difference,” says Diana Passow, Marketing and Communications Director at Toastmasters. 

The nonprofit is undertaking a digitization journey to better meet member needs and grow for another 100 years. Recently, the Colorado-based organization adopted Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Service to improve the member experience, generate data-based insights to inform strategy, and gain efficiencies. Strengthening the Toastmasters brand and member loyalty sets up the organization for sustainable growth.

“Toastmasters is about human beings connecting with human beings, and technology is helping us do that,” says Jason Caldwell, Club Quality and Member Support Manager at Toastmasters. “We’re making the world a better place, one Toastmaster at a time.”

Modernizing the member experience 

Toastmasters is best known for creating supportive environments and providing the tools to help people meet their public speaking and communication goals. In the process, members find camaraderie, build community, and forge meaningful relationships with diverse groups. That positive experience is what draws in new members and keeps people in clubs.  

Toastmasters is leveraging technology to create a similarly positive experience throughout members’ interactions with the nonprofit.  

With just 30 call center staff serving 270,000 members worldwide, Microsoft's CRM is helping the team answer questions and track concerns more efficiently. Dynamics 365 Customer Service offers a centralized place to record all interactions, from calls to emails. Seeing all points of contact within a single omnichannel platform saves staff time, as they do not have to switch between applications.  

“With this CRM, it’s very easy for our team to look at the history of a member and their contacts with us,” Caldwell says. “It connects all the dots, giving everybody the information they need when they need it.” 

Dynamics 365 Contact Center, a Copilot-enabled service solution, works with existing CRMs. With generative AI, it summarizes customer service interactions into the Dynamics 365 notes section. “What a joy and delight that is,” Caldwell says. Contact Center’s omnichannel view unifies calls, chats, emails, and the CRM platform all on one screen, leading to team efficiencies. This single lens ensures all staff are up to date and able to help members the next time they call. Generative AI-powered case management also means Toastmasters staff do not have to type while talking, allowing them to focus fully on the conversation. 

Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations connects to the Toastmasters website to enable self-service. For the first time, people can apply and pay dues online. “It’s the twenty-first century, so we need to digitize the experience for our members,” says Heidi Hollenbeck, Chief Operations and Information Officer at Toastmasters. “It makes things more efficient on our end, but it importantly makes the process more user-friendly, too.” 

The online self-service improves security because members do not have to share their payment information over the phone or on a membership form. It also improves accuracy because members input their own data, rather than staff reentering the information from a form.  

Toastmasters also leveraged Microsoft Copilot Studio and agents to build Ora Tor, a generative AI chatbot. This always-on resource draws from a knowledge bank staff filled with their trouble-shooting wisdom so members can get answers online, any time.  

Modernizing through technology removes barriers to joining and staying involved. “When we offer the technology-enabled experience they expect, we attract a younger demographic,” Passow says. “Digitizing helps us open our doors to more people.”

Optimizing services with data 

During the COVID-19 pandemic, Toastmasters nimbly shifted its in-person model to online meetings, providing a much-needed outlet for isolated people to connect and learn. The nonprofit continues to adapt to meet members’ needs by securely leveraging data across platforms. 

Dynamics 365 seamlessly connects to other Microsoft solutions that Toastmasters uses, such as SharePoint and Power BI. A single data landscape “allows us to share effective reporting to our executives,” Caldwell says. “This gets them more accurate data so we can make faster decisions.”  

Dynamics 365 identifies themes in member concerns—for instance, if people are having trouble with a glitchy button on the website or need help navigating tricky interpersonal relationships in their club. Staff can share data-backed insights with the relevant team, who then fix the issue more quickly. 

Concrete evidence about common member questions also empowers the customer service team to provide solutions. For example, if members of corporate clubs frequently call for help to split their dues with their employer, the team can use generative AI to draft a troubleshooting document, which they then refine. "This provides us the ability to help members directly, no matter who on the team is answering the question,” says Danielle Mitchell, Director of Club Quality and Member Support at Toastmasters.  

Data also informs strategy and longer-term projects, such as developing new courses for their online learning platform. Mitchell says, “Better reports based on good data helps us improve our systems so members have fewer questions in the first place.”

Gaining efficiencies to grow

Toastmasters customer service staff used to have to search for member communication across platforms, forward messages to colleagues, and manually input data. Dynamics 365 automates many of these time-consuming steps, freeing up staff for value-adding projects. The team has used Power Automate to create even smoother flows of recurring internal processes within the Dynamics 365 ecosystem. “These efficiency wins are big for the whole team,” Hollenbeck says.

The customer service team saves hours each week with streamlined Microsoft technology. "We’ll have the bandwidth to proactively reach out to members, like somebody who’s starting a new club”—a long-held goal they never had the time for, Caldwell says. The team will also be able to use data analytics from Dynamics 365 to guide the development of new products that would benefit members. They can also test systems improvements, relying on data to quantify how tweaks improve outcomes.

“We now have the platform to scale, grow, and create more opportunities for members,” Hollenbeck says. The nonprofit is exploring new products, different types of memberships, partnerships, and even expanding to more countries. “We have the technology to meet our needs now and in the future.”

“It all started with an iconic asset and a magical idea,” says Pratik Thakar, VP and Global Head of Generative AI at Coca-Cola. “We wanted to create a first-of-its-kind holiday campaign by bringing to life the famous Sundblom Santa popularized by Coca-Cola back in 1931. This jolly rendition of Santa is instantly recognized around the world—he’s helped create special memories for millions of people across the decades.”

For Coca-Cola, the desire to create a two-way dialogue with Santa marked a new frontier in its ability to quickly stand up a marketing campaign capable of traversing 43 countries and 26 languages. “It was an ambitious campaign! We knew conversational AI was going to be big, so we embraced the power of technology to help us inspire meaningful connections between friends and loved ones, a hallmark of our holiday campaigns.” says Pratik Thakar, VP and Global Head of Generative AI, Coca-Cola

Using an assembly of innovative, leading-edge technologies, Coca-Cola replicated the beloved Santa in digital 3D, gave him the ability to have real-time, memory-sharing conversations with consumers, then animated him to co-create with young and old a personalized, musical snow globe to instantly share. 

Laying the foundation for AI with Azure

This transformative “Create Real Magic” holiday campaign was possible with Coca-Cola’s migration to Microsoft Azure—a decision that not only modernized its operations, but also instilled the confidence and capability to bring its nostalgic Santa to life. 

Coca-Cola’s migration to Azure began five years ago, with the transformation happening in three phases:   

Initial migration to IaaS: Coca-Cola first moved its enterprise workloads to Azure using infrastructure as a service (IaaS), deploying Windows and Linux virtual machines for scalable computing. 

Adoption of PaaS and SaaS: It modernized to platform as a service (PaaS) and software as a service (SaaS), building scalable applications and automating workflows.

AI-ready transformation: Migration enabled Coca-Cola to co-locate data, reducing latency and ensuring seamless interoperability with AI models.

Coca-Cola understands the significance of having a solid, AI-ready foundation as the backbone for its AI innovation. Using Azure AI Speech in Azure AI Foundry, Coca-Cola was able to assimilate vast amounts of data from global markets into the Santa campaign. “Without this robust foundation,” Ramakrishnappa notes, “innovative campaigns like ‘Create Real Magic’ would not have been scalable or feasible.” 

“Our Azure journey started with IaaS and progressed to PaaS and SaaS, creating a robust platform, and optimized operations to build the kinds of campaigns we are building,” says Thakar. 

Managing a complex global project in 60 days

Creating a holiday campaign sensation that touched millions around the world, and doing it all within 60 days, showcased Coca-Cola’s ability to execute ideas quickly and at scale. 

Key steps taken:

 1. Defining the vision and goals

Coca-Cola aimed to expand its reach and deepen emotional connections with customers. 
The campaign aligned with the company’s global brand ethos of combining “real and magic.” 

2. Assembling a cross-functional team

Coca-Cola collaborated with a host of global best-in-class providers.  
Teams from multiple regions worked in tandem to address diverse market needs. 

3. Accessing Azure capabilities

Azure AI Foundry. Provided the AI toolchain for developing and testing the application.
Azure AI Speech. Simplified the process with the prebuilt multimodal and multilingual capabilities in custom neural voice and text to speech avatar offered within Azure AI Foundry. 
Azure Container Apps. Hosted the campaign’s back end and front end, helping ensure reliability and scalability. 
Azure Functions. Simplified serverless workflow orchestrations across AI, data, and event sources.
.NET Aspire. Built the app using this set of tools, templates, and packages for building observable, production-ready apps. 
Overcoming complexity with Azure

The interoperability of Azure was critical in unifying the diverse technologies required for the campaign. Coca-Cola used the API-driven Azure ecosystem to bring together third-party solutions while maintaining a cohesive development workflow. Serverless features in Azure Functions, such as triggers and bindings, seamlessly handled Coca Cola’s events and data processing across Azure Cosmos DB, Azure Service Bus, and Azure Blob Storage using a preferred format. This approach enhanced productivity with fewer lines of code. 

Azure AI Foundry played a pivotal role in managing and deploying AI models at scale, while Azure AI Speech supported effortless and natural multilingual conversations. This architecture allowed Coca-Cola’s developers to focus on innovation rather than operational overhead. 

Describing the campaign’s unique challenges and collaborative efforts, Thakar explains, “We wanted to create something never seen before while staying authentic to our heritage. With Microsoft’s support, we co-created tools to solve complex technical challenges like multilingual lip sync for Santa’s avatar.”

Using Azure to create a repeatable blueprint for developers  

The modularity and integration capabilities in Azure provide a blueprint for managing complex, large-scale projects. Developers can: 

Use Azure Container Apps for scalable app deployment

Rapid scaling to accommodate millions of users simultaneously interacting with the campaign.
Coca-Cola used Container Apps to orchestrate its containerized applications. The service’s built-in tools for load balancing and autoscaling helped ensure the platform remained responsive even during peak usage. 

Simplified serverless workflow orchestrations across AI, data, and event sources. Using Azure Functions, Coca-Cola automated the communication between different components, such as processing user inputs, querying AI models, and generating personalized outputs. This serverless approach reduced operational overhead and improved resource efficiency. 
 

Employ Azure AI Foundry tools and services for multilingual and multimodal applications

The campaign relied on Azure AI Speech, found in Azure AI Foundry, and text to speech services to deliver seamless multilingual interactions. Developers fine-tuned neural voice models to ensure authenticity in every supported language, while multimodal capabilities enabled the integration of text, voice, and visual elements. 
 

Build with confidence, using end-to-end monitoring and security features in Azure

Coca-Cola used Azure Monitor and Microsoft Defender for Cloud to help ensure compliance with global data regulations and maintain high availability. These tools provided real-time insights into system performance and security, enabling proactive issue resolution and helping ensure the campaign’s reliability. 

Ramakrishnappa emphasizes the measurable benefits, explaining, “With end-to-end solutions in Azure, we achieved unprecedented global scale and personalization. The campaign’s ROI exceeded expectations, driving both engagement and brand loyalty.” 

Confirming Microsoft technology as best choice

Coca-Cola’s decision to adopt Microsoft Azure was instrumental in the campaign’s success. Key differentiators included: 

1. Comprehensive AI capabilities

Azure AI Foundry. Developers used the AI platform to efficiently test Azure AI Speech features, enabling Coca-Cola to quickly scale from proof of concept to production within tight deadlines.
Azure AI Speech. Coca-Cola used the tools in this service to implement real-time, natural-language conversations across 26 languages, with sub-millisecond performance outcomes. This was achieved using prebuilt multimodal and multilingual neural voice models in Azure, fine-tuned for cultural nuances and accents, which made interactions with Santa feel authentic and engaging. 

2. Scalability and flexibility

Azure Container Apps. Supported the massive scale of the campaign by managing containerized workloads. The platform’s autoscaling features helped ensure responsiveness, regardless of user traffic spikes. 
Interoperability with third-party tools. With the open ecosystem of Azure, Coca-Cola brought together third-party services for image generation and conversation logic, creating a truly multimodal experience that combined text, images, and speech seamlessly. 

3. Security and compliance

Built-in security features. The multilayered security controls in Azure helped protect user data from potential breaches so that Coca-Cola could meet stringent global privacy standards. 
Compliance with regional regulations. Coca-Cola used the platform’s ability to operate within multiple regions while adhering to local data compliance laws. For example, .NET Aspire services helped ensure the campaign met General Data Protection Regulation requirements in Europe and other similar standards worldwide.

By combining these capabilities, Coca-Cola achieved a unified and reliable platform that met the campaign’s ambitious goals. Thakar summarizes the value of the partnership: “Azure AI Foundry has taken us to the next level of marketing, consumer engagement, and economic impact. AI technology has become essential to communicating our brand essence securely and broadly.” 

Realizing tangible ROI

The “Create Real Magic” campaign generated impressive results. 

Global engagement. More than 1 million users interacted with Santa across 43 markets in just three weeks.

Personalized experiences. Customers created snow globes tailored to their holiday memories, sharing them widely on social media.

Emotional connections. Users could share their favorite holiday memories with Santa and watch him recreate them in personalized snow globes, enabling Coca-Cola to bring joy and nostalgia to countless families.

Brand impact. Coca-Cola reinforced its image as an innovative, customer-centric brand, resonating across diverse cultures and age groups. 

The application was easy to use. Customers scanned a QR code, entered their favorite holiday memory, and watched as Santa responded in their language. Moments like these created an emotional ripple effect. Parents captured their children’s amazement as they heard Santa’s personalized responses. Grandparents shared stories of their favorite snow globes, sparking laughter and warmth in households around the world. 

Thakar shares a heartfelt observation, recalling, “When I saw videos of kids giggling as Santa spoke to them, and families bonding over their snow globes, I knew we had created more than just a campaign. We were creating memories.”  

Innovating with more freedom and creativity

Coca-Cola’s “Create Real Magic” campaign exemplifies how cloud migration and AI integration can drive innovation, efficiency, and customer engagement. The collaboration with Microsoft not only met but exceeded Coca-Cola’s goals, setting a new standard for global, personalized advertising campaigns. 

With a solid AI-ready foundation, Coca-Cola is poised to continue delivering groundbreaking consumer experiences that combine the magic of its heritage with the power of modern technology. As Ramakrishnappa puts it, “This is just the beginning. With Azure, the possibilities are limitless.”
