With the rise of AI, healthcare institutions like City of Hope are seizing the opportunity to transform physician workloads and empower more focused, personalized patient care. By harnessing the power of Microsoft Azure, City of Hope has developed an innovative generative AI platform that supports oncology doctors in preparing for new patient appointments and building treatment plans. This cutting-edge solution helps doctors spend less time reviewing documents and more time engaging with patients face-to-face, revolutionizing the way care is delivered.

Transforming cancer care with AI: City of Hope’s legacy of innovation

Founded in 1913, City of Hope is one of the largest and most advanced cancer research and treatment organizations in the United States. With a rich history of using cutting-edge technology and innovations, City of Hope continues to stay at the forefront of advances in data science and AI to bring breakthroughs to its patients.

Recognizing the potential of recent AI advancements, City of Hope set out to tackle one of the healthcare industry’s biggest challenges: the administrative burden of patient referrals. In 2024 alone, City of Hope onboarded more than 150,000 patients. Doctors often see new patients with extensive medical histories spanning 10–20 years of test results, notes, and treatment reports. Doctors need to spend significant time—often during nonworking hours—to review hundreds of document pages, leading to less time interacting directly with patients due to extensive medical history review.

“One of our physician executives jokingly told me that because this is such a big pain point, if we could come up with a solution to digest all this information and provide an accurate summary, my statue would be placed in the City of Hope hospital,” says Nasim Eftekhari, Chief AI Officer at City of Hope. “That’s how we started working on this use case.”

City of Hope aimed to build a responsible large language model (LLM) platform to give valuable time back to doctors and their patients. From the outset, City of Hope’s decision makers knew they wanted to use Azure OpenAI Service and the optical character recognition technique, which recognizes printed and handwritten text in image files, as instrumental parts of the solution. “We want to work with the best and brightest out there who can bring the right technologies to bear for us,” says Simon Nazarian, Chief Digital and Technology Officer at City of Hope. “That’s where Microsoft came in. It’s a very mutually agreeable collaboration, where both sides are dedicated to advancing what is best for healthcare.”

Building a time-saving solution in three months

City of Hope created minimum viable capabilities for its physician-facing LLM platform in just three months. Then, it worked closely with Microsoft cloud engineers from customer success programs to bring the groundbreaking generative AI solution to life. “City of Hope has closed the loop of going from data and information to action and continuous optimization,” says Eftekhari. “It’s not just conceptual; our clinicians are using this solution now.”

City of Hope’s solution is one of the first uses of AI in general oncology, and the team worked diligently to implement it responsibly. The solution underwent multiple rounds of approvals, regulatory controls, and adoption scenarios to ensure accurate summaries of patient information. Remarkably, the AI platform provided a clean and comprehensive view of patients’ histories.

With this solution, doctors at City of Hope can drastically reduce the time spent reviewing patient referral documents and thus focus more on their patients and personal lives. Detailed and searchable information at their fingertips helps doctors quickly determine the best treatment options. “The main driver for this project was improving provider and patient experiences,” says Eftekhari. “Doctors can now look their patients in the eyes, already knowing their history, rather than trying to scramble to look at PDFs.”

This solution not only boosts physician productivity but also reduces costs. Doctors can potentially see more patients, thanks to the time-saving features, and avoid ordering redundant tests, scans, or biopsies by identifying prior labs and tests.

Patients benefit directly from the AI solution as well. Typically, patients and doctors share the burden of providing and verifying medical history. However, City of Hope’s Azure-powered platform shifts this responsibility away from patients, helping them to receive more personalized care and engage in focused, future-looking discussions with their doctors. Now, patients can concentrate on their primary responsibility: recovery.

Empowering high-quality patient care

Building an innovative generative AI platform with support from Microsoft has been a rewarding journey for City of Hope’s data and technology teams. Not only did they develop new guidelines, processes, and tools to create a solution with wide-ranging impacts in the healthcare industry, but they are also aiming to make a direct, positive impact on the quality of patient care as well as the patient and provider experience. “You can work on algorithms anywhere,” says Eftekhari. “But bringing them to life and having them improve and save lives—that’s not something you can do everywhere.”

Looking ahead, City of Hope plans to continually enhance its AI solution to empower even better experiences for doctors and patients. The institution’s next step is exploring more applications of the LLM platform, such as clinical-trial matching, and incorporating multimodal AI models to work with medical images and genomics in addition to text and electronic medical record data.

“We want to take advantage of innovative technologies to support real-time decision making,” says Nazarian. “We want to do it responsibly. We want to do it together. And, at the end of the day, we want to help improve healthcare for all.”

As CIO of Mike Morse Law Firm and Fireproof Performance, John Georgatos helps law firms with security and digital transformations. “Most law firms use technology that’s 10 years behind. They’re not able to defend against sophisticated threats, or grow efficiently,” he says.

Efficiency and security are paramount. "Our clients’ lives are in our files—from medical to estate, trust, and bankruptcy data. We’re ethically bound to protect this confidential data," says John R. Nachazel Junior, appellate attorney with Mike Morse. “We’ve also always been cutting edge with technology, to make cases go better and faster.” 

In 2022, the Mike Morse Law Firm went cloud-first, adopting Microsoft 365 in 90 days and using Microsoft Surface devices. The firm was ready to adopt AI in 2024, knowing that if it didn’t, its competitors would. Jen Harvala, Chief Learning Officer and Head of Pre-Litigation at Mike Morse Law Firm, saw it as futureproofing. “Hiring, training, and retaining top talent are pivotal to our growth,” Harvala says. “Training was an area of opportunity for us.”

Security and productivity upgrades

"We wanted employees to have AI ready to help them in any application, without logging into multiple accounts, switching environments, or compromising security,” says Georgatos. The firm chose Microsoft 365, bringing in Microsoft experts to demonstrate Microsoft 365 Copilot, and trained those who were most interested to help colleagues adopt the technology. Harvala invites solution champions to share their successes at quarterly meetings, to foster a culture of learning. 

Mike Morse applies conditional access policies to its devices. Employees log on using facial recognition or a PIN instead of passwords. The firm implemented security layers across the company, enrolling new devices automatically out of the box using Microsoft Intune and Windows Autopilot, combining this conditional access with identity management for single sign-on. 

The firm saves time and improves security. “Conditional access is tied to each employee’s Surface, so even if someone’s credentials get compromised, attackers can’t use them on another device,” says Georgatos. “By adding Microsoft Intune Autopilot and OneDrive, we provision new devices with apps in 15 minutes, versus 2 to 3 hours.”

Harvala uses natural language prompts in Copilot to create training materials, which employees gave a positive rating. Nachazel Junior uses Copilot in Outlook to draft emails on his phone, typing short, high-level answers that Copilot fleshes out into full messages. He uses Copilot in Microsoft Word with the CoCounsel Drafting add-in to write complaints and other documents based on the firm’s data and the trusted Thomson Reuters legal database service. “With Copilot and CoCounsel, I can write documents about a case without exposing clients’ data to the internet. It’s very secure,” he says.

Seamless safeguards, targeted data use

Georgatos says some sophisticated attacks had bypassed multi-factor authentication: “But with Microsoft Defender, Intune, Entra ID, and Surface devices, we’ve taken security to the next level.”  

Harvala appreciates the option to base documents on internal or external sources with Microsoft Graph connectors. ”Copilot guides us through difficult conversations—no more staring at a blank page. It uncovers organizational data, reviews documents, and helps us be more productive and efficient,” Harvala says.

AI is helping the firm do higher-quality work with fewer people. “Our original strategy was to grow to 500 employees; with Copilot, we might not need to. We can handle more clients and attend to them better, which has a cascading effect,” says Georgatos. “When I first heard of Microsoft 365 Copilot, I expected a steroid-infused Clippy. But it’s there in the name—Copilot helps us orchestrate business processes, finds information we might otherwise miss, so we can get the best out of our people.”

Miami Dade College innovates with Microsoft 365 Copilot to transform education

At Miami Dade College (MDC), education goes beyond the classroom – it’s about shaping futures. With a strong commitment to student success, MDC continuously seeks innovative ways to enhance learning.

“Our mission is to prepare students for the workforce and ensure they have the skills they need to succeed,” says Dr. James Thomas, Chair of the School of Engineering and Technology at Miami Dade College.

As artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes education, MDC sees an opportunity to pioneer, embedding AI into its core strategy and driving meaningful transformation at every level. Already a heavy user of Microsoft 365 and Teams, expanding its partnership and deploying Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses among the President’s Cabinet and senior leaders, was a natural step in kickstarting its AI journey.

Reclaiming valuable time

For educators, time is essential. Copilot removes administrative burdens, enabling faculty to focus on teaching and student engagement.

“We complete tasks in minutes instead of hours,” says Dr. Thomas. “If just 15% of our more than 6,000 employees save 12 minutes a day, that’s nearly 50,000 hours a year – time reinvested in meaningful work.”

“Copilot has given us the luxury of time,” continues Antonio Delgado, Vice President of Innovation and Technology Partnerships at Miami Dade College. “It’s helping us work smarter, not harder.”

Elevating student engagement

Copilot is a 24/7 study companion, offering on-demand support and personalized guidance.

“Copilot acts as an always-available tutor, supporting coding exercises, essay structures and math problems – even at 2 AM when professors aren’t available,” reflects Dr. Ernesto Lee, Faculty Member in Artificial Intelligence and Data Analytics at Miami Dade College.

Through Microsoft Copilot Studio, MDC has enhanced student engagement, creating AI-powered assistants that help with personalized learning and study support. The impact has been especially significant in the first semester of implementation in STEM and advanced analytics courses, where the enhanced AI assistant has led to a 15 percent increase in pass rates and a 12 percent decrease in dropout rates. 

Students love the instant feedback and flexibility, making learning more accessible and engaging.

“We’re seeing a clear link between Copilot-assisted learning and student success,” says Antonio Delgado. “Students are more engaged, more confident and achieving better grades.”

Sparking creativity and making learning fun

Copilot isn’t just about automating tasks – it’s a creative assistant. 

“The key isn’t just using AI to find answers – it’s about understanding the ‘why’ behind them,” says Dr. Thomas. “Copilot explains concepts, breaks down processes and enhances learning.”

Beyond its practical benefits, Copilot is making work and learning more dynamic, interactive and engaging.

 “There’s real excitement in seeing what’s possible. Copilot isn’t doing the work for you – it’s helping you do it better,” adds Dr. Thomas.

Ensuring responsible and enthusiastic adoption

Implementing Copilot wasn’t just about innovation, it required secure, structured training to ensure faculty, staff and students could integrate AI effectively into their work.

“Of course, there was initial skepticism,” says Dr. Lee. “People hesitate to embrace change, but history shows innovation moves forward regardless. No one wants to be the best horseshoe maker in an era of cars – adaptation is key.”

MDC addressed concerns with gradual onboarding and education, building a Microsoft Teams community where faculty and staff share best practices, AI prompts and insights, keeping Copilot a continuous driver of innovation.

“We often hear, ‘We’re building the airplane as we fly it.’ Well, in this case, Microsoft already built the airplane – we’re just learning how to fly it properly,” says Dr. Thomas.

Positive feedback fuels further adoption

Once faculty and staff saw Copilot’s real-world impact, adoption took off.

“I’ve received so many ‘wow’ moments from employees when they realize just how powerful Copilot is,” says Antonio Delgado. “The moment it clicks – the moment they complete a task in seconds that used to take hours – that’s when you see the real impact.”

A survey reinforced Copilot’s success:

77% of users reported completing tasks faster

76% saw improved work quality

81% increased productivity

Encouraged by these results, MDC expanded its Copilot deployment by 400 licenses, prioritizing student-facing employees.

Shaping the future of education

With AI already transforming education at Miami Dade College, the institution is looking ahead – expanding its Copilot adoption, sharing its success with other colleges and pushing the boundaries of what AI can do in higher education.

“Our next step is scaling,” says Dr. Thomas. “We’ve proven success with 500 users – now we’re looking at expanding.” 

By the end of 2025, MDC aims to have Copilot embedded in most classes, ensuring that every student interacts with AI in a meaningful way.

“What Copilot can do today is incredible but imagine what it will be capable of next year,” emphasizes Dr. Thomas. “AI adoption will only accelerate, and how we embrace it will define its impact.”

Looking forward, MDC’s plans include enhancing staff-to-student response time, improving staff efficiency and boosting workforce readiness for students, with Microsoft 365 Copilot at the center of their educational tools.

 “Since implementing Copilot at MDC in 2024, the impact has been extraordinary – saving thousands of hours across the institution,” concludes Antonio Delgado. “We’re not just improving efficiency – we’re reimagining education.”

Story Content:
A company can be defined by many things—its branding, market share, and employees. But without securing ownership of intellectual property (IP), a company is little more than a logo and a dream. As a market leader in IP management solutions, Anaqua helps companies maintain those dreams in reality by protecting their most valuable assets. The Boston-based software and services provider is trusted with safeguarding the patents and trademarks for some of the world’s most prominent corporations and law firms.

Having so many influential ideas in one place—or, in this case, one platform—inspires Anaqua to provide both sophisticated capabilities and security. “Our platform is a management tool for the entire innovation life cycle,” says Chief Information Officer Erik Bailey. “It helps people go from thinking of an idea to getting it to where it’s doing something useful. We have workflow engines that can take your idea and route it to the appropriate people who can say, ‘Yes, we can monetize this.’ It then walks you through the whole IP prosecution process.” 

By streamlining IP operations through the entire patent life cycle with process automation and analytics, Anaqua helps clients expand their IP portfolios and make informed business decisions. “Patents are mentioned in the United States Constitution. They’re a fundamental right,” says Bailey. “People innovate because of the protection of patents and trademarks. By facilitating that, we’re facilitating innovation. And by facilitating innovation, we’re making the world a better place.”

Planning for the future

Anaqua found that its ambitions to facilitate innovation required a change in its cloud-hosting model. “We used bare metal servers. You could go to a datacenter and say, ‘This is my database server,’ and touch it. And that worked for us in 2016,” says Bailey. “But by 2021, that model was no longer the right fit for our customers and our hosting team.” Adds Igal Bluvol, Senior Director of Hosting Operations at Anaqua, “We wanted to be able to respond faster if faced with an issue and to have a virtual machine–based platform with strong governance.” The company sought to move to a cloud environment that offered the flexibility, infrastructure, and support to scale globally well into the future. 

The new cloud platform also had to provide exceptional data security and reliability for the clients that trust Anaqua to protect their most prized intellectual possessions. True end-to-end encryption (including within the datacenter itself, with network traffic and native disk encryption), fine-grained control of firewall rules, and streamlined disaster recovery procedures were all key requirements.

Migrating to Azure 

After conducting a year-long, exhaustive, and competitive evaluation to assess its options, Anaqua chose Microsoft Azure as its next-generation cloud platform. With help from Microsoft, Anaqua successfully migrated to an environment where the growing IP solutions company feels highly empowered and comfortable. “Anaqua is ISO certified and SOC 2 Type 2 audited, and so is Microsoft,” notes Bluvol. “The maturity of the governance that we gained with this move was a big factor.”

Anaqua worked with Microsoft on technical, architectural, and financial models. “Our work with the Azure team gave us the confidence that we could make this transformation real, and that gave us confidence to proceed,” says Bailey. The migration, involving almost 400 clients across four product lines in just 22 months, was smooth for both clients and the Anaqua team, finishing four months ahead of schedule in August 2024.

Enhancing security, scalability, and support

Security plays a vital role in the world of IP management. “Fundamentally, we’re selling security, telling our clients, ‘Trust us with your most valuable assets,’” says Bailey. ”Industrial espionage is real and can cause billions of dollars in losses if unchecked. So, we need to make sure that our software package—the application plus the hosting environment and our staff workstations—are all deeply secure.”

To that end, Anaqua significantly enhanced its security posture by deploying multiple advanced technologies, including Azure Application Gateway, which enforces TLS 1.2 and 1.3 for inbound traffic and helps ensure true end-to-end encryption within the Azure datacenter. The company further strengthened security by restricting outbound traffic and only allowing known good endpoints. While Anaqua uses a variety of vendors for its security solutions, Azure serves as the bedrock of the company’s security efforts. “We get a suite of powerful tools from the Azure portal along with assessments from within the environment, greatly improving our monitoring and overall protection,” says Bailey. “We have a concise view of our servers and get reports that flag if anything needs to be tweaked.”

By improving its monitoring, Anaqua can better identify and solve issues to optimize its IP management platform proactively. “We now have a consolidated view of server metrics across the global enterprise using Azure Monitor, enabling identification of performance bottlenecks before they rise to a critical level,” says Bailey. “Virtual machines can easily be resized during a brief maintenance window, which lets us balance cost versus performance without either under- or over-resourcing our servers.”

Having enhanced its security and operational efficiency, Anaqua immediately began to scale its capabilities within Azure. “I found Azure flexible and extremely easy to work with architecturally,” says Jeff Marshall, Director of Hosting Operations at Anaqua. “Building the infrastructure from scratch, tearing it down, and building it up again was effortless.”

Anaqua also takes advantage of in-depth technical support and preventative services from Microsoft Unified with Support for Mission Critical. “The value we get from Microsoft Unified with Support for Mission Critical is immeasurable,” says Bailey. “We not only have a Customer Success Account Manager but also immediate access to an entire team of professionals who know us and our environment. And they have access to the entire Microsoft organization to address all of our questions.”

Impressing clients and improving performance

Anaqua and its clients recognize the impact and potential that comes with this migration. “From identifying that a virtual machine is down to using additional CPU memory, graphs, and charts, we have so much feature richness available to us with Azure and so many more data points than we’ve ever had before,” says Bluvol. “And all the tools now in our back pocket help us demonstrate our increased maturity to existing and prospective clients alike.”

Anaqua’s focus on clients helped spur its migration in the first place. As Bailey explains, “The clients were leading us in this direction, saying, ‘Azure is where we want you to be.’ We heard that strong message from both the corporate and the law firm sides.” And those clients are now experiencing the benefits, with Anaqua exceeding their expectations early on. “When we first started migrating some of our clients to Azure, they were surprised by the performance boost they got,” says Bailey. “We never told them it would be faster. The requirement was that it couldn’t be slower. But it’s faster. In some use cases, in fact, Azure is two to three times faster.”

This increased speed not only helps Anaqua bolster its client relationships, but it also helps those clients streamline their operations. “When our clients say, ‘It’s faster, we haven’t had any downtime, and there haven’t been any outages,’ that makes it exciting for our clients and really worth it for us.” Anaqua realized impressive results from its migration and is now using that momentum to develop new, cutting-edge offerings.

Innovation never ends

Anaqua’s enhanced security, data governance, and performance form the foundation on which it plans to build transformational AI and machine learning capabilities. Having improved its AI readiness by migrating to Azure, the company now aims to evolve its platform even further. For example, its clients and employees now extract useful information far faster from documents using Azure AI Document Intelligence. “We’re providing the mechanics along with the added value of helping patent attorneys and trademark attorneys, including those on our staff, do their jobs more easily,” says Bailey. “We want to guide our users to make the right decisions. They still own the decision, but the more that we can provide guidance, analysis, tools, and synthesized data, the more efficient our clients can be.” Anaqua is currently piloting the use of Microsoft 365 Copilot for additional operational efficiencies, and it will be working with Microsoft to further integrate advanced AI, direct access into Microsoft 365 documents, and other technologies into their products and services.

Anaqua also aims to further enhance its security capabilities by implementing products like Microsoft Sentinel and Microsoft Defender. “We’re interested in taking advantage of additional integrated logging and alerting with Microsoft Sentinel and in further protecting our workloads with the Defender suite of tools,” says Bailey. “Knowing we can improve our security and other organizational capabilities incrementally and continually is important to us.”

Husch Blackwell is at the forefront of implementing AI and unlocking its benefits in the legal sphere. With AI, the firm is creating unique opportunities for lawyers and other legal staff to save time, increase efficiency, and form deeper connections.

Many law firms are seeking ways to help attorneys spend less time performing routine tasks and more time engaging with clients and doing meaningful work. Husch Blackwell has used solutions like Microsoft Azure, Azure Compute, Microsoft Copilot, and Microsoft Teams to meet those goals, cutting the time and costs associated with common repetitive jobs.

Empowering the legal community with the latest technologies

Husch Blackwell, a law firm with expertise in renewable energy and other large industries, hosts more than 20 offices across the United States, including a virtual office called The Link. Since its founding, Husch Blackwell has been a pioneer in implementing new technologies, championing remote work, and hiring data scientists and IT staff that many firms do not employ—all to improve efficiency while lawyers focus on legal responsibilities. “We’re different than typical law firms,” says Blake Rooney, Chief Information Officer at Husch Blackwell. “That has allowed us to become more diverse in our staffing of both lawyers and business professionals and a very data-driven law firm. We hired data scientists who helped us solve problems even before AI came on the scene.”

As the renewable energy sector brought in more cases, Husch Blackwell saw a major opportunity to revolutionize its legal practice. The firm faced the challenge of costly, repetitive tasks, like transcribing meetings, summarizing depositions, managing emails, and listening to voicemails, which left less time for engaging with clients. Recognizing that these routine activities were not adding value, Husch Blackwell partnered with Microsoft to implement Copilot and Azure, tools designed to help automate these tasks while maintaining the security and accuracy essential for legal matters. This strategic move not only saved thousands of hours but also allowed attorneys to focus on what truly matters—building stronger client relationships and delivering high-quality legal services.

Deploying AI tools to hundreds of lawyers with Copilot

In 2023, Husch Blackwell began deploying generative AI tools that quickly scanned and summarized large documents or online databases to help its workforce accelerate research and analysis. Lawyers used these tools to search for specific information and quotes from transcripts. AI was able to highlight that text in large documents or files so attorneys could save the time needed to read or search through them manually. Husch Blackwell also developed a tool called Prompt Composer where lawyers could upload specific datasets and obtain swift answers to questions about them. After the success of such tools, Husch Blackwell wanted to implement AI to ease other tasks and make way for more meaningful jobs and better interactions with clients.

The firm deployed Copilot to attorneys in 2024. It worked closely with Microsoft and used Azure compute to ensure scalability. “We have derived a lot of value from the collaboration with Microsoft,” says Thom Hutchison, Director of Data Science and AI at Husch Blackwell. “We’ve been able to access the tools available in Azure and then create complex solutions from those tools, which has been a real force multiplier.”

Additionally, Husch Blackwell appreciated how flexible Copilot could be to meet the demands of each individual attorney so they could use it for whatever work was taking up most of their time and energy. “We recognized that the application of the technology could cover multiple needs and trained the workforce on those capabilities,” says Justin Helms, Senior AI Solutions Strategist at Husch Blackwell.

Improving relationships and saving thousands of hours of work with Microsoft Teams and Copilot

Husch Blackwell attorneys outsourced much of their meeting note-taking to AI, freeing them up to focus more on engaging with clients during meetings. “Using Microsoft Teams makes the interaction between our attorneys and clients more seamless,” says Rooney. “They’re now more focused on making eye contact with clients. For us, AI is creating more personal human relationships.” AI transcription is also removing the need to hire transcriptionists for attorneys who have hearing loss, both cutting costs and increasing accessibility.

In one instance of success, Husch Blackwell used AI technology to save hundreds of hours of work writing website content. In 2024, the firm hired more than 100 summer associates. Writing their bios would have taken staff up to 160 hours, but with Prompt Composer and the Microsoft framework, it was done in one afternoon. “This is the sort of project a lot of knowledge workers get saddled with, but we were able to use this technology to automate it instead,” says Rooney.

Using Copilot, attorneys can find information easily. “One amazing thing you can do is ask, ‘What do I know about [insert topic]?’ and it will go across your entire Microsoft landscape to find Microsoft PowerPoint presentations, documents, emails, etc., on that exact topic and help you recall important information quickly,” says Helms. This and other Copilot capabilities helped attorneys save 8,800 hours of work in 2024 so they could put together cases and help clients more swiftly.

Advancing efficiency in the legal sphere with AI solutions

Husch Blackwell is pioneering new ways of using AI to serve law firms, which traditionally have been slow to adopt new technology. Moving forward, the firm is excited to see how it can implement AI for specific needs across the legal sphere, from reading patents to drafting entire contracts.

Seeing AI empowering so much efficiency for lawyers, Husch Blackwell is working with Microsoft to increase access for all staff. “Everyone is using these solutions,” says Helms. “Our tools have really good integration at all levels, and we hear from everyone how much they love using them. AI is really becoming that thought partner that will help legal workers succeed.”

Epiq is a global technology-enabled services leader to law firms, corporations, financial institutions, and government agencies. With almost 8,000 associates and operations worldwide, Epiq offers solutions for large-scale and complex client matters such as class action lawsuits, mass torts, bankruptcies, eDiscovery, and more. The company has a long track record of successfully managing highly visible litigation, regulatory, and compliance projects.

For Epiq, handling large class action lawsuits on behalf of major corporations often involves tens of thousands of claimants. This can generate huge spikes in volume to Epiq’s call center, often resulting in long wait times.   

To better manage this traffic, Epiq has developed AI-driven agents using Microsoft Copilot Studio. The agents use generative answers in Copilot Studio to address common questions around a class action suit, such as eligibility and how to file a claim. Claimants can also enter an existing file number to obtain personalized information directly from the agent. If claimants require more assistance, they can be automatically transferred to a live call center agent. 

At the time of development, a pre-built connector wasn’t available for the company’s specific call center platform, but the team was able to develop a custom handoff adaptor in Copilot Studio. The component was then added to a custom component collection, making it easier to reuse for AI agents developed for other class action suits. 

The Copilot Studio project quickly met expectations, with one AI agent successfully able to handle almost 50,000 messages for one of Epiq’s largest class action cases. 

To provide even greater support, the team is testing an autonomous agent which can answer questions that customers submit over email. The agent scans a general inbox, emails responses, and can even send follow-up emails. Customer emails that require further attention are automatically routed to another mailbox managed by employees. 

Copilot Studio for IT support 

Epiq is also using Copilot Studio to streamline internal operations. 

The company’s latest AI agent “Eva” provides a wide range of IT support services for employees. The agent makes it easier to look up travel and HR policies and other corporate information stored in Dataverse and SharePoint. Connectivity to Service Now, Epiq’s IT support system, enables employees to open helpdesk tickets and quickly check on their status. 

With Microsoft Entra integration, Eva streamlines access to Verkada, the company’s security software, for quicker access to building locations. Eva can also be used to create and modify distribution groups in Microsoft Exchange and create channels in Microsoft Teams. 

“With Microsoft Copilot Studio, we have developed an AI agent that can handle an amazingly wide range of IT requests from employees,” said Jordan Bardwell, Manager, Rapid Development and Innovation at Epiq. The plan is to add even more capabilities in the future, including integration to Workday and Okta.

Power Platform for onboarding automation

Along with Copilot Studio, Epiq is effectively leveraging other parts of Power Platform to drive its enterprise-wide applications. A good example of this is the company’s ‘Launchpad’ onboarding solution. 

Launchpad is delivering game-changing benefits, saving Epiq approximately 2,000 hours of work each month and more than USD$500,000 annually in associated costs. “It used to take week or more to onboard an employee. With our automated system, that same process takes just a few days,” Bardwell said.

As a project-driven organization, Epiq is often required to build teams in a hurry. That can be hard to do with a very small IT team. Launchpad was developed to help automate many aspects of the onboarding process, including ordering and tracking of laptops, provisioning of Outlook accounts, and managing of employee documentation. The system can also be used to automatically compile and report on laptop inventory, making it much easier to budget for laptop refresh cycles.

Power Apps provides the user interfaces and orchestration logic, with more than a dozen apps supporting different roles and processes. Power Automate manages the complex workflows and integration points with HR, IT, and other systems. Pre-built connectors integrate the system with the company’s Workday and ServiceNow systems. All onboarding data is recorded in Dataverse, which makes it easier to set up multiple access points to check this data. There’s an AI agent for administrators, a Power BI dashboard for managers, and connectivity to Eva that managers can also use to check onboarding status. 

Launchpad also leverages other AI capabilities in Power Platform to address specific onboarding challenges. 

For example, to complete a form for hiring multiple employees, managers often copy and paste employee IDs from various third-party applications. The result was inconsistent formatting that required manual corrections. Using AI Builder in Power Automate along with Azure OpenAI, Epiq created a model that cleans up formatting of new employee submission forms and allows for more efficient onboarding at scale.

A coordinated development platform

Solutions like Eva and Launchpad are just a few of the hundreds of Power Platform solutions created across Epiq. Along with basic, personal productivity apps, citizen developers work closely with more experienced developers on advanced, mission critical applications. “Our business users often come up with the vision, while my team develops the architecture and provides governance,” Bardwell said. 

A Center of Excellence helps manage and maintain this increasingly active maker community. Epiq is also using Managed Environments, including pipelines in Power Platform to make it easier for users to apply ALM rigor to their Power Platform solutions. Meanwhile, Dataverse provides a centralized and protected store for both apps and agents, with enterprise grade security, compliance, and scalability. 

The system is driving well-coordinated development efforts across the company. As Bardwell said, “Power Platform is enabling really effective collaboration between the business and IT teams. And that is resulting in more effective solutions for our business.”

AI is revolutionizing the way businesses operate, accelerating outcomes, and streamlining internal processes. Jones Lang LaSalle (JLL), a leader in commercial-real-estate (CRE) services, is at the forefront of this technological transformation, using cutting-edge tools to enhance operations and decision making.

JLL recognized the challenge of disparate data in the CRE industry and aimed to help its clients collect, incorporate, and use data more effectively for informed business decisions. The company harnessed the power of Microsoft Azure and Azure AI Services to develop solutions that provide clients with accessible, practical insights.

Empowering global clients with 250 years of CRE expertise

Boasting more than two centuries of industry experience, JLL supports occupiers and investors with a comprehensive suite of services, including portfolio and workplace management, leasing, buying, selling, and debt and equity management. Working with Azure Databricks, JLL aims to provide cleaner data to help real estate clients track trends and unique business challenges that might affect their workplace experience, facility management, and sustainability goals.

Recognizing a significant challenge in the CRE industry—collecting and analyzing diverse data—JLL sought to develop technology that would help clients across various industries gather standardized data efficiently. “CRE data is different from what many other companies deal with,” says Yao Morin, Chief Technology Officer at JLL. “In our world, we have a wide-data problem, not a big-data problem. It’s usually dirty data as much of it is generated manually, but you really have to understand the nature of the data to use it.”

JLL collaborated with Microsoft partner Databricks and Microsoft to design a secure, compliant solution that addresses this challenge.

Creating a solution to accelerate data aggregation and insight discovery with Azure

A long-term Microsoft customer, JLL benefited from Microsoft’s early investment in AI. JLL has partnered with Databricks since 2019 in storing and gleaning insights from vast amounts of data. “Databricks is proud to collaborate with the JLL team and Microsoft to drive transformative outcomes in real estate,” says Chris Camino, Vice President and General Manager, Enterprise Sales, at Databricks. “Together, JLL, Databricks, and Microsoft are empowering real estate professionals with AI-driven insights that optimize portfolios and enhance sustainability for clients worldwide.”

This partnership facilitated the decision to move forward with Azure. “In the AI revolution, Microsoft and Databricks have been the fastest to figure out how to unlock business value out of technology,” says Srihari Kumar, Chief Product Officer, Insights and Data, at JLL. “Azure has been a leader on the cloud front and provides the full stack, from the infrastructure to the platform to the AI, streamlining implementation and delivery.”

JLL aimed to aggregate data from multiple sources, providing a comprehensive real-time view to help clients make informed decisions. The company’s analytics solution, JLL Azara, built on Azure Databricks and JLL’s AI platform JLL Falcon, delivers vital insights into workplace performance management. JLL Azara turns JLL’s extensive CRE experience into a comprehensive CRE data model combined with the latest AI and business intelligence tools and Azure data storage capabilities. Using this solution, clients and their JLL partners can inquire about nearly any aspect of their portfolio to instantly uncover personalized insights, measure workplace performance, and gain the intelligence needed to develop and implement business strategies. Insights that once took months of data engineering and analytics development can now be done in minutes or seconds.

In 2024, JLL introduced new AI capabilities to JLL Azara to significantly optimize the cost, speed, and scale of delivering insights—thus offering a year’s worth of insights in one week. These capabilities include a conversational analysis experience to help clients gain insights through natural language queries. “It can be daunting for some business users to log in to a sea of dashboards and try to find actionable insights,” says Kumar. “We help users unlock the value of their data by asking questions specific to their business to make better data-driven decisions.”

JLL’s corporate occupier clients are among the first to benefit from this enhanced data access and exploration. Each month, clients have asked an average of approximately 300 previously difficult questions and generated impactful insights. Collaborating with the JLL team, clients are measuring the number of new questions asked and answered, data-driven hypotheses validated or refuted, predictions delivered, anomalies detected, and data fields enriched—all from straightforward natural language inquiries.

Cutting costs by millions and making 100% of data accessible for CRE clients

Since deploying JLL Azara powered by JLL Falcon, JLL has helped clients discover the root causes for challenges faster, meet business goals, and save research time. “Now, you can get insights instantly and at a much lower cost,” says Sharad Rastogi, CEO of Work Dynamics Technology at JLL. “It used to be that 70% of the data we had was not accessible, but now all of the data is accessible.”

Companies can use this readily available information to create a better workplace experience. JLL Azara has helped companies track facility management trends and challenges so they can proactively address them to reduce costs and improve administration practices. With personalized intelligence, JLL clients can see exactly where to focus their real estate efforts to meet efficiency challenges and pursue sustainability goals. In some cases, clients are revealing opportunities to save millions of dollars on portfolios and employee costs by empowering their teams with broad access and unencumbered exploration of data.

“Our philosophy is to create a wow experience that people didn’t imagine was possible before,” says Rastogi. “Democratizing access to advanced insights through a simple user experience does just that for business users—they are amazed at the speed and quality of analytics that JLL Azara provides them.”

Empowering CRE clients to work faster and more effectively in a data-driven future

JLL is now seeking to aggregate data in real time so that clients can make decisions and take action immediately. “We are at the beginning,” says Kumar. “We are looking to have more intelligent AI agents working alongside CRE agents, looking around the corners and alerting them on things to watch for.”

JLL will continue to democratize data using advanced tools like agentic AI. “We are on a mission to transform CRE with technology, and AI and generative AI are the most powerful tools we have seen to help in the transformation,” says Rastogi. “It’s all about how to operate more effectively in a dynamic world and offer a better experience for our clients and their employees so they can meet their biggest goals.”

Breathing new life into healthcare through AI observability and cloud infrastructure

Connecting 34 hospitals, 400 clinics, and more than 66,000 caregivers, Intermountain Health has a rich history of providing quality, sustainable, and affordable healthcare to millions of people. The Salt Lake City–based healthcare system supports patients and communities in Utah, Idaho, Nevada, Colorado, Montana, and Wyoming with best-in-class care at every stage of life. It has positioned technology, including AI and machine learning, at the forefront of its business model to streamline operations, distill data, scale patient communications, and achieve healthcare breakthroughs more efficiently.

In its pursuit to reimagine care, Intermountain prioritizes and champions responsible AI. For transparency, fairness, and reliability, responsible AI governance committees review both externally and internally developed AI solutions. Intermountain also expanded an enterprise AI and data science group, born out of its population health team, to accelerate the improvement of patient care with innovative AI and machine learning products.

AI observability is central to Intermountain’s commitments and is built into every stage of the healthcare pipeline. Having insight into the performance and fairness of AI products not only supports current and future planning and service reliability but also helps build trust with patients and clinical workers, making technology initiatives more transparent and effective. By implementing Arize Al for LLM evaluation and AI observability, Intermountain can proactively monitor and mitigate the impact of AI performance issues.

Inspired by the work of pioneering doctors in its network, including those who established early electronic medical records systems and clinical quality improvement programs, Intermountain is reducing caregiver burnout, streamlining clinical operations, and improving patient care every day. To sustain this success and develop scalable and reliable use cases, it wanted to combine AI, language models, and advanced algorithms with cloud infrastructure. By running its AI infrastructure on Microsoft Azure, Intermountain has done that.

Committing to trustworthy AI and delivering better performance, consistent patient outcomes

Intermountain first gained interest in AI and machine learning as potential solutions for complex, specialized health industry challenges, particularly patient outcome improvement and healthcare affordability. When Intermountain’s Digital Technology Services (DTS) caregivers started to develop, accelerate, and interweave the system’s cloud and AI strategies, the goal was to have caregivers use Azure Databricks and Arize, alongside Azure OpenAI Service and Azure API Management services, to deploy new, advanced, and custom AI models quickly and responsibly with clear observability. “You can deploy something very quickly but forget to enable machine learning observability. Suddenly you have a great product, but you don’t know its performance and whether it’s helping or harming patients,” explains Mark Nielsen, Senior Machine Learning Operations Engineer at Intermountain Health. “The cloud infrastructure that we built with Azure and Arize AI has been helpful in meeting both of those needs, and we’ve been able to speed up our deployment process while keeping our commitment to responsible AI.”

Always fine-tuning and improving, one of Intermountain’s goals is to have enough trust from caregivers that they start to reap the reward of improving patient outcomes, in addition to clinical caregivers spending less time at home documenting their visits. On the DTS side, engineers are already able to spin up or audit code quickly without feeling like they need to spend time outside work hours getting things done.

Using AI and cloud tools as a force multiplier in an innovation-led culture

With Azure OpenAI, Intermountain caregivers take advantage of new AI language models as they evolve and build or adapt custom models for maximum benefit. They use Azure Databricks and API Management to develop and deploy AI models and cloud resources with minimal administrative effort and very securely use industry-standard models at scale. “We have a culture of continuous improvement and mission-driven technical caregivers who help us maintain our level of innovation, efficiency, and excellence,” says Nielsen. “Easily scalable cloud tools become a force multiplier by making it simple to be agile, iterate, and improve.”

Given its focus on custom model development, Intermountain set up automated continuous integration and continuous delivery processes using GitHub Actions for Azure to empower data scientists and machine learning engineers to make quick checks and help ensure a minimum level of accuracy as they do development work. “If we’re creating a model and want at least 80% accuracy and see it performs lower than that, we know we need to iterate and try to improve it in a different way,” explains Nielsen. “These automated checks help us implement responsible models.”

To further support its responsible AI pillars and progress, Intermountain brought its technology partner Arize on board by configuring and installing its AI observability and large language model evaluation solution in the Azure environment. On top of monitoring its Azure OpenAI models, Intermountain DTS caregivers use the Arize platform to help them identify the root causes of poor performance and bias to make proactive, versus solely reactive, updates.

Saving hours of work and improving efficiency

As Intermountain continues to enhance and expand its Azure environment, it’s saving time and effort while extending its clinical impact. “Making Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Copilot available to all our caregivers, whether they’re clinical or engineers, helped us save an estimated 4,300 hours of work last year,” says Nielsen—and these numbers continue to grow.

For doctors and caregivers, spending less time on documentation is a major win. They can use the saved time to focus on complex clinical problems and improving patient experiences. As its next step, Intermountain is currently collaborating with Microsoft and several other leading healthcare organizations on enabling citizen development of personalized AI agents to automate more complex manual processes. This includes applications that allow nurses to focus less on paperwork and more on patients.

Likewise, with the help of Azure and Arize AI, Intermountain DTS caregivers don’t have to build and manage AI workloads themselves, saving 40 hours of work per quarter for each AI product. “As you get multiple AI products into production, those savings really start to grow,” shares Nielsen. “AI models that previously took months to deploy can be deployed in weeks, and in some cases, days.”

Notably, doctors and data scientists are no longer expected to become experts in the other’s field of study. Additionally, before moving to the cloud, Intermountain didn’t have dedicated Linux administrators on hand who were familiar with the tools and software required for machine learning computation. When necessary, data scientists had to set up their own systems, infrastructure, and tools needed to deploy AI without formal training. “Moving to Azure allows us to use these AI systems, solutions, and cloud tools without needing to be a jack-of-all-trades,” explains Nielsen. “We’re now able to be more efficient because we can stay within these prebuilt frameworks, such as Azure Databricks, to spin compute resources up and down really quickly and worry about less about tool administration.”

Caregivers and patients benefit from AI in action and plan for more

To date, Intermountain has used AI to support many parts of its operations, including the summarization of clinical notes and generation of responses to patient emails based on individual medical histories. An AI model was also used to identify high-risk patients with multiple comorbidities to whom care managers could reach out to help manage their doctor and specialist appointments, drug coordination, and medicinal interactions, with the goal of helping them be healthier while reducing the time, cost, and stress burden. Intermountain plans to continue using and experimenting with AI models to find new and innovative ways to respond to the ever-evolving complexity and rising costs of healthcare. It could soon begin reshaping precision healthcare with customized, data-backed treatment plans for patients based on their individual care needs.

Responsible AI will remain a cornerstone of Intermountain’s strategy as it plans for the future. This translates to the accountability of every caregiver and clinical worker to the patients they care for across every physical and digital touchpoint. Agentic and retrieval-augmented generation frameworks, among others, continue to grow and evolve, and Intermountain wants to grow with them by scaling quickly without causing undue harm. “We’re passionate about our responsible AI commitments, and tools like Azure and Arize AI will help us deploy responsible AI solutions that can be scaled quickly,” concludes Nielsen.

Newman’s Own is in the highly competitive food industry, making an array of products, from sauces to snacks, drinks to dog treats. The company continues Paul Newman’s founding commitment to “give it all away,” with 100% of its profits going to Newman’s Own Foundation, whose mission is to nourish and transform the lives of children who face adversity. Newman’s Own is seeking new ways to improve employee productivity and reduce costs. Microsoft 365 Copilot is a critical part of how it runs a lean, efficient organization to maximize its profits. “We need to keep growing, operating efficiently, and staying relevant to consumers and their needs,” says David Best, President and CEO of Newman’s Own. “Having greater insight into what consumers want today and tomorrow is crucial to our success.”

How Newman’s Own competes in a crowded market

Copilot is an integral part of the daily operations of Newman’s Own; many employees, including Best, use it every day. He explains how important it is to use technology to the company’s advantage. “Using Copilot and AI to its fullest potential so we can be smarter than our competition is a key piece of our recipe for success,” says Best. Newman’s Own is quickly seeing a tremendous impact, with increases in creativity, effectiveness, and efficiency driving its business forward.

The marketing team has been able to triple the number of campaigns they run in a month and rely on Copilot to stir up their creativity. “Before, a brief might take three hours to complete. With Copilot, I can have an outline in 30 minutes to an hour as a starting point, and I can stay focused on key messages and KPIs,” says Riley McCarthy, Social Media Manager at Newman’s Own. With social trends that can change in a moment, she uses Copilot to help put the Newman’s Own spin on things. “I can do several campaigns in a month now because I have more time to come up with more ideas, which matters because we are getting more eyeballs on us,” says McCarthy. 

Copilot is an invaluable coworker 

Copilot is seen as an additional coworker on the team. McCarthy shares how Copilot helps her flesh out ideas and get past a creative block, like a colleague she would brainstorm with to build on ideas. 

Jennifer Millones, Chief Legal Officer at Newman’s Own, reinforces how valuable Copilot is, explaining, “Copilot is my junior associate. I use it to handle legal questions and gather citations, which accelerates my ability to support the company.” It also helps her by cutting unnecessary legalese out of contract templates, making them easier to use. Millones shares how Copilot helps her craft company-wide emails that are more approachable, with less “lawyer language” that may be intimidating.  

 The Logistics and Transportation team receives many industry publications every day. Sherry Linson, Director at Newman’s Own, says, “I have Copilot summarize each one; it only takes 30 minutes when it used to take me all morning. With these summaries, I quickly discover ways to keep costs down and introduce new initiatives.” Linson adds, “It’s my information database. My creativity platform. A jumping point. All at my fingertips.”

Finding new ways to be more productive with limited resources is a core principle for Newman’s Own, because this affects the bottom line. Bruce Wallace, Chief People Officer at Newman’s Own, says, “Giving our people the best possible tools is important so they can be successful because that drives everything we do, supporting our ability to transform children’s lives, and leads to everyone feeling a sense of fulfillment.” 


McCarthy shared how Copilot is making a difference with her dyslexia. “I have confidence whatever I’m writing—whether to an executive or posts on social media—it will be spelled correctly, with the proper grammar, using Copilot.” 

Copilot saves Newman’s Own both time and money 

Best reinforces how Copilot is a key part of the company’s money-saving plans because the team is gaining time and productivity efficiencies. Copilot is an integral part of how Newman’s Own has been able to give even more to help children in need. Best concludes, “Nothing could be better than helping more kids, and that’s what Copilot allows us to do.”  

Newman’s Own doesn’t have the scale of some of its competitors, so it’s essential for employees to be able to work smarter, not harder. Best believes Copilot will continue to take the company to the next level of growth and have greater impact toward its mission.

Bruce Wallace, Chief People Officer, shares his perspective on empowering employees with Copilot

After 13 years in Financial Services, I made the leap to Newman’s Own. It’s as different and rewarding as you can imagine. ​

Our mission of helping kids who face adversity really resonates with me, and being here fulfills me in ways I didn’t expect. I get to help the people so they can help more people.​

​One of the biggest challenges in the nonprofit sector is making sure our team has the best tools to do their jobs. We run extremely lean.​ ​With Microsoft Copilot, we’ve supercharged every person. It’s an absolute game changer for us. ​

​Copilot helps our finance team move quickly from data to insights, so they can make sure every dollar is spent wisely. Our marketing team can now pinpoint the best audience at the right time, which ​has really boosted our outreach. And our legal officer now has Copilot acting like a junior associate, making their workload much more manageable.​

​For me, the real value of Copilot is in empowering our employees. By giving them the latest technology, we’re not only boosting their productivity but also showing them that their work is valued and supported. This has a huge impact on employee engagement and retention. When our team feels invested in, they’re more committed to our mission, and that ultimately helps us make a bigger difference in the lives of the kids we serve. ​

​It’s hard to believe a piece of technology has this kind of human impact. But it does.​

T-Mobile operates the second largest wireless network in the United States, serving over 130 million customers. The company has consistently ranked highest among major wireless carriers for retail-store satisfaction for six consecutive years. One reason for this success is that T-Mobile is continually improving its retail operations, including new tools for customer service representatives (CSRs). Much of this work is being done using Microsoft Power Platform. 

T-Mobile has been developing enterprise-wide solutions on Power Platform for years. The company’s Orbit app, for example, was developed to streamline project planning and go-to-market activities and is saving the company 97,000 hours and over $4M USD in costs every year. An acquisition of Power App premium licenses has paved the way for even more complex solutions, including widespread use of Dataverse for greater scalability of enterprise-wide apps. 

With its latest Power Platform tool for retail, the company focused on better access to promotional information. This data includes new devices, discounts, and trade-in offers currently available to customers. Previously, a daily report was sent to CSRs with the latest updates. However, the document had become increasingly complex and difficult to search. The retail group wanted to streamline that process – with one, integrated application.  

The group had initially looked at a custom-coded option - but was told that it would take over nine months to complete. That’s when they decided to check in with the Power Platform team at T-Mobile. “We took a look at the requirements and realized that the same solution could be developed in a less than week with Power Platform,” says Brian Hodel, Principal Developer for Power Platform at T-Mobile.

Power Apps for integrated data access

Work quickly began on an app that the company calls PromoGenius.

Using Power Apps, the UI was designed with a series of drop-down menus to minimize the time that a CSR spends entering a query. “Power Apps enabled us to a create an interface that’s easy to work with—even during a live conversation with a customer,” says Hodel. The app runs on iPads which CSRs carry with them on the retail floor and can also be accessed online by call center representatives. Results from a query are displayed in a presentation format that can be shared directly with customers. 

Along with all the data from the original promotions report, the app also integrates with other systems to provide additional information, such as trade-in values. Previously, a rep would have to check multiples system for this data. Now, it can be all accessed and assembled in one app in a matter of seconds.

As Hodel says, “Our investment in Power Apps premium licenses is enabling us to build advanced capabilities into frontline solutions that are delivering real business value to our retail team.”

Copilot Studio for better search 

While the app successfully streamlined access to internal data sources, customer service representatives still had one additional challenge: gathering technical details on devices, which often involved going directly to the device manufacturers’ web sites. This was often an equally time-consuming task - especially if the customer wanted to compare products across multiple sites.  

Power Platform has helped address this challenge. Using Microsoft Copilot Studio, an AI-driven agent was developed that connects to over 20 device manufacturers’ web sites and assembles product information instantly and automatically. 

The agent, which is embedded directly in the app, is driven by generative answers in Copilot Studio, enabling a CSR to ask deep technical questions using natural language queries. This not only pulls up relevant technical details faster but in direct context of a customer’s question. Better yet, with multi-turn capabilities, the agent can understand a question in the context of previous questions. “Our reps are using our new agent in Copilot Studio to gather product information in a fraction of the time of a manual search,” says Hodel. 

The agent has proven to be particularly useful for product comparisons, where it not only gathers the data but formats it into clear, comparison tables that can be presented to a customer.

Strong results 

The PromoGenius app was rolled out to all T-Mobile retails locations across the United States. Together with the new AI agent, the PromoGenius app has become the second most used Power Apps application in the company, with over 83,000 unique users and 500,000 launches a month. 

And it’s not just usage metrics that has made PromoGenius a success at T-Mobile. PromoGenius is driving more effective sales experiences overall. Previously, to gather details on a product question, CSRs would often have to leave a customer conversation, check data resources, and then return with the answer. Now, product information can be sourced instantaneously, with no interruptions.

Exciting enhancements 

Work continues to make PromoGenius even better. For example, the PDF in function in Power Apps will soon enable CSRs to generate a PDF reports of data sourced for a customer and have it sent automatically to a customer via email using a Power Automate flow. Adding voice capabilities to the AI agent will enable even faster access to data. 

There are plans to customize the UI, depending on a user’s preferences. Some prefer less information up front, for example, with high-level details organized in a grid view. “What we particularly like about canvas apps in Power Apps is that we can create different views to optimize the way different people use and consume data,” says Hodel. 

Updates to the data layer are also in the works. Currently, data is drawn from the company’s Oracle systems into SQL Server before it is moved into Dataverse. Now, the plan is to create a direct connection between Dataverse and the source system using the pre-built connectors available with Power Platform. 

“Connecting our systems directly to Dataverse will provide us with greater accuracy, efficiency, and performance – without sacrificing security,” says Hodel. He also explains how the new architecture will provide an additional layer of system redundancy. “With a direct a pipeline into Dataverse, we don’t have to worry about gateway issues or SQL going down. It just works. That’s especially important at the retail level where 100% uptime is so important.” 

More AI agents planned 

Based on the success of the PromoGenius AI agent at T-Mobile, it’s not surprising that new AI agents are planned for both new and existing Power Platform solutions across the company. 

Next up: an AI agent for the Orbit app which will be used for a wide range of functions, including summarizing of long text fields within the app; faster, more contextual search, and more. With Copilot Studio, the team will be able to easily re-purpose components of the PromoGenius agent, as well as prompts from other Power Platform solutions.   

As Hodel says, “One of the big benefits for us of Power Platform is that it all works together so seamlessly. That’s making it even easier to leverage the benefits of AI and add it to applications that have a real impact on our business.”

Story Content:
Montgomery County, Maryland, wanted to offer more accessible and convenient services to its constituents. The county is dedicated to leading the charge in revolutionizing public service with cutting-edge AI technology, so, in 2024, it used Microsoft Azure to expand its AI chatbot and promote accessibility and convenience.

Harnessing AI to enhance services for more than 1 million Montgomery County constituents

The government of Montgomery County—located just outside Washington, DC, and the most populous county in the US state of Maryland—is dedicated to fostering equity, inclusivity, and opportunity for its more than 1 million constituents. For more than two decades, the county has harnessed innovative technology to provide public services, such as transportation, infrastructure maintenance, and waste removal, and support safety, education, and climate action. “Our strategy is wrapped around this idea of serving our internal employees so that they can then serve our constituents better,” says Shayna Taqi, Chief Change Officer at Montgomery County. Montgomery County’s technology-first approach to public services has earned multiple awards over two decades, including a Top Digital County award and a Tech Savvy designation.

During COVID-19, Montgomery County faced an influx of vaccine and other pandemic-related inquiries, which strained its 311 hotline and call center. To alleviate this, the county launched Monty, an AI chatbot, to bolster its 311 services. The solution, built in five days with technical support from Microsoft partner Zammo.ai, an independent software vendor, reduced call center wait times and helped agents focus on the most complex questions. However, the chatbot only covered 20 topics, and usage declined as vaccines became more readily available, leading to Monty’s retirement.

This experience highlighted the transformative potential of generative AI for enhancing the constituent experience. Recognizing that expanding Monty's capabilities to cover more than 3,000 topics would significantly improve constituent services, the county decided to move forward despite challenges and concerns around AI hallucinating—presenting false or misleading information as fact. To address these issues, Montgomery County partnered with Microsoft and Zammo.ai to develop Monty 2.0, a generative AI solution capable of maintaining context in conversations.

“We often rely on things to be perfect to be able to present them to the public,” says Skyler Grubbs, Change Management Manager at Montgomery County. “Our team, throughout this exercise, has really done a good job of not promising perfection and instead promising continuous improvement alongside learning with our constituents and testing with them.”

Using generative AI to answer questions about 3,000 topics in 140 languages

Over the course of 10 months, Montgomery County expanded its use of the Zammo.ai software to build the expanded Monty 2.0 chatbot using Azure OpenAI Service, which helps developers create custom generative AI solutions. This updated model uses Azure AI Search, which delivers a knowledge retrieval system built for advanced retrieval augmented generation. It instantly and exclusively accesses Montgomery County’s knowledge base and selects relevant content to respond to queries without sourcing misleading information from the internet. Monty 2.0 also harnesses Zammo.ai’s software as a service solution to boost the front-end user experience through automatic translation into 140 languages and improved multi-turn conversations.

Before deploying Monty 2.0 to the public, the IT team worked closely with Microsoft and the Zammo.ai customer success team to meticulously develop the model’s new framework and reduce hallucinations. During a seven-month beta phase that began in March 2024, the team collected feedback from a constituent focus group and made improvements to the knowledge base and architecture. Montgomery County also focused on training employees to use generative AI safely and effectively. “As a government organization, we need to be very careful about what information we’re putting out to the public,” says Michael Zanfardino, Change Management Specialist at Montgomery County. “When we finally reduced the hallucinations, I knew we had gold—a good product that would really help our constituents.”

When Monty 2.0 fully launched in late 2024, it supported more than 3,000 topics—a hundredfold increase from the previous iteration. The chatbot now provides public health guidelines, emergency notifications, and information about local services and regulations—all in the language that is most comfortable for each constituent. And because the model was trained on Montgomery County’s geographic information system, Monty 2.0 can even provide personalized responses based on a user’s address, such as trash pickup days and local voting precincts.

Since its beta deployment, Monty 2.0 has facilitated more than 20,000 constituent conversations, achieving a 50% customer satisfaction rate and reducing unanswered queries from 35%–45% to just 10%–15%. The chatbot's services continue to improve based on learnings from the Zammo.ai conversation analytics and click-to-add constituent feedback, such as thumbs-up and one- to five-star ratings, in the conversational experiences. Now, the IT team consistently makes enhancements to Monty 2.0’s prompts and modeling. The chatbot has received several positive reviews, with one constituent sharing that Monty 2.0 was “quick, accurate, and gave me exactly the information I needed to report a downed tree.”

“We wanted to get our constituents’ stamp of approval before we went live, and we want to continue collecting and evaluating their feedback on a daily basis,” says Grubbs. “We’re giving people the opportunity to tell us what their experience with Monty 2.0 is like and how they would like to see it change.”

Scaling AI services across Montgomery County

Montgomery County’s bold leadership in generative AI has greatly enhanced the experience of its constituents and employees. By working side by side with Microsoft and Zammo.ai, Montgomery County’s IT team also expanded its AI knowledge, which will empower future innovations. “It was amazing to see how, even though we weren’t formally trained in this, we could rally together to learn, take risks, listen, and iterate,” says Grubbs. “It wouldn’t have been possible without the strong partnerships we have with Microsoft and Zammo.ai.”

Moving forward, Montgomery County plans to expand its omnichannel AI strategy, broaden customer service topic areas, and deploy Monty 2.0 in other areas of the county’s website. These improvements will drive internal efficiency and enhance the support Montgomery County provides to its constituents. Thanks to its positive experience with building and rolling out Monty 2.0, the county expects several more departments to welcome the adoption of AI models across the organization.

“We generated so much excitement around this project that we have many departments asking for their own chatbots,” says Taqi. “We’re excited to see how we can use similar technology to improve some of our customer service areas. The better customer service we can provide, the more successful we are.”
