In 2023, Cyclone Freddy dropped six months of rainfall in just six days, devastating Malawi. Over the next month, the storm took lives and destroyed livelihoods. The relentless deluge caused disease in farmers’ fields, particularly affecting the staple soya crop. “Our farmers did not know what to do. Some harvested literally nothing,” remembers Bhahati Zimba, a farmer and Senior Program Officer at Opportunity International.

Worldwide, most of the 659 million people living on less than $2.15 a day are smallholder farmers. Opportunity International develops innovative financial solutions and delivers agricultural support to empower the world’s most vulnerable communities to build sustainable livelihoods.  

“Opportunity has always been an innovator, developing new ways to assist people to lift themselves out of poverty,” says Greg Nelson, Chief Technology Officer at Opportunity International. “We bring the latest and greatest ideas to our mission, and that new chapter is using generative AI.”

Opportunity collaborated with AIS Partners and Artefact to develop a Microsoft Azure-based AI solution that immediately and accurately answers farmers’ questions in Malawi. Called Ulangizi AI, the chatbot solution provides authoritative information in English and Chichewa by text and voice. Ulangizi, which means “advisor” in Chichewa, is using responsibly developed AI to strengthen Opportunity’s network of farm support agents (FSAs), spread sustainable agriculture practices, and help more farmers overcome extreme poverty. 

“With Ulangizi, generative AI brings knowledge, power, and agency to people, even if they have limited educational opportunity or literacy,” Nelson says. “AI is a new enabler for supporting individuals who are the most excluded, so we can end extreme poverty in our lifetime.”

Designing human-centered AI

In alignment with the responsible AI principles of inclusiveness and human-centered design, Opportunity conducted a series of interviews with farmers and FSAs in the wake of Cyclone Freddy. They learned about farmers’ most pressing challenges, including the difficulty they faced in getting timely, reliable agricultural advice. Opportunity leaders tested generative AI’s ability to answer common farming questions. 

One FSA who worked on this demo was amazed. “When can I have this?” asked Anna Chimalizeni, who lost her harvest during the cyclone. “If I had this, I could have saved my crop.”

After going through development, pilots, user feedback, and refinement, Ulangizi AI was built as an open platform using Azure, Azure AI services, and other services. By using WhatsApp, one of the most widely used communications tools in the country, the generative AI solution is readily accessible and familiar to individuals with limited digital literacy. It also works in rural areas without broadband coverage. 

Based in its Azure OpenAI back end, the solution receives a user’s text or audio prompt from WhatsApp. Azure AI speech-to-text services decode voice messages, while machine translation services convert prompts into English and answers back into Chichewa or Nyanja. The chatbot draws on Malawian Ministry of Agriculture information stored in an Azure database, then large language models (LLMs) generate answers to user questions in a conversational tone. Ulangizi AI can even analyze photos to help farmers answer questions about crops and livestock, though this feature is still being fine-tuned. 

Opportunity trained its hundreds of FSAs and government outreach workers to be intermediaries between the technology and the 100,000 households they support. This approach ensures even farmers without a mobile phone can access valuable information, and it reduces risks involved in using a generative AI solution. 

FSAs are knowledgeable about the type of content Ulangizi AI needs (such as soil type) and how to craft prompts for the most helpful answers. Trusted as the most successful farmers in their communities, FSAs help growers apply Ulangizi AI recommendations to their unique circumstances.  

Zimba says, “Ulangizi AI is a farmer advisor in our pocket.”

Educating farmers for sustainable agriculture

Global instability disproportionately affects people who are poor and can worsen the impacts of poverty, especially for people who depend on the land for their livelihood. Opportunity is using generative AI to help farmers in Malawi adapt to more severe and unpredictable weather patterns.

FSAs help farmers ask Ulangizi AI for recommendations on crops and animals better suited to today’s conditions. For example, choosing drought-resistant varieties helps families become more resilient during dry spells. “For the first time, farmers have access to authoritative, accurate content that helps them build sustainable livelihoods,” Nelson says.

Ulangizi AI also empowers farmers to solve problems faster. It could have helped address the moisture-caused disease that devastated soya crops during Cyclone Freddy, for example. The generative AI chatbot surfaces answers in mere seconds, rather than the several days it might take for an FSA to visit a farm, travel to a Ministry of Agriculture extension outpost, and then bring the answer back to the farmer. 

Finally, FSAs are spreading sustainable farming practices. With the support of Ulangizi AI and Opportunity training, they teach farmers to regenerate soil through crop rotation, choose plants to fix nutrients in the soil, and more—all to steward the land for generations of farming families. 

Nelson says, “By preparing smallholder farmers, who are some of the most vulnerable people on the planet, we can strengthen the world’s food supply and help farmers become more resilient in the face of growing instability.”

Growing farmers’ incomes

Most smallholder farmers produce a fraction of their potential yields, limiting their financial mobility. Ulangizi AI is helping farmers sow and care for the right crops, leading to more bountiful harvests. Farmers then have the capital to plant more, increase their herds, and hire laborers, improving the local economy for the entire community. “When they approach farming as a business, their lives can transform,” Zimba says.

The generative AI chatbot gives detailed guidance, such as how much seed to buy for a farmer’s acreage. It also integrates sources such as weather forecasts and market data so farmers know when to water, harvest, and sell crops for the greatest profit. This circumstance-specific content helps farmers reduce costs and free up time to learn new skills or start another business, Zimba says. 

Extra income can help families build a better life. “We use the money for things like paying school fees, hiring labor in peak periods, and taking care of our children and our homes,” Chimalizeni says.

Reaching more growers

About 80% of Malawi’s population are smallholder farmers, but Opportunity does not currently have the capacity to support all of them. Technological innovation such as Ulangizi AI is expanding the nonprofit’s reach. 

The chatbot’s speed and ease of use eliminates most of the need for FSAs to travel to agricultural extension offices. They can then spend more time with the families they serve and welcome more farmers into the program. 

Opportunity anticipates that investments in AI will cut the cost of training new FSAs by more than two-thirds, making it financially feasible to scale up its FSA program. Ulangizi AI will bring new FSAs up to speed faster, empowering them with vetted information and leading to even better outcomes for millions of Malawian farmers. 

Ulangizi AI is just the beginning of how Opportunity will leverage technology for life-changing transformation, Nelson says. The nonprofit is developing a suite of AI-powered solutions to support agriculture, education, and upward mobility in Malawi, Kenya, Ghana, and beyond. 

“Generative AI opens up information access like we’ve never seen,” Nelson says. “By applying this technology at scale, we’re going to help hundreds of millions of people. The faster we can go, the more people we can reach.”

Textron Aviation, a Textron Inc. company, is the producer of more than half of all general aviation aircraft flying today, including the iconic brands Cessna and Beechcraft. Its mission is to inspire the journey of flight for its customers located in more than 170 countries. For nearly 100 years, Textron Aviation has been committed to maintaining the highest standards of aircraft service that its customers expect.

To advance its mission, Textron Aviation has established 20 global service centers through a network staffed with nearly 3,000 employees. Customers have direct access to a team of expert service representatives offering maintenance and inspections, parts and repairs, avionic upgrades, equipment installations, refurbishments, and other specialized services. To ensure the highest level of service, maintaining more than 50 different aircraft models requires aircraft maintenance technicians (AMTs) to query more than 60,000 pages of documentation to get the detailed, accurate technical instructions they need. Although the information is available, it is often time-consuming to locate the specific details needed.

Increasing efficiencies with generative AI 

“We presented the challenge to Microsoft, emphasizing the need to provide technicians with quicker access to the information they need,” explains Brian Adams, Vice President of Aftermarket Innovation at Textron Aviation.

Textron Aviation saw a fit with generative AI to improve the AMT experience and reduce their upskilling time. It chose Microsoft to help ensure compliance with Textron Aviation’s data access and system policies and processes. 

“We weren’t just learning about generative AI for Textron Aviation,” says Adams. “We were learning for the whole enterprise, and that’s what steered us to Microsoft.”

Delivering fast, accurate, concise answers to technicians    

Textron Aviation selected Microsoft Cloud for Manufacturing to build and deploy a generative AI solution that would serve as a quick, efficient one-stop shop for data its mechanics need. Using Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service, the company created TAMI—the Textron Aviation Maintenance Intelligence assistant. TAMI has three layers: a chat layer that AMTs interact with, a middle layer that delivers decisions from key information stored in Azure, and a workflow ingestion sublayer that moves the data into a cognitive search location for TAMI to read.  

“TAMI quickly digests all of that data with accurate, concise answers for our AMTs,” says Adams. “We found Azure OpenAI Service provides capabilities beyond our traditional experiences, especially the ability for our mechanics to interact with TAMI using natural language—even multiple languages—and that became a real win for us.” 

Sean Wiles, an AMT using the Microsoft solution daily, adds, “As mechanics, there are many tools we rely on every day—a screwdriver and a 9/16 wrench. TAMI is now an added tool in our toolbox.​” 

​Reducing aircraft time under maintenance 

The company’s AMTs report that using TAMI saves time and helps to significantly improve workforce training and upskilling. Troubleshooting that previously took up to 20 minutes can now be accomplished in one to two minutes. The company is minimizing the time that aircraft are under maintenance, which ultimately translates to happier customers. Textron Aviation is now looking at ways to make use of generative AI throughout its manufacturing divisions.  

“TAMI is proving to be a competitive advantage for our service centers and our brand,” says Adams. “The success story of TAMI has leaders across the company talking about how we can deploy more Microsoft AI solutions—and the excitement around that is incredible.”

Biopharmaceutical solutions organization Syneos Health stands at the forefront of combining science and data to accelerate drug development, clinical trials, and commercialization for its pharmaceutical customers. Syneos Health provides services and solutions for all aspects of the drug development process to help get lifesaving therapies into the hands of patients and healthcare providers. The company is accelerating the adoption of generative AI to address the scale and complexity of data demands for its customers and clinical trials across the globe and for the pharmaceutical industry as a whole.

“In our clinical organization, at any given time, we’re conducting well over 500 clinical trials,” says Michael Brooks, Chief Operating Officer at Syneos Health. “If you look at just the last five years, we completed 300 studies. Over 190,000 subjects participated in those trials at over 9,000 research sites, and the trials that we’re conducting have significant complexity.”

Syneos Health analyzes large, complex data sets to advance pharmaceutical trials and bring new therapies to market. The company sees generative AI as one of the keys to helping its customers make quicker, more informed decisions. “We’ve evolved into a tech and data insights–enabled organization, where we use AI-driven insights to help our team members and our customers make really good decisions about the design, development, and commercialization of products,” says Brooks.

Incorporating generative AI into a cloud-based ecosystem in nine months

Syneos Health turned to trusted partner Microsoft to modernize the company’s analytical capabilities and optimize workflows with generative AI. The company had already migrated its data estate to the Microsoft Azure environment to incorporate traditional machine learning and quantitative data analytics. Syneos Health uses data storage and analytical products, including Azure Data Lake Storage and Azure Databricks, to securely manage its terabytes of data. What began as a discussion around fundamentally upgrading the company’s data platform has evolved in the last couple of years, and Syneos Health is now experiencing gains in efficiency, time savings, and raw capabilities.

Azure helps Syneos Health deliver scalable ingestion, transformation, machine learning operations, AI, and data quality capabilities across the company.

Syneos Health was eager to include generative AI capabilities in its existing Azure environment to streamline daily workflows, incorporate predictive modeling, and help manage the extensive documentation requirements common in the pharmaceutical industry. The company worked with Microsoft to create a data platform that incorporates Azure OpenAI Service, which helps Syneos Health to build its own generative AI apps.

The company deployed its new analytics solution after nine months of development with Microsoft and is systematically considering how generative AI can improve each step of its processes, from clinical trials to commercialization. “The scalable, practical solutions that we can use are helping both our clinical and commercialization teams become better and faster at what they do,” says Diana Cucos, President, Functional Service Provider 360 at Syneos Health. “That, in turn, not only reduces cost but also allows us to meet our goal: accelerating clinical trials.”

Reducing site-activation cycle by about 10% and empowering employees

The company’s use of generative AI showcases its potential to revolutionize the industry by addressing complex data demands and enhancing decision-making capabilities. Syneos Health is accelerating critical timelines, facilitating predictive forecasting, and empowering employees to find new ways to work. For example, selecting clinical trial sites was previously a painstaking, manual data collection process that took several months to complete. Using AI-driven insights, Syneos Health greatly accelerated this process, now generating an initial site list within approximately 24–48 hours and narrowing down the selection process to a few weeks. “In 2024 alone, we reduced our site-activation cycle time by upwards of 10%,” says Brooks. “Every day that we can accelerate development means more patients can get access to a therapy or potentially receive a lifesaving cure.”

As Syneos Health streamlines the site-selection process, its generative AI solutions are also improving predictive forecasting, alerting clinical trial teams to potential delays so they can take early steps to mitigate problems. The company used the technology to upgrade its forecasting system, so teams now have a more robust system to help them think about various scenarios and approaches to a clinical trial.

Employees at Syneos Health are finding new ways to work and engage with pharmaceutical customers, clinical sites, and patients. Employees are using generative AI–driven tools to walk customers through the implications of various scenarios in real time instead of having to schedule additional meetings. “We feel that AI has a great opportunity to drive more active and efficient engagement across the entire ecosystem that will result in less downtime, less reprocessing, and ultimately improved outcomes,” says Cucos.

Accelerating innovation in pharmaceuticals to deliver benefits to patients faster

These steps are only the beginning for Syneos Health. The company is excited to innovate with new applications to help its customers navigate the complexities of drug development, regulation, and commercialization. It sees enormous potential for generative AI to automate manual processes and help its teams of experts to focus on value-added tasks that ultimately benefit patients.

Syneos Health offers a blueprint for the pharmaceutical industry to harness generative AI and deliver new therapies to patients and healthcare providers more quickly. Its collaboration with Microsoft and adoption of innovative technologies are at the heart of the journey.

Driving growth for Heritage Grocers Group by modernizing its data lake

Heritage Grocers Group, a prominent figure in the retail sector, proudly operates across six states under the banners of Cardenas Markets, El Rancho Supermercado, Tony’s Fresh Market, and Los Altos Ranch Market. Specializing in catering to Hispanic communities, the group experienced rapid growth between 2022 and 2024, expanding its territory through strategic acquisitions. In an industry as dynamic and competitive as retail, meeting the diverse expectations of customers at each new location is paramount. “Understanding the unique purchasing preferences of the Texas customer compared to those of Tony’s in Chicago is crucial,” says Prabash Coswatte, Chief Operating Officer of Heritage Grocers Group. “The quicker we grasp this, the better we can cater to each community’s needs.”

To more efficiently gather, organize, and analyze vast amounts of point-of-sale (POS) data from varied enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems across its numerous outlets, Heritage Grocers Group forged a partnership with Adastra, a renowned global IT consultancy and Microsoft partner. The companies developed a scalable, robust solution aimed at achieving data consistency, ensuring high availability, organizing the large amount of data, and creating a solid foundation for future expansion. By deploying a comprehensive data analytics and AI framework on Microsoft Fabric, Heritage Grocers Group has revolutionized its approach to data unification and analytics, demonstrating what’s possible in retail data management and customer service excellence.

Using AI to streamline data organization during acquisitions

As Heritage Grocers Group expanded, the imperative to streamline and optimize data management became increasingly apparent. Recognizing the transformative potential of AI within the company’s ERP system, Adastra envisioned a future where both historical and upcoming data could fuel AI-driven decisions. “A pivotal aspect of navigating an acquisition is the ability to quickly provide comprehensive operational and sales reporting to gauge business performance,” says Dilraj Sehdev, Senior Vice President of Adastra.

Developing a solution of this magnitude typically extends beyond a year and a half. Yet, amidst fierce market competition, Heritage Grocers Group set an ambitious goal to complete this project in fewer than six months. It embarked on a collaboration with Adastra to establish a state-of-the-art data lake. The companies introduced Lucid Data Hub—a groundbreaking, generative AI–powered data and analytics tool that uses Microsoft technology—to centralize data management and automate data workflows. “To achieve this independently would have required expanding our team to construct the necessary schemas and models for data integration,” says Darla Sebastian, Vice President of Special Projects at Heritage Grocers Group. “With Microsoft Fabric, we were able to significantly expedite our timeline.”

Lucid Data Hub, which harnesses the capabilities of Microsoft Fabric and the Microsoft Azure offering Azure OpenAI Service, organizes data from intricate ERP systems, delivers exhaustive data profiling for analytics, and accelerates the decision-making process. Heritage Grocers Group’s ERP system already ran on Microsoft Dynamics 365, which helps businesses adapt and innovate with intelligent ERP business applications, making the integration of the new solution with the company’s preexisting infrastructure seamless. “Microsoft stands as our preferred partner. Our operations are integrated with Microsoft technologies,” says Coswatte.

Informing critical business decisions with AI-powered insights

Within a mere two months, Heritage Grocers Group, in collaboration with Adastra, successfully implemented the new data lake and integrated data from diverse sources and formats. “Following any acquisition, the immediate demand is for sales data accessibility, so the rapidity of deployment was paramount,” says Coswatte. “The process’s speed and fluidity were astonishing.”

Adastra then began automating the classification of three years’ worth of historical data. Using the Azure OpenAI Service, Lucid Data Hub now processes 1.3 terabytes of both new and historical POS transaction data, encompassing 3 billion item transactions, to analyze consumer behaviors. Furthermore, by using Microsoft Fabric, Adastra has helped Heritage Grocers Group reduce overhead costs and reallocate staff efforts from data management to business-driving activities. “The power behind our acceleration is Microsoft Fabric. The extensive automation through generative AI has significantly cut capital expenditures,” says Sehdev. Heritage Grocers Group has reported savings of at least $500,000 by employing Lucid Data Hub alongside Microsoft solutions.

Heritage Grocers Group now has the capacity to thoroughly examine data from an array of POS transactions, improving decision-making as it scales. The group has seen an increase in data acquisition speed and swiftly integrated data from the acquired stores, bringing the total number of stores to 115. “The Hispanic grocery sector presents a vast opportunity, being the fastest-growing demographic yet underserved,” says Coswatte. “Our acquisition strategy positions us to effectively support this community.”

With the AI functionalities of Azure OpenAI Service and Microsoft Fabric, Heritage Grocers Group is set to continue automating data management and accelerating expansion. This technological foundation informs pivotal business decisions with precise sales data and forecasts. “Our partnership with Microsoft and Adastra has seamlessly unified data from various sources, providing us with a singular source of truth to better orchestrate and oversee our operations,” says Sebastian.

Building for the future with AI

With the implementation of a cutting-edge, centralized data solution, Heritage Grocers Group has significantly enhanced its ability to understand and cater to its customers’ needs across various store banners and geographical locations. To drive sustained growth and innovation in the retail industry, the group plans to continue using AI to further refine its data organization and modeling practices.

“Microsoft Fabric stands as a comprehensive solution that significantly reduces our reliance on traditional IT infrastructure,” says Sehdev. “Its robust and forward-looking design ensures that Heritage Grocers Group is well equipped to scale operations not just to meet current demands but also to anticipate and adeptly navigate future challenges and opportunities.”

Like many academic medical centers, Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (BIDMC) continually strives to improve patient care and optimize efficiency for providers and staff. The difference maker for this teaching affiliate of Harvard Medical School is the innovative way it embraces leading-edge technology to eliminate barriers and help it deliver exceptional patient care experiences.

BIDMC is part of Beth Israel Lahey Health (BILH), a nationally awarded healthcare system with more than 4,700 physicians and 39,000 employees in the greater Boston area. The medical center wanted to improve its ability to search its digital document repository, which many clinicians found cumbersome to use. BILH used its Innovation Lab team—an internal assembly of data scientists, software developers, and product managers—to find a solution that could unlock fast, accurate access to over 3,800 critical policies, procedures, guidelines, and directives (PPGD) used on a daily basis.

“The previous methodology was limited to keyword search, which was not user-friendly and wasted valuable time to locate information,” says Venkat Jegadeesan, Vice President, Technology and Innovation at BILH. “To compensate, our clinicians would find other ways to get the answers they needed, creating staff inefficiencies.”

Initiating a Microsoft Azure solution

After reviewing several search-based technologies, the Innovation Lab team decided to develop an AI-driven, natural language processing solution. During the discovery phase, the team looked into Azure AI capabilities and found a range of integrated service advantages built into Azure AI Foundry.

“Azure AI Document Intelligence proved especially useful for indexing and searching the high volume of documents we use,” explains John Shang, Director, Data Engineering and EHR Systems at BILH. Shang also emphasizes that Azure OpenAI Service provided BILH with the latest GPT-series models, creating additional advantages in app performance.

Innovating with its first generative AI search app

Using Azure AI Document Intelligence, Azure OpenAI Service, and Azure AI Search, the Innovation Lab team built a mobile-friendly application called ChatPPGD. This generative AI app lets staff ask questions in natural language and quickly get a response, along with a reference to the originating documents and relevant medical, academic, and research citations. Shang notes Microsoft’s safety and filtering options were critical in helping ensure secure and accurate responses.

“The benefits of using these integrated services together allowed the app to read all information stored in documents, extract key details, index it, and create embeddings,” explains Shang. “Azure AI Search helped us provide both vector and hybrid search, which significantly improved the usability of the service and provided the right context for searches.”

Optimizing patient and provider experience

“Since launching in February of 2023, ChatPPGD has shown 98% accuracy in its responses,” says Jegadeesan. “We are consistently seeing upwards of 800 queries per week, improved efficiency and policy compliance, and user feedback has been incredibly positive.” Jegadeesan notes these outcomes are helping the hospital deliver on its goals.

“The internal success of the ChatPPGD app has opened up new possibilities for us to accelerate development of solutions that help optimize the patient and provider experience,” says Jegadeesan. “Our Innovation Lab team is getting many requests for AI-based services and solutions, so we’ve begun meeting twice a week with clinicians, researchers, and staff from across BILH to hear their ideas, collaborate, and create AI solutions together. We see this as a big win.”

Bringing automation and AI to life sciences labs

Discovering and creating new drugs takes the coordinated efforts of hundreds of scientists, operators, and technicians, often across multiple sites and countries within different pockets of an organization. As a result, scientific labs are notoriously complex environments with massive datasets, which makes maintaining efficient workflows and data accuracy challenging. Manual processes and scattered data can lead to errors, delays, and increased operational costs.

Given the obstacles, life sciences professionals face immense pressure to run their labs with precision and speed. Artificial helps them do both using natural language processing and AI. The startup’s software suite, the Artificial Platform, helps life sciences laboratories digitize their scientific work and get data off their instruments and equipment more efficiently. “We’re tool builders who like making elegant, stylish tools for scientists and other people to accomplish tasks they couldn’t normally do on their own,” says David Fuller, Chief Executive Officer and Cofounder at Artificial. 

The goal is to make lab experiments reliable, repeatable, and trusted. Artificial’s founders knew this was a great opportunity for the cloud. “Using the cloud gives you global visibility and scale, particularly along the data storage front but also with real-time observability of what’s happening as different scientists manage different parts of the process,” says Fuller. 

Artificial also wanted to unlock the future for life sciences professionals through AI-driven labs. This led to the creation of a cloud-to-edge connected productivity layer for labs to conduct more efficient experiments—spanning their researchers, equipment, and locations—and achieve better, faster results. “We’ve taken a legacy control system and reimagined it as a born-in-the-cloud control system, globally distributed across cloud infrastructure and edge devices,” says Fuller. “It’s a containerized set of microservices that runs on Kubernetes and delivers live, globally centralized visibility into experiments.”

Building around Azure Kubernetes Service, Azure OpenAI Service, and digital twins

To gain a global platform that’s ready to scale its AI solution, Artificial migrated from its previous cloud platform to Microsoft Azure, taking advantage of Microsoft APIs and working with Microsoft Global Black Belts to provision and commission applications and infrastructure tailored to life sciences for the cloud. “Microsoft is a trusted brand for security and data governance, with built-in tools and building blocks that help us stay compliant in accordance with this industry’s best practices,” says Fuller. “For example, we have to be ISO certified, and moving to Azure helped us achieve that.”

Artificial’s system architecture now comprises a static front end with a dynamic, responsive web app built using Vue.js. A fleet of services behind it is orchestrated via Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) and sent to Azure Virtual Machines running Vanilla OS, a Linux on Azure–based operating system. “Many of our services are internally stateless but need some way to offload stateful queries and process events, and we use a combination of Redis and PostgreSQL for that,” says Charles Crain, Chief Technology Officer at Artificial. “We store every step of every job in a queryable PostgreSQL database, and we use Redis as our message broker.” All the cloud applications, plus point-in-time backups for PostgreSQL and Redis, use Azure Blob Storage.

As Crain explains, “Our product is based around a workflow that runs in a laboratory authored using a domain-specific dialect of the Python programming language, Orchestration Python, that’s designed to pair with a language model–based assistant. But you can’t just ask any off-the-shelf model to work with Orchestration Python or to have contextual awareness of a customer’s lab.” In response, Artificial developed a prototype bot based on Azure OpenAI Service and Azure AI Search. “Customers will have greater success with our product if we augment it with context,” adds Crain. “Our Azure-based bot uses retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to guide customers through coding in our specific Python dialect to work in their particular application domains.”

Artificial’s Digital Twin provides customers with a 3D digital twin of their laboratories, offering both a spatial picture of the lab and rich experiment observability through an API. “You can view state changes in your lab in real time via your browser and see bits of the digital twin highlighted as the workflow starts activating equipment in the lab,” notes Crain. “That’s all events flying back and forth over Redis, so Redis and the digital twin come together to form the full data picture of the lab. We also plan to help customers fine-tune their workflow designs by bringing in context for the data model that gives the coordinates of a piece of equipment or how many pieces of equipment are in those positions.”

Artificial is now using off-the-shelf technologies such as managed AI or semantic search from Azure to deliver rapid business benefits. As they manifest, scientists step into self-driven labs where they’re now able to elevate their proposals for further drug experiments and automate overhead to be involved in design from a more strategic and truly experimental capacity versus completely hands-on. In the case of drug discovery and molecule design, pretrained AI models can suggest new experimental candidates or "score" experimental candidates, which helps scientists avoid excessive and expensive wet lab time and vastly increases the number of candidate molecules that can be screened. More molecules screened more quickly at a lower cost per data point allows scientists to arrive with more effective drug candidates and bring them to market more quickly than was previously possible.

Supporting industry breakthroughs

Since making AI more accessible in lab settings, Artificial has made tangible impacts on the industry. Using the Artificial Platform, a leading US pharmaceutical and biotechnology company was able to fast-track how it creates vaccine delivery mechanisms for its therapeutics. To support other areas of the business’s development of therapeutics, Artificial created libraries of different lipid nanoparticle properties and characteristics, which frees up time for scientists to conduct additional research and create more particles. Artificial is also helping a cell and gene therapy company, which focuses on novel therapies through gene editing, use the Artificial Platform to gather more information ahead of development discussions. Its staff is then able to use automated lab equipment more optimally with fewer errors and more accessible data and unlock insights to continuously improve time and cost per data point.

Artificial’s pharmaceutical customers, who must safeguard their information, share that they’re more comfortable coming on board because Artificial runs on Azure alongside Azure connectors. “The ability to have Azure instances connected on-premises inside the bounds of the pharma companies is going to be of major value for the truly fundamental, critical data that they simply won't let out of the lab,” says Fuller. “We get and provide all the benefits of Azure without any trust or security concerns because they're very comfortable that it’s all within their control.”

“Customers use our platform and tools to accelerate drug discovery,” adds Fuller. “It makes me proud to help these world-class, brilliant minds solve problems that are fundamentally relevant to our lives—and to have a team and a set of solutions that they like. I love making our customers successful with a group of people I like working with.” 

“Making more drugs available to more people in more ways”

By digitizing lab operations, Artificial helps its customers accelerate training, reduce errors, and enhance the overall efficiency and reliability of scientific research. “There’s this sweet spot in the lab for technology that’s substantially useful, optimal from a cost-savings point of view, more effective, more repeatable, more seamless, easy, and approachable with a low barrier to entry so that more people can adopt it,” says Fuller. “The ubiquitousness of the cloud makes us better able to deliver the digital experience through whatever device scientists and staff want to use.”

Artificial is at the cusp of building the sustainable architecture and customer-facing features that would automatically give life sciences customers an enhanced, fully semantics-capable copilot they can query about their lab and everything in it. “The data that’s produced all comes through Azure AI Search, RAGing, and Azure OpenAI language models via tools we’ve written to enable agency for the lab,” says Fuller. “AI is just a brain in a jar if it doesn’t have something to tell it what to do or to ask about, so we want to be that interface. And because we’re already running the experiments and gathering the data, we obviously want to be what collects the data and standardizes its shape.”

Artificial is rapidly tracking growth on multiple axes—more customers, bigger customers, more GPU supercomputing, and bigger customer labs with more data points and more experiments in parallel. “The world is making more drugs available to more people in more ways, and we’re helping enable that across the markets,” says Fuller.

Early adopters of Atom have seen immediate benefits. One customer reported a 20% deflection rate on initial implementation, which increased to 65% within 6 months. Aside from productivity gains, the Agentic service management platform has reduced operational costs and increased employee satisfaction, and enabled service teams to focus on more strategic projects.

Customer background


Atomicwork, an agentic service management software provider, was founded in 2022 and has quickly grown to over 50 employees in the United States, Singapore, and India. The company specializes in an AI-first approach to IT and enterprise service management, setting itself apart by developing its platform from the ground up with artificial intelligence at its core. The company's unique value proposition is its conversational service management platform, which fundamentally reimagines how businesses approach IT service management (ITSM) and enterprise service management (ESM).

As hybrid work reshapes the modern enterprise, efficient IT service management and digital workplace automation have become essential to driving productivity and enhancing employee experience. With Microsoft Teams and Slack at the heart of workplace collaboration, Atomicwork delivers service management solutions directly to end users, simplifying IT operations and empowering businesses to scale faster and operate more efficiently. With Atomicwork the portal experience comes to the users; the goal is to avoid going to a portal altogether.

Unlike traditional service management providers who have had to retrofit AI capabilities into legacy systems, Atomicwork's platform was designed in the age of advanced AI, allowing them to create an AI-native architecture from the get-go. This timing advantage has allowed them to develop a more integrated, efficient solution that directly addresses the changing needs of the modern hybrid workforce rather than bolting-on AI as an afterthought. Since emerging from stealth mode, the company has achieved significant milestones, including replacing established players in enterprise environments.

The challenge: from service desk to innovation leaders

Traditional service management systems struggle to provide the agility and efficiency required in today's digital workplace. Atomicwork identified a critical issue: legacy platforms are siloed, with disconnected tools and outdated technologies impeding real-time communication and adaptability. Implementing enterprise-ready service management solutions becomes a complex task, requiring significant effort to build and maintain integrations across various components of the employee tech stack.

The effects on productivity are significant. Service teams such as IT and HR are inundated with operational tasks and repetitive inquiries. Basic questions like "How do I get VPN support?" or "Where can I find my payslip?" consume their workday, diverting valuable resources away from strategic initiatives. This reliance on human involvement for routine service requests causes delays and inefficiencies, especially in Level 1 and Level 2 support scenarios.

The burden extends beyond service teams and affects the entire organization. Employees experience app fatigue and productivity drains as they deal with massive amounts of digital data across numerous software tools. Teams at all levels, from individual contributors to leadership, find themselves spending too much time looking for information and status updates on traditional support portals, rather than focusing on value-added tasks. The cumulative effect undermined organizations' ability to set and achieve strategic objectives.

According to Lenin Gali, Chief Digital and Business Officer at Atomicwork, "Over the last three decades—from BMC Remedy to ServiceNow—traditional service management has evolved but still requires high setup overhead and maintenance. However, they have all been focused on how IT can best serve employees. What we needed in the next generation was to empower employees and IT to best serve themselves using automation and an Agentic AI approach."

The transformation of service management from a cost center to a strategic enabler required a complete rethinking of how employees interact with IT services. The key is to embed operational knowledge and business automation directly into the flow of work—in the collaboration tools that employees use every day.

The solution: building an AI-native service platform 

Atomicwork chose Microsoft Azure AI as the foundation for their next-generation service management platform because of its deep integration into business ecosystems and widespread adoption by global enterprises. Recognizing that many of their target customers were already using Microsoft products like Teams, Atomicwork saw an opportunity to integrate their AI Agent, Atom, directly with the tools employees use daily. This includes everything from Teams to Microsoft Entra ID, Intune, SharePoint, Outlook and GitHub Enterprise; every knowledge and workflows app an enterprise is likely to be using.

"When it came to AI models, the Azure AI platform was miles ahead for enterprise-segment offerings compared to alternatives," says Lenin Gali.

“The combination of accuracy, performance, and built-in security aligned perfectly with our AI and information security principles.” Most enterprise environments already had Microsoft Teams, so embedding Atomicwork's conversational interface was a natural fit.

Atom is the platform's AI Agent, built on an ensemble architecture that uses multiple AI models for various aspects of service management. Unlike traditional systems that add AI capabilities to existing architectures, Atomicwork designed its platform with AI embedded at every layer, ensuring seamless integration and optimal performance.

Atom connects with an organization’s knowledge sources, including SharePoint, Confluence, Jira, among others. The data is segmented into manageable chunks and embedded using OpenAI's embedding model, after being hydrated with user and enterprise context. A troop of AI agents manage user interactions using a sophisticated set of steps. When a user submits a question, it goes through content moderation, ambiguity checking, and multiple guardrails in place, before retrieving and serving the right answers generated to the user. Cohere's Reranker model also plays a crucial role in prioritizing the best result to return. For service requests requiring structured data, Atomicwork’s AI streamlines form completion by automatically filling in known details saving users time and reducing manual input using Cohere’s Command model. Model evaluation and selection are critical steps in the implementation process. Atomicwork uses a curated golden dataset to evaluate model accuracy and efficiency across a variety of use cases, including re-ranking and slot filling. They use performance metrics, such as similarity and relevance scores, to ensure that each model meets precise accuracy and performance requirements.

Results and benefits: delivering impact from day one

Atomicwork's Agentic service management platform has produced impressive results for its organizations, unlocking enterprise IT and service teams’ productivity. One customer's experience of achieving a 65% deflection rate within six months of implementation with projections of an 80% rate by the end of the year demonstrates that efficiency improves quickly as the system is adopted across functions in the organization.

Technical performance metrics demonstrate the Azure AI platform's effectiveness. The implementation of Cohere Rerank resulted in a 20% increase in accuracy, while overall system performance showed a 75% reduction in response latency when compared to competing solutions.

“Our decision to build on Azure OpenAI Service has proven instrumental to Atomicwork’s success. The platform’s capacity and throughput enable us to handle enterprise-scale demands with exceptional response times, while multi-regional support ensures consistent performance for our global user base. Combined with GPT-4o’s enhanced accuracy, we’re delivering AI solutions that don’t just meet enterprise standards—they set new ones." says Suresh Ponnusamy, Head of Platform Engineering at Atomicwork.

The transformation achieved through Atomicwork's solution is particularly well illustrated by the experience of Karthik Chakkrapani, SVP, Corporate Operations & CIO at Zuora, who explains: “With Atomicwork’s modern service management and Agentic AI platform, we are transforming the digital workplace experience at Zuora. Our employees now enjoy instant support, seamless information access, and automated service workflows—all via Slack. This partnership is driving faster resolutions, enhanced productivity, and a smarter, more connected workplace.”

The impact on operational efficiency has been similarly impressive. The platform's ability to automatically handle routine Level 1 and Level 2 support requests has given IT teams more time to focus on strategic initiatives. This efficiency extends beyond the IT department, as Ryder Hampton, Head of Technology, Enterprise Services at Peppermoney points out: "Atomicwork is a valuable partner in our journey towards World-Class IT Operations. We were able to deploy this new platform and replace a number of incumbent solutions within 6 weeks. We have already seen significant improvements across ticket deflection, self service and most importantly employee experience. Moving across to the Atomicwork solution also reduced our TCO by consolidating 3 different solutions into one platform."

Atom's seamless integration with Microsoft Teams and other enterprise systems has greatly enhanced the employee experience. Employees can access information and services without having to switch between multiple applications or wait for human intervention, as the operational knowledge is embedded directly into the workflow. This has resulted in lower operational overhead for service management teams and faster response times for employees who require assistance.

Looking forward: blueprint for evolution

Atomicwork's platform roadmap aims to broaden its capabilities through deeper Microsoft service integrations. The company is actively developing connections to Azure DevOps for improved collaboration between IT teams DevOps teams, PowerApp and Power Automate for expanded automation capabilities, and Power BI for advanced analytics and reporting. They also intend to integrate with Microsoft's Copilot ecosystem, which will expand the capabilities of their AI Agent.

"At Atomicwork, we are committed to building and deploying AI solutions with TRUST - Transparency, Responsibility, User-centricity, Security, and Traceability at our foundation. Microsoft’s technology and partnership align with our mission. Their focus on security, compliance, and responsible AI practices plays a pivotal role in enabling us to meet these commitments for enterprises," says Aparna Chugh, Head of Product at Atomicwork.

The platform's ensemble AI architecture will evolve further, optimizing the use of various AI models specialized for different service management tasks. By leveraging these expanded integrations and enhanced AI capabilities, Atomicwork hopes to provide even more seamless automation and self-service capabilities within their customers' existing Microsoft Teams.

Arcadis is the world’s leading provider of sustainable design, engineering, and consultancy solutions. Operating in over 70 countries, the company employes over 36,000 architects, designers, engineers, and project managers. Together, this team is addressing some of the world’s most pressing challenges, from the impact of climate change to increasing urbanization and digital transformation—all with the ultimate goal of improving quality of life for people around the world.

Arcadis works on more than 40,000 client projects every year—from intelligent rail and highway design to construction of advanced industrial facilities, sustainable buildings, transportation infrastructure, and green spaces. Given this wide range of solutions, Arcadis wanted to drive greater efficiency with customized business process automation tailored to each project and client. 

The problem was cost. “We found that the cost of hiring a development team to automate at the project level would often be higher than the value of the project itself,” says Bram Mommers, Global Technology Officer at Arcadis. And that’s what led to the company’s adoption of Power Platform. “Power Platform has enabled self-service automation at the project level with minimal training—and it’s flexible enough to cover an incredibly wide range of projects at Arcadis,” says Mommers. 

Establishing a Center of Excellence 

The company had access to Power Platform through its Microsoft 365 licenses. Better yet, many employees were already using Power Platform to build solutions—even before the company had started to offer any formal training or support. As Mommers says, “Our team is naturally innovative so I’m not surprised that so many jumped into the platform early on and were building innovative apps and automations entirely on their own.” 

Success with this early development led to a shift away from other low code platforms, including a migration of over 50 automation projects to Power Automate. “We really liked the way Power Platform was evolving and how it continues to rapidly evolve today,” says Mommers. 

Management was excited about the innovation, but they also recognized the need to start establishing security and development guardrails. Training was another priority to encourage more employees to start using the platform. 

Work on a Power Platform Center of Excellence (CoE) quickly followed. “The establishment of our Center of Excellence marked a pivotal moment for Arcadis. It provided fully global support for the platform which drove greater usage and fueled significant growth across the business," says Freek Matheij, Global Citizen Development Director at Arcadis. “From an IT perspective, the journey to establish a Center of Excellence for the Power Platform showcased our commitment to efficient governance and optimization of digital capabilities.”

Supporting citizen and professional developers 

One of the cornerstones of the CoE at Arcadis is an innovative Citizen Development Hub. With an elegantly simple design, the online experience starts with a spot assessment—a series of questions covering the business objective of a proposed solution along with the number of users, data requirements, and system integration requirements. 

Responses are automatically processed through the hub and generate a set of support materials specific to the solution described. This includes everything from technical guidance to design templates to an archive of similar solutions that could be leveraged as a starting point. If a solution is intended for more than 100 users, the application is directed to the CoE team for deeper assessment and support. For smaller apps, a Power Automate flow automatically creates an environment, enabling the maker to get started on development right away. 

The site also provides access to an active Power Platform community of over 3,000 members, including a growing network of Power Platform champions. The CoE team also organizes regular hands-on workshops, practical demonstrations, and success case showcases that highlight the value and potential of Power Platform. “We have implemented a multifaceted approach that focuses on design principles, practical use cases, and subject matter expertise to drive adoption and empower our teams,” says Matheij.

The CoE has been an enormous success at Arcadis and now supports over 2,700 app and flow makers, including both professional and citizen developers. These makers have also created portals using Power Pages as well as over 50 AI-driven agents using Microsoft Copilot Studio.

Delivering solutions for employees and clients 

Power Platform solutions at Arcadis support a wide range of business needs, from automated extraction of data in SharePoint and Oracle to classification of documents using natural language processing (NLP). Additionally, many of the basic apps developed earlier are now being re-engineered for enterprise scalability. Apps that previously integrated with SharePoint are now running on Dataverse. As Matheij says, “Dataverse provides the enterprise security and scalability we need for larger or more strategic apps and it gives us the tools to handle complex data.”   

One solution in particular that has proven extremely successful is the company’s health and safety application. Built using Power Apps and Power BI, employees have used the app to submit over 60,000 health and safety reports, driving more than 6,000 proactive safety actions. “With Power Platform, we have developed a solution that helps us identify potential risk, improve our procedures, and prevent accidents before they occur,” says Philip Houtermans, Global Health and Safety Director.  

Along with internal applications, Arcadis is also using Power Platform to deliver innovative solutions for its clients. Over 50 apps were developed to streamline management of a major rail construction project. Another solution enables real-time monitoring and resolution of roadside issues like traffic incidents and signal failures. A Power Pages portal was designed to provide businesses with incentives to schedule truck deliveries during off-peak hours, reducing traffic congestion.

Arcadis is also leveraging Power Platform to build next-gen, AI-driven apps. Using Power Apps along with the Azure AI API, the team created a pilot project that streamlines traffic and safety analysis for a public transportation client. Now, a traffic engineer can simply upload incident data and modelling files into the app, click one button, and generate a draft report. The app is expected to significantly reduce the manual processing effort, shifting an engineer’s valuable time from repetitive analysis to designing creative solutions.

“By integrating our subject matter knowledge into Power Platform, we have been able to deliver truly innovative solutions for our clients. That’s contributing to enhanced client experiences and new business opportunities for Arcadis, helping us stay ahead of the curve,” says Prasoon Sinha, Global Director of Digital Solutions.

Leveraging new Power Platform innovations 

Along with current Power Platform technologies, Arcadis is working with new and emerging innovations on the platform.

One example is the pre-built Autodesk connector. Autodesk Construction Cloud is an important project management tool for Arcadis and the company is planning to use the new connector to optimize use of Autodesk data. With the connector, project updates in Autodesk can be easily sent to users through email, Teams, and mobile applications in Power Apps—and even visualized in Power BI. Additionally, by integrating Autodesk Platform Services (APS) APIs with Power Automate, Arcadis can drive more efficient data connectivity and workflows. 

"Integrating the Autodesk connector with the Power Platform will be a game-changer for our design projects. It ensures that designers and project managers stay aligned with real-time data, leading to smarter decisions and more efficient project delivery," says Josha van Reij, Arcadis ACC product owner. 

Arcadis is also involved in early testing of Plan Designer—an AI-powered experience that can build an end-to-end Power Platform solution in a matter of minutes. “We see how Plan Designer can significantly boost our developer experience and really accelerate the documentation process,” says Matheij.

Additionally, Arcadis is exploring news ways to leverage Microsoft Copilot Studio, including autonomous agents, and related AI tools. “The AI technologies in Power Platform will soon have an even bigger impact on how we make informed data-driven decisions,” says Matheij. To help drive this potential, Arcadis continues to expand its maker community, including plans to triple its premium Power Platform licenses in 2025. As Mommers says, “Our significant investment in Power Platform underscores our strong belief in the platform's ability to drive digital transformation, enhance project outcomes, and support future development initiatives within the organization.”

Story Content:
Finding the right car can be time-consuming and confusing for consumers wanting to balance style and performance with affordable payments and servicing. Tekion is committed to making it easier for people to locate and purchase cars that suit their specific needs. The company’s automotive retail technology platform helps consumers navigate every aspect of car ownership, from financing to leasing and vehicle maintenance.

With offices and employees across North America, Europe, and India, Tekion helps dealerships and car companies around the world improve operational efficiency and consumer experience. It also works closely with major automotive brands and dealerships to power digital retail experiences.

“It’s an industry with many complex parts and large transactions,” says Binu Mathew, Chief Technology Officer at Tekion. “Historically, it was underserved by outdated software solutions, making it difficult to provide a seamless, modern experience. Tekion was founded with a mission of changing that.”

Deeper customer connections

To streamline vehicle purchasing for consumers and dealerships, Tekion aimed to create a unified, cloud-native platform that uses generative AI. “We built Automotive Retail Cloud (ARC) to help buyers and retailers better connect—a modern, cloud-native stack that integrates CRM and ERP systems and could securely streamline dealership operations, providing a modern SaaS experience without legacy system constraints,” says Mathew.

“Microsoft Azure has the scale, security, and foundation to manage business continuity and realize our vision for our global customers,” continues Mathew. With Microsoft Azure, Tekion employed Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) and Azure OpenAI Service. “We use AKS extensively to manage our containerized applications,” says Mathew. “This helps us efficiently deploy, scale, and manage our cloud-native stack, ensuring seamless operations and high availability for our ARC.”

The team used Azure SQL, Azure Cosmos DB, and Azure Database for PostgreSQL to manage and store customer data more efficiently and securely. It employed Azure Cosmos DB for critical configurations and transactions demanding high availability. Mathew says its flexible schema supports rapid development, allowing seamless updates in production with zero downtime during upgrades. The team used Azure SQL for scenarios requiring strong transactional guarantees, ensuring impeccable data integrity for read/write operations with minimal tolerance for errors.

“Azure OpenAI Service helps us simplify customer search, appointment scheduling, interpreting customer queries, and providing salespeople with information to respond effectively,” says Mathew. Buyers can search for vehicles and receive detailed information and matching options based on their preferences. They can also get real-time updates on vehicle orders or service status. Dealerships can support digital signatures and electronic forms, streamlining contract processes and reducing physical paperwork.

Smart Communication, an ARC CRM feature, uses Azure OpenAI Service to analyze and summarize communications between car shoppers and sales agents. Using natural language processing, it extracts key points and insights from phone conversations, chats, texts, and emails, providing customer-specific recommendations and prompts for agents to deepen engagement. Smart Communication also automatically creates emails for agent follow-up, facilitating ongoing connection with potential buyers while saving agents’ time.

Within ARC, Azure OpenAI Service and Azure Cosmos DB are also used for CRM to boost sales efficiency and a customer support chatbot to handle less-complex customer questions. This helps in managing customer interactions and sales processes more effectively.

Fluid and efficient

“Azure OpenAI Service removes friction from the customer experience, making interactions fluid and efficient,” says Mathew. Consumers can interact with car companies and dealerships seamlessly across websites and physical stores without losing continuity. Tekion dealerships report greater ease in handling leads, which is driving accelerated sales pipelines, larger transactions, and cost savings. One Tekion customer reports up to $5,000 savings a month.

Since 2021, Tekion’s valuation has grown from $1 billion to $4 billion, in part due to the company’s ongoing AI innovation. “When we started, we had goals of differentiating our products to increase market share, average transaction value, and customer retention,” says Mathew. “With help from Azure OpenAI Service and the power of the Azure environment, we’re doing that and simultaneously continuing to innovate. That’s powerful.”

Discover more about Tekion on Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, X/Twitter, and YouTube.

A difference on day one with Microsoft 365 Copilot for Finance

Microsoft 365 Copilot for Finance brings together Microsoft 365 Copilot with a finance agent in Excel to summarize spreadsheets, calculate queries, find information, and work with financial data faster and more easily. U.S. AutoForce, a division of U.S. Venture, deployed it on two recurring, time-consuming processes: reconciling credit card transactions and bank statements. It took just four weeks to set up, and now Copilot for Finance saves the accounting team more than 30 hours every month. According to Samantha Rooks, Assistant Finance Operations Manager for U.S. AutoForce, "I've been running Copilot for our US Bank reconciliations for three months and it's cutting 80% off the time I used to spend on them. It's freeing me up to do other functional tasks and making month-end easier."

Next up for Copilot for Finance is processing vendor statements, which can take 1.5 hours each when done manually, and cash reconciliation, which typically takes the accounting team several hours per month.

A need to modernize an outdated system

For more than 70 years, U.S. Venture has been recognized as an innovative leader in the distribution of renewable and traditional energy products and vehicle lubricants, tires, and parts. The Wisconsin-based company prides itself on using data-driven insights to manage energy and information in the global movement of goods. More than 5,500 employees work in 70 distribution hubs, warehouses, and offices across the nation. To improve business operations and support expansion in new regions, the company adopted Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance in 2021, expanded to Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management in 2023, and recently began leveraging Microsoft 365 Copilot for Finance.

As the company expanded over the years, U.S. Venture faced several challenges with its dated IBM iSeries-based enterprise resource planning (ERP) solution. The system was unintuitive to use and hard to navigate, which also made training new users difficult. Significant human intervention was required to handle business volume, and many work streams ran outside the system, leading to inefficiencies and higher costs. It was time to move to a modern solution.

After transforming finance and accounting with Dynamics 365 Finance, employees found that the improved workflows and new visibility into accounts payable and receivable saved them time. Dynamics 365 Finance was easier to learn than the legacy system had been, and it could be easily configured to meet changing business needs.

Leadership next focused on improving supply chain management at the company’s U.S. AutoForce division. A leading distributor of automotive parts and tires, industry-specific B2B software, and customized marketing services, U.S. AutoForce serves independent tire dealers, big box retailers, and car dealerships around the United States. The company implemented Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management to improve operational efficiency,  gain business-critical insights, and scale up to support expansion in both the East Coast and West Coast regions.

With 80-90% of customer orders flowing through multiple in-house e-commerce platforms and 50-60% of the orders needed for same-day delivery, orders must be shipped almost as fast as they're received. Managing such a short cycle time requires optimized and automated ordering, picking, and shipping processes, all of which Supply Chain Management provides. The new system was also easier to use and to learn, with an intuitive, web-based dashboard and centralized data, and would eliminate the high cost of maintaining the on-premises legacy system. As Ben Hermus, Director, Operations – Systems & Training, explains, "While all of our systems worked, they had hit their efficiency and capability limits. With the business expanding, and more customers requesting same day deliveries, we needed an integrated solution that could automate processes and help us make the best use of our time."

Out-of-the-box improvements

U.S. AutoForce went live with Dynamics 365 in March 2023. The solution includes core financial functions, procurement and sourcing, product information management, inventory control, sales and distribution, and warehouse and transportation management capabilities. It integrates with key independent software vendors, including Zilliant for pricing, Gentran and Boomi for Electronic Data Interchange (EDI), and Elite EXTRA for route optimization and logistics, and incorporates workflows created in Microsoft Power Automate and Power BI on-demand reporting.

U.S. AutoForce also takes advantage of Supply Chain Management's many out-of-the-box features, including the ability to look up inventory from e-commerce sites and a mobile app for warehouse workers. The solution was easily extended to meet the unique needs of 70 warehouses and thousands of customers, needs less human intervention than the legacy system, and makes operations more efficient.

Today, the benefits are felt at every link in the supply chain.

Automated invoice matching

With improved EDI options, standard mapping, and vendor integrations in Dynamics 365, receiving 10,000 to 15,000 invoices per day is no longer a challenge. Invoice automation created by combining EDI and optical character recognition replaced several manual processes. Now, daily jobs import supplier invoices, match them to receipts, push them into the correct workflow for approval, and send them out for payment. This process improvement has alleviated past system overload issues and saves the accounts payable team hours per month.

Improved order fulfillment processes 

Better inventory visibility, cycle counting automations, and job status makes order fulfillment more efficient. For example, in the past, each SKU item for an order was scanned after picking and loading on the truck. If an employee overlooked an item or accidentally scanned one twice, the error wasn’t detected until later. Now, the system double-checks accuracy at each step, saving valuable time when a customer places an order for same-day delivery. "Dynamics 365 helps us support same-day turnaround in the automotive supplies business. After orders come in, there might be a cutoff at noon, and everything may need to be delivered by 4:00 PM. This creates a set of business problems, and Dynamics 365 helps us solve them,” says Ryan Metzner, Director of Enterprise Applications at U.S. AutoForce.

Teamwork without confusion or duplicated effort

Dispatchers are no longer solely responsible for tracking workflows for each order. Approved team members can now view who’s doing what and jump in where needed to help complete the most pressing orders without duplication of effort or confusion.

More accurate order tracking

A customer might have an order that can be partially fulfilled by the main warehouse, but the remaining stock needs to be transferred from a warehouse in another state. To streamline the process, the solution combines all loads into one order, allowing the items to be scanned and shipped together in a single delivery for smoother and more accurate tracking through the company’s “hub and spoke” distribution model.

Workflow automation eases pricing challenges

When a customer order requires billing a supplier, an automated workflow creates an accounts receivable invoice that pulls in the supplier pricing and matches it to the corresponding accounts payable credit, and automatically clears them in the system. A process that used to require manually cutting, pasting, and importing data now runs automatically.

More efficient warranty claims

Processing warranty requests is more efficient and accurate with automated workflows, too. For example, if a car dealership receives an order that was damaged during shipping and needs to be replaced, the claim is filed automatically, including any special pricing negotiations that are specific to the customer. When the reimbursement is received, it matches the correct amount due and can be resolved more quickly. “Our warranty related workstreams have been improved with the capabilities that Dynamics 365 offers. Having a system where all relevant information is easy to access increases our efficiency not only during the claim processing but thereafter. Implementation was seamless and we found it to be very easy to train associates,” says Trevor Hermus, Senior Manager, Warranty & Returns.

Promising results with AI tools

U.S. AutoForce plans to build an internal chatbot to automate complex warranty claims for the more than 40 tire brands the company sells. It’s also exploring building custom chatbots for key supply chain processes. Says Mary Koester, Director – Finance Digital Transformation, U.S. AutoForce, “Our trust in the products we’ve used for years, and Microsoft’s handling of our data gives us confidence to adopt new AI-driven tools. So far, it’s serving us well and we’ve just begun implementing Copilot for Finance.”

The results are promising. For example, the company deployed Copilot in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management for warehouse and operations employees to access when questions arise. So far, it references 110 operating procedures, when prompted the procedures display in the sidecar feature in Dynamics 365 using the Generative help and guidance with Copilot. Having answers at employees’ fingertips is saving time by eliminating the need to sift through SharePoint documents for answers to their questions. Other groups are expressing interest in applying AI to their teams and processes. According to Metzner, “AI will help give us visibility on granular information and Q&A that takes time gathering. It’s going to make a lot of manual processes just go away, in a good way.” 

Transformation based on trust

Since 2021, U.S. Venture has transitioned from its aging, on-premises ERP system to a modern, cloud-based solution and is already using the latest AI tools to help its teams operate more efficiently and effectively. As Metzner says, “We have trust in Microsoft. It’s that simple. We have no reason not to believe in their products and promises.”

Now operational in 40 states, U.S. AutoForce receives, picks, transfers, and ships orders faster with less friction. Its finance department uses AI automation to pay invoices and process warranty payments, which improves accuracy and gives time back to employees.
