To keep pace with rising clinical demands and evolving care models, Apollo Hospitals needed digital systems that will be agile, stable, and built for change. As one of India’s largest and most trusted healthcare providers, Apollo operates more than 74 hospitals and manages over 10,000 beds nationwide, handling upwards of 20,000 outpatient visits, thousands of admissions, and hundreds of complex procedures every day.

For years, Apollo relied on its own hospital information system and in-house Electronic Medical Record (EMR) platform. But its on-premises infrastructure had become difficult to maintain and scale. As data volumes grew and performance expectations rose, the limitations of its legacy setup became harder to ignore. “We knew our existing systems were holding us back,” said Shankar Krishna A, General Manager of IT at Apollo Hospitals. “We needed a platform that would support where we’re headed next, not where we’ve already been.”

Apollo had already made progress in digitizing care delivery, with strong EMR adoption among outpatient physicians and rising engagement from hospital staff. What it needed now was the flexibility to develop faster, deploy more efficiently, and build the kind of long-term digital foundation that could power the next generation of care.

From legacy systems to a flexible architecture

Apollo’s transformation began with a clear directive: modernize its core hospital systems to support a growing digital footprint and rising clinical demands. Its internal development and IT teams had already built and maintained a custom hospital information system, but the infrastructure behind it was no longer keeping pace. Apollo needed to rethink how it delivered performance, scalability, and flexibility across its network. Security and regulatory compliance were also key drivers of the move. Sridhar Yadla, General Manager at Apollo Hospitals, explains, “The infrastructure was quite fragmented. We had to work harder just to maintain availability, which left very little room for innovation. There was too much firefighting and not enough time to think about what’s next.”

That urgency drove its decision to move from a rigid on-premises environment to Microsoft Azure. One of the first priorities was to replace its Oracle-based backend with Azure Database for PostgreSQL, a choice that reflected Apollo’s commitment to open-source tools and a more future-proof architecture. “The Oracle stack was getting harder to maintain, and scaling it meant significant investment every time,” says Shankar Krishna A. “We saw Azure Database for PostgreSQL as the right foundation for the future. It’s open, cost-effective, and capable of supporting the hospital information system we built in-house.”

Apollo worked with its longtime cloud partner, Quadrant Technologies, to manage the migration. Its development, support, and infrastructure teams coordinated with Quadrant using Azure DevOps to manage deployment, testing, and code delivery across environments. This gave Apollo the structure to keep work moving without downtime or disruption. “Having Azure DevOps in place gave Apollo the control it needed,” says Sreeram Sivakumar, Technical Program Manager at Quadrant Technologies. “There was a lot of coordination across test, staging, and production environments, and the pipelines helped us manage updates without causing delays.”

Apollo’s core application now runs on Azure Virtual Machines, deployed across nine zones. Azure VMs gave Apollo flexibility to lift and shift critical systems while planning for future modernization. The application layer uses Windows-based VMs, while the PostgreSQL database runs as a managed platform as a service (PaaS). Image-based VMs, including Linux on Azure, help standardize configurations, reduce errors, and simplify environment expansion and replication. With fewer infrastructure variables to manage, the hospital has improved application stability and simplified scaling. That foundation also positions Apollo to support more advanced capabilities, including real-time analytics and AI-powered tools like Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft Fabric. “This shift wasn’t just about moving data,” says Sridhar Yadla, General Manager at Apollo Hospitals. “We wanted our team to be ready to support a more scalable and dynamic setup. That meant rethinking how we work and plan for what’s next.”

Handling the volume and complexity of data was one of the most demanding aspects of the project. Apollo’s environment includes more than 80 interfaces connecting the hospital information system with lab equipment, billing, pharmacy, and diagnostics. The team used Azure Databricks to synchronize data between the legacy Oracle system and the new PostgreSQL environment. “Data migration wasn’t just about copying tables,” says Shankar Krishna A. “We had to preserve integrity across thousands of procedures and forms. Azure Databricks helped us keep everything aligned in near real time.” The migration required extensive testing and custom workarounds, including recreating .NET source code from compiled libraries and replacing Oracle’s replication model with a custom solution that minimized lag.

Apollo also strengthened visibility and security. With Azure Application Insights, teams monitor system health continuously and can respond faster to issues. “Database observability was a big gap in our old setup,” explains Shankar Krishna A. “Now with Application Insights, we have much better visibility and can pinpoint issues before they affect our users.”

Operating in a regulated environment, Apollo built its architecture for compliance and secure connectivity. It uses Azure Virtual Network to isolate workloads and Microsoft Defender for Cloud to monitor threats, enforce security policies, and safeguard sensitive data. Sivakumar notes, “The healthcare industry has specific demands for how data moves and where it resides. Using Azure Virtual Network and Microsoft Defender helped ensure we met those from day one.” These tools also give Apollo the scalability to expand securely while maintaining compliance with healthcare data regulations in India.

Adoption was part of the plan from the beginning. Apollo’s internal development team played an active role throughout the migration. That involvement helped reduce friction and set the stage for long-term agility. “Our development team didn’t just watch the migration happen—they were part of it,” says Shankar Krishna A. “They understood the logic behind the move and had the hands-on experience to support it post-migration.”

A platform for the next generation of care

Yadla says the impact on day-to-day work has been significant. “When we were on-prem, tuning and troubleshooting ate up so much of our time,” he says. “Now we’re using Azure Virtual Machines, Azure Database for PostgreSQL, and Application Insights to stay ahead of issues instead of reacting to them. It’s changed how we work.” These tools work together to streamline deployment, monitoring, and performance.

The application layer includes more than 100 applications, mostly legacy .NET with some components in Java. These apps were migrated to Azure and now run on Azure Database for PostgreSQL. Modernization is ongoing, with efforts focused on improving portability, performance, and long-term scalability. The environment spans 200 schemas and packages, with approximately 5,000 tables and 6,500 procedures. In total, the codebase includes millions of lines of code, with some individual procedures exceeding 5,000 lines. “Some of the procedures were over 5,000 lines long,” says Venu Gopal, Principal Architect at Quadrant Technologies. “It was all in Oracle format, and we used our QMigrator tool to convert and optimize it for PostgreSQL.” With everything running in the cloud and integrated into Application Insights, the team can spot issues early and act before they affect performance.

Apollo’s teams are now operating in a more agile environment, with greater control across development, infrastructure, and support. With the cloud foundation firmly in place, the organization is positioned to keep evolving its hospital systems and take on new initiatives faster and with fewer constraints. Apollo also exploring AI-enabled tools, including a chatbot for appointment booking and potential Copilot integration. The hospital is also considering Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) for future development to support containerized workloads as part of its ongoing modernization efforts. Microsoft offers guidance for organizations on similar modernization paths, including migrating PostgreSQL workloads, automating deployments with Azure Pipelines, and configuring Azure Database for PostgreSQL.

The move to Azure has brought measurable gains across performance and operations. From infrastructure to development to support, Apollo has shifted from maintenance mode to modernization. Its teams are more nimble, systems are more resilient. With greater stability and faster deployment cycles, staff now spend less time troubleshooting and more time focused on patient care and operational priorities. “We’ve seen nearly 90% of transactions execute within five seconds since the migration, and our uptime has consistently hit 99.95%,” says Yadla. “Opportunities opened up to optimize the operational cost, thanks to decreased overhead and database efficiencies. That stability gives staff the confidence to work without interruption.”

Upgrades and fixes that once took weeks are now completed in days. With Azure DevOps pipelines in place, Apollo can push updates into test and production environments with less risk. “Our deployment timelines have dropped by 40%,” explains Sivakumar. “That means faster access to new features and fewer workarounds for hospital staff.”

Beyond technical improvements, the migration has sparked a shift in mindset. “We’re no longer stuck reacting to problems,” Yadla adds. “Now we’re thinking proactively and looking at how we can evolve.” Shankar agrees that the shift has unlocked new momentum across the organization. He sees Apollo’s foundation as one that’s ready for the future. “We’ve opened the door to future technologies,” he says. “We’re now in a position to build the next generation of hospital systems, not just maintain the current one.”

To help it deliver a greener, fairer, and healthier county for the people of Oxfordshire, the County Council is transforming the way it works. It is transitioning to become a digitally-led local government and position itself as an employer of choice in a diverse constituency which includes pockets of high-tech innovation. The goal? To become lean and efficient with an effective modern workforce.

Because the county council leadership sees generative AI as an important toolset in this transition, it took the bold decision to roll out Microsoft Copilot to every member of its 5,000-plus workforce, with everyone having access to Copilot Chat and 4,500 users of Microsoft 365 Copilot for office and knowledge workers. 

“This is organisational change through a piece of technology—cultural, transformative, with new ways of working,” says Caroline French, Head of Transformation and Digital at Oxfordshire County Council. “And we want everyone to have a role to play in how this transforms us and how we’ll continue to transform.”

Inclusivity during pilot phases ensures the global rollout is shaped successfully

The council was confident in its decision to power forward with a global rollout of Copilot thanks to the wide-ranging pilot it ran during 2024. Involving 500 users from across all council services, the pilot was designed to explore what a full rollout of Copilot would mean for every employee.

Different personas were represented in the pilot. Innovatively, and to keep the number manageable, these personas were based on common skillsets, rather than the service or department in which someone works. They included knowledge worker, management, and business support.

“We wanted to make sure we captured the breadth of different roles across local government. That helped us shape the programme and enabled us to run cross-service training opportunities,” reports Caroline French. “This project has been a fantastic example of how we can work holistically across the organisation, rather than the traditional siloed way of working by service area or department.”

Jo Myers, Senior Organisational Effectiveness and Culture Change Consultant in HR at Oxfordshire County Council explains that working with the directors was critical to the success of the pilot: “They helped us identify the potential champions, who we knew we needed to engage, but also the less-enthusiastic users. If we don’t engage with them, we’re losing valuable insight. So we brought in different voices and viewpoints in a safe and supportive environment. We challenged our own assumptions and learnt from their feedback and concerns so that we could shape the best change programmes going forward.”

Impressive results give confidence in further investment

By asking the different persona groups to share the high-volume, high-intensity, and low-efficiency tasks in their area, the council identified ten use cases to explore during the proof of concept. Benefits identified as a result included:

25,200 hours saved for managers and practitioners by reducing the time taken to write supervision notes. 

30,000 hours saved annually for managers through Copilot’s assistance with meeting notes and follow-ups. 

Public communications to residents can be more accessible and inclusive with the support of Copilot. 

8,000 hours saved annually in hiring processes, with support creating job descriptions, generating interview structures and approaches, as well as composing offer letters. 

Together, the pilot results identified £3.3 million net present value—giving the council the confidence to push forward with the global rollout of Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat. 

Louise Tustian, Director of Transformation, Digital Data and Customer Experience at Oxfordshire County Council, emphasises, “Microsoft Copilot is an important technology and it is critical to us that everyone has an equal chance to benefit from it.”

Excitement is the powerhouse of engagement

Another important learning from the proof of concept was the degree of essential training required to onboard people to the change—from terminology to prompting skills. 

“We recognise that to make this a success, it’s going to take people,” explains Jo Myers. “It isn’t just a technology sitting there. We need to build engagement.”

The team fostered that sense of excitement around Copilot by creating The Hangar—a Teams channel for resources and advice—and The Flight School, which communicates training opportunities. Copilot Ambassadors from across the business also helped to generate a buzz and make the learning relevant to their area.

“Not a single day goes by without me using Copilot. I love it,” says Maggie Wang, a Copilot Ambassador and Information Systems Specialist in HR at Oxfordshire County Council. “I use Copilot to help me brainstorm, to research and question different options, and to debug code. The fact Copilot is in the place where I’m working—Microsoft productivity tools and Power BI—makes it so convenient. I don’t have to leave what I am doing to find help or answers. I just love it.”

“Change is hard in local government,” acknowledges Louise Tustian. “Having Maggie demonstrate the art of the possible excites people. That helps us duplicate her success across the organisation. The feedback from our launch event was ‘I want what Maggie has!’”

It’s important to create “see it to believe it” moments

The team was conscious it needed to keep the sense of excitement around Copilot high; they did not want use to plateau. Oxfordshire County Council brought escape rooms to multiple council buildings across the council estate. 

These “AIscape” rooms created a gamified, team-based experience designed to introduce colleagues to AI concepts and Microsoft Copilot capabilities in an engaging and immersive format. Teams competed to solve AI-themed challenges, making the experience both educational and entertaining. This initiative aimed to demystify AI, build digital confidence, and reinforce the council’s commitment to inclusive digital transformation. As part of a broader engagement strategy, the AIscape Room supported key objectives: raising awareness of Copilot, fostering experimentation and prompt literacy, and embedding Copilot into everyday workflows. 

“We had a great response because it was fun, energising, and so unlike local government,” says Caroline French. “We don’t want people to think, ‘Oh no, this is a new technology I need to learn,’ or feel pressure. Doing something different, creating excitement, boosts the success of our embedding programme.”

To maintain the sense of excitement, the council leant into the support of Microsoft to host a Copilot Hackathon. This was a full-day event designed to foster innovation and collaboration. Its primary objective was to empower teams to design and prototype AI agents using Microsoft Copilot technologies, with a focus on solving real operational challenges. At the end of the day, teams made a “Dragons’ Den” style pitch presentation. Over 80 participants formed 11 cross-functional teams, each tasked with developing agents that could automate tasks, analyse data, and improve service delivery.

“It was another of those ‘see it to believe it’ moments,” says Caroline French. “It gave us a baseline which will help to propel us through the next six months of embedding.”

Breaking down silos by sharing knowledge, challenges and use cases

During the hackathon, the teams created Copilot agents to solve the problem they brought to the day. For example, an operations team from adult social care created a Copilot agent to handle large volumes of invoices and customer enquiries. The commercial team built an agent to guide people through the commercial procurement process. The HR team built an agent which provides links to essential forms and gives real-time updates on candidate progress.

“At the end of the day, I could see so many Copilot agents that we could borrow or adapt for our service,” says Maggie Wang. “I think it’s most powerful when you can see your peers use Copilot to tackle a real problem which you can relate to and apply in your own daily work.”

“The hackathon was a key moment where we came together as an organisation, breaking down those silos,” agrees Jo Myers. “I don’t think we anticipated that when we first went on this journey. Especially after COVID, finding those moments to come together, have moments of learning and connection together, and to feel proud of our organisation is fantastic.”

After six months, the project remains on course to meet its efficiency and savings goals. Copilot has so far enabled the release of approximately 174,000 hours, which if fully realised equates to £2.2 million in officer capacity, allowing individuals to perform tasks aligned with their skills and abilities that add real value.

Innovation must be safe—and continuous 

“We’ve learnt as well that Copilot doesn’t stand still,” says Caroline French. “So we need to keep learning and adapting too.”

As the council progresses into developing agents, it is exploring how to ensure good governance and compliance around agentic AI. As part of the global rollout, it has already upgraded its cybersecurity and compliance approaches with Microsoft security solutions, including Microsoft Purview and Data Loss Protection via E5 licencing.

“To support the Copilot rollout, a strategic decision was made to upgrade from E3 to E5 licences,” Alastair Read, Head of IT at Oxfordshire County Council, explains. “’Check your wheels are down before you land’ was one of the main messages. E5 was the technical side of it. The people side of it was the training.”

This upgrade was essential to unlock advanced Microsoft security features such as data loss prevention and sensitivity labelling; critical tools for safeguarding sensitive information and ensuring compliance. These capabilities were not available under E3 and were deemed necessary to mitigate the risks associated with AI-assisted workflows and data handling. The move to E5 also aligned with the Council’s broader digital posture, which prioritises secure, ethical, and responsible AI adoption. By keeping data within the Microsoft ecosystem and restricting unauthorised external AI tools like ChatGPT, the Council reinforced its commitment to protecting organisational data from being used to train external models.

Alastair Read continues, “This licensing upgrade was not just a technical requirement—it was a foundational step in enabling Copilot to operate effectively within a secure environment. It also supported the Council’s ambition to embed AI into real service delivery processes, rather than treating it as a standalone tool. As part of this transformation, the Council has invested in comprehensive training, ongoing updates to policy and governance frameworks, and a migration from shared drives to SharePoint to enhance data labelling and retention.” 

“There’s a lot to think about through the lens of Copilot—the skills we need to bring into the organisation, how we position ourselves as an employer of choice—it is a massive journey,” acknowledges Louise Tustian. “We have a long way to go but we are doing well. We want to keep this sense of excitement alive!”

AD Ports Group oversees 34 ports and terminals that connect the United Arab Emirates to the wider world. Its mandate is both practical and ambitious: to position Abu Dhabi at the frontier of global trade. By combining large-scale infrastructure with digital innovation, it aims to meet the shifting demands of global supply chains.

A legacy of AI innovation

AI at AD Ports Group is more of a reflex than a program. “AI is a major part of everything we do—it’s not separate from our core operations,” says Mohamed Jamal-Eddine, Group CIO at AD Ports Group. The Group has been using AI and machine learning from day one, in areas ranging from yard management to container allocation. “Now, with next-generation AI, we’re finding entirely new ways of working to solve our challenges and scale rapidly,” shares Jamal-Eddine.

To unlock even more potential from next-gen AI, AD Ports Group formed a compact AI Agents Workforce—a selected mix of data scientists, software engineers, cybersecurity specialists, infrastructure engineers, and domain experts who share an enthusiasm for AI. “Their goal was straightforward to build purpose-designed AI agents to address stubborn pain points, automate repetitive tasks, bring together fragmented knowledge, and improve decision-making to paper-heavy procurement and compliance tasks,” recalls Sultan Al Ghaithi, Group Chief HR Officer at AD Ports Group.

Growth supported by technology

AI Agents Workforce then used various tools with a focus around Azure AI Foundry to securely design, test, monitor AI agents, and Copilot Studio to build the agents quickly with little coding knowledge required. “We first built agents horizontally, such as for generating job descriptions or automating letter drafting that every department could use and then went vertical, creating more specialized agents for particular business clusters where work was more complex,” recalls Al Ghaithi. 

The Group then deployed agents in the business and gave employees access to a live AI Agents Directory, which allowed them to experiment and find new use cases that suited their needs. 

To manage the creation of AI agents, AD Ports Group built the AI Agents Directory, an internal platform where employees can “hire” new agents. By entering information such as the target user, success parameters, and role description, the system can produce a product-requirement document and a ready-to-build blueprint. “Today, it can take us about an hour to develop and deploy a simple new agent,” says Jamal-Eddine. “Now, we have a pipeline of over hundreds of agents in our Agent Directory.”

Tailored agents for every challenge

One of the flagship agents is the Vessel Speed Optimizer, set to give real-time guidance to AD Ports Group’s fleet of 270 vessels on how fast to sail. By factoring in weather and congestion at the destination port with many other data points, it can recommend slowing down when it predicts a berth will not be free, reducing fuel use in the process. “Fuel usage is one of the main drivers of costs, so financial savings are the primary benefit,” says Jamal-Eddine. “On a single leg, a vessel can save thousands of dirhams. When we follow the AI’s recommendations from waypoint to waypoint, we’re also reducing CO₂ emissions. Beyond the numbers, the system also offers softer benefits—fewer idle hours for crews, less stress on engines, and potentially longer vessel life.

Another key AI agent is the Container Balancer, which predicts where empty containers will be needed and prompts the team to move them in advance. For instance, if demand is expected in one region, it can recommend shifting an idle container from another region ahead of time. It also checks storage costs and contracts, so containers end up where they’re cheapest to keep. “Previously, this was manual process. Now, AI lets us do it far faster and more scientifically,” notes Jamal-Eddine.

As the pipeline expanded, more specialized agents appeared. The Claim Detective scans and checks incoming documentation against international shipping and insurance rules. “With it, we can respond to customers quickly and in line with global regulations,” says Jamal-Eddine. 

Another, the Investment Advisor, supports AD Ports Group’s investment teams before proposals are submitted. It checks for missing data, ensures alignment with internal investment guardrails, and significantly reduces review time. By handling the groundwork, the AI agent frees decision-makers to focus on judgment and strategy rather than paperwork.

Giving employees time and power

On top of the AI agents, the team also implemented Microsoft 365 Copilot to handle everyday tasks such as summarizing port notices, drafting updates, and extracting key actions from meetings and emails so employees could focus on higher-value work. “The impact was immediate. In priority functions like finance, legal, and procurement, employees could draft documents and emails in a third faster than before, while long meetings and email threads were condensed into actionable summaries in minutes rather than hours,” says Al Ghaithi. “Executives who once waited for piecemeal updates could now get a single, cited answer to policy questions almost 40% faster.”

By offloading repetitive tasks such as writing job descriptions, compiling routine reports, scanning policies, the AI agents can give people back time to think and strategize. “We took the principles, knowledge and encoded them into AI,” Jamal-Eddine explains. “Anything repeated more than once becomes a candidate for AI.” For the staff, the rise of AI agents has been less about replacement than about relief. “Agents now take care of repetitive work, so our people can focus on what really matters: planning, problem-solving, innovating, and strengthening relationships. Humans always make the final decisions, AI just clears the way,” says Al Ghaithi.

Ready to scale

Looking ahead, AD Ports Group is pushing its experiment to scale. The goal is for 90% of all new code to be generated by AI by the end of the year, allowing agents to be built and deployed at unprecedented speed. “We envision everyone in our organization working with multiple agents assisting them,” shares Al Ghaithi. Today AD Ports Group has over 7,000 employees; within three years, the company expects its agents to outnumber its workforce, an agent at least for each employee. With operations expanding, Jamal-Eddine concludes, “By combining human expertise with AI, we’re driving innovation, sustainability, and growth. And as we expand, that partnership will be key to shaping the future of global trade.”

Founded in 2018 in Estonia, Haut.AI combines cutting-edge generative AI, dermatological science, and advanced machine learning. Haut.AI empowers beauty brands, skincare manufacturers, and retailers to drive innovation at every stage of the product lifecycle.

The challenge

Even with thousands of high-quality skincare products on the market, consumers still struggle to find what truly works for them. Haut.AI was created to bridge this gap, guiding consumers to the best product for their skin through highly accurate, scientifically backed AI skin analysis and personalized product recommendations. The aim: deliver accessible, data-driven insights directly to consumers’ smartphones, helping them make informed choices that deliver real results. At the same time, Haut.AI is committed to helping brands create engaging, educational experiences that build lasting trust and loyalty.

The integrated solution

Haut.AI began working with generative AI in 2021, recognizing its potential to revolutionize both beauty research and personalized skincare. It enables dynamic simulations, predictive modeling, and hyper-personalized solutions, making it a game-changer for the industry. Haut.AI has developed several breakthrough innovations, including the Skin Atlas, a patented facial image anonymization technology that uses generative AI to eliminate artifacts in anonymized image analysis, ensuring privacy protection without compromising accuracy. SkinGPT is the first-of-its-kind AI platform for scientifically accurate, hyper-realistic skin simulations, allowing brands to visualize how skin evolves over time and providing applications across R&D, clinical testing, and personalized consumer experiences.

Partnership with Microsoft

Haut.AI’s expertise in AI, dermatological science, and aging research made them a great fit for Microsoft for Startups, where the company gained access to state-of-the-art cloud-based AI infrastructure, expert guidance, and an expansive network in the tech and retail sectors.

All training, coding, and AI development at Haut.AI are conducted within Microsoft services, including Azure AI, Machine Learning Studio, and Visual Studio Code. These tools provide compute power, data handling, and job execution, enabling Haut.AI to train advanced models efficiently and develop highly scalable AI solutions for skincare research and consumer applications.

"Haut.AI’s entire AI ecosystem runs on Microsoft Cloud, providing the highest level of security, reliability, and scalability. The fact that we could build on such a powerful infrastructure meant we didn’t have to worry about operational limitations—we could focus entirely on innovating, developing pioneering solutions that redefine beauty technology," said Anastasia Georgievskaya, CEO & Co-Founder of Haut.AI.

Go-to-market success

Haut.AI’s SkinGPT is the first scientifically accurate, hyper-realistic skin simulation engine, built on Haut.AI’s deep dermatological expertise and advanced generative AI technology. It enables users to visualize how skin evolves over time in response to real-world variables—aging, environmental exposure, product use, and lifestyle changes—turning complex biological processes into interactive, visual experiences.

Following its commercial debut in January 2025, SkinGPT quickly drew global attention, generating media buzz and capturing interest from beauty businesses seeking to embed next-gen intelligence into their innovation pipelines.

"We’re proud to partner with Haut.AI to push the boundaries of innovation in the beauty industry. Through our collaboration, we’re elevating Ulta Beauty’s digital skin experience to deliver more personalized, customer-centric solutions. This enduring partnership reflects our shared commitment to leveraging cutting-edge R&D to meet evolving needs," said Agustina Sartori, Head of Digital Innovation at Ulta Beauty, Managing Director at Prisma Ventures.

By modeling both biological and perceptual aspects of skin changes, SkinGPT brings unmatched depth to skincare simulation. It helps brands develop smarter products, enhance education, and bridge the gap between claims and results with data-backed confidence.

This groundbreaking work continues to attract leading global brands who see SkinGPT as a critical tool for merging scientific precision with consumer insight, solidifying Haut.AI’s role as a category-defining innovator in AI-driven skincare.

In the world of small and medium-sized businesses, managers are often stretched thin. They face cumbersome administrative tasks, compliance requirements, and a steady stream of employee requests that require immediate attention. What gets sacrificed in all the busywork is what every growth-focused company needs to compete and thrive: a proactive focus on culture development and employee retention. Factorial set out to close this vital gap. 

Carlos Cuadrado Barril, Managing Director at h&k and a Factorial customer, sums it up: “Our HR team was overwhelmed with operational tasks like absence tracking, document management, and vacation approvals—all managed manually. This was keeping them from focusing on initiatives that add real value to our business, such as improving our work culture and developing our people.”

Factorial knows about this unique challenge firsthand. It evolved from a promising startup into a European “unicorn,” breaking into competitive markets and securing multimillion-dollar funding within a very short time frame. Its rapid growth shaped a clear mission: create an intuitive, all-in-one business management platform that helps small and medium-sized businesses leave paperwork behind and put people first. But to deliver at scale and across diverse global markets, Factorial needed a technology partner that could do more than just host its infrastructure. It needed a collaborator and a strategic partner invested in helping the company innovate its technology to get to market faster. 

An infrastructure ready-made to innovate with speed and scale   

After working with a competing cloud provider, Factorial chose to migrate to Microsoft Azure. The decision wasn’t just about performance; it was about unlocking new possibilities. “We chose Microsoft Azure for three reasons: AI infrastructure, interoperability with day-to-day business applications, and go-to-market strategy,” says Jordi Romero, CEO of Factorial. Romero knew that the scalable, highly secure models in Azure AI could support the company’s planned agentic architecture. 

To support global scaling and meet developer needs, Factorial deployed Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) with real-time autoscaling. This functionality was critical for onboarding thousands of its customers across regions, including Italy, France, Portugal, and Latin America. Azure Database for MySQL helped reduce Factorial’s operational overhead, so its engineers could focus on building features rather than managing infrastructure.

Factorial also uses Azure OpenAI in Foundry Models to power its AI agents so they can answer employee questions instantly and trigger workflows, all without human intervention. Factorial’s agents now interact seamlessly with Microsoft productivity tools such as Microsoft Teams, Outlook, and Dynamics 365 Business Central. As a result, users can engage with Factorial’s platform through familiar environments, without needing to open the Factorial app directly. The company is further solidifying its industry leadership role, introducing a new MCP agent built into Business Central for even more seamless, autonomous people management. 

This wasn’t just modernization; it was transformation. Sergi Molins, Director of Strategy and Business Development at Factorial, explains, “We built our Factorial product to be more than a software solution. It is a platform that saves time, connects data, and gives managers the visibility they need to lead with confidence.”     

Offering customers more than software 

Factorial customers used to manage every HR, finance, or internal request using endless Excel sheets and email threads. Today, they run everything on one simple, modern platform, built for people—not paperwork. “AI is not here to take jobs but to eliminate boring tasks,” says Barril. “This technology frees us to focus on meaningful work, leading to better job satisfaction and higher productivity.”

Barril cites the early outcomes for h&k in using the Factorial One solution. “We’ve reduced our weekly administrative time by 65%, increased participation in climate surveys by 34%, and decreased vacation approval times by two days. Most importantly, we reduced involuntary turnover by 22%, which is impact you can feel.”   

The Microsoft partner ecosystem also played a pivotal role. “Microsoft has been a great school for us in understanding how to maximize our collaboration with channel partners,” says Marcel Queralt, VP of Strategy and Alliances at Factorial. “We are working together globally to help small and medium-sized businesses do more.”

Serving the global need for human-centered AI workplaces 

“HR and finance teams used to think their job was to fulfill administrative requirements,” says Romero. “Now their focus can shift to what truly supports a company’s workforce development and growth goals, giving them more power wherever they are located globally.”

Romero continues, “Our customers can talk, co-create, document scan, auto-schedule, pull reports, and answer questions on the same infrastructure that is compliant, scalable, and highly secure—all built on top of Microsoft Azure and its AI-ready APIs. We’ve taken our foundational Factorial offering and built upon it to create Factorial One—an industry-leading solution that meets the day-to-day needs of our growth-focused customers.” 

The Factorial journey proves that with the right collaborator, a team of any size can achieve global impact. “Microsoft, for us, is more than a technology provider,” concludes Molins. “They’ve made sure that Factorial gets a whole new global scale.”

As a leading force in the cosmetics industry, L’Oréal Groupe has been creating beauty that moves the world for over a century. Thanks to the power of Beauty Tech, L'Oréal Groupe offers personalized, inclusive, and responsible beauty experiences for each. Always striving to develop the best products, the Group is also shaping the future of beauty by leveraging the latest advances in cosmetics… and new technologies.

From this ambitious approach comes “Beauty Genius” by L'Oréal Paris a personal beauty assistant powered by generative AI, available 24/7 in consumers' pockets, offering a seamless and personalized customer experience, along with technical prowess. Moutia Khatiri, Chief Technology Officer of Online & Omnisales, together with William Lenoir, Beauty Genius Solution Architect at L’Oréal Groupe, give us an exclusive look behind the scenes.

Beauty Genius by L’Oréal Paris, a highly technological beauty advisor

How can we fully exploit the opportunities of the virtual world while ensuring customers receive the same level of expertise and support as they would from a real advisor in a beauty store? This strategic challenge for all industry players is the starting point for Beauty Genius, driven by L’Oréal Groupe’s Beauty Tech—the department dedicated to innovation—and based on Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service technologies.

The idea? To develop a Generative AI-powered assistant that directly interfaces with customers, capable of interacting simultaneously with each user. To achieve this, the infrastructure hosting Beauty Genius’ GenAI components must meet several technical requirements: ensure stability and consistent latency—both essential in cases of high traffic—be available and reliable, with the platform relying on a fully managed service and benefiting from the elasticity and high availability of the Cloud. Not to mention the security and confidentiality of customer data, which are essential criteria for the Group. “Being the first company to release a GenAI-based beauty assistant was a challenge, but also an exciting journey alongside the Microsoft teams. We worked together to continuously optimize the accuracy and the performance of the tool to make the most out of Azure OpenAI service,” explains Khatiri.

Pay as you go, Provisioned Throughput Units … Designing a hybrid architecture

“We didn’t want to sacrifice the performance, neither waste provisioned, non-used resources, so this hybrid architecture came out as the best compromise in alignment with our eco-design principles," Khatiri continues. Faced with these requirements, the Azure OpenAI Service environment was chosen by the L’Oréal Groupe’s tech teams. Interactions generated by the conversational agent remain strictly private, in a dedicated L’Oréal environment, precisely meeting the Group’s commitments to data protection and ethics.

Equipped with powerful LLMs (Large Language Models) such as GPT-4o, which is particularly suited for advanced chat completions, and Ada—which enables the implementation of a RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) system specific to L’Oréal Groupe—Azure OpenAI Service offers two deployment modes: a classic pay-as-you-go model and a Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) mode.

While the pay-as-you-go model was initially chosen to launch Beauty Genius, the increase in traffic due to the application’s success quickly led the teams to consider PTUs, in order to benefit from more predictable performance, with guarantees on maximum latency and throughput.

“While we have mastered web performance where milliseconds matter, Generative AI presented a new latency frontier. The challenge was to balance the speed users demand with the high-quality answers they deserve. Azure OpenAI Service PTU provided a crucial element to solve this equation, ensuring a seamless and performant experience,” mentions Lenoir.

More specifically, the group devised a hybrid architecture, combining a base of fixed PTUs and automatic switching to the pay-as-you-go model, when the PTU limits are reached. The goal? To ensure that 100% of requests receive a response, while guaranteeing optimal performance for a given volume of requests per minute via PTUs. This approach was also more efficient in terms of cost management and resource allocation, avoiding the need to size the infrastructure based on a theoretical maximum traffic peak.

Next, a series of load tests was conducted to determine the robustness of the architecture. Initially, the system was deployed in a temporary environment dedicated to performance testing, configured with a minimum of 15 PTUs. A simulation of 100 simultaneous users was carried out. The load gradually increased up to 2,000 simultaneous users, and the number of PTUs was adjusted as needed to support this scaling.

Scaling up without compromising user experience

Switching from a pay-as-you-go model to a hybrid architecture played a key role in significantly improving performance. PTUs made it possible to keep maximum latency below 5 seconds, while offering greater stability in response time variance. Since PTUs are also independent of the used model type, they could be reassigned to different models as needed. This flexibility allowed L’Oréal Beauty Tech teams to gradually migrate certain workloads and further optimize performance results. The result: Beauty Genius can truly scale up without compromising user experience.

By relying on Azure OpenAI Service, L’Oréal Groupe demonstrates its ability to integrate the most advanced technologies into its Beauty Tech ecosystem, with a strategy resolutely focused on performance, ethics, and scalability.

Beauty Genius is much more than an AI assistant. It is a foundational building block in the digital transformation of beauty consulting, capable of reproducing, on a global scale, the personalized experience of an expert.

Capricorn Co-operative, Australasia’s largest automotive cooperative, supports over 28,000 members, including mechanics, panel repairers, auto electricians, and commercial vehicle businesses across Australia and New Zealand.

With annual sales topping $3.4 billion, Capricorn needed a more reliable and flexible contact center solution. Capricorn’s old on-premises contact center solution had frequent performance issues: dropped calls, slow performance, and limited flexibility. To fix this, Capricorn implemented Microsoft Dynamics 365 Contact Center as a standalone voice solution. The result? Better service, greater agility and scalability, and smoother operations.

Shifting to modernization

Founded in 1974 by a small group of Western Australian service station owners, Capricorn was built to give small businesses more buying power and level the playing field with large multinational oil companies. Today, it offers members access to financing, business protection, billing services, and exclusive rewards, supported by over 2,000 preferred suppliers.

When its Genesys system neared its end-of-life, the company didn’t just replace it. Instead, it modernized its entire technology ecosystem by moving to the cloud with Dynamics 365. It became the first organization in Australia to deploy Microsoft Dynamics 365 Contact Center as a standalone voice solution. This milestone was celebrated during a visit by Capricorn’s board of directors to the Microsoft Innovation Hub, which significantly elevated the visibility of the initiative across both organizations.

What makes Capricorn’s journey truly unique is its bold decision to begin with contact center capabilities—a reversal of the typical adoption path, where most organizations start with Dynamics 365 Customer Service and later expand into contact center functionality.

Strong partnerships for success

Capricorn worked closely with Microsoft FastTrack and Velrada to ensure a smooth rollout. After evaluating several leading systems, Capricorn chose Microsoft Digital Contact Center Platform for its deep integration, cloud-native foundation, and powerful AI capabilities.

With advanced automation through the Interactive Voice Response (IVR) bot framework, Capricorn streamlined processes, improved responsiveness, and laid the groundwork for a future-ready contact center.

Overcoming old challenges in a new world

The old system needed heavy customizations to support distinct duties between Sydney and Perth centers. Due to the lack of flexibility, any change—no matter how small—required extensive IT support.

With Dynamics 365 Contact Center, IT administrators and business users gained significantly more control, especially over IVR flows and call routing. For example, if there’s a flood or another emergency, they can swiftly update phone numbers, reassign teams and queues, and adjust IVR messaging in real time. This newfound ability to manage and configure the contact center internally puts ownership directly into the hands of the business and enables faster, more flexible responses to changing circumstances.

Managing call queues—adding users, assigning supervisors, and configuring who handles which queues—is now straightforward and user-friendly. Setting opening and closing times, including adjustments for public holidays that vary by state, is fully self-service, eliminating previous reliance on third-party vendors.

Updating voicemail messages is also much simpler. Instead of recording, uploading, and managing audio files as required in the old system, staff now simply input text, which the system converts to speech automatically.

With Dynamics 365, Capricorn can easily modify call scripts—the order of questions asked and escalation paths. This flexibility enables a contact center experience tailored precisely to business needs. Given the critical role of the contact center in business continuity planning, having a reliable, easily manageable system is essential. “The improvements in Dynamics Contact Center have significantly enhanced our ability to communicate effectively with members and employees, even during disruptions,” explains Mary Karborani, Chief Information Officer at Capricorn.

Capricorn also implemented an emergency line that can be activated immediately to prioritize calls during critical events such as natural disasters. This setup allows Capricorn to respond quickly without waiting days for external support, greatly enhancing their operational agility.

Smooth workflows yield better service

Capricorn had been using a customized Epicor ERP system for case management which led to inefficient workflows. Agents would take a call, jot down notes, then switch to another call and repeat the process. “The agents had to manually copy and retype notes into the system. There was a lot of double handling, and it was error-prone and wasted agents’ time,” says Sachin Patani, Project Manager, Strategic Projects, Capricorn.

By connecting Epicor with Azure Communication Services (ACS), agents can now make outbound calls directly from the CRM. The screen pop feature automatically displays the caller’s information, enabling faster access to records and more efficient service.

Microsoft Copilot’s call summarization also saves time. Agents no longer need to retype notes during calls. This shift improved the overall member experience, ensuring callers feel truly heard and supported.

“The new system’s automated call summaries have been a game-changer for our team. It takes care of most of the notetaking, allowing agents to reflect and make quick edits afterward. This process, which used to take a lot of time and mental effort, now happens much faster—saving valuable minutes per call,” says Karborani. This efficiency means agents can handle more calls, which translates to better member service.

Capricorn plans to fully roll out summarization through its phone system to make work smoother and more efficient. Since the solution is built into the platform, it works naturally with their communication tools without the need for complicated integrations or extra setup. “As we continue to expand into Dynamics 365 CRM and ERP systems, this native compatibility ensures smooth, ongoing connectivity across our technology stack,” says Patani.

Contact Center insights unlock operational efficiencies

Out-of-the-box dashboards and reports provide significantly more detailed and near real-time insights than the organization’s legacy system. The dashboards allow contact center leaders to monitor queue activity closely and respond dynamically. For example, if one queue is overwhelmed with calls, supervisors can quickly reassign agents to balance the workload and reduce member wait times. Previously, long hold times with repetitive music caused frustration among members, but these improvements have relieved even the busiest call days for Capricorn.

During the Members Convention, the ticket sales overwhelmed Genesys. Members tried repeatedly to get through, sometimes after enduring long wait times over days or even weeks, eventually giving up. The event wouldn’t sell out, and members were frustrated. But with Dynamics 365 Contact Center, Capricorn created a dedicated IVR to handle ticket sales. All 700 tickets sold out in a single day without any complaints.

In fact, on its first day of going live with Dynamics 365 Contact Center, Capricorn managed thousands of calls without major disruptions or technical issues.

Dynamics 365 Contact Center as a standalone solution has strengthened the support and development for contact center teams, improving agent performance and member experience. “With the call sentiment analysis feature in Contact Center, supervisors monitoring live calls can jump in if required when sentiment shifts negatively,” says Shane Lovegrove, Procurement Advisor at Capricorn. “This helps teams resolve issues in real time.”

Additionally, the call transcription feature enables better performance management by allowing supervisors and agents to review conversations for coaching and quality assurance. With a more reliable and easier to manage system, remote work is now efficient and straightforward, eliminating hassles for agents and management.

The road ahead

Capricorn’s Dynamics 365 Contact Center solution is revolutionizing operations, and its impact will grow as the organization implements Dynamics 365 CRM and ERP solutions. Native communication between these systems will benefit not only call center agents but also area managers and risk managers who engage directly with members in the field.

Key Copilot initiatives aimed at improving operational efficiency and enhancing customer experience are in the works. This includes the development of a chatbot interface that enables call agents to quickly access knowledge base articles while assisting customers. This tool is designed to streamline the support process, allowing agents to provide faster, more informed responses during calls.

The second initiative focuses on creating a 360° customer view making it easier for agents to access all relevant client information at a glance to improve efficiency and reduce response times.

A planned Copilot Center of Excellence will serve as a hub for best practices, enabling continuous improvement in how Capricorn uses AI and automation to support agents and improve the overall customer experience.

The organization also plans to introduce features such as a virtual agent for frequently asked questions like resetting passwords or checking reward point balances. This will help reduce the number of simple inquiries handled by call agents, freeing them up to focus on more complex cases. As Capricorn continues to adopt Dynamics 365 solutions, it shows its commitment to innovation. The drive to always elevate customer service is part and parcel of its cooperative values—using Dynamics 365 to foster resilience, responsiveness, and shared success.

Capricorn modernized with Dynamics 365 Contact Center, enabling cloud-based automation, real-time insights, and seamless integration with business apps.
The new system improved member service, boosted agent efficiency, enabled rapid scaling, and empowered supervisors with actionable analytics.

Challenge: Making knowledge usable and modernizing processes sustainably

As a global leader in innovative adhesive solutions – from high-tech tapes for the automotive and electronics industries to office supplies – tesa SE operates in a highly complex environment. With around 5,400 employees at 11 production sites and activities in over 100 countries, the international orientation places high demands on efficiency, transparency, and decision-making. The diversity of markets, broad product portfolio, and regulatory requirements call for precise management and continuous development. At the same time, there is a growing demand to operate more sustainably and use resources more purposefully.

The company has a strong foundation: highly qualified teams, deep expertise, and an established technological infrastructure. This solid starting point enabled tesa to position AI not as a reactive problem solver, but as a strategic growth lever.

“We operate in a field of tension between global complexity, regulatory density, and dynamic market cycles,” says Christoph Hummel, Head of IT at tesa. “This requires not only technological excellence but also the ability to make knowledge quickly and specifically usable.”

A key aspect of tesa’s approach was systematic preparation: The company recognized early on that successful AI integration requires a harmonized data base and established governance structures. These formed the foundation for the holistic introduction of Copilot across all business areas. The consolidated knowledge from various systems – from SharePoint to individual team structures – and the existing expertise created ideal conditions for intelligent networking and effective value creation through AI-driven solutions.

At the same time, the desire grew to make processes not only more efficient but also more sustainable. In areas such as supply chain, transport, or administration, resource use was high – both in terms of personnel and technology. At the same time, the demand for data-based decision-making increased, and tesa aimed to become more agile to respond more quickly to market changes. “It wasn’t about eliminating individual tasks, but about modernizing our existing structures so that our employees can use their time and knowledge more purposefully,” says Hummel.

“We wanted to create freedom – for value-adding tasks, creativity, collaboration, and for what really drives our teams forward,” Hummel continues. The solution was not only to optimize processes but also to promote a new work culture – with more room for initiative, collaboration, and meaningful activities.

The solution: More efficiency, transparency, and innovation with Copilot and Agent Factory

With the introduction of Microsoft Copilot, tesa deliberately chose a low-threshold, integrated AI solution that reaches all employees – regardless of prior knowledge or department. “Copilot was the perfect entry point for us. The integration into the existing M365 environment reduced barriers and made usage easier,” says Holger Ruskowski, Head of IT Cloud, Integration & Operations. As an additional button rather than a new system, Copilot integrates seamlessly into everyday work. This facilitates access, promotes acceptance, and enables broad usage.

Instead of a classic top-down rollout, tesa relied on a pull principle: all employees could actively apply for a license. The response was overwhelming – within the first weeks, demand was over 60 percent, and today around 90 percent of registered users use Copilot actively every day.

The introduction was accompanied by practical workshops, a prompt buddy with hundreds of pre-made examples, and an active user community. Around 90 AI ambassadors support as multipliers and contact persons. This approach strengthens initiative and trust – and shows how new technology can support cultural change.

In close cooperation with Microsoft, more than 50 concrete use cases were identified in so-called ideation workshops – nine of them with particularly high business impact and quick implementability. An outstanding example is the Supply Risk Agent in procurement: a multi-agent system that analyzes internal and external data sources daily to identify risks in the supply chain at an early stage. Whether financial difficulties with suppliers or environmental disasters – the agent provides automated alerts that enable proactive action. “Previously, this was manual research,” says Ruskowski. “Today, we receive automated notifications and can react immediately.”

The benefits of Copilot are also evident in everyday work. Quote comparisons that used to take up to 45 minutes are now completed by Copilot in seconds. After vacation, employees can use a specially developed super prompt via Copilot to easily retrieve a summary of all relevant emails, Teams messages, and SharePoint updates – a real efficiency gain when returning to work.

In customer service, around 80 percent of inquiries are already automatically classified – the backlog has noticeably decreased. “Copilot helps us automate repetitive tasks and creates space for what really matters: creative, value-adding work,” says Hummel. “We don’t see AI just as a tool for cost reduction, but as a lever for transformation and sustainable competitive advantage.”

To drive the development of more complex AI solutions, tesa has established the Agent Factory – an internal competence center that, together with specialist departments and in close coordination with Microsoft, designs, develops, and scales new agents. This enables the implementation of demanding use cases – for example, by connecting external data sources or integrating into existing systems.

But tesa’s AI vision goes far beyond tactical optimizations. With a well-thought-out AI roadmap, the company is already preparing for the next development phase: systematic further development of existing AI applications, expansion of successful use cases to other business areas, and targeted development of AI-supported decision-making processes are the focus. “We have by no means exhausted the full potential of Copilot,” says Ruskowski. “But we are ready – and so are our employees.”

Founded in 1899, Rohto Pharmaceutical has produced and sold gastrointestinal medicines, eye drops, and topical drugs. Since 2000, it has expanded into skincare with brands such as Obagi, Hada Labo, and Melano CC. The company has also entered regenerative medicine, agriculture, and food services, delivering "well-being" to people and society through its core value of health.

Today, the group has over 100 subsidiaries and delivers products to more than 110 countries. Respecting local regulations, cultures, and values, Rohto emphasizes business development tailored to each market. As a result, the company’s enterprise resource planning (ERP) solutions were implemented and operated independently in each country, making it difficult to integrate supply chain management (SCM) and financial data across the group—a significant challenge for future growth. The company recognized the need for a unified core system that could generate synergy across regions and support global expansion.

Rohto chose Dynamics 365 for its ability to enable cross-functional SCM processes, its compatibility with Microsoft 365, and, crucially, its scalability, ensuring the company is positioned to grow and innovate as technology advances. With Microsoft Fabric as the interface, Rohto leverages a seamless, integrated foundation for connectivity. 

Respecting local growth, aiming for global expansion

Rohto has actively pursued global expansion, starting with the acquisition of Mentholatum in 1988. "We aim to generate international synergy while respecting local business growth, leading to future global expansion," says Mr. Yasumitsu Mori, General Manager of the Enterprise Information Systems Division. However, the previous core systems could not fully support these initiatives.

Ms. Kyoko Kino, Manager at the Global IT Center, explains, "Each country had its own ERP, resulting in siloed operations and information. Data was not integrated between ERPs, and sharing SCM and consolidated information required significant manual work. Reports submitted to headquarters lacked standardized formats, increasing workload and leading to person-dependent operations." To fundamentally solve these issues, Rohto began considering a global ERP in November 2020 and launched a dedicated project team in April 2021.

Devising a formula for success

Rohto’s unique corporate culture was at the root of its digital transformation design. As Mr. Yoshiki Masuda, Accounting Group Manager in the Accounting and Finance Division, explains, “Rohto Pharmaceutical has a culture of respecting the local customs and practices of each country, and of conducting business while carefully listening to local voices. For this project as well, we thoroughly engaged in ‘Sharing and Learning’ discussions, gathering input from major production and sales countries. This approach enabled us to gain a deep understanding of the situation in each country, which we then reflected in the design of our platform.” 

The result was a two-tier platform: “Tier 1” ERPs for each country and a globally integrated “Tier 2.” Not only was Dynamics 365 the superior choice for its cross-organizational SCM capabilities, adaptability, and strong integration with Microsoft 365 and Power Platform; it was cost-effective too.

Enhancing flexibility and data utilization

Mr. Tatsuya Maeda, Leader of the Development Team at the Global IT Center, Enterprise Information Systems Division, Rohto Pharmaceutical, explains, “A key focus of this implementation project was how to effectively utilize the information we collect. Even though we talk about ‘gathering data,’ it is by no means simple when each country has its own ERP. However, with Microsoft’s platform, everything from data transformation and management to subsequent utilization can be handled by Microsoft Fabric, allowing us to establish a simple, global data foundation.” 

The US Mentholatum Company became the first country to start the Tier 1 implementation project in January 2024. The rollout of Tier 2 and Microsoft Fabric began four months later. The company made the strategic decision to not roll out Tier 1 all at once. “Each country’s business environment, accuracy, and resource situation are different, so the timing of ERP migration must be optimized for each country,” says Ms. Kino. For the Tier 1 rollout, the team takes the time to fully understand the circumstances of each country and, through mutual learning, develops and executes implementation schedules tailored to local conditions.

But where Tier 1 is complete, the company is already seeing drastic changes in productivity and efficiency. “By implementing Dynamics 365, we are now able to collect information much more quickly. Data previously entered manually into the management accounting system is now integrated through transactions, reducing the time required for data entry by half,” says Mr. Masuda.

The next implementation site has already been decided, and the kickoff for the rollout project is planned. To ensure efficient and speedy deployment, the implementation in the US will serve as a core template, which will then be localized and rolled out to other countries.

 Unlocking the future with AI

As Rohto Pharmaceutical continues to expand its use of Microsoft Power Platform, it is also adopting Microsoft Copilot. By aggregating data in Dynamics 365, the company expects to enable future AI-driven initiatives and further accelerate business operations.

Rohto reduced data entry time by 50%, improved productivity, and established a foundation for AI-driven operations using Microsoft Copilot.

In the race to deliver seamless digital experiences, companies are searching for tools that not only measure customer behavior but also translate those insights into business growth. Few know this challenge better than Contentsquare, the Paris-based experience intelligence firm whose platform is used by 2,500 Enterprise brands and over a million websites worldwide to optimize user interactions.

As Contentsquare expanded globally, one problem persisted: reaching enterprise buyers at scale. The company had the technology, but without the right partner, its go-to-market motion risked stalling. In 2022, Contentsquare chose to deploy its platform on Microsoft Azure, using Azure’s cloud services and Microsoft Marketplace as the foundation for enterprise delivery.

The growth dilemma

Contentsquare’s technology was already in high demand, but enterprise sales cycles are long, complex, and often built on trusted vendor relationships.

“Even the best product doesn’t sell itself at the enterprise level,” said Mike Marzano, Global Head of Cloud, Data & Platform Alliances at Contentsquare. “We needed a cloud platform that could support scale, secure operations, and integrate easily into our customers’ digital environments.”

That urgency was amplified by the needs of Contentsquare’s core industries (retail, financial services, and telecommunications), where digital leaders are under pressure to deliver personalized and frictionless experiences. Yet, as Marzano noted, only 12% of digital and product leaders believe they’re providing customers with truly personalized, engaging experiences. “That means 88% of the market still sees a massive gap, and that’s the opportunity.”

Why Microsoft Marketplace makes sense

Three aspects of Microsoft Marketplace and Microsoft Azure proved critical for Contentsquare:

Scalable Infrastructure – Azure's global cloud infrastructure allowed Contentsquare to handle massive volumes of interaction data from millions of websites without latency or downtime.

AI & Data Services – Azure OpenAI, Azure Cognitive Services, and Azure Machine Learning enabled Contentsquare to enrich raw behavioral data with actionable insights, powering personalized recommendations at scale.

Marketplace & Integration – Listing on Microsoft Marketplace simplified procurement, standardized agreements, and streamlined integration into customer environments.

“Deploying on Azure wasn’t just about cloud hosting; it allowed us to leverage AI, machine learning, and global infrastructure to deliver the depth of insights our customers need,” Marzano said.

Leveraging Azure technology

By deploying its platform on Azure, Contentsquare enhanced its capabilities across multiple layers:

Data Ingestion & Storage – Using Azure Data Lake Analytics and Azure Synapse Analytics, Contentsquare captures and organizes every interaction in real-time (hovers, scrolls, clicks).

AI Enrichment – Azure Machine Learning and Azure Cognitive Services process behavioral and survey data to generate predictive insights, pinpointing the most impactful areas for optimization.

Security & Compliance – Azure's enterprise-grade security, compliance certifications, and data privacy tools allowed Contentsquare to meet stringent client requirements across global markets.

Accelerated Sales & Deployment – Microsoft Marketplace enabled faster adoption with standardized contracts, co-sell visibility, and financial incentives like Multi-Year Azure Consumption Commitments (MACCs), accelerating customer onboarding.

“The combination of AI services and scalable infrastructure on Azure enables Contentsquare the ability to deliver customer insights far beyond traditional web analytics,” Marzano explained. “It is actionable intelligence delivered at enterprise scale.”

What it all means for customers

For enterprise clients, the partnership delivers practical benefits: easier procurement through Microsoft Marketplace, access to sponsorship funds that make adoption cost-effective, and seamless integration with Microsoft’s broader ecosystem.

By using Contentsquare on Azure, businesses gain insights across every user interaction, enriched with AI and correlated with backend performance and survey data. This depth of analytics allows brands to act quickly on friction points, optimize journeys, and personalize experiences in real-time.

The road ahead

The momentum comes at a pivotal moment. Contentsquare recently announced its acquisition of Loris AI, a conversation intelligence company, signaling a push into analyzing real-time conversations alongside clicks and page views. 

Leveraging Azure’s AI and data services, this capability could redefine how businesses measure and manage customer experience across digital and conversational channels.

“With Azure, we have the infrastructure, AI capabilities, and global reach to scale rapidly and deliver new intelligence layers for our clients,” Marzano said. ”AI can help identify issues today, implement changes tomorrow, and revisit results the day after. That’s the future of digital experience.”

Jonathan Cherki, founder and CEO of Contentsquare, emphasized the importance of Azure for trust and long-term innovation. “Privacy is a very important pillar for Contentsquare. When we pick a partner, we need the highest level of security. Microsoft Azure delivers that, which is critical as we scale the future of digital.

Story Content:
For over a hundred years, Danone has played a pioneering role in bringing health through food to as many people as possible. With operations spanning over 120 countries, achieving competitiveness and fostering sustainable, profitable growth is essential to keep fulfilling this commitment—and innovation serves as one key pillar of reaching these goals. As part of a multi-year collaboration, the group has partnered with Microsoft to empower its employees with digital tools and skills they need to thrive in the new AI-driven economy, as well as integrate artificial intelligence (AI) across its operations. Erwin Logt, Group CIO at Danone, shares insights into the company's ongoing progress and strategic direction.

First milestones in AI adoption: Microsoft 365 Copilot global roll out

As an organization committed to people, Danone has aligned its digital transformation plan with its most valuable asset—the 90,000 employees worldwide. In 2024, the organization launched a program designed to upskill and reskill approximately 100,000 Danone employees to meet future job requirements and enhance talent attraction. This initiative highlighted a strong emphasis on enhancing personal productivity through AI, notably by deploying Microsoft 365 Copilot to over 50,000 employees, including 10,000 licenses distributed from day one. By automating routine tasks, employees were able to significantly reduce time spent on routine activities, thereby allowing greater emphasis on innovative and high-value tasks. The swift and large-scale implementation of Copilot demonstrated the immediate advantages of AI, serving as a catalyst for further organizational transformation.

Turning to Agentic AI for operational transformation 

"AI doesn’t sit still. It is challenging and reshaping our strategy," Logt highlights. Building on this momentum and the rapid advancement of AI, Danone consistently reviews and refines its transformation journey. The focus naturally shifted to Agentic AI while the technology is emerging—autonomous agents designed to streamline and enhance business processes. 

HR, Procurement and Shared Services emerged as primary topics at the forefront of this new transformation step. Previously, organizational changes such as promotions or new assignments required manual form-filling and coordination between managers and HR, often leading to errors and poor user experience. Danone leveraged its collaboration with Microsoft in AI to automate the HR process: managers now interact directly with an agent that pre-fills data, validates information, and ensures correct organizational structures, resulting in faster, more accurate, and more satisfying outcomes.

Order-to-cash optimization is an additional area where agents have the potential to effectively address and reduce process bottlenecks. Danone processes thousands of customer orders daily, received through various channels and formats—such as email, PDF, and Electronic Data Interchange —resulting in pricing inconsistencies and data entry errors. These issues frequently led to billing disputes, delayed payments, and put a strain on customer relationships.

Danone implemented an autonomous agent that enhances order processing. Powered by Microsoft Copilot Studio and integrated with Microsoft Collaborative suite such as Microsoft Teams, this agent analyzes all customer orders regardless of format and cross-references prices against internal systems such as ERP and promotional tools. It also proactively detects potential discrepancies so that any issues can be resolved before invoicing takes place. 

The autonomous agent goes beyond simple error detection, it provides actionable recommendations, suggests tailor pricing adjustments, and can even generate professional email drafts to help employees quickly resolve pricing issues with clients. 

The approach has led to notable gains in Danone’s procurement process. Automated validation workflows have sped up order handling and sharply reduced billing disputes. Payment delays have also dropped, improving cash flow. Beyond these achievements, it fosters an integrated workspace where AI precision enhances human judgment, leading to greater efficiency while maintaining strong, personal customer connections. 

From hype to impact: how Danone turns AI ambitions into real business value

"What's exciting is when I visit the many markets of Danone, I see Agentic AI really coming to life - how we leverage it in marketing, in engaging consumers, in better understanding our patients, in transforming Research & Innovation, in operations," Logt says. Danone’s approach to AI success centers on the prioritization process that begins with aligning AI initiatives to the company’s digital and commercial strategies. This ensures every project is relevant to core business goals. “We managed to embrace that excitement for AI, funnel it and focus it more on two or three key priorities,” he highlights.

Early in the ideation process, Danone determines if an idea can be implemented on a large scale in different markets and factories. The company also reviews technical feasibility, data maturity, process harmonization, and readiness for change to ensure it only invests in projects that can be successfully adopted and expanded. By focusing on a small number of high-impact priorities, Danone secures executive sponsorship, financial resources, and broad employee adoption, ultimately ensuring that AI delivers concrete P&L impact and supports the company’s long-term transformation.

Driving organizational change: skilling and adoption

Danone’s approach to digital transformation goes beyond technology. By integrating digital transformation with a human-centric approach, the company is leveraging AI and data to enhance decision-making while maintaining its commitment to wellbeing, equity, and purpose. "Transforming the culture, building the capabilities and truly generating digital and a data savvy organization within Danone can only go through the Danone x Microsoft partnership". By launching initiatives such as the Danone Microsoft AI Academy, the organization intends to equip employees with the necessary skills and confidence to use new technologies and services. It offers a wide range of learning opportunities aimed at boosting AI literacy and fosters a dynamic, inclusive environment for developing expertise. "We don't only deploy Copilot because of the impact on productivity. We also deploy Copilot because it is a way for our employees to experience and to learn about AI," Logt highlights.

 "What really excites me is to think about what we are doing with AI today and extrapolating that to see how we can better serve our customers in the near future, " he concludes. Danone’s journey demonstrates how clear vision, strategic partnerships, and a commitment to people can turn AI from a buzzword into a powerful driver of business transformation while maintaining its commitment to responsible AI development.
