Safeguarding the products we trust 

Groundbreaking inventions may keep the world turning, but safety is nonnegotiable. Innovators have turned to TÜV SÜD since 1866 to navigate the complex quality and regulatory landscape that protects consumers. As a trusted partner to businesses the world over, TÜV SÜD ensures that everything from children’s toys to infrastructure and digital products are designed to be safe, sustainable, and of the highest quality. TÜV SÜD issues certificates to ensure product quality, creating a safer, more sustainable tomorrow from more than 1,000 locations around the globe. 

Unifying security for simplicity and safety

TÜV SÜD’s safety commitment has been a cornerstone of its existence from day one. That assurance extends to its digital environment. “We approach information security holistically: technology, processes, and people working together. And Microsoft is one of our strategic cybersecurity vendors,” says Norbert Vetter, CISO at TÜV SÜD. The company’s confidence in Microsoft Security solutions began with the Microsoft Defender suite. “We protect the identities, data, and devices of about 28,000 employees with Microsoft Defender solutions,” says Karsten Bode, Enterprise Security Architect at TÜV SÜD. He’s referring to Microsoft Defender for Identity, Defender XDR, and Defender for Endpoint, respectively. TÜV SÜD deployed Microsoft Sentinel as its security information and event management (SIEM) system. Bode explains, “Microsoft Sentinel fulfills strict regulatory requirements in all our datacenters. It’s a dynamic SIEM that delivers visibility across our global locations. The potential to automate security tasks with playbooks is a big step forward.”

Amping up team effectiveness with Security Copilot

Bode was immediately intrigued with Microsoft Security Copilot. “We joined the early adopter program for Security Copilot,” he explains. “The product evolution was amazing.” Productivity immediately surged by 60% to 70%. Bode continues, “The embedded Security Copilot makes life easier for me. Its convenient interface makes it easy to go deeper into the situation or choose to start a remediation action directly from the sidebar. That’s what I appreciate about this solution.”

Both experienced and new security analysts jump-start their productivity with automation. “No two people document their investigations in the same way. But with Security Copilot, we have consistent reporting that everyone can easily understand,” Bode points out. “And it’s also easier to get enriched data, like additional information about the IP address from which a threat originates. We can view the information graphically, in a table, or in the way that makes the most sense for that situation.”

New analysts gain skills more quickly, thanks to the Copilot automation that uses their prompts to create detailed queries. “After using Security Copilot for three months, a new analyst who began without any security skills has a very solid knowledge base and is an effective team member,” affirms Bode.

Forging ahead with automation

In an era of increasingly dynamic threats and a scarcity of skilled security professionals, TÜV SÜD isn’t just keeping up—it’s making gains on overall security, and on analyst productivity and effectiveness. “We have a holistic view of our environment with Microsoft Security solutions. Faster intelligence from Security Copilot means I can act faster. That’s a huge advantage,” says Bode. He looks forward to further Copilot automation. “My advice is to go ahead with this wonderful solution,” he continues. “Bring security to the next level with AI integration. We’re beginning to deploy other Copilot solutions, and I’m looking forward to a more secure future.” 

Vetter agrees and concludes, “We analyze results about 60% to 70% faster with Security Copilot. It plays a central role in our ability to speed up threat analyses and activities, fundamentally reducing the risks for our IT landscape worldwide.”

KakaoBank is Korea’s leading internet-only bank and a pioneer in mobile banking. Living up to its motto, “A New Beginning for Banking,” KakaoBank has spearheaded IT-driven innovation in the Korean financial industry and is now ushering in a new wave of transformation in the AI era. In 2024, KakaoBank opened a dedicated AI data center as part of its preparations, and in collaboration with Microsoft, it launched Korea’s first Azure OpenAI-powered conversational AI Search service in May 2025, followed by the release of its AI Financial Calculator service in June. These services, designed to enhance customer convenience and improve financial accessibility, align closely with KakaoBank’s vision of becoming “my personal bank, easier and more frequent to use in daily life.”

The First Conversational AI Search and Financial Calculator Services in the Korean Financial Sector

On May 26, 2025, KakaoBank launched its Azure OpenAI-powered AI Search service within its mobile app. Customers can now ask natural, conversational questions about KakaoBank services or general financial knowledge, and receive AI-generated answers that include related service links, original content, and even follow-up question suggestions, all in one place. Questions related to KakaoBank’s products and services are answered based on documents prepared in advance by KakaoBank to ensure higher accuracy, while inquiries about general financial knowledge are addressed using generative AI.

The AI Search service is one of the two in-app mobile services KakaoBank developed under Korea’s Financial Services Commission's Innovative Financial Services designation, enabling customers to easily access financial information in a mobile environment and seamlessly transition to related services. The other service, also built on Azure OpenAI’s generative AI, is the AI Financial Calculator.

Launched on June 23, 2025, the AI Financial Calculator allows customers to easily calculate interest on major deposit products, determine required contributions for savings goals, estimate loan interest and borrowing limits, calculate early repayment fees, and access exchange rates for 12 major currencies, including value comparisons between foreign currencies and the Korean won, as well as overseas remittance estimates. All responses are provided by generative AI, enabling customers to conveniently plan and make informed financial decisions directly within the KakaoBank mobile app. 

K.K. Seo, Leader of Conversational AI Service Team at KakaoBank, commented on the initial performance of these two AI services:

"First of all, we are seeing a substantial improvement in customer experience, as evidenced by increased transactions. The customer click-through rate to product pages from the AI Search service is as high as 30%, which is a remarkable achievement."

Innovation through Collaboration with Microsoft and Azure OpenAI

Zane Kim, Manager of AI Technology Strategy Team at KakaoBank, explained the background and process of collaborating with Microsoft in developing these two AI services:

“The financial sector faces strict restrictions on cloud-based services. But being designated as an Innovative Financial Service let us experiment in a regulatory sandbox. This let us use Microsoft’s Azure OpenAI API and build on their proven performance and stability. Microsoft’s technical excellence and agile support were a tremendous help.”

In developing AI-based services, stability is critical, but cost is also an important practical consideration. Microsoft offers Azure OpenAI customers the ability to allocate throughput based on Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs), providing predictable costs, with options for monthly and annual reservations to reduce overall spending through flexible billing.

Jiwook Lim, Manager of AI Product Development Team at KakaoBank, praised the answer quality and reliability of Azure OpenAI models:

“Above all, the answer quality of the OpenAI models was exceptional. And it was particularly attractive that Microsoft’s PTU offering ensured we could maintain this level of quality and performance in a stable way. In addition, integrating with various Azure services significantly enhanced the overall stability of the services KakaoBank launched.”

Meanwhile, Alan Choi, Digital Specialist at Microsoft supporting KakaoBank’s AI service development, shared his perspective on the collaboration:

“At Microsoft, we value security as much as service quality. When new services launch or updates reach customers, we communicate quickly and work on improvements. We hope KakaoBank’s AI services will be firmly established and look forward to supporting their evolution while fostering growth for both companies.”

KakaoBank’s Roadmap for AI-Driven Financial Service Innovation

K.K. Seo stated that the launch of the AI Search and AI Financial Calculator services marks an important milestone in KakaoBank’s roadmap for AI-driven financial service innovation:

“As AI advances, we expect more diverse services to emerge. Our AI Search and Financial Calculator lay the foundation. While we now focus on KakaoBank’s products, we aim to support broader aspects of our customers’ financial lives. Ultimately, we seek to grow beyond a banking app into a ‘comprehensive financial platform,’ with AI at the core.”

KakaoBank plans to leverage its close partnership with Microsoft to actively utilize stable cloud infrastructure and advanced AI technologies, driving ongoing customer-centric innovation. Through these efforts, KakaoBank aims to establish itself as the most trusted digital financial partner throughout customers’ financial journeys and continue contributing to improving financial accessibility nationwide.

KakaoBank, a leader in mobile banking, is accelerating AI-driven financial service innovation by launching Korea’s first Azure OpenAI-powered conversational AI Search service in May 2025, followed by its AI Financial Calculator service in June.
Through KakaoBank’s mobile app, customers can now ask questions in natural language and instantly access AI-powered responses on product and service information, financial knowledge, and currency or interest rate calculations, with direct navigation to related services.
KakaoBank’s AI services are built ensuring proven stability and cost efficiency, and have significantly enhanced customer experience from the moment of launch. Modernize, satisfy, and stabilize with IT

In 2022, Grupo Dalton was at a pivotal moment. The company, one of the most prominent automotive groups in the country, was amid expansion: from 17 dealerships, it projected sustained growth that would soon surpass 30, including its first operations in the United States. However, the IT department faced opportunities for improvement in modernizing its infrastructure, addressing legacy processes, and with little focus or priority on serving internal customers. All of this affected the agility needed to set up everything required for each new dealership opening.

With this assessment, and by direct mandate from the President, in 2023 José Manuel Solis Martinez took over as IT Director with a clear challenge: radically transform the department. His plan was to outline a six-year strategy (2023–2029) based on three pillars—stabilize operations, modernize technology infrastructure, and raise internal customer satisfaction—with concrete goals, such as resolving 95% of incidents in less than 24 hours and achieving 97% satisfaction on every completed ticket.

"We began a profound transformation that, after a year and a half, culminated in a key decision: choosing Microsoft Dynamics 365 as our new ERP platform and strategic technology partner for the future of Grupo Dalton. Currently, we are in the middle of the implementation process, moving step by step towards the consolidation of this transformation," says Solis Martinez, IT Director at Grupo Dalton and General Manager of NOVACTI, the group’s technology division, which now operates as a Microsoft partner.

From manual to automation: Shifting to do more with less

For Grupo Dalton, embracing digital transformation was not just a technological decision. It was an urgent response to a more dynamic, demanding, and customer-oriented environment, where maintaining physical and fragmented processes was no longer a viable option.

 At the same time, a strategic dilemma emerged: should the pre-owned car division remain under the traditional dealership model or evolve into an independent digital operation? The pandemic accelerated this reflection. In a context where consumers were increasingly demanding and technology was advancing rapidly, it became clear that continuing with an analog model would not allow them to compete effectively.

The inspiration was clear: digital-native models were redefining the pre-owned vehicle sector, proving it was possible to operate with agility, scalability, and an experience centered on omnichannel engagement.

“We needed to drive a paradigm shift: move from processes that were 90% physical and fragmented to a digital-first structure. It wasn’t just about adopting technology, but about redesigning operations so that customer service could flow seamlessly between physical and digital channels without losing the human touch,” recalls Jalil Daher, Divisional Director of Grupo Dalton Seminuevos.

This led to the creation of a new technology-based unit, capable of offering a frictionless experience throughout the buying and selling process. Omnichannel became an operational necessity in the face of multiple touchpoints, interdependent processes, and rising expectations. The goal was clear: leave behind outdated systems and build a modern, agile, and connected architecture. Speed of response, real-time analytics, and scalability became key to staying competitive. With this vision, the search for strategic technology partners began—a journey that ultimately led to Microsoft.

97% of incidents resolved in under 20 hours and USD350,000 saved

Digital transformation was also cultural. Starting in 2024, the IT department redefined its purpose—not just as an operational area, but as a strategic driver of internal service. A proactive support culture was adopted, with personalized follow-up, empathy, and shared responsibility, achieving resolution of 97% of incidents in less than 20 hours and maintaining a satisfaction rate above 97.5%. These indicators reflect not only a cultural shift, but also tangible economic benefits: less downtime, greater productivity, and lower technical support costs. “Information is power, and today the company has power because it has information in real time,” says Juan Carlos Chidan, General Director of the Automotive Division.

In this context, the implementation of Microsoft Power BI was fundamental for providing immediate visibility into the performance of each business unit and enabling informed decisions in seconds. Jalil Daher summarizes it this way: “Before, months would pass between data analysis and decision making. Today, with Power BI, we react in real time. If we detect that the market is cooling due to a drop in leads or reservations, we instantly adjust prices based on model, mileage, or inventory age. That speed makes the difference between winning and losing.”

Antonio García, Grupo Dalton’s CFO, affirms, “Without concrete data, decisions are based on feelings. Today, with BI dashboards, every morning I review sales, credit lines, and overdue accounts. Without that, I don’t know where I stand.”

The transformation was made possible thanks to the partnership with its technology division, which supported software development, data integration, the use of AI, and the implementation of Dynamics 365, which is now the core of the group’s new ERP.

“Thanks to the support of NOVACTI and more efficient management of licenses and services, Grupo Dalton accumulated nearly USD350,000 in additional savings from technology solutions,” adds Solis Martinez.

Migrate 99% of infrastructure to Microsoft Azure

Grupo Dalton set ambitious goals: eliminate support tickets, go paperless, migrate 99.9% of its infrastructure to Microsoft Azure, and incorporate AI as a key tool for its leaders.

They chose the cloud because opening new operations—especially abroad—used to take too long. With Azure and their new technology division (NOVACTI), they can now expand more quickly and reduce the number of vendors, which has generated savings. All their applications, including security tools like Microsoft Sentinel and Microsoft Defender, now run on Microsoft cloud technology. This has allowed them to optimize costs and achieve significant economic benefits.

At the same time, the IT team is about to implement a long-awaited ERP system to strengthen operational stability. AI is also gaining prominence: they are creating digital advisors with Microsoft Copilot Studio, which improves efficiency and the customer experience.

Instead of investing in renewing obsolete hardware (planned for March 2025), they accelerated their digital transformation. The automotive division migrated to the cloud in 2024, and the real estate and corporate areas will do so in 2025. This change allowed them to save around USD100,000.

A unified, scalable, AI-powered platform

With expansion in mind, Grupo Dalton defined a robust technology strategy to consolidate its operations into a single digital ecosystem. Although each division currently operates with different tools—all based on Microsoft technology—the goal is to unify processes, data, and platforms under a common architecture built on Dynamics 365.

The company is progressing in the development of specialized verticals for each business line—new cars, used cars, real estate, corporate, and soon financial—connected in real time and powered by standardized data. This architecture will eventually allow its US subsidiary to be integrated under the same accounting system.

Collaboration with NOVACTI remains key, both in the implementation of Dynamics 365 and in the development of customized solutions tailored to business needs. With tools like Microsoft Power Apps, Power BI, and Microsoft Fabric, dashboards, automated workflows, and data warehouses have been created to enhance operational accuracy.

AI is already part of daily operations: from bots developed with Copilot Studio to proprietary predictive models for price management, marking the beginning of a new era of analytical autonomy.

Next steps include a complete overhaul of internet infrastructure, improved connectivity, ERP consolidation, and maintaining high standards of efficiency and satisfaction. “Dalton is a company born out of transformation. Our case is an example of transformation with a guiding principle: the customer,” emphasizes Juan Carlos Rodriguez Villava, CEO of Dalton Motors USA.

Grupo Dalton is betting that technology will not only support its expansion but also enable it to do so more efficiently, with lower investment and better sustainable results over time.

For over a century, Amey has been keeping the UK’s infrastructure and public services running safely and sustainably. It is committed to driving even greater progress in the decade ahead, supporting the country’s journey to net zero. At the heart of this ambition is a bold vision to integrate AI agents into core business processes, unlocking new ways to work, empowering employees and solving real-world challenges with greater speed, intelligence and impact.

Connecting the dots between challenges and technology

Amey is building innovative, future-ready technology solutions to tackle tomorrow’s challenges head-on, delivering resilient, sustainable infrastructure, enhancing lives and protecting our shared future.

“We touch around 75% of people’s lives in the UK every day,” says Andy Richards, Chief Digital Information Officer (CDIO) at Amey. “With our solutions, we’re supporting the country in delivering services that truly matter.”

With this kind of impact, Amey’s vision goes beyond addressing surface-level complexities. The organisation is focused on uncovering root causes and shaping solutions that last. This mindset sparks a powerful question: how many of today’s challenges could be solved by embedding AI directly into day-to-day operations?

“There are always things that could be done better and more efficiently. We set out to connect the dots, identifying real problems and applying the right technology to solve them,” explains Damian Bell, AI and Power Platform Lead at Amey

Productivity is just the beginning

Amey’s journey with AI started with a limited rollout of Microsoft 365 Copilot to business users.

“Through our use of Copilot, we recognised early on that it delivers real business value,” reflects Damian Bell. “It opens up new ways to address issues we hadn’t been able, or aware enough, to solve before.”

The impact was immediate, especially for workers spending their days behind a screen. From writing up meeting notes to managing inboxes, chasing actions and producing reports, Copilot alleviates the weight of routine work.

Damian Bell adds, “Instead of spending hours in emails and documents, people suddenly have access to powerful out-of-the-box productivity tools that remove friction and free up their focus.”

This early success prompted a wider rollout of the tool and validated a bigger ambition: to move beyond individual productivity and explore how AI could solve more complex, specific challenges. That’s where AI agents come in.

Powering progress with SharePoint agents

Amey operates in high-risk environments, so safety is always a top priority. Field teams often work on roads, railways and complex facilities in challenging weather conditions, where fast, reliable access to information can make all the difference.

Damian Bell explains, “As an organisation, our core focus is to keep people safe and make sure they go home fit and well at the end of the day.”

To support and safeguard its frontline teams, Amey rethought how safety information is delivered, developing a SharePoint agent that places essential procedures at employees’ fingertips, anytime and anywhere.

“We’re a data-rich organisation, with 99% of our information stored across SharePoint sites,” adds Damian Bell. “Accessing the right file at the right moment can be difficult. So, we built an agent that sits in people's pockets and allows them to interact directly with the safety documentation.”

With this agent, frontline workers can now retrieve information instantly and in any preferred language, making their work safer, more efficient and more responsive in real-time situations.

Patric Collier, Highways Electrical Team Leader at Amey, highlights this, “Using agents in SharePoint makes my job 100% safer. Problems can be solved a lot quicker compared to using paperwork and other tools.”

Collaboration at the core of breakthrough

Amey’s progress with agents has been accelerated by close, cross-functional collaboration with Microsoft and the Microsoft partner FOIL AI.

“Microsoft has always been our platform of choice. Outlook, Teams and SharePoint are deeply embedded in how we work,” says Damian Bell. “Just as importantly, we know that with Microsoft, everything stays within a single security boundary. That gives us peace of mind and makes everything simpler.”

Amey’s longstanding relationship with Microsoft brings far more than tools. It offers access to trusted experts, secure infrastructure and early innovation programmes like Co-Innovation Lab, where Amey collaborates directly with Microsoft engineers to explore and solve complex business challenges.

Tony Rigby, Chief Technology Officer (CTO) at Amey adds, “We’ve been on the journey with Microsoft for over 10 years. From the start, we knew it was a true win–win partnership. We’re embracing Microsoft’s expertise and best practices to ensure long-term success and sustained innovation.”

FOIL AI also plays a vital role. As a trusted technology partner, it brings deep AI expertise and a collaborative mindset that aligns with Amey’s ambitions. “It takes a certain type of organisation with trust and bravery from senior leadership to capitalise on change whilst ensuring human centric innovation,” says Simon Turner, FOIL AI Chief Technology Officer. “This is exactly what we have seen from Amey, and together with our partners at Microsoft, the team has pushed the boundaries of what we thought possible. The end result is not just exciting technically but also has a positive impact on the people using it.”

Fernanda Souza, AI Adoption Lead at Amey, explains further, “The technology landscape is constantly evolving, and with Microsoft and FOIL AI, we’re keeping pace with that change. Together, we’re staying ahead of the curve and pushing innovation forward.”

Innovation starts with mindset

Amey believes meaningful change starts with people, empowered to think differently and shape what comes next.

To encourage that mindset across the organisation, Amey launched a company-wide initiative run in Microsoft Teams, inviting employees to share how they’re using AI or automation in their daily work. One standout idea came from Muhammad, a part of Amey’s Neurodiversity Affinity Network. He uses Copilot to decode complex or nuanced emails, helping better understand tone, intent and social cues.

“When you're neurodivergent, navigating a world built for neurotypical communication is challenging,” says Muhammad Najm-ul-Hassan, Business Support Coordinator at Amey. “For me, Copilot acts as a friendly, unbiased guide, helping me find clarity in conversations with nuanced communication styles and structuring my thoughts so I can express myself with confidence.”

Damian Bell admits, “It wasn’t a problem I’d ever considered until the campaign surfaced it. But now we’re turning Copilot into a sophisticated accessibility agent to help others too.”

And there’s more to come. From connecting agents in intelligent workflows to orchestrating new, scalable use cases, Amey is just getting started.

“We’re definitely thinking outside the box. Linking agents together in a chain, with orchestration on top, takes it to another level,” reflects Tony Rigby. “The possibilities are endless. And for us, we’re only at the tip of the iceberg.”

What’s next: scale with purpose

With a mindset of exploration, adaptability and continuous learning, the organisation sees AI not as a goal, but as an evolving opportunity.

Having laid its foundations with Microsoft 365, Copilot and leveraging tools like Power Platform to streamline manual processes and reduce operational friction across the business, Amey is building on that success. The organisation has progressed to use Copilot Studio to create tailored, AI-powered agents. Now, Amey is focused on scaling adoption, deepening impact and expanding the reach of intelligent tools.

Damian Bell enthuses, “We want to build AI literacy across the organisation. Because when people see what’s been built, they start imagining what they could do – and they can do even more.”

“We’re now exploring which other parts of the business we can support with agents,” adds Fernanda Souza. “We’re eager to give people back their time, so instead of repetitive work, they can focus on building new skillsets, doing meaningful work and driving ideas forward.”

Looking ahead, Amey will continue to expand its use of Microsoft solutions, exploring new capabilities, collaborating with experts and embedding AI even deeper in the way it works.

“We’re stepping into the pro-developer space now, bringing in more Microsoft advanced tools,” says Damian Bell. “Every challenge we face is a chance to build something smarter. With Microsoft and FOIL AI, we’re not simply reacting – we’re shaping how problems get solved through agents that work in the real world.”

Founded in 1782, Phoenix Group is one of the largest long-term savings and retirement businesses in the UK. More than two centuries on and a few name, location, and product changes later, one thing has remained constant – their purpose of helping people secure a life of possibilities.

Phoenix Group always has one eye on the future. That’s why they launched a digital transformation program, aimed at improving internal processes and delivering the innovative experience customers expect today – such as their pension management app and online pension calculator.

To support these ambitions, Phoenix Group is partnering with Microsoft, adopting Microsoft Dev Box and GitHub Copilot to rapidly onboard developers and empower them to build solutions more efficiently.

Matthew Griffiths, Head of Cloud at Phoenix Group, illustrates this drive for change, “We want to give our developers and engineers a good experience. We want them to join Phoenix, have the tools to do their job and focus on adding value.”

Transforming the developer experience

By implementing Microsoft Dev Box, a cloud workstation platform built for development teams, Phoenix Group enabled developers to rapidly spin up workstations with pre-configured tools and source code, allowing them to start projects immediately. With seamless integration into Microsoft Azure and Microsoft Intune, administrators can extend policies and optimise resources, ensuring each workstation remains secure and cost-efficient.

Matthew Buchanan, Principal Platform Engineer, explains, “Our aim was to make the onboarding process even smoother and get people up and running faster. Dev Box has enabled this and delivered a powerful change for us. Now, we can put more control into the hands of the developers who are actually using these services.”

With instant access to customised cloud workstations, developer onboarding has dramatically reduced from up to one month to just one day, enabling Phoenix Group to hire more experienced developers, reduce reliance on third parties and build more complex applications at pace.

Andy Furness, Systems Infrastructure Architect, adds, “Onboarding new developers so they can write code on the afternoon of their first day – instead of three to four weeks later – is a real big shift. On one project, the process of preparing and transferring files to a third party would’ve taken days. Now we can do it ourselves in minutes.”

As an all-in-one platform, Dev Box supports multiple environments on one machine, reducing context-switching and boosting efficiency. It also offers modern security and authentication, eliminating the need for multiple passwords.

Driving even more results with GitHub Copilot

To further support its developers, Phoenix Group is also adopting GitHub Copilot, an AI-powered coding assistant, that acts as a pair programmer to enhance productivity. Integrated seamlessly into text editors like Visual Studio, it provides in-project code suggestions, along with chat and review features. This allows developers to write code faster, fix vulnerabilities automatically and do it all with greater accuracy.

Matthew Griffiths highlights its value, “GitHub Copilot enables our developers to do their job well. The main benefits we’re seeing are around developer productivity, efficiency and heavy lifting. Although we’re relatively early in our adoption journey, those using it have told me they are delighted.”

By delivering instant code suggestions, GitHub Copilot accelerates in-house development. Developers complete tasks more quickly and focus on meaningful work, improving both job satisfaction and employee engagement. It’s empowering teams and inspiring innovation across Phoenix Group.

Elevating modernisation without increasing costs

As cloud-based solutions, both Microsoft Dev Box and GitHub Copilot integrated smoothly with Phoenix Group’s existing multi-cloud estate, allowing fast deployment, minimal downtime and immediate return on investment.

Matthew Buchanan adds, “With Dev Box, the software's always at the latest release, which is fantastic. It’s also very easy to stay up to date in terms of connectivity.” He continues, “There would normally be challenges preventing us from adopting solutions like Copilot, but these have been removed now. We never could’ve achieved this in a legacy desktop environment.”

These tools also support Phoenix Group’s broader commercial IT strategy, with no upfront costs or on-premises maintenance required.

Firing up innovation to deliver value

Phoenix Group sees a bright future for technology in the organisation. Adopting Microsoft Dev Box and GitHub Copilot has opened the door to faster innovation, enabling the company to roll out mobile apps and digital tools months earlier, enhancing the customer experience.

Following this success, Phoenix Group is expanding its rollout of Dev Box and GitHub Copilot to other technical teams, enhancing coding capabilities and encouraging greater collaboration. The company is also exploring new features in Dev Box, including Windows Subsystem for Linux, to support developers with even more flexibility.

James Head, Head of Capital Markets Transformation, concludes, “Adopting Microsoft Dev Box and GitHub Copilot has given us a great springboard to continue to innovate and develop new solutions internally.”

In a bold move to shape the future of collaboration and redefine employee engagement, Aviva, the UK's leading diversified insurer, has partnered with Microsoft to help transform its business. With over 20 million customers, Aviva's commitment to innovation and excellence is paramount. “AI will absolutely shape the future of how each and every one of us work, and how a customer experiences their engagement with Aviva,” says Sarah Self, GenAI Director at Aviva.

Strategic imperatives

Aviva's four key strategic pillars - customer, growth, efficiency and sustainability - are at the heart of this transformation. By leveraging cutting-edge AI and technology, including Microsoft Azure and GitHub Copilot, Aviva aims to improve customer service, boost productivity and enhance workplace enjoyment, by allowing colleagues to focus on more complex tasks and provide support to customers.  

A partnership for the future

Microsoft has been a pivotal partner in Aviva's journey, providing scalable, effective and resilient technology solutions. Over the past few years, this collaboration has seen Aviva modernise its physical legacy hosting platform, transitioning to the cloud with great success. 

“We have to work with really strong strategic partners who provide us with scalable, effective, resilient technology. And that's what Microsoft has been doing with us over the last couple of years,” reflects Sarah Self.

Cloud technology and Bamboo migration

Aviva has successfully moved its main policy system, Bamboo, to Microsoft Azure — one of the largest migrations of its kind. This move has made customer data more secure and resilient, while also boosting performance. Response times are now 80% faster, with quotes from comparison sites coming through in under five seconds. Overall system performance has improved by 30%, helping teams work more efficiently.  

Operational wins

Aviva have made big improvements in how they process their customer data. Tasks like renewals, cancellations, and generating documents are now handled up to four times faster. That means important customer transactions are completed much more quickly and efficiently. “We've delivered capability across hundreds of our claims handlers, which shorten the call length, reduce the amount of time a customer is on hold, and enhance personalisation in the conversation with that customer,” comments Sarah Self.

Positive feedback and future innovations

Aviva's colleagues have praised the new technology, and the company is not stopping here. Plans are underway to integrate further innovations, such as Microsoft Copilot Studio. A proof of concept for GitHub Copilot, involving 150 users across various technology platforms and coding languages, has already shown immediate efficiency gains and fostered collaboration. As a result of the success of the proof of concept, GitHub Copilot has now been rolled out to 1750 users. “The impact on efficiency was almost instantaneous for us. There was a lot of collaboration between teams to use GitHub Copilot in many different and innovative ways,” shares Gurinder Parmar.  

A collaborative path to excellence

Aviva's partnership with Microsoft is more than just a business alliance; it's a journey of innovation and excellence. Together, they are set to revolutionise customer experience, ensuring that Aviva remains at the forefront of the industry. With a shared vision and unwavering commitment, the future looks bright for Aviva and its millions of customers.

Story Content:
On average, a clinician gets a scant 10 minutes to gather detailed information about health history, symptoms, exams, and test results when meeting with a patient It's a race against time, where crucial facts can be easily missed.

This all-too-common scenario creates care gaps in which many patients are left undiagnosed, misdiagnosed, miscoded, and without the care they need. With up to 90% of patients with rare and prevalent hard-to-diagnose conditions falling into these care gaps, an alarming percentage of the world's population is currently left untreated or under-treated.

Pangaea Data: Closing care gaps

With offices in South San Francisco and London, Pangaea Data provides an Al-powered platform for the healthcare and pharmaceutical industries, focusing on closing the care gaps that can cause patient care to be delayed-or come too late.

Pangaea's platform applies Al to analyze patient health records based on clinical guidelines, thus emulating a clinician's manual review, to uncover information and knowledge buried in medical records and find untreated and under-treated patients. This enables clinicians to take timely, informed action at the point of care. The platform is deployed behind the health system's firewall and seamlessly integrates with electronic health record (EHR) and scheduling systems, ensuring privacy compliance and no disruption to existing workflows.

To achieve its growth goals, Pangaea needed to scale rapidly and reach more healthcare customers. Built on Azure, Pangaea's platform is automatically accessible to any Azure customer through the Microsoft marketplace. By adopting the marketplace, Pangaea streamlined procurement and sales processes-freeing up time and resources to focus on innovation rather than administrative overhead.

Speeding sales, boosting security

Pangaea needed a solution that would give them access to an expanded pool of healthcare and pharmaceutical customers, and as part of the Pegasus program, the company entered the Microsoft marketplace to increase its market reach.

Security and privacy was a top concern for Pangaea, enabling them to continue to meet stringent, evolving healthcare compliance standards. Another priority was reducing the length of the sales cycle. On average, the process for healthcare companies onboarding a new vendor can take 6-9 months, so Pangaea looked to Microsoft marketplace as a way to streamline traditional procurement and onboarding processes. "For healthcare companies, the procurement process takes about six to nine months because there is a lot of information that must be exchanged," said Vibhor Gupta, Founder of Pangaea Data. 'With the marketplace, that's already been done in the background, and they can get access to Pangaea's platform in just a few clicks."

Partnering with Microsoft 

The company’s partnership with Microsoft grew organically out of the increasing use of Microsoft Azure by Pangaea’s customer base—particularly in the healthcare sector. Pangaea enhances its platform’s features with advanced Azure-based AI tools and services, including Azure OpenAI Service, which provides powerful natural language processing and reasoning capabilities; Azure Machine Learning, enabling continuous model training and iterative improvements to the system; and Azure AI Foundry to provide a robust environment for building and testing new AI-driven features.

Because many of Pangaea’s healthcare customers already use Microsoft Azure, the alignment with Microsoft made it significantly easier for Pangaea to deploy their platform directly into each customer’s existing Azure environment, streamlining integration with customers’ existing systems and ensuring no disruption to workflows.

The Microsoft partnership helps Pangaea advance its imperatives around privacy and compliance, security, innovation, and scalability. Azure’s HIPAA-compliant infrastructure aligns with the strict privacy requirements of the healthcare industry, enabling Pangaea to deploy their platform behind the firewall of health systems, ensuring that no sensitive patient data leaves the organization’s secure environment.

Using tools within Azure AI Foundry, Pangaea rapidly innovates and expands their platform capabilities—releasing new features based on real-time feedback and performance data. Azure also provides an integrated pathway to reach new customers and grow Pangaea’s platform’s market presence. With these capabilities, Pangaea can now deploy a full platform environment for a customer in just 30 minutes.

Scaling smarter with Microsoft marketplace

By introducing their platform on the Microsoft marketplace, Pangaea dramatically simplified deployment for healthcare and pharmaceutical customers. The robust Azure capabilities enabled faster implementation with minimal disruption to customer environments, dramatically reducing setup and configuration times. This accelerated deployment has been especially valuable in the healthcare sector, where agility and compliance are critical.

“Microsoft marketplace has become our preferred platform to close deals. It's faster for the customer, and it's faster for us,” stated Jingqing Zhang, PhD, Head of AI, Pangaea Data.

As demand for AI-driven healthcare solutions increases, the Microsoft marketplace helps Pangaea scale their platform more efficiently. Having their platform on the Microsoft marketplace unlocked new visibility and revenue potential for Pangaea. Being vetted and endorsed by Microsoft gave immediate credibility with customers, and the marketplace made Pangaea’s platform discoverable to hundreds of potential healthcare and pharmaceutical customers. In fact, Pangaea landed a customer just eight weeks after going live—a stark contrast to the traditional six- to nine-month healthcare vendor onboarding cycle.

By purchasing through the marketplace, Pangaea customers bypass time-consuming procurement processes, fulfill their MACC commitments, and standardize purchasing on a single platform—all of which contribute to faster revenue recognition and enhanced customer satisfaction. The co-selling support provided through the partnership further amplified Pangaea’s reach, with Microsoft account executives proactively introducing Pangaea’s platform to health systems and pharmaceutical companies. 

Together, these marketplace benefits have enabled the company to achieve operational efficiency, accelerated sales, and scalable growth, supporting Pangaea’s mission of delivering tools that close care gaps in the healthcare and pharma sectors. Zhang confirms this, stating that, “using the Microsoft marketplace, we're making our platform more available to our customers, enabling clinicians to focus their time engaging directly with patients and improving their outcomes.”

AUDI AG is known worldwide for redefining what's possible in automotive design, and that same spirit of innovation drives its internal operations. As employee expectations for fast, seamless access to information grew, Audi leaders saw an opportunity to modernize how support services were delivered across the enterprise.  

Rather than adding more manual processes or increasing operational overhead, Audi wanted to empower employees with real-time access to critical information—anytime, anywhere. To meet rising demand and scale support efficiently, the company set an ambitious goal: deliver a production-ready, AI-powered self-service experience in weeks, not months.  

“To provide an enhanced employee experience and relieve operational HR from answering easy questions, it became clear that employees needed convenient access to information anytime they needed it,” says Melissa Wischner, HR Digitalization at Audi. “Our goal was to create a self-service solution that delivers accurate, specific, and fast answers to employee questions 24/7.” 

Audi puts innovation to work inside the enterprise   

To improve employee access to information, Audi accelerated chatbot development using several Microsoft solutions—including Azure AI Foundry, Azure App Service, and Azure Cosmos DB. Azure AI Foundry provided a customizable architecture that helped the team move fast while meeting enterprise requirements for security, scalability, and compliance.  Azure Functions acts as a connector between Azure Key Vault and Azure Cosmos DB, enabling secure, event-driven data flow within Audi’s chatbot framework.

“We had a lot of expertise in AI and web applications, but we had never built an Azure application before,” notes Hendrik Drath, Solution Architect, AI and Big Data at Audi. “I found a solution accelerator that provided everything we needed—infrastructure code, back-end orchestration, and a ready-to-go front end.”  In just two weeks, Audi launched its first AI-powered assistant, the Smart Assistant for HR, delivering real-time, natural-language answers with enterprise-grade performance.

Moving fast, staying secure with enterprise AI   

Audi knew that accelerating development with confidence required the right foundation.  

“The Azure accelerator helped us skip months of foundational work. It gave us a solid base, so we could build quickly and roll out a proof of concept for an enterprise use-case,” says Apoorva Suresh, Machine Learning Engineer on Audi’s AI Enterprise Team. 

Audi’s chatbots run on a tightly integrated Azure stack that delivers security, scale, and real-time performance. Azure App Service provides the managed infrastructure Audi needs for production workloads, including built-in authentication, telemetry, and compliance monitoring. This simplified operations by reducing infrastructure complexity, helping Audi’s development team focus on rapid innovation and efficient releases.

To power intelligent, real-time responses, Audi relies on two products in Azure AI Foundry:  Azure OpenAI in Foundry Models and Azure AI Search. Together, they surface accurate answers from internal sources, including SharePoint and Yammer, using a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) approach. 

“RAG forms the core logic of our system,” Suresh shares. “We use Azure AI Search to store and retrieve vectorized content. Azure OpenAI generates the final response based on the retrieved context.”

For managing millions of discussions in large communities, the Microsoft Viva Engage connector operates with Azure Cosmos DB. The process starts with a bulk upload of existing discussions, followed by a caching and high watermark system that syncs only new discussions. This approach ensures fast, efficient updates for Yammer or Viva Engage, keeping information current and accessible. 

Azure Cosmos DB will also serve as the backbone for developing a performance cockpit, enabling chatbot customers to monitor key performance metrics and identify opportunities for improving data quality.

To safeguard operations, Audi used the native security toolset in Azure, including Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Azure Key Vault. From encryption to compliance scoring, the team had full operational visibility to meet security requirements across multiple internal stakeholders.  

“We put different compliance controls in place using Azure App Service and other tools and even used Azure OpenAI to enforce non-compliant answer filtering. Security wasn’t an afterthought—it was built into the foundation,” explains Drath.  

The following diagram shows the architecture of the solutions Audi is using to create its new chatbots. The user accesses the chatbot with a request for information, with Azure Cosmos DB, Azure AI Search, and Azure OpenAI playing pivotal roles in the flow and retrieval of data.

Navigating the road ahead with confidence  

Audi’s modular, production-grade architecture allows teams to reuse proven patterns for further large language model (LLM) solutions while adapting to each department’s unique needs. After the success of the Smart Assistant for HR, Audi launched a second chatbot for its Enterprise Helpdesk, extending the same framework to IT support scenarios.  

“The experience of getting answers is night and day. Working with Microsoft means we’re saving time for employees and operational HR,” says Wischner. 

That success is now fueling enterprise-wide expansion. Audi is building more LLM solutions across different business areas—each tailored to business-specific data and workflows but sharing a common foundation for deployment, security, and compliance. 

“We’ve been working with Azure for quite some time now, and we’re seeing even greater strides recently,” adds Suresh. “Microsoft understands our needs—and it’s only getting easier to scale new use cases into production.”

What Audi learned: Start small. Build smart. Hit the gas.   

Audi’s approach wasn’t just about building a chatbot. It was about building trust across the organization. By delivering fast, secure, and scalable access to information, the team earned confidence from both leadership and employees.   

The success of the first chatbots did more than validate the technology. It reinforced that enterprise-grade AI can be deployed responsibly, at speed, offering clear lessons for business and technical decision-makers:   

Start with a real business challenge: HR’s use case was urgent and actionable.   

Build on proven frameworks: Azure AI Foundry, Azure App Service, and Azure Cosmos DB provided a strong starting point, enabling the AI Enterprise Team to efficiently develop a robust, modular framework tailored to Audi's specific enterprise needs. 

Architect for scale: A modular stack helped ensure fast, secure deployment across departments.  

With multiple chatbots live and more in development, Audi is preparing for next-generation capabilities, such as multi-agent orchestration and deeper integration into business systems. This isn’t experimentation. It’s operational AI at enterprise scale in weeks.  

“We’re already seeing the relief. Automating answers lifts a huge weight off internal teams and helps employees get what they need, fast. With secure, lean solutions like Azure, it’s easy to scale what works and focus on what matters,” says Drath.

Kortext and Microsoft are reshaping higher education with Kortext fusion, a unified data platform that accelerates digital transformation for universities using the power of content, data, and AI. With its cost saving accelerating model, the application layer on fusion redefines how institutions make decisions and support user experience, harnessing data from multiple touchpoints to drive value for leaders, academics, librarians, and students.

This ground-breaking innovation is built on Microsoft Fabric and Azure AI Foundry leveraging a partnership with Microsoft that stretches back to 2013. Together, Kortext and Microsoft are delivering positive change for the higher education sector, enabling thousands of universities worldwide to transform and achieve better outcomes for their users.

Addressing challenges in higher education

Digital transformation can be a challenge for universities with cost, resources, and legacy systems all presenting barriers to change. In the UK, for example, an estimated four in 10 universities are facing financial challenges.

“We built fusion to join up data feeds and enhance the student experience,” highlights Robin Gibson, Director of External Affairs at Kortext. “Before, universities had to purchase multiple solutions, leading to inefficiencies, high costs, and technical debt. With the applications built on fusion, students and academics can access content and data in one place, streamlining and simplifying the learning experience.”

With fusion as the base layer, universities can eradicate data silos, pulling data from across the institution to use with Kortext’s product range—such as study or stream—to drive data-driven insights and support different user experiences. Moreover, they can integrate their own applications, safe in the knowledge that fusion is a secure platform. As fusion is delivered at scale, on a “buy not build” model, this also eliminates the high costs associated with building an in-house solution, enabling universities to embrace a cost-effective, OpEx approach.

In addition, AI is disrupting the higher education sector, with 92% of students now using AI to support their studies. Whilst this presents multiple opportunities for universities, it also raises fears around bias, equity, security, and unvetted content.

“Too often, students use AI that detracts from the learning experience and universities are right to be concerned,” says Robin Gibson. “Some of these AI tools hallucinate, providing inaccurate information. There are also big issues around equitable access—not everyone can afford a subscription.”

These challenges motivated Kortext to build Kortext fusion, enabling university technologists to embrace AI safely at their institutions, through bespoke user applications on a single, unified platform.

Empowering universities with AI-driven technologies

"We’re enabling university leaders to dive deep into multiple sources of data and understand student engagement, experience, and outcomes. The fundamental elements for this are Microsoft Fabric and Azure AI Foundry,” says Robin Gibson.

Kortext fusion is built on Microsoft Fabric and Azure AI Foundry, two cutting-edge solutions that support generative AI innovation, with seamless integration into Microsoft Azure.

Microsoft Fabric is the foundation for fusion, offering a single space for collecting and analysing data from multiple touchpoints across a university. As Fabric sits within Azure, this data can be fed into Azure AI’s LLMs for training, delivering AI-powered insights for the end user.

“We wanted to integrate Large Language Learning Models (LLMs) into fusion,” says Andrew Bates, Chief Product Officer at Kortext. “With AI evolving quickly, we didn’t want to be locked into one kind of LLM—and that’s the same mindset as Microsoft. This encouraged us to adopt Azure AI Foundry.”

Azure AI Foundry gives Kortext access to a range of different LLMs, optimised for specific tasks. As part of Microsoft’s Ethical AI Commitment, the solution also includes bias detection tools, ensuring responsible AI and alignment with Kortext’s mission to ensure safe AI use within universities.

“We’re building solutions that deliver a better, more personalised learning experience for students, helping them to develop skills for their future lives and careers,” says Robin Gibson. “In partnership, Microsoft and Kortext are delivering this together, reshaping higher education to enhance the student experience.”

This approach has been positively received by PJ Hemmaway, CIO at The University of Manchester, who commented on fusion in a recent HEPI blog: “This technology could also help me accelerate my digital-first strategy, being a foundation to support flexible and inclusive education with equitable access for all."

Working in tandem with a trusted partner

Kortext is a leading Microsoft ISV Solution Partner specialising in higher education, having forged a 10-year partnership with Microsoft based on trust and innovation. The two companies have a powerful synergy, blending Kortext’s deep expertise and reputation in the higher education field with Microsoft’s pioneering AI technology.

Seeking to bring Kortext fusion to market successfully, Kortext leveraged this partnership and joined the Microsoft Independent Software Vendor (ISV) Program. Designed for software vendors, the ISV Program offers tools, support, and access to Microsoft’s commercial marketplaces, enabling Kortext to understand the technology, collaborate with engineers, and market fusion to a global audience.

“Being an ISV Partner enables us to launch our solutions into Azure Marketplace and benefit from global reach,” explains Robin Gibson. “We’ve fully embraced the Marketplace as a route to market and commercial extension of our business. Placing our products alongside the Microsoft brand sends a powerful message of trust, which is hugely important in the higher education sector.”

Leveraging the secure infrastructure of Azure

Working with the higher education sector, Kortext also requires technologies with robust security credentials. This makes Microsoft Fabric and Azure AI Foundry the clear choice, being compliant with global data regulations and built on the secure, enterprise-grade network infrastructure and hardware of Azure.

“Security is first and foremost in everything we do,” highlights Andrew Bates. “As we’re working with data in the higher education sector, we need to be mindful. Microsoft ticks all the boxes for us, offering out-of-the-box security controls and a best practice approach to data protection to ensure compliance.”

Delivering innovation in higher education, together

Together, Kortext and Microsoft are transforming higher education, bringing AI-powered solutions to market that deliver trusted content and valuable insights for university, students, academics, and leadership. At the heart of this partnership lies innovation—a desire to help institutions navigate the complex technological landscape and reach new frontiers using AI.

“As Microsoft continues to innovate in edtech, we’ll have plenty of opportunities to work together,” says Andrew Bates. “We want to collaborate around the evolution of AI content, how it's consumed by end users and how universities control access to trusted, vetted, adopted sources of information. These are interesting areas - and we're exploring them with Microsoft.”

Kortext plans to leverage this partnership again in the future, extending Kortext fusion’s AI capabilities further to deliver even more personalised experiences. With Microsoft, Kortext benefits from technological expertise and access to commercial marketplaces, as well as a partner with a clear understanding of AI and the unique needs of edtech.

Andrew Bates illustrates this. “Microsoft's vision around AI, investment into infrastructure and understanding of what companies like Kortext need to be successful has been really encouraging. I think Microsoft has been thoughtful about AI optionality, integrity, and the relationship between data and the relevancy of the context data provides in building user experiences with AI. The amount of innovation in the edtech space is unprecedented and the Microsoft strategy around dealing with unknowns is reassuring.”

As one of the UK’s most influential charities, the British Heart Foundation (BHF) funds groundbreaking cardiovascular research and provides direct, life-changing support to people affected by heart and circulatory diseases. Its mission, which is to help everyone live with a healthier heart for longer, includes backing AI-driven diagnostics, building CPR training tools, and maintaining the UK’s national defibrillator registry.

BHF also offers vital support services, from a helpline staffed by cardiac nurses to peer support groups and public education. By 2035, it aims to prevent 125,000 heart attacks and strokes across the UK and improve the quality of life for millions already living with heart conditions.

To fund its efforts, BHF operates one of the largest nonprofit retail networks in the world. With nearly 700 shops across the UK, it is the country’s biggest charity retailer and the largest charity seller on eBay. These shops transform donated goods into research funding and community impact.

“We have shops and stores on nearly every high street across the UK,” says Sarah Boardman, Head of Retail Transformation at the British Heart Foundation. “For many people living with, or supporting someone with, heart disease, our shops are their first touchpoint after hospital. People walk in and say, ‘You saved my life,’ and show their scar. Our red heart logo means something to people.”

Working and fundraising smarter

As BHF scaled, its unique hybrid model of operating as a research funder, healthcare supporter, and retailer became both a strength and a complexity. The organization faced some serious operational challenges in its retail systems.

First, there was no standard method for creating donated stock records in its ERP system. This made it hard to track items, assess value, and claim eligible Gift Aid—a UK tax incentive that could return up to 25% on donated sales. Secondly, the charity lacked tools to consistently determine which donated items should be sold online, where some command premium prices, versus in-store. Finally, the growing volume of donated stock meant that shipping low-value items to BHF’s central listing hub in Leeds was becoming inefficient, environmentally costly, and often unprofitable.

“We needed to be smarter,” says Michael Spivey, a retail expert and long-time staff member in BHF’s eBay operation. “It wouldn't be cost effective to sell an item valued at £10 if it costs you £12 to list, store, and ship it. But without the right data, our shops were using their own judgement.”

For a mission-driven organization relying on volunteer labor support, legacy systems, and limited tech infrastructure, the cost of inefficiency was ineffective fundraising and its impact on how well BHF could serve those in need.

Building an intelligent retail system

Gareth Campbell-Julian, Director of Technology Transformation, at the British Heart Foundation says that in late 2023, the organization committed to something very brave by reinventing how it handles, prices, and channels donated items. “We decided to do a full-scale, cloud-first transformation using Microsoft technologies.”

The British Heart Foundation reimagined its stock management process using low-code Microsoft Power Platform, Azure OpenAI, and Microsoft Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management. Power Platform is the backbone for BHF’s donated stock processing solution. Its low-code capabilities helped BHF to quickly build, test, and deploy a new retail pricing and inventory app in just a few months, something that would have previously taken years.

“We started with a blank page in September 2024,” says Campbell-Julian. “We used agile sprints to go from idea to what we call a ’minimum lovable product’ in just three months. By January 2025, a live Power App was in select stores.”

Store staff can now use a guided, intuitive interface built with Power Apps and Dataverse to assess and record donations. The app uses Azure Functions, Azure API Management, and AI Builder, a Power Platform feature. AI Builder has custom connectors and PCF components to help analyze item attributes like brand, condition, and seasonality. It also can suggest an optimized price and channel (storefront, eBay, or Depop). Power Automate helps orchestrate the flow between front end and backend systems, while Microsoft Dynamics manages the inventory lifecycle and Gift Aid tracking.

BHF used Microsoft Azure and Power Platform tools as integration layers instead of embedding logic inside the ERP. “We wanted to avoid the technical debt that could slow us down,” explains Alex Paraman, Solutions Architect at the British Heart Foundation. “A Power Platform architecture lets us evolve without breaking ourselves.”

Behind the scenes, Azure Machine Learning and Microsoft Fabric provide the analytical power. AI models trained on 1.9 billion rows of historical retail data began identifying patterns in pricing accuracy and sell-through rates. Campbell-Julian says the AI model, affectionately dubbed “Arti,” became a pricing helper for store staff and volunteers, empowering them to get value right the first time and cutting waste from the system.

Expanding what’s possible

With its solution live across more shops, BHF is already seeing measurable gains. The organization projects a £500,000 rise in Gift Aid revenue in year one and over £1 million in additional sales from improved pricing and smarter channel allocation. But the benefits go beyond numbers.

For one, the workload has shifted from repetitive tasking to high-value human interaction. The organization’s approximately 20,000 store staff and volunteers are working within a data-smart system, freeing them to offer richer customer experiences rather than wrestling with spreadsheets and labor-intensive stock handling.

They’re also cutting environmental waste by minimizing unnecessary shipments and reducing landfill disposal from unsold stock. In addition, the app is impacting volunteer and staff morale, by allowing them to be more engaged in store operations using AI. “You can see the spark when they realize they’re teaching the machine,” says Paraman. “It’s not just automation, it’s collaboration.”

With its rich, integrated data platform, BHF is making evidence-based decisions at scale. “We’re now processing nearly 800,000 items a week across all the shops,” says Paraman. “AI is essential in this—no human team could accurately track, price, or optimize the processing of that many items manually.”

Paraman continues, “This helps us fulfill a moral obligation to our doners. When someone takes the time to gives us their goods, we owe it to them to extract the most value we can— to power lifesaving research.”

BHF’s innovation efforts are being recognized. The transformation of its stock management processes recently won Best Breakthrough Data Project at the UK’s Digital Technology Leaders Awards 2025. BHF also won the Best Not-for-Profit Project award.

Looking ahead, reaffirming the mission

BHF’s modernization isn’t over. “We're moving toward a time where AI can list donated stock on eBay without human intervention,” says Campbell-Julian. “It sees the item, generates the title, description, price—done. That will be transformational.”

Boardman adds that AI may also soon handle full product listings, image recognition, and volunteer coordination by effectively delegating tasks to volunteers. Copilot Studio is being explored for managing patient and volunteer journeys. And with Azure Machine Learning forecasting retail trends, BHF is gaining new visibility into future fundraising capacity.

“Technology is helping BHF reaffirm its mission to create a world where everyone has a healthier heart for longer,” says Boardman. “As it helps us be more efficient, improve sales, and optimize listings, it brings us even closer to our goal."

GroupeActive is an SME with a staff of around ten, whose mission is to promote the development of VSEs and SMEs throughout France, by supporting independent professionals. CIOs, CFOs, HR managers, sales managers and supply chain directors: the company supports a network of 80 experts in launching and managing their businesses.

The aim is to provide them with a range of programs and tools, including AI, a technology that is set to transform their daily lives. Frédéric Barbier, General Manager, explains.

Innovating to increase human expertise

"Every day, we pool our individual intelligence with the collective intelligence of the network", observes Frédéric Barbier, "so why not use artificial intelligence to amplify the scope of our actions?". It all started there, when the SME became fully aware of the accelerating role that technology could play. "AI enables us to gain operational productivity, while anticipating the needs expressed by our experts and their customers".

It was against this backdrop that GroupeActive approached Witivio, the company's long-standing AI partner, and a specialist in deploying solutions for Microsoft Teams. "We've always operated in a Microsoft environment," he says, "so designing an AI project based on Witivio's expertise was an obvious choice."

Co-constructing an intelligent agent

The aim is to imagine the tool that would be best suited to the field reality of GroupeActive experts and perfectly integrated into a known and mastered technological ecosystem. To this end, an ideation session orchestrated by Witivio helped gather the needs expressed by the community, outlining multiple use cases, one of which was identified as a priority: sales prospecting assistance.

"Our experts need to develop their business, and writing sales proposals is usually not their core activity. In fact, it's a major challenge," Frédéric Barbier emphasizes, not to mention the administrative burden inherent in the task.

Conversely AI, and more specifically AI agents, can provide the layer of intelligence needed to simplify this prospecting work. Through its "GAIA" program, dedicated to the design of AI-based tools, GroupeActive then entrusted Witivio with the development of an intelligent agent, tasked with supporting independent professionals in drawing up their sales proposals.

"GAIA Propale": an unrivalled agent

Known as "GAIA Propale", the agent was custom-designed using Microsoft Copilot Studio, and can be accessed via Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, according to the desired level of interaction. "All members can converse with this agent," explains Frédéric Barbier, adding that the solution can be activated at each key stage in the sales process.

Whether in a face-to-face meeting or via Microsoft Teams, the "GAIA Propale" AI agent works from the notes taken by the expert during the various customer meetings, and is trained to structure the data according to the SOFA model (Situation, Opinion, Future, Action). "By following a very precise methodology, the agent is able to draw up several chapters of a sales proposal, including elements linked to the prospect's context, needs and challenges, and does so extensively".

The strategic benefits of time savings and enhanced performance

Then, experts simply need to review and validate the chapters drafted by the agent, saving precious time, since a sales proposal can be drafted in two hours, compared with one day previously. In addition, the GroupeActive proofreading committee - whose task is to check the content of a sales proposal after it has been drafted by an independent - has reduced its turnaround time to just a few hours. "Our members save an average of 75% on drafting time," asserts Frédéric Barbier, "it allows them to concentrate more on defining their price and sales pitch. They are undoubtedly more efficient."

The conversion rate has also been boosted as the interval between proposal and contract signature is now divided by four. In other words, although GAIA Propale is still in the early stages of deployment, the solution is already proving revolutionary. "From now on, we can draw up a clear, relevant and personalized sales proposal in record time. This approach provides structure to our experts," enthuses Frédéric Barbier.

The system will be rolled out to the entire community in the coming months, as part of a dedicated training program designed to "maximize the agent's appropriation by teams, and therefore maximizing its effectiveness".

The solution is proving its worth in the pilot phase: drawing up a sales proposal takes no more than two hours now, and the time taken to sign a contract has been divided by four.
