The National Gallery Singapore is a visual arts institution overseeing the largest public collection of modern art in Singapore and Southeast Asia. Its vast collection sits inside a beautifully restored 64,000 square-meter venue that was formerly Singapore’s City Hall and Supreme Court. As a public museum, the National Gallery Singapore aims to help as many people connect, resonate, and fall in love with art.

Making art more accessible through tech

Technology plays an important role in this work. “It takes effort to make art accessible, engaging, and relevant. That’s where technology comes in,” shares Ryan Ho, Head of Innovation and Experience Design at the National Gallery Singapore. “Our innovation initiatives focus on helping visitors experience and connect with art in more intuitive and personal ways."

To accomplish this, the Gallery works with various innovation specialists and partners—such as NCS.Partnerships like these have made it possible to tailor experiences to Singaporean visitors, incorporating local cultural references while maintaining the experience accessible to international audiences. The partnership with NCS has led to several pilot projects, mostly around ways to enhance visitor engagement with art. “It’s one thing to brainstorm ideas about how technology could enhance visitor engagement, but we value collaborative partnerships like these because they let us build, test, and refine these ideas. NCS have been great at that,” Ho adds.

NCS shares the gallery’s vision. “At NCS, we harness technology to revolutionize how people connect with art and culture. As the innovation partner of National Gallery Singapore, we are enhancing the museum experience with cutting-edge solutions like GenAI and our proprietary Automated Speech Recognition (ASR) to personalize visitor experiences, making art more accessible and immersive,” said Wynthia Goh, Senior Partner, Global NEXT, NCS.

The Gallery’s technology initiatives aim to bring the wealth of Southeast Asian art and social history to life for its visitors. “When someone walks into the museum today, they often feel lost or intimidated,” explains Ho. Wall texts provide limited context, and guided tours—while insightful—are constrained by schedules, language, and capacity.

The National Gallery Singapore decided to build an AI-powered docent to bridge that gap. G(ai)le searches the Gallery archives and delivers information about its artworks in conversational, accessible language and humor. “One of our longstanding challenges has been translating dense, academic research into content that is digestible for the average visitor. We quickly realized that AI could do more than just retrieve information; it could act as a bridge between academic language and visitor-friendly storytelling,” Ho shares.

Choosing the right AI foundation

The Gallery knew that getting the kind of responses they wanted required a highly capable AI solution. “We compared responses from various AI models to determine which ones returned the best levels of accuracy for our needs, and the Azure OpenAI came out on top,” Ho shares. The decision to choose Azure OpenAI Service was also influenced by the Gallery’s existing reliance on Microsoft Azure, ensuring that the AI docent would integrate seamlessly into its broader digital ecosystem.

Together with NCS, National Gallery Singapore started building G(ai)le, an art-loving companion through the museum’s galleries. The team designed the experience to encourage visitors to form their own perspectives, reinforcing the museum’s role as a space for dialogue rather than instruction of what to think or feel. This approach required extensive work to fine-tune the AI’s responses, ensuring it provided insights without imposing a singular viewpoint.

“We spent a lot of time adjusting prompts, phrasings, and response structures to create a balance between informative content and open-ended discussion,” Ho explains. “The baseline quality of Microsoft’s AI technology allowed us to have the level of nuance and depth we wanted in G(ai)le’s responses. If the underlying technology weren’t strong enough, we wouldn’t even be having conversations about personality, relatability, or tone.”

Making art more personal

G(ai)le was designed primarily for visitors who are art-curious, but without existing art-historical expertise, and who typically feel a little shy about engaging with art at a museum. “For the everyday audiences who visit the museum on a date or a family trip, the combination of giant gallery spaces and austere framed paintings on walls might feel intimidating,” Ho explains. “They might find themselves looking at the artworks and thinking, ‘I just don’t get this.’ That is where we see G(ai)le really stepping into reach across the aisle and break down that barrier.”

G(ai)le engages such visitors in unexpected ways. “If someone said, ‘I really like Taylor Swift,’ it would bring up parallels between Swift’s evolution as a musician and the development of the piece of art or artist behind the work they’re looking at,” shares Ho. This approach allows visitors to see art through familiar cultural references, creating a more personal connection to the museum’s collection.

What makes G(ai)le even more exciting is its ability to remember visitors. If someone mentions they love K-pop, G(ai)le starts framing artworks through that perspective—highlighting relevant connections and comparisons. “The AI-driven platform personalizes interactions, making art more engaging and accessible,” adds Goh.

A lot of this approach was also the product of institutional self-reflection and awareness, like acknowledging that some local visitors today might even feel apathetic, or distant from art. With G(ai)le, the Gallery was able to include prompts like, ‘Meh. Why should I care about this?’ to address that head-on and to connect art to contemporary culture.

“For us, using a solution like Azure OpenAI is about new ways to make art feel accessible, rather than forcing visitors to talk or engage with it in our way. That’s something we’re able to do with G(ai)le,” adds Ho.

Expanding access through inclusive design

The AI docent is enhanced with multilingual support and inclusive design. “G(ai)le supports Singapore’s four main languages—Malay, Tamil, Mandarin, and English... and as a bonus even understands Singlish terms,” Ho explains. This multilingual capability addresses the Gallery’s aim to serve diverse local audiences, especially as in-person tours are not always available in the language a visitor may prefer. The Gallery also plans to expand the AI docent’s language offerings to better serve its international audience. “Our proprietary Automated Speech Recognition (ASR) achieved 95% accuracy in real-time speech-to-text transcription (STT) for Singlish," Goh shares.

Beyond language, accessibility features were built into the AI docent to accommodate different visitor needs. “We’ve put in the effort to ensure that G(ai)le meets all World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) accessibility standards,” Ho shares. The system includes a high-contrast mode and an open-source, dyslexia-friendly typeface that users can toggle on for easier reading. An audio-only format allows visitors to listen to responses instead of reading them, which opens possibilities for broader use among visually impaired visitors. The National Gallery Singapore also introduced an "eyes-up mode" to encourage visitors to spend more time looking at art rather than their screens. “Lots of small loving details like these are tucked away under the hood, making it quite a comprehensive product,” Ho adds.

Assisting staff with production and insights

The AI docent is more than a tool for visitors—it has also become an essential resource for the Gallery’s staff. “Internally, we’re thinking of G(ai)le like a new teammate—another docent that could work alongside our tours team,” highlights Ho. One of its biggest contributions has been in translation, not just across languages but also within English itself. “If we wanted to create different versions of a tour, a writer would have to manually rewrite the same content multiple times—for academic audiences, general visitors, kids, and sometimes from different cultural perspectives. Even the most talented writer can’t switch mental gears instantly; it takes time. But G(ai)le can do it in seconds,” Ho shares.

But the role AI plays is still clear, used to generate strong first drafts of content and allow staff to focus on refining and curating, rather than start from scratch. “We’re excited about this shift because it means we can spend less time on logistics and formatting, and more time crafting meaningful content and experiences,” Ho adds.

Beyond content production, the AI docent provides real-time insight into visitor engagement. “For the first time, we'll be able to see and analyze what people are actually asking about the artworks in our collection,” Ho states. “Insights into the conversations and questions visitors have could grow out of the digital space and inform the way we evolve our shows and reach our audiences.”

Redefining the role of museums

Moving forward, G(ai)le will only improve. "Designed for seamless integration with emerging innovations, including robotic assistants, the future-ready solution continuously refines interactions, delivering tailored insights that enhance visitor engagement,” Goh adds. “The future-ready platform ensures that the gallery can evolve with technology. This breakthrough enriches storytelling, enhances accessibility, and creates intelligent cultural experiences for all.”

G(ai)le is just the beginning of the Gallery’s vision for a more interactive and inclusive museum experience. The museum is also exploring integration with robotics and new ways for visitors to engage with G(ai)le beyond the physical space, through platforms like WhatsApp and smartwatches.

As the National Gallery Singapore marks its tenth anniversary, it is rethinking its role in a world where people create and consume culture online. “We’re seeing a shift toward museums becoming more collaborative and interactive spaces. The value of coming here isn’t just to look at paintings—it’s to engage in discussions, meet people, and participate in cultural experiences that can’t be replicated online,” shares Ho. “G(ai)le represents just one part of that shift. Instead of the museum being a one-sided institution that delivers knowledge, it’s becoming a space for dialogue and personal exploration. As exciting as it is, we see this as just the beginning—we’re only scratching the surface of what’s possible.”

CapitaLand Investment (CLI), headquartered in Singapore, operates across more than 45 countries and 270 cities worldwide. A leading global real asset manager, CLI focuses on fee income-related businesses, comprising listed and private funds management, lodging management and commercial management, and its real estate investment business. CLI uses digital technology to drive business outcomes and deliver greater value to its customers and partners.

One such value-adding initiative is its CapitaStar program, a lifestyle loyalty rewards platform designed to encourage repeat patronage of its retail services. Running for more than 13 years and currently having 1.8 million members, the program has seen many changes, including the transition of vouchers from paper to digital. The CapitaStar app today includes features like eCapitaVoucher, a gamified rewards system, and personalized promotions. Through these, CapitaStar strengthens the customer base, while bridging the physical retail mall presence with digital initiatives.

Defining goals of modernization

As CapitaStar program’s capabilities expanded, its manually managed DevOps processes were no longer sufficient. CLI needed to rethink its computing resources to meet business demands. Automation was the clear way forward to ensure continued scalability and efficiency.

CLI’s top priority was modernizing its legacy infrastructure while maintaining its robust security controls to protect customer data on the loyalty platform. Leveraging generative artificial intelligence (AI) to meet platform growth goals and drive significant bottom-line impact was another key priority.

“The decision to use Microsoft solutions came down to a few factors,” explains Darrence Tan, Assistant Vice President, Digital International (retail and workspace systems) at CLI. “We weren’t building something from scratch, so we couldn’t afford to use third-party products that didn’t integrate seamlessly with our existing tech stack.”

Ease of use was also key.  Tan notes, “When introducing tools, the product team had to be able to use them easily without requiring lengthy training.” With these needs in mind, CLI chose Microsoft solutions that aligned with its ecosystem, ensuring a streamlined modernization journey.

Moving to scalable architecture

The first step was addressing CLI’s legacy infrastructure by transitioning from virtual machines (VMs) to a managed service. “Traditionally, we relied on a large number of manual VMs. This setup posed challenges during peak retail seasons, such as in December and during Chinese New Year. During festive periods, we had to manually scale the infrastructure, which required time and effort. Everything was reactive and done manually,” Tan adds.

To overcome these limitations, CLI adopted Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS). Over the last three years, CLI shut down all its VMs and moved 90% of its tech stack into Azure Kubernetes. This shift not only enabled CLI to handle business fluctuations more effectively but helped achieve greater scalability and reliability. Today, platform uptime is at a 99.8% standard. There are now fewer production issues, and even if one is detected, recovery time is much faster.

“With Azure Kubernetes Service, we reduced critical priority incidents by 60%,” Tan shares. “The transition from VM-based architecture to AKS also resulted in a 50% cost reduction.”

Automating and streamlining development

The next step was addressing its development processes. Previously, CLI was hindered by siloed data, and coordination between its in-house and outsourced development teams was inadequate. "Our teams faced long feedback loops which slowed down our delivery cycles,” explains Tan.

With Azure DevOps, CLI automated the entire release management process. This also included code scanning capabilities with GitHub Advanced Security for Azure DevOps. With these solutions, CLI streamlined workflows and introduced early-stage security measures into their Software Development Lifecycle.

CLI’s security scanning, integrated directly into the development pipeline, ensures vulnerabilities such as hardcoded secrets are flagged early. “The entire cycle is shortened because fewer issues arise at a late stage of development,” Tan adds. This proactive approach minimizes costly fixes during production and improves compliance.

“With Azure DevOps, we measured a 25% increase in productivity through full end-to-end automation of release management,” shares Tan. Code quality has also improved, with Azure DevOps preventing untested code from being pushed to production.

Finally, CLI used GitHub Copilot to transform how its developers operate. “We started using it early in 2024 and since then, GitHub Copilot has been the biggest contributor to our productivity improvement,” says Tan.

Traditionally, CLI’s developers spent significant time writing and debugging code, which distracted them from more value-adding activities. “With the adoption of GitHub CoPilot, 25% of the code is written by AI and there is still further room for improvement with increased adoption,” Tan adds. The integration of GitHub Copilot also accelerated CLI’s ability to deliver product features. “We saw a 50% increase in product release frequency, enabling faster delivery of app updates or new features,” Tan shares.

Enhanced telemetry and monitoring now provide CLI’s developers with actionable insights. “Through Azure DevOps and GitHub Copilot, we can track how many lines of code have been generated, how many releases have been done, and how many code check-ins developers have performed,” Tan explains. “This visibility and predictability allow us to confidently commit to delivery timelines while reducing transaction failure rates by 70%.”

For the development team, the impact extended beyond productivity. Replacing manual processes like email-based consultations and release management with automated tools has increased job satisfaction and employee retention.

Scaling success across teams

Looking ahead, CLI is preparing to replicate its achievements across other business verticals. “What we have done is act as an innovation lab for the organization. Our leadership team is very excited about the improvements we’ve been able to realize with Microsoft solutions so far,” says Tan. “If we replicate this modernization process across other business verticals, the benefits will be even more substantial. That’s why one of our key priorities is to institutionalize this knowledge and create a playbook.”

The company plans to use this playbook to guide other teams in adopting Azure DevOps, GitHub Advanced Security for Azure DevOps, and GitHub Copilot. Future plans also include introducing Microsoft Dev Box to further optimize costs and improve productivity.

Reflecting on CLI’s modernization journey for CapitaStar so far, Tan emphasizes, “What made our journey successful is the fact that we started small, proved the value, and involved key stakeholders. There are many teams involved, such as the architectural board review team, cybersecurity, product managers, developers, operations, and quality assurance team. When all these people are equipped with the right tools to do their jobs and aligned on the process to do it, then you can move the needle and drive significant bottom-line impact.”

CATRION is a premier catering and hospitality services provider headquartered in Saudi Arabia. With a legacy dating back to 1981, the company first established itself as a leader in aviation catering, later expanding into tourism, healthcare, and large-scale event services. Today, CATRION serves over 115 international airlines and plays a key role in major initiatives such as the United Nations’ Conference of Parties (COP16) and the Dakar Rally. “Our ambition is to become the global provider of choice for catering and hospitality services across both public and private sectors,” says Ashraf Mahmoud Nadeem, Chief Information Officer at CATRION. 

To support its strategic shift toward non-aviation markets, CATRION launched a digital transformation strategy in 2020 aimed at rebalancing its revenue streams, targeting a 50/50 split between aviation and non-aviation by 2026. The IT department emerged as a critical enabler of this transformation, leveraging Microsoft Power Platform to build and deploy business applications rapidly and cost-effectively. 

By empowering internal teams to create over a dozen apps from HR onboarding solutions to financial tracking tools, CATRION reduced development timelines from weeks to mere hours, accelerating innovation and enabling smarter, faster operations across the organization.

Building capacity for strategic growth

CATRION’s IT division oversees a broad range of functions to support its fast-paced catering operations. One team develops in-house tools like the Universal Catering Automation System, a proprietary tool that helps standardize and simplify critical workflows. Another group ensures the reliability and scalability of CATRION’s data center infrastructure, while dedicated teams oversee day-to-day IT operations and enforce robust governance practices. About two years ago, the IT services and support team began optimizing one of the most manual and sensitive workflows in procurement: food and supplier evaluations by an internal committee. 

“We used to run tests with paper and pen, gather feedback in person, and then spend three or four days consolidating everything,” recalls Nadeem. “We saw a quick win and reached out to Microsoft to digitize the food evaluation processes using Power Apps,” he says. 

CATRION developed a supplier evaluation app that committee members can access via desktop or tablet. It enables standardized scoring across criteria like pricing, service quality, delivery performance, and compliance. “The user experience has completely changed,” explains Nadeem. "We can have attractive interfaces and include images of the food, so participants can be certain they’re evaluating the correct product.” Instead of taking up to four days to be seen, test results can be consolidated almost immediately, and the shift to digital has also eliminated the need for printed forms, reducing paper use. 

Afterward, CATRION saw the possibilities that Power Platform could offer. “Thanks to Microsoft’s amazing support, we saw how we could improve other business processes with Power Platform as well. That’s when our real journey started,” concludes Nadeem. 

Expanding automation to financial operations

As part of its forward-looking strategy, CATRION’s finance division set a bold objective: to embed Robotic Process Automation (RPA) into the very fabric of its daily operations. Rather than rely solely on external developers or packaged solutions, the team embraced a self-learning, self-developing approach, enabling finance professionals to design and maintain their own digital workflows using the Microsoft Power Automate low-code platform.

This shift wasn’t just about efficiency; it was about empowerment. By building automation skills internally, the finance team gained the agility to rapidly respond to evolving business needs and eliminate manual tasks.

By adopting automation as a core capability, CATRION’s finance team didn’t just enhance operations, they cultivated a culture of innovation that drives continuous improvement and sets the foundation for future AI-powered transformation. 

“Automating our reconciliation and customer communication processes has been a game changer. What once took days of manual effort, gathering data, aligning balances, and following up, is now completed in just a few clicks. This has dramatically improved our responsiveness and strengthened client trust through accurate and timely engagement,” says Abdulrahman Alsamadani, Specialist, Account Receivables at CATRION.

The finance team also deployed a custom RPA to handle Expected Credit Loss (ECL) calculations. Data from the enterprise resource planning (ERP) platform and receivables systems are automatically aggregated, matched with internal risk classifications, and converted into reports that support compliance and strategic forecasting. This eliminated error-prone spreadsheet work and introduced a repeatable, auditable workflow completed in minutes. “With the ECL and aging report automations, we’ve turned what used to be complex, time-consuming tasks into fast, reliable outputs, reducing manual efforts and human errors,” shares Mohanad Al-Harbi, Manager of Credit Control at CATRION. 

“We targeted processes that were repetitive, high-volume, and prone to delays,” says Abdullatif Bukhari, Digital and Transformation Sr. Manager at CATRION. By automating ECL, aging, and invoice validation, CATRION created fast wins that unlocked capacity and improved accuracy. “We didn’t just adopt a platform, we adopted a mindset. Power Platform has empowered our teams to solve real business problems without waiting on external vendors,” adds Nadeem.

Automating invoice validation

After automating financial reporting, the team shifted focus to streamlining invoice processing, starting with a targeted subset of trained vendors and invoice formats.

“We developed a background Power Automate process that matches purchase orders with incoming invoices,” explains Bukhari. “It uses Azure AI Vision to extract data from PDFs and scanned images, verify the information, and update our ERP system automatically. If there's a mismatch in the data, it’s flagged for review.”

Previously, validating each invoice attachment manually took at least three minutes. Now, for trained invoices, the system processes them in less than one minute, cutting review time by two-thirds. “The new automation doesn’t just save time; it gives us control and consistency. We’ve minimized human error and can now trust the accuracy of our invoice workflows,” says Shahzad Bashir, Manager of Accounts Payable at CATRION.

These early results validated CATRION’s approach. “This gives us a solid baseline to continuously improve accuracy as we train the system on more invoice types,” says Bashir. “The insights gained from implementing automation systematically are now guiding the refinement of models and processes, accelerating the roadmap to full-scale automation across broader invoice types and supplier categories,” adds Bukhari.

Scaling impact into HR operations

CATRION strategically expanded its use of Microsoft Power Platform into Human Resources to modernize and unify workforce management. “We developed the Talent Hub using SharePoint, Power BI, Power Automate, and Power Apps, creating a centralized digital solution that now supports organizational development, talent acquisition, HR operations, medical services, and government compliance,” says Bukhari.

The Talent Hub, built by the Digital and Transformation team, streamlines the employee lifecycle. It automates critical workflows such as interview scheduling, medical evaluations, permit issuance, and badge provisioning, ensuring consistency and speed across the process. “This transformation highlights how HR and IT can partner to create a lasting impact. It’s a blueprint for how digital solutions can drive people-centric innovation at scale,” shares Saeed Ahmed Al-Mufadali, Vice President, Human Resources at CATRION.

“Building the Talent Hub wasn’t just about digitalizing HR, it was about designing an intelligent, scalable platform that empowers teams to manage the entire employee journey all in one place,” says Bukhari. “It’s now a driving force behind HR transformation across the organization.”

To support smarter decision-making, Power BI dashboards were integrated to deliver real-time insights into recruitment metrics, process bottlenecks, and hiring timelines, enabling proactive planning and continuous optimization. “The goal wasn’t just automation, it was to build a smart, unified system that simplifies the employment lifecycle. It’s incredibly fulfilling to see it creating real impact across CATRION,” explains Manar Zainy, Robotic Process Automation Developer at CATRION.

By embedding automation into HR operations, CATRION has significantly reduced administrative overhead and established a flexible, intelligent framework for talent-driven growth.

Embedding automation across the organization

CATRION also created Power Platform-based applications for operations, health, safety, and travel. The Travel Order application, used company-wide, integrates with the company’s travel agency to automate travel request approvals, ticket issuance, and per diem processing.

“The Travel Order app transformed how we manage company-wide travel, from request to ticket issuance to per diem processing. By integrating with our travel agency and automating approvals, we’ve removed bottlenecks and created a seamless experience for employees and approvers alike,” says Rafaa Alsahafi, Assistant Manager of Digital and Transformation at CATRION.

CATRION also built a lightweight customer relationship management (CRM) system to track opportunities, contracts, and complaints. “During our business requirement meetings, we discovered that customer complaints came from many channels such as emails, calls, guest experience, and even our on-site reps,” adds Bukhari. “So, we built an app to consolidate complaints and improve visibility. It’s helped us respond faster and show our clients that we take feedback seriously.”

Elevating audit and inspection standards

CATRION introduced Standardize PRO, a Power Apps solution that digitizes inspection workflows, from checklist creation to reporting and monitoring. The system provides a unified platform for both auditors and administrators, auto-generates detailed PDF reports, and triggers scheduled daily, weekly, and monthly reminders to ensure timely follow-ups.

“Standardize PRO has been a key enabler in elevating our operational standards. It brought consistency and accountability to our inspections, transforming fragmented efforts into a unified, data-driven approach,” says Sumayyah A. Khawaji, Director of Operations Efficiency and Standardization at CATRION.

The solution does more than digitize; it enables proactive compliance, tracks performance trends, and reduces response time to issues. With centralized dashboards, leadership gains real-time insights into non-compliance hotspots, audit frequency, and resolution rates. It also supports role-based access and standard operating procedures, ensuring a consistent experience across units.

By embedding this platform into daily operations, CATRION has not only reduced paperwork and improved compliance, but also created a scalable foundation for continuous improvement in quality, safety, and performance audits.

Exploring the next generation: AI agents and Copilot at scale

CATRION is now advancing into AI-powered automation, leveraging Microsoft Copilot Studio and Azure AI Services to build internal AI Bot Agents. These bots handle everyday tasks like answering policy questions and guiding users through workflows directly in Microsoft Teams.

The long-term goal is to deploy intelligent agents that go beyond support, executing actions across finance, HR, and procurement. From auto-initiating travel requests to validating documents, these agents will reduce manual load and accelerate decision making. “We’re building an environment where bots don’t just assist; they act,” says Nadeem.

The team is also piloting Microsoft 365 Copilot to summarize reports, generate insights, and boost productivity across roles. By fusing AI with Power Platform, CATRION is evolving from process automation to autonomous operations, where intelligence drives speed, scale, and smarter growth.

Looking ahead with confidence

CATRION’s success stems from the combination of powerful technology and strong internal collaboration. “It takes two to tango,” says Nadeem. “We’ve put in the time to develop these solutions, but we’ve also invested in training our business users to fully adopt them seamlessly. As a result, most business units come directly to us instead of sourcing external vendors.”

As more and more teams turn to the IT division for solutions to their needs, CATRION is already exploring new technologies to extend its capabilities even further. The company built a chatbot using Copilot Studio and Azure OpenAI to make policy documents accessible in Teams. “We see strong potential in combining AI Agents with our existing Power Automate workflows,” shares Nadeem.

To keep pace with planned growth, the company’s strategy remains clear.

“IT isn't just a support function; it’s a core enabler of business growth,” concludes Nadeem.

upGrad, South Asia’s leading online higher education platform, was founded in 2015 with a mission to drive career success by making quality education accessible to learners worldwide. As one of the few fully integrated lifelong learning edtech companies, upGrad empowers working professionals to upskill without disrupting their careers. With a presence in over 100 countries, partnerships with 300+ universities, and collaborations with 1,000+ enterprises, upGrad has built a global learner community of over 3 million.

Aiming to unify the IT ecosystem and enhance cybersecurity

As upGrad’s learner base grew rapidly, the reliance on multiple tools led to fragmented learning experiences and operational complexities. Coordinating with various providers while ensuring seamless support was becoming increasingly challenging. To address this, upGrad sought a mature, scalable solution that could unify various functionalities, streamline administration and enhance efficiency. Additionally, with cybersecurity and data privacy being top priorities, the platform needed enterprise-grade security and greater control over its IT infrastructure.  

upGrad aimed to transition from a startup-oriented infrastructure to an enterprise-grade, secure platform to support its growth, security, and scalability needs. To achieve this, upGrad partnered with Crayon, a global Microsoft partner.  

Gajanan Toraskar, Technical Lead- Infra and Infosec, upGrad, shares, "As a fast-growing enterprise, our priority is to build an integrated IT ecosystem that optimizes costs while achieving economies of scale. After a thorough evaluation, we chose Microsoft for its capability to provide a unified, scalable, and security-driven platform that aligns perfectly with our business needs."  

Partnering with Crayon, a global Microsoft partner, upGrad initially implemented Microsoft 365 A3 before upgrading to Microsoft 365 A5 to better meet its evolving requirements. The solution also included Microsoft 365 Copilot. The deployment was seamless and took three months to complete.

Enhanced collaboration, security, and learner experience 

upGrad’s adoption of Microsoft’s solutions has delivered significant benefits across collaboration, security, and operational efficiency.

Seamless collaboration: By leveraging Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, and Excel—along with education-specific versions of Microsoft Teams—upGrad has enhanced instructional practices and streamlined communication across internal teams. These tools have also strengthened engagement between students, educators, and administrators, fostering a more interactive learning environment.

Superior learning experiences: With 4,000 active users and a vision to skill 3 million learners in AI, upGrad now offers Microsoft Copilot to students enrolled in advanced AI courses. This integration enhances student productivity and delivers immersive, hands-on learning experiences. 

Advanced security capabilities: Microsoft Defender for Office 365, included in Microsoft 365 A5, has significantly bolstered cybersecurity by providing integrated protection for email and collaboration tools. It safeguards sensitive data while ensuring robust identity protection and security.

Simplified App and device management: With Microsoft Intune, upGrad has adopted a secure and unified IT administration approach, enabling seamless control over mobile devices, desktops, and virtual environments. The implementation of Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies across email, chat, and cloud storage has further strengthened data security, preventing unauthorized sharing of sensitive information. Additionally, upGrad has enabled secure access from any device, ensuring flexibility without compromising security. 

Intelligent operations and enhanced efficiency: upGrad has embraced AI-powered automation to optimize IT operations and internal workflows. By integrating GitHub Copilot, the enterprise has improved coding efficiency, while Microsoft Copilot has enhanced ticket resolution for its 50-member IT support team, which handles 70 tickets daily. Additionally, upGrad has implemented a fully automated solution for onboarding partners and vendors using Microsoft Power Automate. This one-click process has streamlined operations, saving valuable time and allowing teams to focus on strategic initiatives.

Ashok Kumar, Consultant- Infra and Infosec, upGrad, says, "With the Microsoft solution, we have transformed our learning ecosystem, enhancing collaboration, security, and productivity across the organization. The integration of advanced tools has streamlined operations and improved user experience for internal users, students, and external faculty members".

Upgrading for the future with autonomous systems and advanced analytics

upGrad is continuously exploring innovative ways to leverage Microsoft solutions to enhance efficiency and drive business growth. As part of this strategy, it plans to fully migrate to the Microsoft environment by August, unlocking the full potential of its suite of products. With vast amounts of data generated through customer support tools, upGrad aims to harness advanced analytics for deeper insights into sales and lead generation. 

Handling nearly 5 million calls per month, upGrad is also focused on implementing automated quality control to enhance customer service and optimize business outcomes.

 Raj Dogra, CIO, upGrad, shares, "Our aim is to create a smarter, data-driven environment to enhance learner experiences and operational excellence. We are automating procurement and vendor management, adding customizable SLA alerts, and optimizing email management. We plan to integrate Copilot and autonomy in operations for more insightful decision-making and long-term growth."

Crayon is working with upGrad to deploy Microsoft 365 under Microsoft’s End Customer Investment Funds (ECIF) program. Additionally, Crayon facilitated seamless cloud migration through the Azure Migration and Modernization Program (AMMP). It has also supported the assessment and implementation of large language models (LLM) on Azure. The team from Crayon collaborated with upGrad to manage the Cybersecurity Investment (CSI) initiative and conducted both pre-sales and post-sales workshops on Microsoft 365 Copilot, accelerating upGrad’s adoption of AI-powered productivity tools.

“We all have a digital standard in our day-to-day lives which sets our expectation of being able to do seamlessly on a mobile device. That is what employees expect of us. So we constantly asked ourselves – how do we bring that standard into our store employees’ day-to-day work to help them with daily tasks?”

Jelle Gijsbers, Product Manager at Albert Heijn, is explaining the driving force behind the supermarket chain’s latest initiative. As a frontrunner in AI adoption, the company uses innovative technology for customer-facing initiatives and more recently, for employee initiatives too.   

“In the retail industry,” continues Gijsbers, “we still have the labor-intensive process of stocking shelves and at Albert Heijn, this job is usually completed by minors who work a couple of hours a week after school. As they're relatively young and working fewer hours, we set ourselves the goal of making our store employees’ work easier.”

Albert Heijn previously launched an employee app, @AH, designed to enhance its digital experience for its employees. With the help of Microsoft technology, the supermarket has taken a next step to better reflect the needs of its workforce while also positively impacting satisfaction among the workforce in their day-to-day jobs.

Paving a way for a more tech savvy workforce 

Albert Heijn is one of the largest supermarket chains in the Netherlands. Its presence is so big in the country, that around one in four Dutch people are estimated to have worked there at some point in their lives or work there currently, and many of them gain their first experience of work at the retail chain. For its 700 owned stores across the Netherlands, it employs over 80,000 people who work on the shop floor, interacting with the millions of customers that come through its doors each day. 

“The broader challenge that many businesses are facing today, including us, is that the labor market is getting tighter,” explains Gijsbers. “The age of our store employees is getting younger over time and talent retention is crucial. In the long run, this isn’t sustainable. So, we need to ensure that we are optimizing the work we’re doing.”

To do this, Albert Heijn focused on finding ways to make the store employee experience more relevant and inclusive for all ages. “I myself started at the company when I was 16,” begins Gijsbers, “and having that personal experience of working in the store I understand and empathize with the struggles they face.”

“These 14–16-year-olds come after school for a couple of hours to help stock the stores,” continues Gijsbers, “but often they’re approached by customers with questions or they’re unsure where a product needs to be restocked. It’s a hurdle for them to ask management for the answers to queries because they don’t want to come across as untrained or unaware. It’s all a bit daunting for them.”

Gijsbers and his team saw this problem as an opportunity to transform the store employee experience and see how generative AI could support its entire store workforce.

A conversational assistant is envisioned

Albert Heijn is no stranger to innovation. Last year it became the first Dutch supermarket to use generative AI to make the customer experience more convenient with its AH customer App, a smart tool that provides recipes and tips for cooking and storing dishes.

“We already had a foundation built using Microsoft technology,” says Gijsbers, “so we set ourselves a goal: to find a way to leverage the enablement platform to make the labor-intensive processes our store workforce encounter more efficient by 1%.”

The supermarket chain teamed up with Microsoft once again and its partner EPAM to come up with a strategy. “We started with a traditional product approach where we all came together for ideation workshops to explore the challenges from a business and employee perspective,” says Gijsbers.

“We created personas, used empathy mapping and looked at the frictions people at the company experience,” adds Gijsbers. “We defined a few hypotheses and then looked to validate them. Based on our findings, Microsoft suggested we build a virtual assistant that could answer questions that store employees are confronted with while on shift.”

Using low-fi prototyping, the team imitated a conversational AI solution with store management to see how it could work. “In the backroom of the store,” explains Gijsbers, “we had five people sitting around computers with our website open while holding handheld devices. Employees ask a question, and we quickly type back the answer. We did it in three stores for one shift and it was really explorative, helping us to focus on truly valuable use cases for the end users.”

“As we were developing the concept,” says Gijsbers, “we tried to get feedback from those who would be using the conversational assistant to check that each part of the solution was helpful. For example, we were originally going to make the tool speech-to-text or speech-to-speech. But our store employees said they found talking to their phones awkward and even a bit rude in front of customers – so we listened and rescoped the experience.”

Having validated the concept of a virtual assistant, it paved the way to build the minimum viable product. 

“This collaboration with Albert Heijn was about more than just technology; it was enabling a cultural shift by building an AI assistant hand-in-hand with employees, ensuring it met the needs and inspired adoption by a Gen Z workforce,” explains Raman Bakanovich, Account Director at EPAM. 

“One of the success factors was establishing a robust technical foundation with the AH Gen AI enablement platform. This not only makes implementation of AI-enabled business solutions faster, cheaper, and safer but also provides Albert Heijn with an efficient base for future AI initiatives,” he adds.

Building on a proven foundation of technology

The conversational assistant was developed on top of the central generative AI platform, similar to the supermarket’s customer conversational assistant. It was hosted on Azure Kubernetes Service, a solution that could deploy and scale the app. All the company’s data was stored using Azure Database PostgreSQL, a fully managed database that can integrate with AI tools at a low cost. 

“Some of the capabilities that we built up in that foundational layer of technology we were able to reuse,” says Gijsbers. “We found we could optimize the original model, reducing the cost to build.”

The assistant lives on the employee-facing @AH app, which is accessed on the personal mobile devices of the staff. “Everybody understands a conversational way of interacting with software, so we didn’t need to train anyone to use the assistant, and using personal devices added that familiarity.” says Gijsbers.

Using Azure OpenAI, the conversational assistant is able to answer a whole range of questions from what needs to be restocked on shelves to where a product can be found in store. 

“Barcodes are a really important means of identifying a product,” says Gijsbers, “so we also added in a barcode scanner. There’s also a store floorplan and a planogram of the shelves.”

“Assistants have mainly been used to optimize office work or to handle return shipments, for example,” adds Gijsbers, “but our sole focus has been on supporting store employees in their day-to-day tasks by addressing their specific needs.”

Sparking a cultural evolution

So far, the assistant has been piloted in eight stores, with a view to scale up to 25 stores in summer 2025 and has been met with a lot of positive feedback with store employees saying the technology is easy to use. Its success is, in part, down to the store employee's willingness to adopt the new technology and their openness to a cultural transformation. 

“Adoption is definitely a huge challenge when it comes to a new solution,” says Gijsbers. “There has been a lot of discussion around whether it’s okay for employees to be walking around the store looking at their phones. But employees are on their phones all the time outside of work and we need to adapt to these generational nuances.”

“The majority of people are behind it and customers don’t see an issue with it, especially since store employees are able to answer their queries much faster now,” continues Gijsbers. “Introducing this assistant proposition has helped us to become an attractive employer and we’re able to retain staff because they’re excited to work for us now that we have the solutions in place that makes their work experience better.”

“It will take time for store employees to get used to this new way of working, and to encourage them to use the AI assistant as a first line response,” adds Gijsbers. “But the great thing about technology like this, is that it's always adapting and as we find new use cases, the app will become more intuitive and an integral part of store employees’ day-to-day working lives.”

Looking ahead to the assistant’s untapped potential 

The conversational assistant is now cemented in the architecture of the company and the supermarket chain hopes to roll out the technology to all its 700 owned stores later this year. Since piloting the conversational assistant, Albert Heijn has noticed an increase in productivity among its store employees and while it’s too early to see the impact on job satisfaction and talent retention, it looks promising.

“We’re continually looking at ways to improve the solution and address the internal issues our employees face,” says Gijsbers. “We’re always finding new use cases and we want to move some of our focus to helping our store management teams and also adding multiple languages to the app.”

“We also want to explore the app’s metanalysis capabilities,” says Gijsbers. “There’s an infinite number of unexplored questions we could get feedback on, and we need to be able to process it and understand where we need to make improvements. This technology offers us so much potential to innovate.”

“From the beginning,” concludes Gijsbers, “the eagerness from the Microsoft team and EPAM to try and make a success of this initiative and their collaboration has made this possible. It’s been amazing to be able to bring our concept to life and improve the work of our all our store employees to ultimately deliver on our mission: ‘Together we make eating better the easy choice, for everyone’.”

With the help of Azure OpenAI, the supermarket chain developed a conversational assistant within its @AH Employee App for store employees which answers questions related to their tasks or customer requests.

“At the Municipality of Breda, our mission is to strengthen and increase the resilience of the city. To achieve this, we’ve had to adopt an innovative mindset that incorporates new technology such as AI.”

Gert-Jan Zandbergen, Digital Innovator at the Municipality of Breda, is explaining why the organization needs a forward-thinking approach to discovering and trying new solutions to streamline internal operations and improve public services.

The Municipality of Breda has always been keen to explore new technology and was among the first to explore generative AI when ChatGPT was introduced back in 2022. “While many governments chose to ban tools like ChatGPT, we decided to educate employees on its risks and opportunities and leverage it in a safe way. Through workshops and knowledge sharing sessions, our employees took their first steps in using tools like ChatGPT,” says Zandbergen "When we encounter transformative technology, it's difficult for us to ignore it.

“We’re always looking for ways to use technology to solve problems. One of our main obstacles as a public sector organization is that our civil servants are often faced with heavy administrative workloads limiting their ability to address complex policy issues while providing quality services to residents and entrepreneurs within our city,” he continues. “We needed to find a way to complete more tasks with the same amount of people while ensuring job satisfaction.”

The municipality had already embarked on a digital journey, but to address workload challenges, the organization turned to AI solutions, such as Microsoft Copilot, to explore its capabilities and enhance efficiency and productivity. In 2022, they participated in a roundtable for municipalities at Microsoft, where they were inspired by the possibilities and innovations. During the Covid pandemic, the municipality was able to continue their work thanks to the flexibility of Microsoft Teams and OneDrive. They could work in any place, anytime, anywhere, because they no longer had a complex existing environment. Teams was introduced on time, so the foundation was already in place and adoption was seamless. This allowed them to pilot Microsoft 365 Copilot at an early stage.

The municipality faces operational challenges

Nestled in the Brabant region in the south of The Netherlands, the City of Breda is home to around 188,000 citizens. Its municipality’s 3,600 employees all work towards a clearly outlined vision that addresses urgent societal issues such as climate change, energy transition, the circular economy, accessibility and housing.

“We aim to grow as an international and national hub that’s a desirable location for businesses and a place for connection and collaboration with partners inside and outside the municipality,” says Lieke Hendrix, Secretary and General Director at Municipality of Breda. "The strength of Breda lies in its greenery, where the city and villages come together. We strive for more green neighborhoods and districts, and our ambition is to have more green business parks and meeting places."

“But there’s operational challenges that must be addressed to enable us to work towards these goals,” explains Hendrix. “Our civil servants are time-poor, and the tight labor market may lead to staffing shortages, meaning we need to do more with less.”

To address these challenges, the Municipality of Breda has focused on their organizational development with 'FIT for the future' since 2023. They are doing this through three layers: investing in employees, strengthening their basic working methods, and driving innovation and renewal. 

 A key aspect of this approach involved leveraging innovative technologies to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the municipal services. 

Like most public sector organizations, the Municipality of Breda also has tight budgets and staffing shortages. As of 2026, the recalibration of the Municipal Fund, aimed at better aligning financial resources with the current tasks and needs of municipalities, results in the so-called Ravine Year. The Ravine Year refers to the situation in which the municipal budget comes under such pressure that drastic cuts or other measures are needed to prevent financial deficits.

Nationally, municipalities are missing out on more than €3bn due to the restructuring of the Municipal Fund, causing budgets to come under considerable pressure. The municipality needed to find ways to help improve efficiency and productivity so employees could focus on providing quality citizen services. This is also where innovative technologies come in.

The next step of the digital transformation is realized

The municipality’s enthusiasm towards exploring new technology has long set it apart from other public sector organizations which, traditionally, are slower to adopt innovation. Its digital transformation started during the COVID-19 pandemic, when the need for hybrid working accelerated its efforts. 

“We’ve been using Microsoft 365 for a few years now and it’s helped us to create meaningful interactions and engagement between employees which facilitates our citizen services,” says Zandbergen. “We were aware of the benefits that AI technology could provide in the workplace, so we were keen to explore its capabilities.”

The municipality partnered with Microsoft to deploy Microsoft 365 Copilot. “With the rapid pace at which new technologies are emerging, flexibility is crucial,” says Zandbergen. “It requires a different approach compared to traditional project-based improvements. Alongside Microsoft, we implemented new processes and technology using a cycle of experimentation, evaluation, and adoption. 

“Our entire pilot is themed around travel,” continues Zandbergen. “We have various travel groups (personas) who plan their itineraries with the travel agency. Together, we identify different excursions (use cases where we test Copilot). The travel plans are shared with customs (our privacy and security officers) to ensure everything is carried out in a compliant manner. Once we get the green light from them, the travel group is guided by the steward and the cabin crew, who answer their questions and provide feedback throughout the journey. The pilot results will be shared in a travel report with the union of Dutch municipalities (VNG), detailing our approach, the results of our journeys and excursions and our souvenirs (lessons learned).”

“Since introducing the solution, we’ve created around 25 use cases to pilot the technology,” says Zandbergen. “Each time we begin a new use case, we start with an analysis to identify challenges and opportunities. We then develop prototypes and pilot projects, testing and refining based on feedback. We also collaborate with external partners and experts to integrate new insights and technologies.”

The team then creates training programs to help employees understand the new technology, including hands-on sessions and continuous support. “It’s crucial that everyone knows how to maximize the potential of the technology,” says Zandbergen.

“My colleagues Peter and Cora are responsible for conducting conversations with colleagues, identifying their needs and problems, and translating how we can address these with Copilot,” explains Zandbergen. “Throughout the journey, they serve as a point of contact, offering advice on how to better utilize Copilot or improve prompts. They are also responsible for training staff in the use of Copilot and effective prompting. This is achieved through the development and delivery of training sessions, follow-up group meetings, weekly tips and tricks videos, and activating our pilot group in a Teams community. The prompt buddy also plays a role in this. Here, we and our colleagues share prompts that have worked for us, serving as inspiration for the rest of the organization.”

The municipality pilots AI-driven use cases

Using Microsoft Copilot has proved successful, with several use cases already providing benefits to the organization. “Microsoft Copilot supports civil servants in processing information, drafting documents and managing emails,” says Zandbergen. “This AI tool helps employees focus more on complex policy issues and better utilize their talents, in light of staffing shortages.”

More than 150 colleagues participated in the pilot – the initial results are promising. With the help of Copilot, Breda works more efficiently and effectively, and it proves to be a valuable addition to various departments and tasks. Many tasks saved multiple hours per month, up to 28 hours per employee. Additionally, there was a clear improvement in the quality of work supported by Copilot. Employee satisfaction with the operation of Copilot is also positive, and the pilot participants were very enthusiastic about the tool. 

For the organization, working with data has become essential and provides advancements in areas such as accessibility, safety and sustainable living.

“We joined forces with Microsoft partner Heroes to build a Digital Twin data platform in a year-long project that helped us to adopt a lighthouse approach, offering a glimpse into the future of Breda, says Zandbergen. “By building a replica of the city, we can simulate the effects of traffic and mobility measures such as noise pollution, air quality and traffic flow.”

Another key use case is the City Host initiative, whereby the municipality aims to help migrants navigate their rights and responsibilities. “We want to ensure that labor migrants feel welcome and informed in The Netherlands by providing all the information they need in multiple languages or as audio versions. This contributes to better integration and a fairer labor market,” continues Zandbergen.

“Using Copilot, we’ve created a testing ground for a national model of information provision and services that’s accessible to all,” says Zandbergen. “We also use Azure OpenAI to ensure everything we do is both safe and compliant. The results of this pilot will be evaluated and could potentially lead to a national roll-out.”

Putting security at the forefront of innovation

While building its use cases, the municipality must use AI in a secure environment where the data remains secure. “Deploying Microsoft Security Copilot has enhanced our ability to detect threats quickly, mitigate risks and summarize information more efficiently. By converting complex security alerts into concise summaries, Copilot enables faster incident response times. Since April 2024, Microsoft Security Copilot has helped us with 717 incidents by summarizing large amounts of information,” says Peter Snoeys, Cyber Security Analyst at Municipality of Breda.

Microsoft Security Copilot has also assisted in reverse-engineering scripts, translating them into comprehensible language and making them accessible to all administrators. “Copilot’s guided response feature offers step-by-step guidance for incident management, including triage, investigation and remediation actions,” adds Snoeys.

“We’ve been using GitHub Copilot since November 2024. GitHub Copilot has proven to be highly valuable for the ICT DevOps team in Breda,” says Snoeys. ” We use GitHub Copilot Chat to find errors in the code or ask for solutions. For instance, if I need code for a module, such as an Azure resource, GitHub Copilot provides suggestions. It completes and proposes solutions, enabling us to work better, more accurately, and faster. It also assists us in deploying Azure resources."

Building a future-ready city using generative AI

Looking ahead, the Municipality of Breda hopes to focus on setting up vital processes like governance and a data catalogue. It hopes to foster the adoption of new technology and support its employees in becoming data-literate. 

The organization also intends to continue in its partnership with Microsoft to explore how technology can help it to work towards its goals. “Throughout the process, Microsoft has been more than just a vendor," says Zandbergen. “The team has helped us to navigate challenges and optimize the AI tools to help us achieve the best outcomes.

“We now see generative AI as an inevitable yet valuable development for addressing the municipality’s diverse systems and processes,” adds Zandbergen. “Through the adoption of innovative technologies like Microsoft Copilot, the Municipality of Breda can now demonstrate how innovation and technology can work together to create a flexible, secure, integrated, and future-ready organization.”

By investing in employees, strengthening working methods and driving innovation and renewal with the help of technology, the municipality empowers employees to utilize talents and focus on policy issues, without hiring new employees or partners.

When presented with a common productivity issue, CleverIT Group developed Pulzen—a new, AI-driven solution capable of improving performance as much as 30 percent—in less than a month. Headquartered in Santiago, Chile, CleverIT Group is a member of the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program specializing in the development of novel software solutions that help improve IT productivity and optimize business operations for its customers.

Recently, multiple customers reached out to CleverIT with similar asks. When hiring outside developer teams, these customers lacked a centralized way to measure, analyze, and compare the performance of these professionals. This lack of transparency was not just making accurate productivity assessments difficult, it was also complicating the decision-making process throughout project development. CleverIT’s customers worried this could lead to ineffective use of resources, delays, and less consistent products. They needed a way to connect developer work to business value, understand why some teams struggled while their peers thrived, and to address higher-than-expected developer turnover rates stemming from low morale.

Hearing these concerns, CleverIT created Pulzen, an AI-powered platform that offers easily digested data-driven productivity and performance insights that help teams understand, optimize, and improve the development process. Initially conceived as an internal tool, the broad applicability of Pulzen drove CleverIT to offer its utility as a service to customers as well. Using Azure AI Foundry, Azure OpenAI Service, Azure Kubernetes Service, Azure Container Apps and numerous other Microsoft solutions, CleverIT was able to take Pulzen from concept to execution in less than a month. “Pulzen is a direct response to a challenge we saw across nearly every client: the lack of objective, centralized visibility into development team performance. Thanks to our partnerships with Microsoft and GitHub, we’ve transformed that challenge into a strategic opportunity to drive real, measurable benefits for our clients,” says Martin Burns, Head of Strategic Partnerships and Growth at CleverIT Group

AI-powered productivity insights

With Pulzen, organizations can generate advanced analytics through the use of integrated AI from GitHub Copilot to uniformly measure and compare developers across internal and vendor-supplied teams. This helps ensure fair and consistent assessment through the use of detailed real-time graphics, tables, alerts, and dashboards. CleverIT was able to prototype this solution as rapidly as it did, without the traditional upfront costs, by making use of the initial benefit credits included in its Microsoft Azure subscription.

CleverIT’s Azure subscription also helped as Pulzen transitioned into production‑grade service. At that point, Clever IT adopted a Cloud Solution Provider (CSP) model—gaining full control over billing, support, and subscription management. CleverIT also enrolled Pulzen in ISV Success, streamlining their go‑to‑market plan by listing the solution as a SaaS offering in the Microsoft marketplace and integrating their billing directly through Azure, allowing customers purchase and renew Pulzen seamlessly through their Azure accounts. As well as helping Pulzen reach the market quickly in a way convenient to its customers, Azure helped CleverIT overcome numerous challenges the company had identified at the beginning of the development process.

To address the increased data coming from GitHub and other sources, the company adopted Azure Kubernetes Service for container orchestration and Azure Container Apps for microservices. Both solutions gave the company the rapid scalability, low latency, and high availability Pulzen required. In order to gain the necessary end-to-end view of their distributed solution, CleverIT went beyond the capacity of manual monitoring tools, implementing Azure Monitor Application Insights to consolidate all application metrics, logs, and traces. This simplified troubleshooting and improved mean time to resolution. From the early stages, CleverIT kept in communication with both Microsoft and GitHub, using both organizations’ expertise to its advantage. Microsoft provided guidance and support through access to key frameworks such as DORA (DevOps Research and Assessment) and GitHub contributed the SPACE framework—both of which have become foundational to how Pulzen monitors and analyzes software development productivity.

All of Pulzen’s user data and operational telemetry are stored in Azure Cosmos DB, a globally distributed, multi‑model NoSQL database that guarantees ultra‑low latency, elastic scalability, and schema‑agnostic storage. This has helped Pulzen efficiently manage large volumes of both structured and unstructured data. CleverIT’s custom AI model “Vera” is also hosted and managed via Azure AI Foundry, allowing for seamless integration with Azure OpenAI Service to deliver fine‑tuned generative AI capabilities for data analysis and insight generation. “With Pulzen, we’ve built more than a dashboard—we’ve created an intelligent, AI-powered platform that unifies data from GitHub and Copilot and delivering the kind of insights that engineering leaders have been asking for. GitHub Copilot was a key enabler that allowed our development team to move at unprecedented speed, helping us go from concept to a working product in under a month. The technical feedback and collaboration from both Microsoft and GitHub were essential in refining and scaling the solution,” says Carlos Gallardo, Chief Product Officer for Pulzen & CleverIT Tools.

Demonstrable productivity benefits and expanded horizons

GitHub Copilot was a key enabler of Pulzen’s fast development. CleverIT’s team used Copilot in the IDE to accelerate coding tasks by an estimated 30%, reducing time spent on boilerplate code, backend scaffolding, and test generation. This allowed Pulzen to go from concept to MVP in under a month.

That internal productivity boost meant Pulzen could deliver value to customers faster. And now, Pulzen helps those same customers realize similar gains—20–30% improvements in team performance by leveraging insights from GitHub and Copilot data. GitHub Copilot accelerated both Pulzen's product development and the customers’ outcomes.

Pulzen has also helped address a second long-standing issue in the industry: the presence of “ghost engineers”—those who appear on rosters but whose output is 10% or less of the average team member’s. Upon adopting Pulzen, customer organizations reported that ghost engineers represented as much as 15% of their teams. Pulzen’s transparent reporting and standardized metrics have enabled them to significantly reduce inefficiencies and improve ROI.

Alongside the rapid ideation-to-implementation process that brought Pulzen to market in under a month, CleverIT continues to demonstrate the benefits of the solution’s innovative development. Because the solution is built to natively incorporate the comprehensive security framework of Azure, CleverIT can easily and demonstrably safeguard sensitive data and maintain strict compliance with international data security standards. This alongside the ability to replicate services across multiple geographic regions in Azure helps ensure that the solution is resilient against outages and prepares CleverIT to expand across broader, more diverse markets than its solutions might otherwise have been able to.

CleverIT is committed to continuing the work it has now proven possible with Pulzen: delivering rapid, effective, and highly secure AI-driven solutions. Company leadership believes that AI is a practical, enabling technology that resolves tangible challenges, streamlines processes, and contributes to the overall competitive advantage of the organizations that adopt it. “Pulzen reflects our commitment to building innovative, scalable solutions that solve real-world problems, and our partnership with Microsoft has been a key catalyst in making that vision a reality,” says Diego Stevens, Chief Executive Officer at CleverIT Group.

“Our overarching plan is simple: to optimize our internal processes. If we can become more efficient across the business, what we are really doing is optimizing costs.”

Fabio Beccari, Group Head of Business Solutions at TeamSystem, is explaining the thinking behind the business’ push to enhance automation and streamline operations. As a leading tech company for digital business management solutions, TeamSystem acquires companies to expand its portfolio, integrating their solutions to provide a more extensive offer to clients.

“Our company experiences double-digit growth year-on-year,” says Beccari, “so we need to ensure that we can scale efficiently to maintain momentum and offer the same high-quality services no matter our size.”

“Therefore,” continues Beccari, “we’re always looking for ways standardize, manage, and improve operations while enabling users to create their own applications. That’s why we partnered with Microsoft and adopted its suite of technology.”

Starting the journey towards a centralized environment 

Based in Italy, TeamSystem offers business solutions to manage SMEs and professional firms to enable digital competitiveness. It has over 200 proprietary solutions and serves over 2.5 million customers across all seven countries where it operates, including Italy, France, Spain, and Turkey. 

“As we operate in multiple countries and across various businesses, we use a lot of different systems,” begins Beccari. “Over the past couple of years, we’ve been building a framework to help us to standardize our entire application stack for vertical processes.”

“But we have several processes that are outside of this landscape that we must manage,” says Beccari. “We needed to find an adaptable solution that could be integrated within different systems and fill the gaps in capabilities that we had.”

So, alongside Microsoft and partner AGIC, TeamSystem used Microsoft Power Platform to build a new infrastructure and explored how AI can help modernize legacy applications.

The platform inspires a cultural transformation

At the very beginning of the project, Microsoft organized a hackathon with the TeamSystem software developers to explain and demonstrate how Microsoft Power Platform works and what it can do.

“After the workshop, I spoke to one of the senior developers to gather feedback,” says Stefano Liguori, Chief Information Officer at TeamSystem. “He saw this technology as a new approach to how we develop, and he believed that it could be lifechanging—and he was right.”

“Using Microsoft Power Platform has transformed our developer culture,” says Liguori. “The technology is relatively simple to use, and we now have a channel with Microsoft that we join for training so if we want to deep dive into anything specific or we want to build a new use case, Microsoft is always on hand to help.”

TeamSystem’s developers have adopted the technology quickly, and building applications has sped up as they can now use the low code tools within the platform to code, automate, and integrate with other apps. “Microsoft Power Platform is so easy to use,” Liguori adds, “that we are seeing employees outside of our developer teams use this technology, training themselves to do so using online tools.”

The game-changing capabilities of AI are realized

For TeamSystem, this new-found speed is the main advantage the company has gained from adopting Microsoft technology. 

“We’ve really seen an increase in the velocity of development,” says Beccari. “This means we’ve been able to move away from using wireframes and instead build prototypes so we can show our business users the real product and how we can improve it. Combined with our change of mindset, we’ve been able to build some ready-to-use prototypes fast.”

Using platform tools, such as Power Apps, the company has also streamlined some of its internal processes, such as its cancellation service with customers. “We can now quickly manage the cancellation process and offer better solutions to clients that we have lost. The process used to take weeks, but we now complete the process in matter of days.”

“By making our internal processes more efficient,” continues Beccari, “we can improve how quickly we respond to our clients’ needs and provide better solutions which, in turn, helps with growth and retention.”

Legacy processes are optimized across the business

Another successful internal use case is the administration process for purchases, which previously could only be managed after the process began. So TeamSystem implemented 11 applications, collectively named the LD app, to manage the initial stage of the purchase process when a request must be submitted for a purchase offer. This allows the business to check if it has the budget to make the purchase, saving time and money in the long run. 

“What’s so interesting about this use case,” explains Beccari, “is that the LD app is the first application that we built for the Italian market that we have shared across other countries such as Spain because it’s so adaptable. We can integrate a current ERP with the legal entity that we acquire. If there isn’t an ERP to cover the process we are working on, we can manage the purchase process solely with this app.”

“The application is really useful and brings us a very competitive advantage for cost control,” Beccari adds.

Efficiency gains like this free up time for employees to work on more innovative products that allow the business to scale. They can start by building a single feature and then easily extend the project to build entire applications which are then easily integrated into the ecosystem.

Leading the way on the international stage

Off the back of its success, TeamSystem has big plans to expand the use of Power Platform across the company, building on the foundation it’s created so far. 

“We’ve started to build agents using Copilot Studio, a tool from the platform, to help employees better use our suite of products,” explains Beccari. “But in future, we hope to introduce the technology and the training to employees in different departments, from marketing to finance, so they can build their own agents to improve productivity which feeds into our overall business strategy.”

“We also have plans to explore governance within Power Platform and to create a center of excellence to manage all of our applications and operations,” says Baccari.

“But this process isn't just about implementing innovative technology and taking advantage of the benefits internally,” adds Beccari. “We’re approaching a change of mindset, not just in Italy, but at a European level. By integrating this technology and standardizing everything we do, we’ve become a real differentiator and gained a competitive edge in the international landscape.”

Many tasks have now been automated, and some administrative processes now take days rather than weeks, reducing costs and improving customer service. Employees report better job satisfaction, and adoption has fostered a culture of innovation.
