Companies in all industries sift through numbers to find the slightest advantage over their competition, and they all agree—data is king. NTT DATA Business Solutions helps a diverse array of customers harness the power of data to drive business transformation in the digital age. With more than 30 offices and 16,000 employees around the world, NTT DATA Business Solutions offers many innovation-enabling services, including application management, automation implementation, and hybrid cloud transformation. Its parent company, NTT, is one of Japan’s largest publicly traded companies. “Regardless of the baseline technology, we create innovative solutions for the pain points facing our customers,” says Hande Odabasioglu, Marketing Director at NTT DATA Business Solutions. The multifaceted technology company serves as a global leader in SAP consulting, providing end-to-end services and solutions to help customers unlock the software’s full potential.

The challenge of integrating SAP solutions

When implemented effectively, SAP can help businesses optimize their operations and increase efficiency by automating processes and organizing data. On the other hand, integrating SAP with other key systems and processes can be challenging sometimes. “When you want to connect third-party tools and applications—like creating and serving APIs with a Microsoft .NET solution—SAP can feel like a closed box,” says Gorkem Aslan, Software Engineering Team Lead at NTT DATA Business Solutions. “We help customers make the most of their SAP implementations.”

SAP users frequently use custom code to manage critical business processes, but SAP platform customization can be labor intensive. It typically involves functional consultants specifying and tailoring solutions before engineers implement them. To streamline these time-consuming tasks, NTT’s growing team of SAP experts based in Istanbul, Türkiye, set out to develop a tool to accelerate time to value and improve customer outcomes with the power of generative AI. “We cannot change the speed of the market. We need to change our ways of working by adapting to the AI phase of the world,” says Arda Calli, Head of Innovation at NTT DATA Business Solutions. The team determined that its AI-driven solution needed both a cloud platform and an integrated suite of technology features to automate code translation and generation while providing in-depth program analysis. NTT DATA Business Solutions selected Azure and Azure OpenAI Service with Azure AI Foundry to provide the bedrock of its groundbreaking Virtual SAP Consultant digital assistant.

Streamlining SAP activities with Azure OpenAI Service

NTT DATA Business Solutions had a clear understanding of the approach it would take. “We needed to deploy an application with the cloud because we wanted to build a SaaS [software as a service] solution,” says Aslan. “We containerized the application in Azure so that if you want to deploy a non-SAP solution, like a .NET or React JavaScript app for web development, you can still continue with a separate back-end application when deployed on Azure.” NTT chose this strategy to enable its Virtual SAP Consultant to integrate with other systems and applications that customers may already have in place.

The team also wanted to reduce the time it takes for SAP users to manually translate functional specifications (FS) into technical specifications (TS). The Virtual SAP Consultant uses the Azure OpenAI Service GPT-4o model to automate this time-consuming process. Using the assistant simplifies FS document creation and writes TS documents, helping developers and others explain and document their processes in a specific format. “We use Azure translation systems and many other Azure AI services with our custom rack solutions and normalization solutions,” says Aslan. 

The Virtual SAP Consultant also generates Advanced Business Application Programming (ABAP) code and provides seamless ABAP program analysis to further assist SAP consultants and facilitate better business decision-making. “You can enter inquiries about SAP through strategically developed input fields and the assistant will generate intelligent answers using the latest GPT-series model,” notes Aslan. “We’re doing prompt engineering with our own experiences so we can guide our customers and give them the best answers and best possible solutions.” This intuitive interface enables developers with varying experience levels to produce their intended SAP output without additional support.

Maximizing the value of data

To store these questions and carefully apply the data they generate to inform future query responses, NTT DATA Business Solutions uses Azure Cosmos DB. “We use Azure Cosmos DB for getting requests and responses in a backlog and storing session data such as when someone signs in, what the request was, and when it was sent,” explains Aslan. “If there is a failed request, we need to understand why it failed and how to prevent a similar request from failing in the future. Having requests, responses, and session information available in Azure Cosmos DB allows us to gain that understanding.” The company also uses Azure Key Vault to protect this valuable information. “We are using Key Vault to keep our back-end application environment variables private.”

Data protection is key, but so is organization. NTT has implemented a queue system with Azure Service Bus to help ensure the Virtual SAP Consultant can respond in an orderly fashion to all the queries it receives. The ever-expanding amount of data generated from these queries is invaluable for NTT as it continues to enhance the insights its Virtual SAP Consultant can provide. To store and leverage this massive amount of data, the company adopted a microservices-based approach, using Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) to manage and scale their microservices. “We can create, release, and deploy to different environments easily,” says Aslan. “We monitor and manage all of our microservice applications easily within AKS.”

NTT DATA Business Solutions also has a large number of developers to manage, and it uses Microsoft Entra ID to determine each employee’s permissions when building and maintaining its Virtual SAP Consultant. “When I want to give a developer a role, create a group for team members working on specific applications, or grant access to customer viewers, I manage those roles with Microsoft Entra ID,” says Aslan.” This helps NTT bolster the security of its innovative SAP assistant while using GitHub Enterprise helps streamline its workflows. “We use GitHub with repository management in the deployment phase,” he continues. “That workflow runs in the background while we build applications.”

Increasing efficiency and expanding capabilities

Developers within NTT DATA Business Solutions and its customers now use the Virtual SAP Consultant, available on Azure Marketplace, to overcome previous custom code–related barriers to upgrading or migrating to new SAP offerings. The company’s developers have found that the assistant automatically converts FS documents into TS documents and generates ABAP code with outputs of up to 80% compliance with SAP best practices. This generates an estimated 70% reduction in development time and 50-70% reduction in costs compared to an average development report process. These promising indicators are a sign of innovative capabilities to come for the solution that was just released in late 2024 and continues to expand daily. As Calli highlights, “The Virtual SAP Consultant is more of an ongoing journey than a finished product. We have a roadmap with questions to answer in the first phase so we can better understand the needs of our customers going forward.”

With this roadmap in hand, NTT DATA Business Solutions plans to continuously expand and optimize its AI assistant—and further establish itself as an industry leader. “We’ll add new features in the near future, and we’re offering our customers access to the OpenAI Academy program to train their developers to build their own solutions,” says Calli. As data lights the path forward, NTT DATA Business Solutions and its Virtual SAP Consultant are setting a new standard for innovation.

ACWA Power, based in Saudi Arabia, develops, invests in, and operates power generation and desalinated water plants. With the capacity to generate 65.6 gigawatts of electricity (enough to power nearly 50 million homes) and produce 8 million m3 of desalinated water daily, it manages 90 assets across 14 countries, including the United Arab Emirates, Oman, and Jordan.

Four years ago, ACWA Power began facing challenges with its on-premises information technology (IT) infrastructure. Due to COVID-19 movement restrictions, its disaster recovery teams couldn’t react fast enough, affecting downtime. “With everything in lockdown, we had limited access to our physical data centers,” explains Bart Boesmans, Chief Technology Officer at ACWA Power. “This sometimes led to significant delays in our service operations.”

As the company expanded, predicting data volumes from the plants also became increasingly difficult, affecting analytics and maintenance operations. “Once we realized all the limitations of an on-premises IT infrastructure, we decided to migrate everything to Microsoft Azure," recalls Boesmans. “With this move, we aimed to address scalability, maintenance, and explore advanced technologies that our legacy systems could not facilitate.”

Scaling in minutes, not weeks

After migrating to Azure, maintaining the company’s data centers became easier. "Previously, we required multiple teams to maintain the data centers and manage hardware updates," Boesmans shares. “By eliminating the need for on-premises hardware and physical data centers, we have reduced our footprint. With cloud-based management, we have significantly lowered operational costs.” Simplifying the infrastructure also enabled ACWA Power to eliminate the redundancy associated with dealing with multiple partners for hardware and software.

By tapping into Azure’s vast, on-demand resources, ACWA Power saw enhanced scalability and flexibility—crucial benefits given the company’s large volumes of processed data. "Previously, we’d have had to wait six to eight weeks for hardware delivery and software configuration if we wanted to expand. With Azure, we can scale up and down instantly without delays that could impact our operations," Boesmans notes.

Seamless failover for faultless operation

ACWA Power’s original challenge—business continuity—was also resolved. ”Before, we had a single disaster recovery site in Dubai, so moving any service required sending a team there to do it manually,” Boesmans explains. “Now, we use Azure Site Recovery to host our virtual machines in multiple Microsoft regions, so setting up disaster recovery is significantly faster.”

The company relies on Azure’s built-in disaster recovery features to ensure resilience. For instance, virtual machines automatically switch to a different zone if one zone fails. Geo-redundant storage stores backups in multiple regions, ensuring data recovery even if a disaster affects one of them.

“Overall, the availability of Azure services has been excellent, with over 99.99% uptime,” Boesmans says. “Since migrating to the cloud, we’ve only experienced one significant downtime this year in contrast to the numerous challenges, such as power outages and internet failures, when we were running our own data centers. This has vastly improved our business continuity.”

Azure’s security features have also enhanced the company’s data protection and regulatory compliance, especially in countries like the UAE and Saudi Arabia, where local regulations require data residency.

30,000 pools of water saved a day

Once the move to the cloud was complete, ACWA Power could start addressing pain points in its business, starting with plant monitoring. Previously, the company relied on manual data collection and traditional monitoring systems. "This limited our access to real-time data coming from the plant, so we couldn’t see what was happening, let alone predict what will happen, leading to delays in identifying issues," Boesmans shares. For example, a team would manually sample the water at intervals to determine the dosage of chemicals needed.

The overuse of chemicals not only increased costs but also had a negative environmental impact. To reduce it, ACWA Power started using Azure AI Services and Azure IoT Hub to monitor sensor data across multiple plants. ”With Microsoft AI algorithms, we can monitor water quality and calculate the exact chemical dosage needed, in real time. This has significantly improved efficiency and minimized environmental impact,” Boesmans explains. The upgrade has also led to remarkable water savings—equivalent to 30,000 Olympic swimming pools, matching the daily water usage across Saudi Arabia. “This achievement is aligned with our government’s sustainability goal of optimizing water consumption across the country.”

Unified data via tailored views

Next, ACWA Power aimed to improve its data capture and reporting processes. Previously, the company's operational, maintenance, and project teams relied on disconnected systems, leading to fragmented data and delayed decision-making. "It used to be very challenging for our leadership to get a holistic view of operations because finding the right information was a task in itself," Boesmans recalls. Fragmented data made it challenging to track water production and energy output with precision.

To overcome this, ACWA Power gathered data from multiple sources—operations and maintenance, IoT devices, enterprise resource planning (ERP), work management, and other systems—and pooled them into Azure Data Lake. It then implemented Microsoft Fabric and developed over 100 reports tailored for specific teams and purposes. “Now, everyone has access to real-time data through Power BI dashboards, enabling timely decisions,” Boesmans explains. “Senior management can see how much electricity and water we produce in a day, which plants are down for maintenance, and which plants are operating.”

From reactive to predictive actions

With data lake pooling operational intelligence, ACWA Power built a tool that provides predictive maintenance insights. “Previously, we addressed problems only after failures occurred, which led to unplanned downtime and increased costs," Boesmans shares. Reacting to issues instead of preventing them also puts the company at risk of penalties due to government service-level agreements, as the company is committed to providing electricity and water 24/7.

Now, the control room and ground teams can detect potential issues ahead of time and perform planned shutdowns. " With insights from Power BI, we know exactly when a device may need replacement or repair, allowing us to fix problems proactively and extend the lifespan of our equipment," Boesmans explains. ”We can also identify the root causes of problems and even predict if similar issues might occur at other plants, thanks to historical data and AI algorithms.”

The company also uses smart cameras and IoT sensors to send automatic alerts for potential hazards and keep its teams safe. “With IoT sensors and Azure-based predictive maintenance tools, we now monitor equipment conditions in real time,” notes Boesmans. This also reduces the need for employees to enter dangerous areas. “For instance, if the system detects an issue—such as overheating or a chemical leak—our control room can alert the field engineers not to enter the area until the problem is resolved, keeping them safe,” Boesmans adds.

Plan for renewables

Building on these advancements, ACWA Power has identified more than 177 use cases to implement, including extending predictive maintenance to solar and wind plants. This will enable the company to predict production based on weather conditions and adjust operations accordingly to bring more impact from renewable energy. "We've just started our digital transformation journey and we’re very excited to continue revolutionizing our operations with Microsoft AI Services," Boesmans concludes.

To address these issues, ACWA Power migrated to Microsoft Azure and started to use Azure AI Services, IoT Hub, Data Lake, and Microsoft Fabric, improving scalability, enabling real-time data, and predictive maintenance.
As a result, ACWA Power reduced maintenance costs, enhanced efficiency, and improved safety for plant workers. Real-time insights and predictive analytics enable proactive maintenance, reducing downtime and optimizing resources across its operations.

Technological advances are producing opportunities to engage with brands faster and more directly, and customers are becoming increasingly sophisticated. There’s a willingness to explore new offerings earlier, and as digital becomes the default for sales and services, the demand for a customized experience continues to rise. Although Blip was prepared for this shift, the company needed the right technology to achieve its forward-thinking goals. 

“Today’s customers are looking for personalized interactions. We help brands know their customers better and make every contact meaningful, which builds customer trust and brand loyalty in a competitive market,” says Roberto Oliveira, CEO at Blip.

With 25 years in the market, Blip is the conversational solution that connects consumers to brands in a hyper-segmented and hyper-personalized way across different channels. The company has expanded to serve brands in more than 32 countries. To maintain its competitive edge, Blip recognized the need to harness its data, accelerate the development and deployment of new features, ensure scalability, and uphold stringent security measures.

Breno Queiroz, Director of Engineering at Blip, says, “To gain a deeper understanding of customer preferences, behaviors, and needs, we had to access the right data and continue delivering exceptional digital experiences.”

AI-powered customer personalization built on .NET

Blip is an AI-first company and has a strong relationship with Microsoft due to the latter’s longstanding leadership in AI. So, to help drive strategy and deliver scalability, Blip chose solutions that included Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service, .NET, and Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS). 

Microsoft has helped Blip achieve an increasingly efficient global scale. “We’re using Azure to scale and best serve our clients, from marketing to customer care, in industries from food to real estate,” says Oliveira.

With a microservices-based architecture hosted on Azure, which comprises its messaging, storage, processing, and AI capabilities, users can connect through multiple channels, including external messaging apps. Azure OpenAI helps to improve the customer experience by suggesting personalized responses based on each individual’s conversation history.

With Azure DevOps, Blip is automating workflows and increasing developer productivity. In addition, the Azure Security Center and other tools offer more secure coding practices and reinforce security best practices. This comprehensive approach to security helps protect Blip’s applications and data. 

“We’re using Azure DevOps to improve our development and deployment timelines in a highly secure environment to deliver consistent performance even during traffic peaks,” adds William Colen, Director of AI at Blip.

Expanding existing technology investments 

For development, Blip had begun its .NET journey with early versions of .NET Framework, laying a foundation for building reliable components in C#. But as containerization and cloud-native practices gained momentum, Blip saw an increasing need to deliver its services more efficiently, which led to its first major migration from .NET Framework to .NET Core, providing cross-platform compatibility and the flexibility required for Kubernetes.

Blip later started migrating to .NET 8 to realize the latest performance optimizations, such as enhanced CPU usage, improved garbage collector (GC) management, and memory allocation optimizations.

“We rely on .NET to achieve high performance and security. We’re developing cloud-native and AI-powered apps, ensuring our solutions are robust and scalable,” Queiroz explains.

Blip is embracing the comprehensive ecosystem offered by .NET, which aligns with the company’s growth goals and the demands of the evolving digital landscape. Blip is now developing a large part of its platform components in C#, providing a scalable and future-proof solution that not only improves system robustness but also opens new opportunities to innovate its products and services. 

Optimizing further to maximize efficiency

Blip can autoscale its resources to meet traffic increases, ensuring consistent performance even during peak times. This scalability is crucial for maintaining a seamless customer experience, regardless of the volume of traffic.

Colen says, “.NET provides support across the platform, and its use with Azure gives us the flexibility to allocate resources on demand.” 

.NET brought significant improvements to platform stability, scalability, and the user experience. In addition, the Azure platform made interactions more efficient for companies that communicate with thousands of customers daily. The combined implementation was a game changer for Blip.

Sérgio Passos, CTO at Blip, notes, “We leverage AI to personalize brand–customer conversations, ensuring more meaningful interactions. By gaining deeper insights into consumer behavior, we empower brands to craft targeted marketing campaigns and innovative strategies driven by data.”

In addition, the improvements that Blip saw directly translated to its customers too.

“The challenge lies in bringing together vast amounts of data from multiple sources, ensuring our platform can scale as brands do, providing an exceptional experience. As one example, we created a copilot for one of our finance customers, giving its customer service agents suggested answers during customer conversations. The agents using the tool completed twice as many loans as the control group,” says Colen.

Realizing impact as the AI journey continues

By adopting Azure, Blip has modernized its architecture to process more than 1 billion messages each month, totaling more than 80 billion to date. The solution Blip built goes far beyond a typical chatbot offering, providing valuable contact intelligence that enhances sales, customer care, and engagement. Blip is also continuing to innovate at an even faster pace to meet and get ahead of customer needs.

Passos explains, “We are seeing a dramatic change in customer behavior, and we understand the way people want to communicate with brands, moving from voice to mobile app to text. With our first copilot for service agents, we saw around a 20% to 30% acceptance rate for AI suggestions. Now, there’s an 80% acceptance rate.” 

Blip’s collaboration with Microsoft has been critical in turning the company’s ideas into reality. By embracing the power of Azure, Blip has enhanced its operational efficiency, delivering high-performance, secure, and scalable applications that meet the needs of its customers and future-proof its business.

“Azure has been instrumental to our success. From on-demand resources to advanced AI models, we’re transforming customer experiences, with true contact intelligence. By harnessing our data with advanced solutions, we’re shaping the future of brand communication,” concludes Oliveira.

Streamlining sales operations to focus on high-value activities

Fujitsu, a Japan-based global leader in information and communication technology (ICT), continues to push innovation to enhance productivity and operational efficiency. Addressing inefficiencies in its sales processes, Fujitsu targeted automating the time-intensive task of generating sales proposals.

Proposal creation demanded significant time, limiting sales teams from engaging in high-value activities like strategic planning, building customer relationships, and tailoring solutions to clients’ needs. New salespeople struggled to navigate Fujitsu’s extensive product portfolio and access dispersed expertise. Both new and seasoned staff faced challenges in identifying current data sources, calibrating and consolidating them from across Fujitsu’s vast infrastructure, and creating accurate, client-specific proposals.

To address these challenges, Fujitsu developed an AI-powered solution to automate repetitive tasks, enabling sales teams to shift focus to more strategic, customer-centric efforts.

Leveraging Azure AI Agent Service for intelligent automation

Building on its long-standing partnership with Microsoft, Fujitsu used Azure AI Agent Service within Azure AI Foundry to develop an intelligent, scalable AI agent for sales automation. Led by Hirotaka Ito, Lead engineer of AI, Digital System Platform Unit, Fujitsu, the project leveraged Microsoft’s platform-as-a-service (PaaS) capabilities to ensure seamless integration into Fujitsu’s existing workflows, enabling the agent to handle foundational proposal tasks that previously required grinding hours of effort by teams.

The AI-driven agent interprets user inputs, integrates data from multiple sources, and produces precise, up-to-date proposals in a fraction of the time. At the solution’s core is Fujitsu Kozuchi Composite AI, powered by Semantic Kernel, a tool that orchestrates multiple specialized AI agents. These agents dynamically retrieve and synthesize knowledge from scattered internal sources, ensuring proposals are tailored and data-driven.

“Conventional generative AI, conversational AI, and retrieval-automation generation (RAG) systems alone didn’t meet our needs,” says Ito-san. “We are using Microsoft’s Semantic Kernel and Azure AI Agent Service to orchestrate multiple specialized AI agents and an orchestrator AI to coordinate them to answer questions as a team,” he adds.

Azure AI Agent Service also simplified integration with tools like Azure AI Search, streamlining knowledge retrieval and organization. “The particularly useful aspect was the ease of integration between Azure AI Agent Service and Azure AI Search—it saved us time, and the implementation was very easy from the Azure portal,” notes Ito-san.

Beyond generating proposals, the AI agent serves as a knowledge retrieval system, providing new hires with detailed product information and strategic guidance. 

During the proof-of-concept phase, Fujitsu refined the AI agent using feedback from sales teams, optimizing usability before full deployment. Fujitsu AI tools including the AI agent empowers around 38,000 users. 

Delivering impact and shaping the future of AI at Fujitsu

The launch of the agent has yielded measurable results. Sales proposal creation is now 67% more productive, saving countless hours that can be redirected toward customer engagement and strategic planning. Sales teams have praised the tool for addressing knowledge gaps and allowing them to build stronger customer relationships.

Looking ahead, Fujitsu plans to expand use of this and other AI agents to address broader organizational challenges, including automating strategic planning, improving customer interaction, and enhancing knowledge sharing. Future iterations aim to optimize collaboration among AI agents and tackle more complex tasks. 

“In the future, we expect AI to not just assist with tasks but also generate strategies and proposals,” Ito-san says. Fujitsu envisions AI as a transformative tool to empower employees and enhance productivity. “AI will support our customers’ needs more effectively by handling tasks and developing strategies, making employees more efficient, and enabling innovation at a level previously unattainable,” he adds.

The learnings from this internally-facing project are also adding valuable guidance to other AI-based initiatives at Fujitsu. Its principles and development are adding insight to the company's ongoing initiatives like Fujitsu Kozuchi and its Composite AI platform, a set of secure, reliable AI services Fujitsu's customers are using to enhance connectivity across an enterprise's tools and improve productivity and processes for employees. 

Similar in ambition to Ito-san's sales agent, “Composite AI understands user requests by natural language input and selects the best AI technologies from our environment to create efficient solutions,” explains Hiro Kobashi, Research Director at Fujitsu Research of America. 

Fujitsu's teams are exploring how Azure AI Agent Service might enhance and expand the capabilities and scale of Composite AI in use by many of Fujitsu's customers. Ito notes that Azure AI Agent Service’s modular design and orchestration features could further expand the capabilities of these tools. 

By leveraging Microsoft Azure’s infrastructure and innovative tools, Fujitsu has not only improved its sales efficiency but also laid the groundwork for broader AI-driven transformation. This partnership demonstrates how AI automation can empower teams, optimize operations, and create value for customers both within and beyond Fujitsu.

Australia is one of the most expensive places in the world to own a home, and the housing crisis there means many people can wait 10 years or more for social and affordable housing. Head Start Homes supports people who face economic, educational, and other barriers to homeownership. The nonprofit’s clients are First Nations Peoples, single moms, people with disabilities, migrants, and refugees. The Head Start Homes team works with clients for free and as long as needed to become ready for a mortgage, secure discounted home loan products through banking partners, and buy a home.  

“We’re providing more equal access to homeownership because it breaks cycles of disadvantage and disrupts intergenerational poverty,” explains Stephen Woodlands, Founder and Managing Director of Head Start Homes.

Client and new homeowner Charlene lived this transformation. A mother and proud Dunghutti woman who had experienced homelessness, Charlene worked closely with Head Start Homes to increase her savings by 500% and buy a house of her own. “Before I met Head Start Homes, I never thought in my wildest dreams this day would happen,” she says. “I’m so excited that my children will now have a forever home.”

This innovative nonprofit has been committed to technology-enabled solutions since its founding, so adopting Microsoft 365 Copilot was a natural next step. “When we saw Microsoft had a secure generative AI product, we got it as soon as we could,” Woodlands says. 

Head Start Homes worked with Microsoft partner ONGC Systems in nonprofit-specific roundtables and workshops. This reinforced Head Start Homes’ confidence that the AI assistant was the right generative AI tool for secure operations and maximum benefits. Copilot now helps Head Start Homes multiply their productivity, focus even more on clients, and expand to address the housing crisis.

Doing more for clients

As a recently established nonprofit, Head Start Homes staff take on multiple roles. “We all wear a lot of hats,” says Jo Formosa, Chief of Empowerment Products, Services, and Projects at Head Start Homes. “Copilot is like having somebody working alongside you. We rely on it to help us deliver what we deliver.” 

The management team reports that Copilot has increased their productivity by 30% or more. They direct Copilot to take minutes and record action items from meetings, create graphics from de-identified data, craft job descriptions, and draft policies that help them serve clients. To generate more support and celebrate client successes, staff instruct Copilot to write first drafts of marketing materials for social media, newsletters, and more. “Copilot helps us get the word out about the good work we’re doing, quicker,” says Natasha Kahn, Chief of Communications, Fundraising and Company Secretary at Head Start Homes. 

Efficiencies gained with Copilot free up more time for getting clients into safe, affordable, and comfortable homes. This creates a ripple effect. When a Head Start Homes client moves into their new home, that can free up social or affordable housing so someone on a limited income can move in.

The nonprofit chose Copilot because, unlike other models, it operates within a closed environment and keeps their confidential information out of the public domain. It easily integrates into the organization’s Microsoft stack and security platform. Head Start Homes always reviews and polishes AI-generated content.

Copilot also helps Head Start Homes improve the client experience. It speeds response time to inquiries, makes it easier to search across platforms to answer questions, and opens up space to forge stronger relationships with clients. Staff also use its coaching function to draft emails faster. Woodlands says, “It’s important for the not-for-profit sector to use technology because it enables you to spend more time with your clients, creating greater impact for communities.”

Growing the homeownership pipeline 

With Australia’s ongoing housing crisis, “we have big waitlists and unlimited demand for our services,” Woodlands explains. Head Start Homes is rapidly expanding to meet this need. It has doubled its team in the last year to help even more clients. Copilot is facilitating this swift growth.

Kahn calls Copilot a “mini HR” that helps find the right fit for open roles and speeds the hiring process. Head Start Homes uses Copilot to draft job descriptions and compare resumes to unfilled positions’ responsibilities. Kahn turned to the AI assistant during her own recent onboarding, asking Copilot questions to draw on organizational knowledge saved in Microsoft Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint, and elsewhere. 

With the benefits and cost savings of Copilot, Head Start Homes can hire high-impact, client-facing positions. The organization just brought on two new financial capability workers, who are essential in helping clients to enhance their financial capability and afford a home. “We wouldn’t have been able to hire them so efficiently without Copilot,” Woodlands says.

The AI assistant facilitates collaboration and accountability for the virtual team, too. While Copilot takes notes, summarizes meetings, and records to-dos, staff concentrate on problem-solving together. They add AI-generated meeting notes to the agenda of follow-up conversations so everyone always knows their deliverables. “Copilot keeps us on the same page in real time,” Formosa says. 

Head Start Homes is making the most of technology to pursue its ambitious vision of an Australia where everyone has a safe and stable home. “With Copilot, I’m not bogged down by the little things that are important but can get in the way of the bigger picture,” Formosa says. “It allows me the freedom to focus on the more strategic work we need to do.”

That crucial work includes generating growth, which includes securing funding to scale up their services and innovate new products. The team uses the time saved through Copilot to write grant applications, and the AI assistant drafts parts of the applications to give development staff a head start. “Without Copilot, we would submit fewer big applications a year, which would greatly reduce the money flowing into our organization,” Woodlands says. 

Finally, Head Start Homes invests even more in supporter relationships with the help of generative AI. Staff use Copilot to help draft reports for funders and industry partners, based on templates of past reports. For example, Copilot draws information from internal documents to help provide reporting as required by their funding agreements. In-depth communication maintains funding and may even increase future support, leading to more people opening the door to their forever homes. 

Woodlands says, “Everything we do is about empowering our clients, so when we save time with Copilot, it means we have more time to help our clients achieve their homeownership dreams.”

Helping people connect to trusted financial opportunities has been the aim of Raiffeisen Bank International (RBI) since its inception. The cooperative bank, with its headquarters in Vienna, Austria, is “at the gateway to Central and Eastern Europe,” says Armin Woworsky, Distinguished Engineer at RBI. “We’ve been building bridges to both established and emerging markets for customers in these regions and internationally for decades.”

RBI’s 43,000 employees offer a wide range of financial services, including retail and corporate banking, leasing, asset management, and mergers and acquisitions, serving 16.5 million customers in 11 markets. “With ongoing growth and our mission of innovation and superior customer experiences, we wanted to be proactive in using new technologies to support our staff. The answer was a full digital transformation with AI at the core,” explains Woworsky.

Focus on customer experiences

Knowing that AI integration is a journey involving stages of innovation and adoption, Woworsky says RBI wanted to start by using AI to automate repetitive tasks and document intelligence. It also aimed to more rapidly summarize legal, regulation, and banking documents. RBI wanted to set the stage for the ability to build applications to enhance customer services. “We decided to build a ChatGPT that could free our employees to provide more personalized customer care, while also helping customers help themselves more effectively,” says Woworsky.

RBI was already using Azure as part of its cloud strategy. “With our need to ensure security, privacy, and compliance with European regulations while adopting robust, scalable AI technologies, Microsoft was the right provider—and we knew Azure AI Foundry would be instrumental in helping us realize our long-term goals,” says Woworsky.

With Azure AI Foundry, RBI used Azure OpenAI Service and Azure AI Search as primary tools. RBI used the latest GPT-series models on Azure OpenAI Service. “With Azure OpenAI Service, we can build solutions to address our company’s unique needs and also specific issues within the banking industry, both of which require assurances for data quality and effective data management,” says Woworsky. With responsible use of AI top of mind for AI deployments, RBI uses Azure AI Content Safety to moderate content. 

“Using Azure AI Foundry, we can build solutions to address our company’s unique needs and also specific issues within the banking industry, both of which require assurances for data quality and effective data management,” says Woworsky.

“Azure OpenAI Service and Azure AI Search are key enablers for us,” adds Woworsky. “They provided the agility and scalability needed to support AI solutions across the organization, helping us design RBI ChatGPT for the bank’s most common use cases.” These include line leveling in reconciliation reporting and extracting and summarizing public news articles and financial reports. Employees can now more rapidly search and access information, creating quick customer summaries, drafting emails, and answering regulatory questions. RBI is also employing automated responses to common customer inquiries and supporting employees in creating content. 

An ongoing evolution

The RBI ChatGPT was first deployed to 2,000 users and now has an active user base of over 20,000. Employees report that previously time-consuming tasks can be performed quickly. They now have the flexibility to spend time on more value-added tasks or helping customers with complex questions. “People are feeling better about their jobs; we’re seeing greater collaboration and faster resolution of customer issues,” says Woworsky.

Based on Azure OpenAI Service and Azure AI Foundry, RBI ChatGPT will support a variety of internal processes, from facility management to legal services and defining complex products for large corporate customers. RBI employees are empowered to support the ongoing evolution of RBI ChatGPT through a new feature called “yellowGPTs.” Designed by RBI ChatGPT users, yellowGTPs lets employees contribute solutions, content, and ideas for improving efficiency. Users can work with their data to build dedicated knowledge bases and share them on the platform.

In addition, as part of its ongoing digital transformation, RBI is developing a platform that can scale and bring RBI ChatGPT and other generative AI tools and functionality to the entire organization. RBI is also experimenting with tying the latest o1 model on Azure OpenAI Service into their application framework. “We hope to make everyone an AI power user,” Woworsky says. “Every employee needs to understand how to interact with language models to remain competitive and provide the best customer experiences.”

Woworsky adds that with Microsoft and AI, RBI’s commitment to customers and their care is stronger than ever. “We’ve set the stage for broad-scale use of advanced technology to provide superior services that can evolve with our customer needs—that's a true differentiator.”

Nature without borders: Protecting, restoring, and enhancing the life of parks and animals through technology

One day, Peace Parks Foundation learned that a herd of wild elephants had arrived at the front gate of one of the national parks it supports. “We watched as the staff opened the park gates, the elephants walked in, and they made it their new home.” recalls Wayne Brider, ICT Manager at Peace Parks Foundation. “As a team, we must be doing something right for animals to be migrating to our conservation areas. It shows we’re creating the right environment for nature to heal and rebuild itself, and we’re providing the right support to enable the teams on the ground to do their jobs properly.”

It’s a remarkable story—and the foundation has many more like it. Based in southern Africa, Peace Parks Foundation has long been committed to supporting the preservation and enhancement of protected areas and ecosystems through partnerships and collaboration. With a philosophy of nature without borders, the foundation focuses on conserving large transboundary landscapes, fostering healthy and balanced ecosystems. This philosophy is in line with the natural migration animals undertook before protected areas were fenced off and national borders were created.

Peace Parks Foundation oversees 68 million hectares of land within transfrontier conservation areas (TFCAs), and recently supported the reestablishment of the first Big Five national park in Mozambique, a country in southeast Africa. It has also relocated more than 18,000 animals and helped create the conditions for the birth of the first rhinoceros in Mozambique’s Zinave National Park in more than 40 years. In support of the Mozambique government, Peace Parks is helping maintain and increase additional wildlife populations. “Working for Peace Parks presents the opportunity to do something on a legacy scale that’s going to be remembered,” says Brider. 

Everyone who works at Peace Parks Foundation cares deeply about animals and habitat restoration. “I love seeing these animals traverse the way they used to, being able to return to watering holes and feeding areas,” says Bronwen Struwig, Financial Controller at Peace Parks Foundation. Staff are equally committed to working with local communities to protect wildlife and reduce pressures on what nature provides. They do so through collaborating on projects and programs that benefit both people and nature, promoting balance and peace. “We work with the people living in these landscapes to build peaceful coexistence between communities and nature, ensuring they are in a position to continue the legacy on their own for generations to come,” adds Ilze van der Merwe, Business Analyst at Peace Parks Foundation.

Given the sheer scale and criticality of its work, the foundation has made technology a “force enabler,” notes Brider. For example, staff use an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system, built on Microsoft Dynamics 365, to plan, monitor, manage, and share information with the right people at the right time. However, its technology needs defy normal conditions. Working in areas where 3G may not exist means field staff have to build infrastructure, bring power, and use satellite technology to communicate from sites located up to several hours away from the closest airport. “If somebody says they need to deploy something, we have to ask if it can withstand being stepped on by an elephant,” explains Brider. If physical equipment is installed too low, it becomes a hyena chew toy. Placed too high, it may get whacked by the tusk of an elephant investigating its blinking light. “We’ve actually had Starlink receivers flattened by elephants because the motor whirred at the wrong time,” he adds.

That’s also why Peace Parks Foundation stress tests technology at a level few do. “If I can run something in a remote national park, I can guarantee it’ll work anywhere in the world,” says Brider. When the foundation wanted to make its environment more current and comprehensive, it decided to move to Azure. The more it can store in the cloud, the more accessible its systems can be—and the less likely they are to be affected by park conditions.

Sustaining and streamlining field, head office, and financial operations

Sustainability—in all of its forms—underpins every decision and action taken at Peace Parks Foundation. From a technology standpoint, the foundation seeks vendors that will be around to support and sustain its long-term projects, which may last more than 10 years. “It’s critical that our technologies grow with us and that we can implement and tie ancillary systems together,” says Struwig. The Peace Parks ICT department also prioritizes vendors that truly understand the value of environmental sustainability and what it’s trying to achieve and, in turn, offer a broad spectrum of scalable solutions that can stand up to the challenge of being deployed in harsh conditions where technology should not necessarily be deployed. “That’s Microsoft,” adds Brider.

Any solution the foundation builds or selects has to improve performance for the people working around the clock on the park grounds. “Through Azure, we give managers and field staff access to real-time information that helps them better plan and report in certain situations. This includes daily updated budgets to allow for better financial planning and pinpoint where financial transactions are in the system, which also allows for better reporting to vendors and consistent on-time deliveries,” explains van der Merwe. “Making managers and field staff’s time on the ground shorter and more productive adds to their efficiency and our effectiveness because we can move on to the next improvement we want to achieve.”

Peace Parks Foundation now uses its Azure environment to streamline planning and prep work within its head office and make conservation efforts more effective and efficient. Tasks like sifting through the massive amounts of data and reporting from the field are time-consuming for workers. One of the departments that’s benefitted most from efforts to consolidate this information is finance, and along with it, the users of financial data. Information is now much more detailed and relevant to managers than it was when financial processing took place in batches. “We’re capturing invoices from our suppliers a lot quicker, and field workers can report back on finances much faster because we’ve given them user-friendly tools with drop-down lists,” says Struwig. Managers have access to their budget versus actual reports on an almost real-time basis as reports are updated each morning with the previous day’s transactions.

The foundation has also introduced commitment accounting. That means once managers place a purchase order or sign a supplier agreement, they can instantly access records to track not just what they’ve spent but also what they’ve committed themselves to. Budgets are captured in the finest detail where required, and expenses are allocated accordingly. This is especially important as some donors are very specific in their reporting requirements, and all donors are entitled to know how their funds are being spent. “We are also able to report at the country, park, and TFCA level to be able to determine and compare costs from one year to the next. This aids us in planning for the future immensely and makes determining our exact financial position so much quicker than was previously possible,” says Struwig.

Analyzing environmental change data and sharing information more securely

Monitoring and evaluation are essential to Peace Parks Foundation’s business, both in the field and its head office. Moving forward, the foundation wanted a unified view of the parks it supports and departments. To better track environmental change and the impact of climate change on human-animal conflict, the foundation is developing a model using Azure and Microsoft Copilot with reporting through Power BI. Business analysts across the foundation, including van der Merwe, work hands on to design custom Power BI reports for this environmental data and for other projects, including budgeting. “When we presented the reports to managers and showed them the information available, they were so thrilled,” says Brider. It will soon use Azure Data Lake to bring together all its information sources and Copilot to mine the data for valuable insights. “We wouldn’t have been able to assist our parks without technology,” adds Brider. “It was never going to work on paper.”

As part of its shift to Azure, foundation leadership also made a conscious decision to strengthen cybersecurity by introducing online backups, sandbox test environments, and other capabilities that it can keep synced and scale as needed. “Moving to Azure made it easier to enhance and grow our environment for whatever we need,” says Brider. It plans to further safeguard its data using row-level and cell-level security from Microsoft Purview.

“The greatest story”

At the outset of its technology journey, Peace Parks Foundation had ideas of what it could do and what it wanted to do. For good reason, Brider says, “Our original plan looked nothing like everything we have now. We unlocked this Azure toolkit, and now we’re seeing all that we can do.” This speaks to the foundation-wide attitude of pushing boundaries, constantly reimagining processes, and being unafraid to try something different.

The foundation now innovates on a daily basis without worrying about the reliability, durability, scalability, or security of its environment. “The true test of our success is that we’re continually evolving and enhancing things, which shows that the business understands our solutions and uses them, not as IT products but as business tools,” says Brider. In fact, discussions with C-suite executives now start with them asking, ‘Can we put it in the cloud?’ “The ability to use this technology to help achieve the Peace Parks Foundation mission is one of the great stories we tell,” concludes Brider.

The foundation moved to Microsoft Azure to make systems more accessible and overcome connectivity challenges in its remote environments. It’s using Power BI to track environmental change and expects AI to help it better deploy people and resources.
With the new environment, Peace Parks Foundation has overdelivered on its initial plans and now plans to bring together all its data, mine it for actionable insights, and take a cloud-first approach for future deployments.

New cybersecurity approaches enable vigorous protection of creativity and intellectual property

Both physical security and cybersecurity represent key challenges for SHUEISHA Inc., whose intellectual property (IP) includes innumerable global successes in manga, novels, and other areas.

Since 2020, several triggers progressively stimulated SHUEISHA’s consideration of cybersecurity, as Information System Department Manager Kenji Okamoto recalls. “We used to rely heavily on Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI) for cybersecurity countermeasures. However, once remote work took off with the COVID-19 State of Emergency declaration in April 2020, we discovered that many employees had no computer at home and relied solely on the office VDI, so we hastily procured and distributed notebook computers. Then in 2022, we learned that support was ending for existing VDI and IP-PBX. This chain of events caused us to rethink the fundamentals of our cybersecurity.”

In June 2022, the company underwent structural reorganization, and the Information System Office which was previously in the General Affairs Division became the independent Information System Department. Establishing an Information Management Office within the Information System Department allowed the cybersecurity enhancement project to proceed swiftly. SHUEISHA was able to select a unified plan from Microsoft solutions to integrate the environment, transitioning away from the previous use of differing products for authentication infrastructure, endpoint security, and VDI. Okamoto describes what happened in greater detail.

“Just before COVID-19 hit, we had signed up with Office 365 E1 and switched over to Exchange Online and Outlook on March 1, 2020. Enabling mail usage both within and outside the company allowed us to transition to remote work without any major disruption to business. During this period, we grappled with what to do next. When it was announced in October 2023 that support would end for Office 2016 and 2019 cloud connections, we considered transitioning to Microsoft 365 E5. A great benefit gained by unifying with Microsoft products is the switch from VDI to Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) and IP-PBX to Microsoft Teams Phone, which enabled a more convenient environment and closed security gaps.”

In December 2022, SHUEISHA decided to introduce Microsoft 365 E5. A major system renovation began the following month once the company had procured its license. About a year was required to realize zero-trust security utilizing Microsoft 365 E5.

“Password-less authentication”—random generation of extra-long passwords

SHUEISHA fully utilizes the Microsoft 365 E5 features. This of course includes endpoint security such as anti-virus measures, as well as sustained secured connections to SaaS apps and automated management of the total network. (See the conceptual diagram.)

SHUEISHA relies particularly heavily on Microsoft Entra ID P2 (previously, Azure AD)—the authentication platform—with Privileged Identity Management (PIM) minimizing information leakage by restricting access to key resources based on time and approval. The restrictive structure requires password-less access authentication not only from employees, but from collaborating external staff as well.

SHUEISHA utilizes password-less employee authentication through Windows Hello, which relies on biometric authentication, and Microsoft Authenticator, a smartphone authentication app. Akihiro Sutou, Information Management Section Chief in the Information System Department, explained that in March 2024, management revised Active Directory passwords, making them longer and completely random, “so that no employee is aware of his or her password.”

“Employees joining the company in April 2024 did not immediately receive a password. Device authentication alone controlled safe access to the company system. This basically eliminated the risk of unauthorized access through password leakage. So today, I would address any information leak by initially investigating internal fraud.”

Mobile devices such as (corporate-issued) iPhones equipped with Microsoft Authenticator are also centrally managed using Microsoft Intune. Compliance with corporate policies is routinely monitored.

Kensuke Watanabe, manager of the Information Management Section in the Information System Department, comments on one success resulting from the initiative: “We are now seeing a change in security awareness within the company. The other day, an editing department requested a new tool. As it could not be incorporated into our single sign-on environment, we responded that ‘at present, you will need to issue and manage your own password.’ ‘Ah, we need a password,’ came the disappointed reaction. This delighted us, as it indicated that people were now aware of the safety and convenience of our password-less, single sign-on. The editing department staff were pleased to learn that we plan to incorporate the desired tool into the single sign-on environment. This marks a significant difference from the past, when the editing department expected to manage their own IDs and passwords every time they used a tool.”

High-level security without special effort and wide range of cost reductions

Sutou explains that, “the major reason SHUEISHA incorporated Microsoft 365 E5 was that we saw the merits of the ‘high-level security without special effort,’ which our IT partner was advocating at the time.”

“We recommend Microsoft 365 E5 for the clear reason that it reduces the enormous time required for security operation maintenance.  When using multiple companies’ products and services, we need to monitor the ever-changing cyberthreat landscape and update individual products. As updates accumulate, their coverage changes, and features may conflict with each other. That is not something which can be handled by a small information systems department. Microsoft 365 E5 allows security monitoring and maintenance of a safe environment by activating each feature in turn and then monitoring the overall system through the dashboard. This is a great benefit. Keeping operations simple has brightened the mood in the Information System Department.”

Sutou also points out great cost savings. “For example, with VDI, updating existing products would necessitate an estimated annual cost per user of 100,000-200,000 (690-1,379USD)* yen. The AVD we are switching over to is a pay-as-you-go system which costs only one-tenth the amount. Differing departments in SHUEISHA used differing BI tools, but they are now unified in Power BI Pro, which is included in Microsoft 365 E5. That also helped with cost savings. Discontinuing multiple security products and switching over to Microsoft 365 E5 enabled great cost reductions.”

*Using an exchange rate of 145 yen/USD.

The dual security reports Sutou issued in late 2023 highlight SHUEISHA’s use of Power BI. One overview visualized the number of attacks on the company in total, while a second individualized report tallied the attacks on each employee’s account along with how many spam mails were received. SHUEISHA has 760 employees (including contracted part-time workers). One might expect that creating a report for that number of individuals would take a tremendous amount of time, but Sutou explained that it took “less than 30 minutes.”

“It was just a matter of exporting data accessed from Microsoft Sentinel, so creating the report took no time at all. Employees could visualize the number of attacks on their own accounts, and many voiced their surprise. It was a great opportunity to elevate their security awareness and illuminate the work we do in the Information System Department.”

Dramatically reducing stress with Microsoft Copilot for Security

The cost benefits from incorporating Microsoft 365 E5 led to smooth approval for adding a new feature—Microsoft Copilot for Security—which supports security management tasks with generative AI. Sutou professes that, from the beginning, his sights were set on incorporating this optional product, which officially came onboard in April 2024. 

“We’d had our eye on the improved work efficiency generative AI empowers for some time. When Microsoft Security Copilot was officially released, an analyst suggested that it would improve response speed by 22%. My sense is that it has exceeded that. And it’s not only the response speed, but the peace of mind you enjoy. At any rate, it has reduced stress in our work. When incidents occur, Copilot quickly issues a summary and can formulate queries with simple commands. I was in the Sales Department before moving to the Information Management Section and have very little experience of drafting queries. It was not easy for us to create KQLs to query Microsoft Sentinel logs, but that task can be handled speedily with Microsoft Security Copilot. We now experience far less stress in operations management.”

Security talent shortages reportedly plague Japanese companies, and SHUEISHA is no different. In fact, Section Manager Watanabe shifted over from the Editing Department, while Sutou was previously in Sales, making a similar in-house transfer.

“The constant fostering of security talent is a major issue faced by many companies.  I think we need a dual focus: the progression towards operations management less dependent on skilled security talent and the continual training and acquisition of such talent. I believe Microsoft Security Copilot can be extremely helpful in that regard,” affirms Sutou.

“The less pressure we experience, the easier we can initially respond to incidents. We have only begun to utilize generative AI, but there is no doubt it will effectively support non-specialized and unskilled tasks. The simplicity of incorporating such a beneficial feature is one of the great things about Microsoft security solutions.”

New working styles for security managers

Microsoft 365 E5 and Microsoft Copilot for Security have generated many benefits for SHUEISHA, but Watanabe points out another direct advantage felt in-house regarding new working styles since the advent of COVID-19.

“We were surprised at how smoothly the transition was to Teams Phone. The shift to Teams Phone was about 99% complete as of April 2024, but we had already begun using the product before that. We can directly find and call employees via the Teams app on iPhones, and we can also use it for conferences and daily communication among worksite editing staff.” 

Watanabe describes how the use of other tools has also changed from the past. “Thinking back on my time in the Editing Department, the staff had used a variety of SaaS apps… but not necessarily for any profound reason. Now when I explain the many benefits—the contract with Adobe, the many digital tools available, and the handy functions and features that Teams offers—they are easily convinced to switch over. SHUEISHA has absolutely no intention of limiting the inspiring environment for creators, and we intend to provide a digital workspace in which all kinds of SaaS apps can be used safely. I find it greatly significant that the company is devising this environment in which everybody can work comfortably and with peace of mind.”

Okamoto adds the following comments in conclusion. “It has been about a year since we integrated Microsoft 365 E5, and a month or so since we added Microsoft Security Copilot. Even the working style in the Information System Department has changed, and we are now interacting more with those in other departments. Despite the beneficial results, switching systems can put a burden on users, so we’d like to collaborate with the help desk in strengthening the support system.”
Executive summary:
Numerous SaaS apps and digital tools are used in the creative pursuits of writers, creators, and editors, but issues surround the protection of intellectual property. Meanwhile, working styles have been changing rapidly since the onset of COVID-19. These challenges have made it essential to strengthen cybersecurity.
Major publishing company SHUEISHA Inc. has incorporated Microsoft 365 E5, putting its features to full use. This of course includes endpoint security such as anti-virus measures, but also sustained secured connections to SaaS apps and automated management of the total network. SHUEISHA is also utilizing Microsoft Security Copilot.
These additions have resulted in high-level security without special effort and have achieved a wide range of cost reductions. Security Copilot has enabled even faster incident response, boosting the confidence and effectiveness of cybersecurity personnel.

legal-i is a Swiss insurtech startup whose ultra-modern GenAI solution helps insurance companies process and assess medical insurance claims more efficiently. Its product transforms PDF-based medical records into interactive patient histories, gives an insight into previous diagnoses, and facilitates predictions about future developments—including the likely course of repeat cases and the best possible treatment options. Cases can be dealt with faster and more equitably as a result. The platform delivers benefits wherever medical insurance claims need to be processed and inspected by hand, such as in the case of accident insurance, daily benefits insurance, disability insurance, life insurance, and liability insurance. These benefits apply at expert assessment centers, during recourse to law and in communication between insurance experts and independent medical examiners.

legal-i signed up for the Microsoft for Startups Founders Hub program in 2023.

legal-i was founded in Switzerland in 2019. Its core mission? To tackle one central challenge in the healthcare and insurance sector: the need to process unstructured medical case histories. The data comes from all kinds of sources—including doctor’s reports, laboratory findings, expert assessments, and administrative documents—and is available in varying formats and levels of quality. Processing all this material by hand is difficult and time-consuming, and the outcome of a case is heavily dependent on the quality of the specialist handling it—and potentially even how that person is feeling on a given day. The consequences for insurers are significant indeed. In contrast, legal-i saw a GenAI-based platform as the solution: “Our aim was to support case processing specialists in a way that helped them find relevant information quickly and analyze it accurately. As a result, skilled staff can make better-founded decisions, while insured individuals benefit from more efficient and reliable processing,” explains Achim Kohli, CEO and co-founder of legal-i. With the aid of Microsoft and leading-edge Azure technology, the startup developed a GenAI solution that is now used by leading healthcare providers and insurance companies such as Baloise. The solution can be understood as a form of augmented intelligence that relieves specialists of laborious tasks and helps them make sound decisions. It optimizes processes, saves precious resources, and improves both employee and customer satisfaction.

AI-driven efficiency: How the legal-i platform works

Medical insurance claims often include a broad spectrum of unstructured documents, which is precisely where the GenAI solution from legal-i comes into play. This solution uses cutting-edge AI technologies such as Azure OpenAI Service to analyze unstructured information, classify it, and transform it into a clear form that can be readily processed.

“Our AI models are specially trained to recognize and automatically categorize different types of documents such as doctor’s reports, laboratory findings, and administrative records. And all this is done irrespective of the language,” Kohli explains. “The next step is for the platform to extract all relevant information and use it to produce a structured overview—what is referred to as the ‘case DNA.’” This DNA serves as the basis for legal-i’s Agentic Large Language Model Framework, which accesses the case DNA to answer specific questions from the experts.

Automation hugely accelerates such complex data processing but takes only a fraction of the time compared to manual processing. Compliance with all current valid security and data protection standards is naturally guaranteed by cutting-edge encryption methods and bring-your-own key concepts. In addition, the models trained by legal-i make life easier for case processing staff by quickly summarizing reports or documents and explaining specific medical terms.

The latest feedback from customers shows that, with legal-i, insurance companies can process cases up to 80% faster, with as much as four times greater accuracy and payout outcomes optimized by as much as 11%.

Microsoft: A strong and reliable partner for technology, expertise, and security

Taking part in the Microsoft for Startups Founders Hub program was a crucial success factor for legal-i. Thanks to free Azure credits and early access to innovative technologies such as Azure OpenAI Service, the developers were able to work on the highest technological level: “Rapid progress in large language models in particular raised our product to a new technological level,” the CEO affirms. “Thanks to our partnership with Microsoft, we have constantly been—and still remain—on the leading edge of technological development.”

That said, the program was about much more than merely providing technology. legal-i also benefits from intensive and productive dialogue with the relevant Microsoft team in Switzerland. Extensive knowledge transfer proved to be especially valuable, as the experts at Microsoft contributed their depth of technological knowledge and strategic insights into market dynamics. All this significantly accelerated further development of the platform and market access. Additionally, access to an international network of experts and potential customers opened up new opportunities for scaling: “Right from the outset, Microsoft walked with us through every step and passed on contacts that played an essential part in our success,” Kohli notes.

The company’s cooperation with Microsoft also turned out to be groundbreaking in relation to the security and data protection standards that are required in the healthcare and insurance sectors. Microsoft Azure guarantees seamless, end-to-end data encryption on the client’s side, but also during transmission and temporary storage in the cloud. Local data centers ensure that data remains within the relevant national borders. Also, the Azure Key Vault’s bring-your-own-key principle ensures that customers retain full control over data encryption. “We work with the most sensitive data in the world,” Kohli stresses, “so for us, the strictest standards of security are non-negotiable.”

More efficiency, less paper: legal-i and Baloise join forces to shape the digital future

Collaboration with Baloise, one of Switzerland’s biggest insurers, illustrates how legal-i is revolutionizing complex processes. The insurance company teamed up with legal-i back in 2020 to launch a pilot project in its Personal Insurance Legal Services department. This initiative was prompted by a new legal provision requiring that the files to be disclosed had to feature a detailed directory and be ordered systematically and chronologically. Doing all that by hand would have taken a vast amount of time, so legal-i developed a tailor-made solution that automated the dispatch of files and the structuring of documents.

After a successful pilot phase, other departments—including Accident Insurance—were also given access to legal-i. In ongoing cases, the software automatically files any new documents in the right order. But it also simplifies the task of reading out and editing case-related data, extracting medical diagnoses, and summarizing documents. “legal-i helps us find relevant information more quickly and structure mountains of complex files more efficiently,” says Philipp Jeker, Head of Legal & Training at Baloise. “Especially in cases spanning several hundred or even a thousand pages, that makes life so much easier.”

Change management is one factor that proved critical to successful implementation. Finely tuned training courses and the introduction of “superusers” as direct points of contact underpinned the success of the software launch. “Change management is not just about adapting your processes,” explains Michèle Eichenberger, Innovation Manager in Baloise’s Processes & Innovations department. “It is also about empowering your people to understand the potential of new technologies and make effective use of them.”

Looking ahead, Baloise already has plans to deploy legal-i in further departments and to standardize its processes. The legal-i software is currently being localized into French, and an Italian version is due to be launched next year. “Paperless case processing is our vision,“ Jeker says. “Together with legal-i, we are creating more efficient ways of working. And that benefits both our staff and the people we insure.”

New markets, new technologies: legal-i’s strategy for the future

In close consultation with its customers—and with the support of Microsoft, its partner—the legal-i team is committed to continually developing and improving its platform. The aim is for new and adapted AI models to analyze complex cases even more accurately and deliver specific improvements in decision-making. Beyond this, Generative AI could in the future provide automated recommendations on the basis of comparable cases in the past. That would further increase efficiency and enhance quality. Concrete plans already exist for one innovative feature: podcast-like case analysis that would let the insurance company’s staff listen to cases even when they are on the move. This approach is designed to make staff more flexible and productive in their routine work.

At the same time, legal-i is setting its sights on new markets and wants to gradually establish its solution as the global standard for the processing of medical insurance claims. Microsoft’s commercial marketplace will again play a key role as the company scales up its international activities. “Our objective is to help organizations around the world manage medical claims more intelligently and more efficiently,” Kohli explains. “That will be good for our staff, obviously, but the main benefit will be for the people who are insured, as more accurate decisions and better support will help them return to normal life more quickly.” Kohli also sees tremendous potential to spread the technology to other industries. “The principle of analyzing unstructured medical data so that it can be put to good use is not restricted to insurance alone,” the CEO insists. “Sectors such as healthcare in general could benefit just as much. For the future of legal-i, it seems that the sky is the limit!"
