Majid Al Futtaim (MAF Retail), a leading shopping malls, communities, retail, and leisure pioneer across the Middle East, Africa, and Central Asia, holds exclusive rights to the Carrefour brand in 32 countries. It also operates over 450 stores in 14 nations, employing more than 37,000 people and serving over 770,000 customers daily. Majid Al Futtaim’s flagship stores are especially notable in the Emirates.

Bringing AI firepower

Committed to innovative solutions to elevate customers’ shopping experiences, boost productivity, and enhance efficiency, Majid Al Futtaim integrated advanced AI capabilities to further streamline reporting. “We chose Azure OpenAI due to its compatibility with our ecosystem and its technical reliability, which aligns with our partnership with Microsoft,” stated Arun Chandra Mohan, Chief Digital Officer at Majid Al Futtaim Retail. “We also trust the data privacy and security protocols of Microsoft Azure OpenAI.”

Leveraging Azure OpenAI Service as the engine and Power BI with Power Apps as user-friendly interfaces, Majid Al Futtaim is developing a suite of machine learning models, including tools for in-store operational analytics, to power a range of solutions designed to support employees and optimize operations.

AI-driven competitive pricing

Majid Al Futtaim offers a range of 7 million SKUs across its 14 markets, requiring significant commercial and technological effort to manage pricing effectively. The new AI engine, "Spider," ensures competitive pricing by considering various scenarios, recommendations, and periodic promotions, ensuring customers receive the best value and price. Additionally, the engine enhances SKU specifications and information, enabling customers to make better choices and easily navigate their specific needs—whether it’s gluten-free, allergy-friendly, organic, or sustainably packaged.

Majid Al Futtaim is also deploying ‘Geo,’ another solution built with Azure OpenAI Service which enables Carrefour to enhance and advance personalized offers, providing an improved shopping experience that matches customer needs, saves them time and effort, and rewards loyalty. The AI engine provides a wide range of geo-spatial insights and analyzes the demographics in each neighborhood where Carrefour operates.

Interpreting customer feedback

Majid Al Futtaim’s third Azure OpenAI Service solution, “Excellence,” focuses on advanced text analytics and mining. Previously, the marketing team manually processed between 60,000 to 70,000 customer responses weekly, categorizing them and recommending actions for each customer. Mohan shares, “Processing customer intelligence took around seven days and provided only basic analytics. Now, using Azure OpenAI, it takes just three to four minutes, enabling us to process and action much faster, backed by deeper insights.” The team can now capture customer emotions and categorize feedback by aspects like delivery, quality, hygiene, or checkout queue times, generating actionable insights for improvement.

With over 465 stores and up to 120 legal documents per location, Majid Al Futtaim manages a large volume of contracts using “Excellence.” The team can extract relevant information and map it to financial data for analysis and action. Previously, the legal team spent up to seven working days on each contract inquiry compared to now where they simply search and extract relevant information automatically within minutes.

Proactivemanagement with less effort

To ensure the successful adoption of digital transformations, Majid Al Futtaim launched the Enterprise Data Management initiative. This involved running awareness sessions, gathering use cases, and advocating the benefits. “Our team has been incredibly collaborative,” said Mohan. “They have a strong understanding of how technology can elevate their work, enhance productivity, and achieve even better results.”

The successful partnership with Azure OpenAI Service has enabled Majid Al Futtaim to achieve its ultimate goal of cost and efficiency optimization while gaining market independence and understanding. A significant boost in productivity and an improved customer experience was also achieved through combining ‘Spider’ with ‘Geo’ to get the best price for each item and where best to sell based on geo-spatial insights. This combination further reflects Carrefour’s customer-centric approach.

Today, teams across Carrefour spend less time on routine tasks, empowering them to further develop, grow, and progress their scopes and careers. “We now have the opportunity to concentrate more on proactively delivering exceptional products with the highest quality at the right price, time, and place—producing exceptional customer experiences across touchpoints,” Mohan noted.

Looking ahead, Majid Al Futtaim is considering implementing master data management in Microsoft Purview. “This could lead to significant savings in capital expenditures and streamline several days of work down to just a few minutes,” noted Mohan.

Majid Al Futtaim remains committed to continuous improvement and innovation. “As an organization, we are not just data-driven but also value-driven. Our conversations always begin with ‘What value do we want to create, and what is our desired outcome?’ To that end, we continuously seek feedback to improve our products, making them more practical, effective, and efficient,” concluded Mohan.

Story Content:
Dynamic Health Systems (DHS) is an ISV with a mission to address the big problem in healthcare today: the immense pressure on the healthcare system from rising demand due to aging populations and lifestyle changes. Overworked clinical staff and slow efficiency improvements further strain the system, leading to long waiting times and services that fall short of expectations and need.

For a large part of the workload, the solution is clear: engage patients in co-creating their health through motivational care planning and implementation. DHS clinicians have successfully applied this method, achieving better health outcomes with significantly lower clinical input. With its VitruCare 365® patient engagement platform, DHS aims to transform healthcare at scale, so all patients benefit from proactive, integrated, motivational care planning. Released clinical time will enable healthcare providers across the UK and beyond to achieve their clinical goals.

Published research shows care improvements

The inspiration for VitruCare was sparked in 2010, when Prof. Shahid Ali BSc. MB., Ch.B., PhD., FICR., FRCP and now Business Director for DHS, began assessing the impact of more proactive, patient-centric care planning in the context of his own primary care trust in Bradford and for the wider Yorkshire and Humber strategic health authority.

Of the 3,600 patients served by his practice, 40% had a long-term condition and 25% had two or more long-term conditions. His work reviewed the impact of care planning consultations on 50 patients with long-term conditions over a 12-month period.

For the cohort of 50 patients, healthcare contacts declined by 46% in the 12 months following care plan implementation compared with the previous 12 months. There were 71% fewer A&E attendances and 83% fewer acute admissions after patients had adopted care planning. Based on the unit costs for each type of contact, total costs dropped from £97,534 in the 12 months before care planning to £42,752 after care planning—a 56% cost saving for the NHS. It takes no imagination to understand what successful scale-up could mean for healthcare.

The need to scale up results

Around the same time, Ir. Axel Schulte, MBA, Managing Partner of DHS and Service Design Architect, was developing a new healthcare solution based on Microsoft Dynamics 365.

He says, “I realised that existing electronic patient record (EPR) systems were not much more than something akin to a maintenance logbook for a machine. A machine has a standard maintenance plan. But a human is so much more complex and people find themselves in very different circumstances. So a Care Plan is put together by the—often multidisciplinary—care team that serves as an instruction on how to care for this patient. It is stored as a document. But with thousands of personalised care plans it is simply impossible to be proactive. Technology is used to create them, but the mental model has not moved on from paper. They tell you what has been and should be done to the patient—but today there’s no anticipation or planning and no long-term relationship service tools that can make care proactive or dynamic. With the VitruCare 365 technology, the person with the greatest interest in the outcome is now empowered to co-create their health. This is the dynamic change we aim to achieve, hence the name of the company.”

When Axel Schulte met with Shahid Ali and Dr. Richard Pope MD FRCP, also working at the Yorkshire and Humberside SHA at the time and now Clinical Director for DHS, at the Microsoft offices in Reading, the team realised that they shared a vision for a more proactive, holistic approach to healthcare delivery. Axel Schulte’s Dynamics-based solution offered an opportunity to scale up the work of Shahid Ali and Dr. Richard Pope on a regional, national, and international basis.

Shahid Ali recalls, “This is where Axel, Richard, Douglas [Dr. C Douglas Muir BEng, PhD, MBA and now CTO for DHS] and I got together with a view to building something that could enable the NHS as a whole to engage with patients much more effectively.”

Developing on Microsoft Azure with Dynamics 365

“For me, it was always going to be Microsoft,” says Axel Schulte, as he recalls the early decision to develop the new DHS software platform on Microsoft Azure, drawing on much of the functionalities of Microsoft Dynamics 365 and the Microsoft Cloud for Healthcare.

He explains, “We knew we needed a cloud infrastructure for extensibility and scalability and there was—and is—only one cloud provider with a business or enterprise-oriented approach. That professionalism, the capabilities of Azure around data governance and data residency, the Microsoft support, and the technology of Dynamics 365 made building our solution on Azure the only choice.”

“The ease with which we can manage the Azure infrastructure, the extensibility of the solution, the support we receive from Microsoft and the continuing development of Microsoft’s product offerings have justified that decision,” Axel Schulte continues. “I love rummaging around in the kitbag of Microsoft to see what new capabilities we can add to our solution. We had a bot for patients before, but now with Azure OpenAI we were able to give every patient a personalised bot that knows about their conditions and motivational care plans and acts as a realistic assistant!”

Testing the VitruCare platform with patients and practitioners

The initial cohort involved in using the VitruCare platform for motivational care planning included 144 patients with diabetes registered across ten GP surgeries in Bradford. Patients could use the VitruCare app to invent personal life goals, be guided through the creation of action plans based on their integrated health record, and progress towards their achievement. The underlying psychological model employed to create motivational care planning is the Theory of Self Determination (SDT), which has been proven to work very well in healthcare.

“Our solution has the flexibility to enable each patient to create and execute their care plan in a way which is meaningful to them,” explains Axel Schulte. “For example, one of the patients at Shahid’s practice tracks his diabetes by counting the number of slices of bread he eats. It’s not always engaging to compare against a scientific population average that means little to patients. Enabling them to create personal plans is so much more effective because, as the SDT tells us, the goal is personal and motivating and it is the outcome that matters, not the manner of getting there.”

With little to no involvement from practice staff, the cohort’s use of the app led to a dramatically reduced workload. Even when telephone consults were counted as practice “visits,” the survey cohort recorded a 40% reduction in the number of contacts with the primary care teams.

Most importantly, after six months, the cohort of 144 patients demonstrated significant health benefits. While the patients tracked their progress in terms of slices of bread or walks around the park to achieve their personal goals, over the cohort, the practitioners reported:

HbA1c fell by average 16 mmol/mol in glucose blood tests for patients with diabetes. This is equivalent to the change seen following introduction of a new hypoglycaemic medicine (none had been introduced).

A fall in mean blood pressure 5.5 mmHg—which pointed to a 50% reduction in stroke risk.

Weight fell by an average of 2 kg—reducing diabetes risk of between 25-50%, depending on a person's body weight.

Building out apps for a holistic approach to patient care

Today, the usefulness of the VitruCare 365 platform has extended beyond the management of chronic conditions in primary care. It has been deployed within a wide array of healthcare settings, including to manage palliative care with Sue Ryder, to manage student community health services at the University of Lincoln and in the NHS and in adjuvant chemotherapy for breast cancer.

In a palliative care setting, VitruCare 365 enables patients to make carers aware of their biomedical and psychosocial information in near real time. The app helps patients to feel much less worried about their situation. One patient says, “Some of the things I have written on VitruCare I have never told anyone before, mostly because nobody asks. Doctors and Consultants don’t realise how draining it is to keep on repeating my story. I feel tired easily, I forget, I simply don’t have the energy.”

Another patient responds, “I forget what has happened in the past, even if it was yesterday. I do tend to recall the bad things, so this might help me to see the good things that have happened too.”

Including the family in the extended care group has also proved beneficial for boosting peace of mind for patients and their families. One relative explains, “Being able to keep an eye on things at a distance is really useful. I struggle more than my sister because I’m a nurse, everyone expects me to know what’s going on. I don’t see Mum often; that makes it difficult.”

In an NHS Oncology department a patient said, “I feel so well cared for, like a private patient.” The Oncologist reports that, “I start my consultations from a totally different place.” Whilst the Oncology Nurse says, “I know my patients so much better."

Improved engagement for co-creating care led to a reduced length of stay. It reduced total bed days by 50% compared with a parallel cohort not using the technology. This deployment was selected winner of the “Patient Safety in Cancer Care” awarded by MacMillan Cancer Support charity.

Built on the Microsoft Cloud for Healthcare

“From one platform, we provide many services and apps,” explains Axel Schulte. “A patient may be provided with digital health services by multiple clinicians to help with several diseases, or co-morbidities, but the patient experiences it as a single, highly personalised app.”

“It's all wrapped around Dynamics 365 with apps, services, and clinical components that we built ourselves to deploy on the Dynamics 365 platform,” he continues. “We draw on all the capabilities of the collection of technologies that make up Microsoft Cloud for Healthcare, including Azure OpenAI and Azure Health Data Services.”

Azure Health Data Services is a suite of purpose-built technologies for protected health information (PHI) in the cloud. It's built on the global open standards Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) and Digital Imaging Communications in Medicine (DICOM). It makes it easy to ensure data privacy within compliance boundaries, share data securely across healthcare organisations, and generate insights with analytics and AI tools. With Azure OpenAI Service, one can build custom generative AI solutions.

To secure interoperability, VitruCare 365 includes Azure Health Data Services as the safe storage for all PHI. Alternatively, for healthcare providers that have this in place, VitruCare 365 is designed to work directly with the Shared Care Record already in place for NHS regions, avoiding the need for data duplication. This ensures that patient data is kept safe, fully within existing information governance arrangements and available to clinical systems.

An integrated approach to care

Secure data sharing and Microsoft 365 integration enables the platform to compliantly enable three tiers of engagement: patient engagement and activation into co-creating health (PEACH); care innovation and health work integration (CIHWI) at care organisation level; and continuity of care and interoperability (CooCI) at a regional health level, aiding commissioning and clinical analytics.

Sophisticated reporting is simplified for healthcare organisations through the integration with flexible Microsoft reporting tools and automated dashboards powered by Power Apps and Power BI.

At a patient level, the personalisation of data, individualised content, features, and communication leads to better engagement, resulting in better health outcomes. At the organisational level, the platform offers an opportunity to achieve clinical systems integration offering continuity of care, improving automation and enabling virtual wards and neighbourhood care.

Continual improvements powered by Microsoft innovation

The DHS team continues to innovate to put the best tools in the hands of practitioners and patients. It is not precious about replacing bespoke development in preference of integrating standard Microsoft tools where possible in order to simplify the user experience.

“We developed our own video telemedicine consultation solution in 2014—long before anyone else had started on this journey,” explains Shahid Ali. “It worked well enough but running video calls met with a lot of resistance from clinicians, until COVID forced us all to take on digital transformation at scale and pace.”

“Today, we replaced it with Microsoft Teams for those telemedicine consultations,” adds Axel Schulte. “Our platform is part and parcel of Microsoft 365. The customer already works in that environment, so it’s easier for them to adopt. They aren’t switching systems: they are working in the same tools they use every day.”

The tight integration with Microsoft 365 and data platforms ensures a better, seamless, and more nuanced user experience.

“It’s great because it’s the same system for my regional and national roles. I don’t need another system because it is the same system I already have,” confirms Shahid Ali. “I use Microsoft 365 to work with my colleagues while VitruCare 365 gives me one inbox per patient so it’s easy to send an invitation for a telemedicine consultation and to rapidly find all communications and care plan information together. At the same time, with the dashboards I keep an overview of my cohort of patients to identify those who need my attention.”

Early access to the best technologies

DHS has integrated Microsoft Copilot to deliver a generative-AI-powered personal chat bot to assist users. A chatbot had already been deployed through the platform to support new University of Lincoln students registering with local GPs and improve access to mental health support with good results. However, the team is excited by the potential of Copilot.

“Generative AI offers a much more natural way to interact with content, rather than via predefined pathways,” explains Axel Schulte. “Early access to tech like this is one of the benefits of using the Microsoft Azure platform. As soon as ChatGPT came out, we had it available in Azure and could start experimenting. It’s absolutely leading edge.”

“Technically speaking, we use retrieval augmented generation (RAG) to limit GPT to a set of curated clinical knowledge bases that we generated. With our RAG Flag technology, we individualise the knowledge of the bot to the clinical situation of each patient when it formulates a response to a query from the patient. Clinicians can thus be confident that the bot has the appropriate knowledge on clinical topics. We also create trackers and dialogues for processes such as motivational goal setting or appointment booking. When in use it is the NHS clinician who works with the patient who ‘prescribes’ the knowledge, features, and dialogues to make the bot act in a way relevant to conditions and motivational care plans for each patient. These digital prescriptions become part of the patient’s Care Plan stored as PHI in the FHIR database. This way, each patient gets answers and dialogues appropriate to their care plans while at the same time limiting the generative AI to curated clinical content only.”

“Today we’re adding the use of Copilot for clinicians, to offer a patient summary automatically and to make messaging patients quick and easy, further enhancing patient engagement and easing clinical adoption of the technology. It is very promising.”

Partnership with Microsoft offers commercial advantages

Access to the latest technologies isn’t the only benefit of the partnership with Microsoft. It also offers compelling commercial advantages.

“We are making our VitruCare 365 platform available through the Microsoft marketplace,” says Axel Schulte. “It means customers anywhere have access to VitruCare 365. I don’t need to operate an office in Europe to sell into the EU post-Brexit because we can serve them through Microsoft.”

“That’s also great for NHS organisations,” agrees Shahid Ali. “The whole package can be implemented within the Azure subscription of an NHS Trust and benefit from the Enterprise Agreement between NHS England and Microsoft.”

Pushing at an open door

“When we first started more than 10 years ago, we encountered a lot of resistance,” admits Shahid Ali. “Colleagues would say to me ‘you’re fundamentally changing the way we work.' I would reply, we need to change the way we work because we’re not patient-centric enough. We’re not really addressing the needs of the patient. We’re just reacting to a set of circumstances.”

“We need to be more proactive and to treat patients as individuals. We need to support patients in a much more proactive way.”

With the new Labour Health Secretary Wes Streeting’s emphasis on three big shifts UK healthcare must make—from “from hospital to community,” “analogue to digital,” and “sickness to prevention”—UK national healthcare strategy is finally aligning with the DHS founders’ original vision.

The Microsoft Dynamics-based VitruCare 365 platform is an enabler for this vital transition.

Ongoing future innovation

“I’ve been a GP for more than 30 years,” says Shahid Ali. “Motivational care planning works: it engages the population and produces better health outcomes at reduced clinical workload.”

“We’d love to see this implemented across the NHS,” says Axel Schulte. “But why stop there? The whole world should be using technology like this.”

Story Content:
Regardless of the industry, businesses are built on relationships. Company culture comes up in every job interview for a reason. Companies that establish clear internal communication throughout their organization are more unified, motivated, and ultimately more productive. But today’s work-from-anywhere world makes these transparent lines of communication harder to maintain and even more crucial to business success. Companies need to keep employees on the same page, empower each person’s sense of purpose, and nurture a strong community.

Staffbase helps them do that. Over 2,000 clients—including Samsung, Domino’s, Aldi, DHL, and Sephora—use Staffbase cloud solutions to inspire their employees ​​through communication. As Staffbase Senior Product Manager Mikael Head explains, “We see communication as a strategic tool and a ​​competitive advantage for companies. That’s why we ​empower companies to build​ narratives that ​help them​ succeed and achieve ​their​ goals.”

Staffbase draws on powerful tools to better connect its clients with their employees, including a branded employee app, intranet, email, text messaging, digital signage, and Microsoft 365 integrations, all of which a client can manage through Staffbase’s cloud platform. Perhaps the most transformative offering the Germany-based company provides is Staffbase Companion, an enterprise-grade AI assistant that puts information at employees’ fingertips to help them work more efficiently and collaboratively. 

The innovative solution includes two main components—a generative AI writing assistant and an information-synthesizing chatbot that will be available soon. “Content owners use Staffbase Companion Editor to help create content, and people in all sorts of roles can use Companion Search,” explains Staffbase Product Manager, Ruud Brok. “The chatbot can take multiple pages and pieces of content, identify the interesting parts, and use those in an answer. It evaluates all the available information related to the specific question and then generat​es​ the answer. You don’t have to comb through multiple pages. The chatbot does it for you in zero time basically.” 

By empowering companies to deliver distinct, ownable messaging, Staffbase helps them enhance employee engagement, streamline communication processes, and foster a more connected workforce. To develop and support its AI initiatives and products like Staffbase Companion, the company uses Azure OpenAI Service.

Building Staffbase Companion with Azure OpenAI Service

A longtime Staffbase partner, Microsoft emerged as the definitive option when it ​was​ time to choose a suite of AI services that would underpin Staffbase Companion. “We wanted to simplify our tech stack and migrated almost the entire stack to Microsoft a couple of years ago,” says Head. “It’s natural to have our infrastructure in Azure for other reasons as well. Microsoft is a household name in internal communication and the enterprise segment, and most of our clients are heavily invested in the Microsoft product ecosystem. It’s also a definite advantage that all the software plays well together. And, of course, the quality needs to be top-notch, and Microsoft offers very high-quality cloud-based solutions.” 

Staffbase considers communication key to business success—and security the ring that ensures that key doesn’t wind up in the wrong hands. As Head emphasizes, “We’re certified by ISO, SOC 2, and many other certificates to show that we take security seriously. That’s a big driver for our clients.” Building its offerings on Microsoft solutions increases Staffbase clients’ confidence in their data protection. “We often get asked if we store the questions our chatbot handles and if they’re used to train the models,” says Brok. “The answer is no, and we can back that assertion with official statements from Microsoft, which really helps.”

In addition to client assurance, using Azure OpenAI Service and Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) provides flexibility for Staffbase to continuously scale its offerings. Staffbase Companion currently runs on GPT-3.5 Turbo and will soon move to GPT-4o mini, opening the door to new capabilities for the AI assistant. “It’s very valuable to be able to change models and experiment with different models and applications so easily,” says Head. “We use Kubernetes to manage applications. We consider it a perfect combination of innovative OpenAI models and the Microsoft infrastructure and everything that comes with it—enterprise readiness, security, and privacy. And of course, the brand name of Microsoft in the enterprise world is highly valued.”

AI-powered communication in action

Using Staffbase solutions facilitates communication across industries, including automotive, education, energy, healthcare, logistics, manufacturing, and retail. The platform also facilitates communication across cultures. “A lot of clients benefit every day from our Azure AI translation capabilities. Many of them operate in 20-plus markets and might need to produce content in 20-plus languages,” says Head. “Content creators use the Azure-provided machine translation to create the right language versions for all of their audiences in different markets, straight from the get-go.”

With its generative AI capabilities, Staffbase Companion Editor can also cure writer’s block in more than 180 languages. “You can use Companion Editor to create different drafts on a specific topic, get ideas, and help the creative process,” says Head. “Often it’s used to optimize content, like changing the tone slightly or making content shorter or longer.” Staffbase relies on Azure data privacy protections to help ensure that clients retain ownership of the content they generate. Says Brok, “Companion Editor does not train language models using your company information from the documents you summarize or create.” This ability for companies to retain ownership of their content is vital to retaining their data integrity and their competitive edge in the age of AI.

The conversation is still evolving

As a company driven to transform communication and inspire change, Staffbase always looks toward the future, an approach that aligns perfectly with its cloud provider. “It’s really nice that the Microsoft and OpenAI collaboration means that the models that OpenAI releases also become available through the Azure environment at almost the same time,” says Head. “I trust the Microsoft and OpenAI partnership to be the cornerstone of future AI development.”

Never content to rest on the breadth of its offerings, Staffbase finds value in the potential growth that Azure supports. “Scalability is important. We can count on our performance and don’t suffer when other customers also have high workloads,” states Brok. “Azure OpenAI Service scales with your usage. If you grow, the platform grows with you.”

Keeping companies connected

In a digital world so prone to overdiversification and distraction, Staffbase remains focused on one mission despite its ambition. “When you look at the playing field of internal communication platforms, the secret sauce that sets us apart from the others is our focus on communication,” says Brok. “We don’t try to be that one app to rule them all. We really focus on empowering companies to transform ​​internal communication into a strategic advantage.”

Whether it’s the never-ending influx of information, fragmented communication channels, or the rise of remote work, it’s never been more difficult for companies to maintain focused communication across their organization. But it’s also never been more important to keep employees informed, engaged, and connected. Backed by the robust security and functionality of Azure OpenAI Service, Staffbase has positioned itself to help enterprise organizations meet the demands of modern communication. As Brok puts it, “​W​e inspire people to achieve great things together.”

Scaling a "superapp" securely, effectively, and efficiently

At its core, Wrtn's flagship technology compiles an array of AI use cases and services, but localized for Korean users to integrate AI into their everyday lives—bringing “AGI close to people,” is their maxim.

“We mainly focus on three domains of productivity, a mixture of AI search, chat, and tools and templates,” says Dongjae "DJ" Lee, Chief Product Officer of Wrtn Technologies.

The platform fuses elements of AI-driven search, chat functionality, and customizable templates, empowering users to interact seamlessly with an "Emotional Companion" AI-infused agent.

These AI agents have engaging, lifelike personalities, interacting in conversation with their creators. Their vision is a highly interactive "personal agent for everybody, unique and specific to you, your data, and memories," says Lee.

Wrtn's earliest generations of their tools have been wildly popular across South Korea—now used by 5.4 million Korean users monthly—creating new challenges of scale: meeting expanding user demands and adapting and evolving to cultural and linguistic localizations. Among the most important tasks is ensuring compliance to strict regulatory protocols in place across the region—for both its existing consumer-focused product and a newer developer-oriented "Studio Pro" tool.

Embracing Azure OpenAI Service and powerful new o1 models

As demand and scale has grown exponentially and quickly, Wrtn has evolved from working directly with a range of generative APIs to reliance on the o1 models integrated into Azure OpenAI Service with Azure AI Foundry. A huge advantage for Wrtn’s evolution is Azure’s native integration with the newest o1 models, with their advanced reasoning, logic, and multi-step problem solving capabilities.

Azure’s robust framework gives Wrtn with the foundations they need to grow and enhance their consumer and developer products: enterprise-grade security, regional data residency, and unparalleled support for regulatory compliance—essential features for a company navigating legal requirements across South Korea.

"One of the most important things Azure OpenAI Service provides is keeping data in the region," says Lee. Azure's regional offices and servers around the world keep the data protected and localized. "The bigger our traffic grows, the more important Azure's enterprise-level service enhancements are to us,” he adds.

Azure AI Content Safety is a critical component for Wrtn, providing built-in ability to toggle elements like content filters and prompt shields for different end users. This lets its developers scale its products while staying compliant, customizable, and responsive to users across different regions across Korea.

“It's not just about the security and privacy, but also safety. Through Azure, we can easily activate or deactivate content filters. It just has so many features that add to our product performance,” says Lee.

“Azure’s seamless integration is one of the key enablers of our agent workflows and multi-action agents,” says Lee. The o1 model has also excelled in handling intricate queries requiring advanced reasoning capabilities. Wrtn’s users could pose complex logical problems, and the AI would generate precise and reliable answers.

“The success rate of accurate answers to queries has grown exponentially in the o1 models, according to our measures,” says Lee.

Wrtn also leveraged the o1 model to develop AI-powered tools that could translate user prompts into fully functional code. This feature not only democratized coding for a broader audience but also empowered Wrtn's internal developers in generating high-quality code quickly and accurately.

Users could now input natural language descriptions of problems and receive comprehensive coding solutions, enhancing both accessibility and efficiency.

This capability unlocked new use cases for Wrtn, from solving advanced mathematical problems to providing nuanced insights into multifaceted challenges.

"There’s a lot of enterprise support that other model providers lack at this point. Microsoft really adds that value on top of the APIs," says Lee.

Advanced reasoning, generating products with rich roadmaps and possibilities

The impact of the Azure OpenAI Service o1 model on Wrtn’s operations has been transformative. 

On the customer-facing side, the introduction of coding tools powered by the o1 model led to a significant surge in user engagement. Wrtn saw a sharp increase in the daily usage of coding features, underscoring the demand for accessible, high-quality AI solutions. 

The company also observed measurable improvements in the accuracy and reliability of responses to complex queries, along with increased responsiveness and speed for end users. 

Internally, the adoption of the o1 model streamlined Wrtn’s development processes—generating valuable operational ROI. Developers used the model to accelerate project timelines, leveraging its advanced reasoning capabilities to address challenges more efficiently. "To people who want to have the most advanced logical thinking process engraved into their models, we would definitely recommend the o1 model integration with Azure OpenAI Service,” says Lee.

Looking ahead, Wrtn plans to scale its offerings by blending foundation models for everyday tasks with heavy-duty models like o1 for specialized use cases. 

This dual impact of the o1 models available in Azure—improved user experiences and heightened internal productivity—has transformed Wrtn's ability to scale its products and meet ROI objectives. 

Azure is a huge help in achieving their ambition. “Wrtn’s aiming to become a local champion in the AI era, just like in the mobile and internet eras,” says Lee. 

Find out more about Wrtn Technologies at LinkedIn, Instagram, and Facebook.

With a passion for technology and making information easily accessible—and manageable—for everyone, Saravana Kumar, Founder and CEO of Document360, launched his first software product from the living room of his home in London. 

“We are not still operating out of my living room,” jokes Kumar. “But our humble beginnings shape how we operate today. Our goal is to be a company that’s humane, respectful, transparent, and inclusive—which aligns with effective knowledge management.” The focus has paid off. Today, Document360 has more than 300 employees serving thousands of customers around the world.  

Unifying knowledge management

Document360 is the fastest-growing product division under the umbrella company Kovai.co. It’s an AI-powered knowledge base and service platform built on Microsoft Azure to help businesses create, manage, and publish online documentation, including product manuals, SOPs, wikis, and more. “Siloed, inaccessible documentation is a common problem,” says Andrew Cloke, Chief Operating Officer at Document360. “Every company needs robust knowledge management, and Document360 is customizable to meet their unique needs.” 

Knowing Document360 could gain widespread use, the developers chose to build the platform on Azure for its scalability, performance, enhanced security, and compliance. “Our customers expect top-notch security, and Azure compliance capabilities provide a comprehensive solution under one roof,” says Cloke. Document360 is commonly used by software companies, tech startups, and other highly regulated businesses that need to create and share comprehensive, organized documentation for products or services with a global user base.

“The localization and multilingual support through Azure are a critical aspect of Document360 for accessibility, inclusivity, and transparency,” says Kumar. “Document360 meets all language preferences and regional documentation requirements.”  

To further enhance user engagement, Document360 used Azure AI, specifically Azure AI Search, to create advanced features like AI-powered search and content management. Azure App Service helped Kumar’s team streamline Document360 web and mobile app services, while Azure SQL fortified its robust database solutions.  

“We use Azure App Service as our web layer,” explains Kumar. Azure App Service also helps Document360 developers increase productivity and time to market for new features. The team also employed Azure OpenAI Service and used Azure Logic Apps and Azure Service Bus “to bring it all together,” according to Kumar.  

Sustaining values 

Sunil Krishna, Vice President of Marketing at Document360, adds, “Having the Microsoft technology stack as a solid foundation helps us build features that address customers’ specific needs. It makes it easy to iterate quickly, experiment, and make changes.” Krishna says that with Azure services, the team can build prototypes, deploy solutions, and architect scalable AI solutions while keeping cost low. “We’ve recently embedded a lot of AI features, which help customers document all their processes, policies, standard operating procedures, etc.” 

On average, Document360 supports upward of 100,000 active users a month. “With the reliability of Azure, we can scale and deliver to 100,000 users with minimal latency risk,” says Cloke. The product’s AI-enhanced capabilities have resulted in a 50% increase in customer engagement, while at the same time helping Document360 reduce operational costs by 40%.

Document360 also used Azure AI to build Ask Eddy, a generative AI solution that helps customers increase rates of self-service and reduce support tickets. “We’re constantly adopting emerging AI technologies into our SaaS products to address real-world customer problems,” says Krishna. “Our generative AI tool kit has vastly eased the process of content creation and management for our customers.”

“Azure helps automate organization, transparency, and create cross-business and societal coherence,” concludes Kumar. “This goes back to our beginnings. Using Azure means that even small companies can do impactful things—and even as we grow, we can retain our agility and responsiveness while retaining our values.”

As a renowned tire manufacturer and pioneer in materials science, Michelin has been developing its expertise in mobility for 130 years, gradually expanding into other key sectors such as aeronautics and construction. Building on its expertise, the group now wants to search for ways to ensure continuous innovation by combining industrial and sustainable development challenges. To this end, the company is banking on the power of new technologies, such as AI.

Beyond technology, a paradigm shift for the entire company

Deploying large-scale applications within factories, developing new materials, optimizing knowledge of road infrastructures… From R&D to manufacturing workshops, logistics activities, services or marketing, AI and generative AI are one of the pillars of innovation in the Michelin way. 

"They represent a dual challenge in terms of skills and the continuous integration of new technologies, which Microsoft is helping us to meet throughout our value chain," says Yves Caseau, Chief Digital & Information Officer.

The firm has set its sights on the Azure OpenAI Service environment, which it is using both to reinvent its devices and production methods, and to open the field of possibilities for its employees. Generative AI is indeed seen as an opportunity to instill a dynamic of progress at every level of the company. 

"Our ambition is to enable every one of our employees to innovate with generative AI," confides Ambica Rajagopal, Chief Data & AI Officer, “which is why we have developed our own Azure-based platform.”

When generative AI boosts team productivity tenfold

The "Aurora" platform is an authentic in-house chatbot fed by the Group's data and numerous LLMs (Large Language Models). On a day-to-day basis, it offers a range of features designed to optimize the work and performance of teams. For instance, Louis-Marie Sol, Environmental Program Manager, uses Aurora to save time on certain tasks like generating summaries or reformulating ideas. The expert also uses the tool's capabilities to create links between different concepts: "That's where the approach becomes interesting, it opens up other perspectives for me," he confides.

At the same time, the tire giant deployed Microsoft 365 Copilot, a tool which is perfectly adapted to its operational needs. "Copilot has revolutionized my productivity," enthused Caroline Gauthier, Service Owner Collaborative Tools. Capable of summarizing meetings, searching for documents or information on a specific subject, or even improving data qualification and classification, the solution seems to be winning over employees.

Aydem Energy brings electricity to around 6 million customers across five cities in Türkiye, managing generation, distribution, and retail to keep energy flowing smoothly. Committed to delivering uninterrupted, high-quality service, it places great importance on customer satisfaction. "Our call center handles around 21,000 calls daily. To deliver excellent customer support, we have to rely on the highest quality digital solutions," shares Süleyman Tosun, IT Strategy and Governance Director at Aydem Energy.

Seasonal challenges, like hot summers or high number of travelers during vacation periods, lead to increased demand while windy winters cause disruptions. This can cause more outages and significantly higher call volumes to the contact center. In fact, 70% of inquiries are related to power outages. “During seasonal peaks, the number of customer calls increases significantly, making it hard for us to quickly scale our staff,” explains Tosun. “The pressure to respond quickly under challenging conditions also causes immense stress to our employees.”

Introducing a scalable, AI-powered solution

Recognizing that WhatsApp is widely used in Türkiye, Tosun set out to implement a generative AI assistant to deliver information at scale through the platform. Tosun and his team decided to start with a proof-of-concept (POC). "We looked at four POCs using different technologies," recalls Tosun. After reviewing the outcomes, they concluded that Azure OpenAI Service was the best choice, and Softtech was the ideal partner for implementation. "Working with Softtech felt like operating as a single, unified team. Their deep understanding of our business requirements and their proactive approach enabled us to address challenges efficiently," he explains.

Understanding that generative AI is always evolving, Tosun established a dedicated test team within the call center. ”Generative AI projects are unique because new models are constantly being released. Each update can bring smarter, cheaper solutions, so we had to test everything thoroughly,“ explains Tosun. The project was a collective effort involving key team members, including Aydem Energy’s Chief Technology Officer, Engin Kavas, Digital Energy Solutions and Data Analytics Group Manager, Osman Marangoz, Call Center Manager, Seda Küçükoğlu, and IT Manager, Özgür Özer. "Many people were involved during the project and their contributions were critical to success," acknowledges Tosun.

Boosting call center efficiency

Aydem was able to launch the AI assistant in just three months. During an outage, Aydem directs customers to WhatsApp, reducing the number of calls to the call center. The digital assistant starts the interaction by securing data protection and other regulatory approvals. It then informs the customer that they are interacting with a digital assistant that’s using generative AI and explains the tasks it can perform.

The AI assistant integrates with Aydem’s internal systems to provide customers with real-time updates. For example, it matches phone numbers with internal customer relationship management (CRM) data, providing location-specific updates. It uses WhatsApp’s location sharing feature to pinpoint malfunctions, guides customers in submitting meter readings, checks outstanding bills, and processes compensation claims. If the customer reports an urgent issue or expresses anger, the digital assistant seamlessly escalates to human agents.

The customers quickly embraced the solution, expressing appreciation for instant, accurate information. “The digital assistant made the WhatsApp channel more accessible and appealing,” highlights Engin Kavas, Chief Technology Officer at Aydem Energy. “As a result, WhatsApp usage surged from 5% to 10%."

Lifting the call center burden

Today, the digital assistant manages about 1,000 customer inquiries daily through WhatsApp, which represents 10% of total customers calling customer service. “Of the inquiries that come through WhatsApp, 75% are fully resolved by the digital assistant without the need for live agent support,” notes Tosun. The team expects these figures to rise. “Over the summer, we may receive 100,000 calls a day, and AI is projected to handle 30% of those interactions,” Kavas adds.

The digital assistant excels at providing accurate and timely responses to customer inquiries. “Of the customers who use the digital assistant, 90% never call customer service again. This means that our agents need to deal with 900 less calls,” Tosun notes.

This has led to significant cost-savings across the company. Tasks that typically took 2,5 minutes on the phone can now be resolved in seconds through WhatsApp. “Now the Azure Open AI powered digital assistant handles the equivalent workload of 10 people. In peak periods, it can scale to handle the workload of 100 people.” adds Tosun.

Aydem Energy’s call center staff appreciate the support. "Agents can now focus on outbound calls for marketing or sales-related topics instead of customer inquiries," Tosun notes. "Our agents are also very happy because this is new technology, and we're one of the first to implement it on a WhatsApp channel. We've achieved something great with this project."

Implementing guardrails for responsible AI

To enhance security, Aydem Energy specified that only phone numbers operating from Türkiye can access the digital assistant functions; others are transferred to an agent. The company also monitors potential risks like AI discussing politics or religion. "We conducted penetration tests before launching the digital assistant to ensure it could handle potential vulnerabilities effectively," says Tosun. "For example, we ensured that the AI doesn’t reveal technical system details or sensitive CRM information. These precautions have been effective in mitigating risks.”

Reducing the operational cost of the digital assistant was another key focus. While initially, the AI assistant was permitted to use the entire internal knowledge base, it also resulted in significant data processing and higher costs. "We then created classifications by analyzing customer needs and scenario possibilities and limited the digital assistant to only access the library relevant for the specific scenario," Tosun explains. The company also addressed the risk of ‘token attacks’, or attempts to overload AI systems by submitting excessively long or complex inputs by directing long, out-of-scope or repetitive inquiries to live agents. “This approach reduced the cost per conversation by 75% compared to what it was when we did the initial POC," Tosun reports.

Exploring new opportunities

Building on this foundation, Aydem Energy is already planning further innovations. "We are working with Softtech to develop new functionalities for the digital assistant," says Tosun. "However, that's not our only focus. Another project we're planning with Softtech is an AI assistant to support call center staff directly." This assistant would provide instant support to agents during calls, eliminating the need to consult supervisors. Tosun sees great potential in these developments. "AI isn’t just helping us handle cases; it’s also creating opportunities for agents to reach new customers, increase revenue, and improve customer satisfaction rates. I can confidently say that we've proven that AI creates value. Moving forward, our future projects will follow the same principles, and we'll continue exploring new opportunities with Softtech and Microsoft," he affirms.

With 150 years’ history, Bank of Queensland (BOQ) has long been a trusted name in Australian banking, known for its customer-centric approach to financial services. Headquartered in Brisbane, BOQ offers a suite of services, including banking, insurance, foreign exchange, and equipment finance. Looking to modernize operations, BOQ turned to Microsoft to streamline its processes and improve customer engagement using AI.

The journey to modernization

To adapt to industry trends, BOQ wanted to launch a journey of digital modernization to ensure agility and resilience and build and scale for the future. At the heart of this was the desire to adopt AI-driven solutions through its partnership with Microsoft. “We want to be a forward-thinking, agile organization that is able to leverage cutting edge technologies,” said Craig Ryman, Chief Information Officer at BOQ. “To achieve that, we had to move from complex to simple, and by doing that, create greater opportunities for automation, and better ways to run our business."

The power of AI to optimize processes, empower employees

To drive agility and scalability, BOQ adopted a solution that included Copilot, Microsoft Azure, and Microsoft 365. Copilot, the AI-powered tool integrated across Microsoft 365 apps and services, is designed to enhance productivity and decision-making with speed and accuracy.

Using advanced natural language processing and machine learning, Copilot enables BOQ employees to automate processes for drafting reports and manuals and building financial models. It also integrates securely with the company’s enterprise data, ensuring privacy and streamlining compliance—a top priority for BOQ.

During training, BOQ employees were encouraged to share feedback and use it to refine how they used Copilot. Hayley Watson, Head of Enterprise Capability at BOQ, remarked, “Copilot puts the power in the hands of the employee to be able to find efficiency.” By simplifying BOQ’s complex workflows and providing real-time recommendations, Copilot has enabled the company to improve customer service, boost operational efficiency, and continue to innovate in a competitive market.

As Microsoft emerged as a market leader in generative AI innovation, BOQ began discussing how to optimize its relationship with Microsoft and adopt Copilot as the foundation of its move into AI. Ultimately, BOQ opted in to Microsoft 365 Copilot to achieve improved data insights, assist in better decision making, and improve efficiency and productivity.

Achieving high value with low risk

The benefits of using Copilot have been transformative for BOQ. The company has streamlined processes and enabled its workforce to shift focus to higher-value activities. The low-risk, scalable approach BOQ used empowered employees to confidently use Copilot in their daily tasks.

With Copilot, BOQ experienced significant gains in productivity, helping accelerate its broader digital transformation. Copilot assists project managers with tasks like note-taking and building meeting summaries, saving at least two hours per activity. The risk analysis team uses Copilot to streamline the production of analyses from weeks down to a one-day process, while also back testing work to ensure confidence in Copilot's outcomes. In HR, Robert Wilson, Group Chief Technology Officer at BOQ reports that, “[Our users] went from a process which was taking them weeks, to spending maybe 10-15 minutes.”

“Copilot just adds a superpower,” said Peter Adolphus, Senior Manager, Transformation and Portfolio at BOQ. “Something that, you know, you'd normally spend 45 minutes on, you spend two minutes on, and then maybe three minutes refining.”

Completing root cause analyses (RCA) improves BOQ’s ability to identify and manage risks Using Copilot has reduced the company’s analyst time on RCAs by 51.8% and provides a 22% boost in the quality of their findings, helping the company maintain the highest standards of customer satisfaction and operational excellence. BOQ estimates that equipping 1,000 employees with M365 Copilot will enhance productivity equivalent to adding 120 new employees.

Looking ahead: Advancing productivity and the customer experience

Looking ahead, BOQ has developed an ongoing strategy that includes expanding Copilot adoption for customers and its end users. For end users, this will enhance user training and develop champions to optimize Copilot use for continued productivity and growth. For customers, integrating Copilot into all of their touch points with the company will improve and enhance their experience, building deeper relationships through best-in-class customer service.

Powered by enterprise data and customized via Copilot Studio, agents will automate tasks, deliver actionable insights, and help BOQ users make informed decisions. “ The power of Copilot agents will help us to identify and deliver on opportunities faster. ” says Bernadette Demasi, Head of Partner Programs, Group Tech at BOQ. “Using agents in the future to assess workflows will be a powerful thing for our customers, giving them the services and support that they need, when they need it.”

By streamlining workflows and ensuring secure, compliant operations, Copilot and agents promise significant productivity gains—helping BOQ deliver exceptional customer experiences and long-term loyalty.

Sanabil Investments, based in Saudi Arabia, commits around USD3 billion annually to private investments, including venture, growth capital, and small buyouts. With a team of 200 employees, it partners with entrepreneurs to transform groundbreaking ideas into tangible realities.

Sanabil’s IT department automates day-to-day business processes. “We are continually leveraging cutting-edge technology to drive productivity and innovation,” begins Saeed Al Kahtani, Head of IT at Sanabil Investments. The company decided to strategically integrate artificial intelligence (AI) into daily workflows. “The integration of AI through Microsoft 365 Copilot enables employees to enhance work processes, make informed decisions, and collaborate more effectively. This strategic move highlights our dedication to equipping our workforce with the tools they need to excel in a rapidly evolving digital landscape,” explains Al Kahtani.

Identifying recurring bottlenecks

This idea stemmed from a few recurring bottlenecks in employee productivity and creativity. For instance, crafting announcement emails to external parties was time-consuming. “The team had to ensure the language and structure were perfect. This often diverted time and resources from more valuable work,” shares Megren Alshaiq, Head of IT Solutions at Sanabil Investments.

Another area that the company wanted to improve was creating presentations to introduce new technology or processes. “Making sure we use branded templates, creating engaging content with relevant information takes time," Alshaiqnotes.

Finally, Sanabil wanted to improve the meeting experience for everyone. “Usually, one person was assigned to take minutes, which meant they had to focus on notetaking instead of actively participating in the meeting," he explains.

In the highly regulated, competitive sector, Sanabil had to choose an AI solution that would securely and seamlessly integrate with its existing enterprise environment. “Microsoft 365 Copilot addressed our concerns, ensuring compliance and enterprise-grade security,” adds Alshaiq. “For example, Microsoft guarantees that prompts and data are not used for machine learning and can be deleted entirely.”

Sanabil Investments decided to collaborate with Netways,a Regional Managed Partner to Microsoft, to ensure a smooth and secure Copilot integration into its workflow.

Implementing a tailored adoption strategy

To get employees on board, Sanabil worked with Netways and managed change using the ADKAR model. "ADKAR stands for Awareness, Desire, Knowledge, Ability and Reinforcement,” remarks Alshaiq. For Awareness, the company crafted a slogan—AI @ Work. “We created snackable content and displayed engaging videos across screens on every floor at Sanabil,” shares Alshaiq.

Once enough people were interested, Sanabil moved on to building Desire, showing employees the value they could gain by using Copilot. To impart Knowledge, Sanabil worked closely with Netways to craft detailed presentations and training materials tailored to the business. “We held sessions, provided content with specific use cases, and gathered feedback to identify areas for further improvement,” Alshaiq explains. Sanabil utilized Microsoft Forms for registration to the early access program, session registrations and feedback collection, ensuring continuous improvement and participant satisfaction.

The fourth phase was Ability. “As they began using Copilot, employees started talking about it everywhere,” highlights Alshaiq. “This excitement spread very quickly too: in just a matter of weeks, adoption jumped by 50%.” The company developed a dedicated website in SharePoint, offering further tips and resources to empower employees to take advantage of Copilot. Sanabil also established a quick support team called Copilot Help to assist employees outside of the general IT queue. And the very last step, Reinforcement, involved standardizing the use of the latest tools across the organization.

Enhancing productivity and creativity with AI

With Netway’s strategic support, Sanabil employees adoption rates grew significantly. "Approximately 70% of our employees use Copilot for Word, PowerPoint, Teams, and Forms regularly," remarks Alshaiq. The change streamlined their daily tasks and reduced manual efforts across the organization. Notable improvements in productivity and creativity soon followed.

With Copilot, employees can quickly summarize lengthy content, generate email drafts from scratch, and even enrich their existing documents with content suggestions and relevant data. “We can now create and summarize documents faster,” highlights Megren. "With Microsoft 365 Copilot streamlining writing and editing processes, we observed the impact on employee's productivity, and now focus on work quality, rather than fetching information or checking grammar.”

Employees can now create visually appealing presentations with speaker notesautomatically generated by Copilot. Customer templates and Copilot’s design suggestions help improve the document quality. “This not only ensures that our presentations are comprehensive and refined but the overall process is 50% faster than doing everything manually," Alshaiq adds.

Copilot also enhanced Microsoft Teams meeting management by offering clear recaps and chat summaries, highlighting key speakers, organizing discussions into chapters, and documenting action items. “Copilot also translates notes from Arabic to English during, making it easier for multilingual teams to communicate,” says Alshaiq.

“The feedback from our staff has been overwhelmingly positive,” adds Alshaiq. “It is truly gratifying to see technology making such a substantial impact on our daily operations and overall success."

For Sanabil, introducing generative AI into daily tasks has been quite transformative. “Implementing Microsoft 365 Copilot represents a pivotal step in enabling our employees to harness the power of AI to enhance their work processes, make informed decisions, and collaborate more effectively," shares Al Kahtani.

Looking back at the implementation, Alshaiq appreciates the role its partners played. “Microsoft's team of experts guided us through best practices, ensuring that the solution was precisely tailored to meet our specific requirements and operational goals,” he shares.

Meanwhile, Netways provided critical support with skilled speakers, tailored training content, and brainstorming sessions. “From a technical perspective, enabling Copilot is as easy as clicking a button. Adoption is the challenging part. Netways did an excellent job supporting us through it,” Alshaiq adds.

Expanding AI applications

Building on these successes, Sanabil Investments plans to further integrate AI into its operations. "One of the things we've started exploring is the idea of using Copilot Labs to create a chatbot embedded within our Teams or SharePoint," says Alshaiq. The company aims to integrate its IT help desk with Copilot through Copilot Labs, enabling employees to get immediate assistance with basic IT queries, like how to reset passwords.

Finally, Sanabil is looking at integrating Copilot with its enterprise resource planning and customer relationship management systems to aggregate data and create further efficiencies. "I’m sure this experience will be the foundation for many more successful AI applications," Alshaiq concludes.

With Copilot, Sanabil Investments saw an increase in employee productivity, particularly in creating documents and presentations. Within two months, approximately 70% of employees regularly use Copilot.

Story Content:
In response to shifting consumer preferences, companies are under increasing pressure to continually transform the digital user experience across every buy-cycle touchpoint and channel. Organizations are taking action to unlock the full potential of their data to prepare for upcoming tech innovations and to better meet customers right where they are. 

Hevolus Innovation is an international leader in the development of technologies for immersive customer journeys. It knew its mission to revolutionize retail, logistics, education, and maintenance sectors demanded a data platform capable of catalyzing its planned innovations, while staying responsive to customer needs and market opportunities. 

An early adopter of AI mixed-reality innovation 

“When I joined Hevolus in 2023, we began shifting from creating custom mixed-reality applications to building a SaaS platform for our customers to bring to life their own consumer experiences,” says Fabio Santini, CEO at Hevolus. 

Hevolus chose to create the entire platform on Microsoft Azure for its ability to combine extended reality and AI to create a digital transformation solution that was economically accessible to its customers. 

As its first solution, Hevolus developed XRCopilot, a novel, cross-industry cloud platform providing immersive consumer experiences. Created using Azure OpenAI Service, Azure AI Services, Azure Service Bus, the Web Apps feature of Azure App Service, and Azure API Management, XRCopilot connects AI with extended reality in a way that lets a user import a 3D model, edit the model, infuse it with AI, generate a QR code, and then make it AI interactive for a full augmented reality experience.

Unique, immersive retail experiences 

With XRCopilot, shoppers at retail furniture partners’ stores can view products without requiring assistance and visualize how they would fit in their homes. “We are seeing a notable increase in conversion rates for customers using our technology to sell products,” explains Santini. “The ability for retail shoppers to use augmented reality to visualize a purchase—then directly interact to get more information about prices, discounts, colors, and materials—also helps our customers significantly reduce consumer product returns.” Continues Santini, “This level of immersive experience within the buy-cycle streamlines business operations and, most of all, ensures a more optimal consumer shopping experience.”   

Consumer engagement beyond retail   

Retail is not the only industry benefiting from Hevolus’s immersive cloud platform. Students are consuming extended reality instruction to learn about, for example, Leonardo da Vinci. “A teacher can create a lesson showing 3D images of da Vinci and his historical works, and students can scan a QR code to interact with these objects, asking questions as if they were talking to Leonardo da Vinci himself,” explains Santini. Hevolus is excited about the potential of this solution, given its growing number of customers within the academic space.

The future envisioned 

Moving forward, Hevolus plans to refine the XRCopilot platform by enhancing the user experience with voice commands. In the long term, says Santini, “We hope to create an algorithm that can automatically understand and interact with 3D models. 

“Microsoft Azure AI makes it possible for extended reality and AI to benefit any business, not just the biggest or most innovative,” explains Santini.  

Santini is excited for the future, concluding, “We believe extended reality will become a mainstream technology, eventually replacing traditional screens with immersive experiences, using products like Azure OpenAI Service. Hevolus will be right there for it all.”

Story Content:
SimpliFi-ing financial services with generative AI

Aditya Birla Capital Limited, one of India’s leading diversified financial services companies, imagines a world where everything finance is made as simple as ABCD. Through its various subsidiaries and joint venture businesses, it provides a comprehensive suite of financial solutions across loans, investments, insurance, and payments to serve the diverse needs of customers across their life cycles. Powered by more than 55,000 employees, the businesses of Aditya Birla Capital have a nationwide reach with more than 1,470 branches and 200,000 agents and channel partners, along with several bank partners—and these numbers keep growing. It’s not only a customer-first company but a proudly digital-first company, achieving several industry breakthroughs and committing to continuous innovation using emerging and evolving technologies like AI, language models, and chatbots.

Aditya Birla Capital formulated a “One ABC, One P&L” strategy to focus on quality and profitable growth driven by data and technology. The three pillars of this strategic approach are “One Customer, One Experience, One Team.” An unwavering commitment to customer-centricity, prudent risk management, and an omnichannel architecture for distribution form the bedrock of this strategy, which gives customers the complete flexibility to interact seamlessly across mobile app, website, branches, and virtual engagement channels. It incorporated Aditya Birla Capital Digital (ABCD) Limited to build the omnichannel direct-to-consumer mobile app ABCD, which would help the company acquire customers digitally at scale and meet their financial needs through a unified yet comprehensive digital platform.

To take the ABCD app to the next level and further streamline its business model, Aditya Birla Capital sought to introduce hands-on, self-management features through a financial personal digital assistant that combines unified intelligent search and AI. The result is SimpliFi, a customer-facing generative AI chatbot built on the Microsoft Azure purpose-built stack for AI applications including Azure OpenAI Service, cloud-scale databases, and app services. SimpliFi completely transforms how customers access and understand Aditya Birla Capital’s financial services. Through customer research and insights, the company found that its target group of customers 25 to 35 years old appreciated do-it-yourself options for exploring financial solutions independently without having to depend on traditional agents and other methods of engagement. With SimpliFi, Aditya Birla Capital addressed that need using Azure OpenAI to help customers easily navigate and understand its full range of financial solutions and have their queries addressed instantly.

“In our continuous effort to deepen customer engagement, we’re working on leveraging an agentic framework where our bot now proactively leads conversations to understand a customer’s unique needs and then guides them to discover tailored financial solutions, thus creating a more engaging and seamless experience for the customer,” says Pankaj Gadgil, MD and CEO, Aditya Birla Housing Finance Limited, and Head, Digital Platforms and Payments Strategy, Aditya Birla Capital.

In addition to answering customer questions and providing product information across every business line, SimpliFi predicts follow-up actions and displays clickable cards suggesting next steps for customers to take. For example, customers might be shown the top-performing mutual funds based on their search queries or receive a link to buy a mutual fund. When appropriate, SimpliFi seamlessly transitions the conversation to a live representative to close the purchase. This added convenience and personalization of the customer experience has already driven increased engagement and lead generation.

Moving fast to achieve minimum latency, maximum scale, and high concurrency

As Aditya Birla Capital evaluated specific Azure AI infrastructure elements for SimpliFi, it sought minimum latency with maximum scale and a high degree of concurrency. It reduced the amount of latency from 30 seconds to less than a second by anchoring to Azure AI Search and other Azure AI services, as well as Azure API Management. The company can now dynamically scale to handle heavy workloads and further increase concurrency with Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS). "AKS has significantly reduced our development cycles,” says Sameer Jadhav, Executive Vice President for Innovation, Digital Products, and Partnerships at Aditya Birla Capital. “The automated scaling and built-in monitoring tools ensure that our applications run smoothly, freeing up our developers to innovate and improve our products." Aditya Birla Capital also caches responses so that common and repetitive query responses load faster using Azure Cosmos DB. This is extremely critical when dealing with a customer-facing application.

As it grows with Azure Cosmos DB, Aditya Birla Capital stores and accesses semi-structured data in a highly secure way. Used to enhance the SimpliFi experience, this data includes customers’ conversation history, voice transcriptions, and website data scraped on a recurring basis. The company is working with Microsoft to evolve the data’s use to encompass the signed-in user journey, where this history will be merged with customers’ existing system context to provide them with richer responses every time they use the chatbot. "With Azure Cosmos DB, we are able to store customers’ interaction history and provide the SimpliFi bot with the necessary context for personalization of nudges on subsequent logins and better engagement, thereby increasing our lead generation,” adds Jadhav. "And with Azure Cosmos DB’s autoscale features, our application can seamlessly scale to accommodate our projected customer growth ambitions."

To ensure SimpliFi provides the most accurate responses to Aditya Birla Capital customers now and into the future, the company recently added Azure Database for MySQL to its stack to maintain data refreshed daily, such as the net asset value of mutual funds, which is loaded via scheduled jobs at a set time each day.

Accelerated by the launch of the SimpliFi bot, the ABCD app has supported more than 2.5 million users to date. The company plans to scale up to 30 million customers and up to 300 concurrent users within the next three years. In the event of any excess traffic on its provisioned throughput units, Aditya Birla Capital can seamlessly augment the solution with a pay-as-you-go (PAYG) setup and still handle the large concurrency. For this, its team uses an Azure API Management gateway to intelligently spill overflow traffic to the next available regional PAYG deployment of Azure OpenAI Service.

Unifying cloud capabilities and business functions alike

SimpliFi is embedded in Aditya Birla Capital’s ABCD app, providing a simple, single, 360-degree customer experience. The ABCD app received recognition as the Best in Class User Friendly Interface Fintech App at the 2024 Global Fintech Fest Awards. SimpliFi, however, is only one AI-based use case. The company’s success with the Azure AI platform and the engagement it’s seen with SimpliFi opened the door for Aditya Birla Capital to use the same products to reach across the organization and build more targeted generative AI copilots. These include its Service Assist, Audit Assist, and Marketing Assist platforms.

The company’s Marketing Assist platform helps marketing teams build personalized marketing collateral in seconds instead of days working with agencies, while Audit Assist cuts audit checklist generation from hours to minutes, and Service Assist improves employee productivity in its contact centers by 20%. Its generative AI chatbot also handles about 40% of the inbound calls to the contact center in Aditya Birla Capital’s life insurance business, alleviating pressure on agents.

Unlocking value through cost consolidation and AI-based role play

Within Aditya Birla Capital, the entire approach for AI and innovation using Azure OpenAI Service has been to develop enterprise-level applications that cut across and then connect its nine different business lines. “We have built a common platform for generative AI using Azure OpenAI,” says Gadgil. “This platform is being leveraged across all our lines of business, leading to accelerated time to market, higher productivity, and more than 40% in cost reductions.”

Aditya Birla Capital is also pioneering and championing a Microsoft text-to-speech avatar service to train sales employees and let them practice sales pitches using AI—a move that aligns with the company’s “One ABC, One P&L” philosophy. Leadership believes that even if an employee is dedicated to working in mutual funds or another line of business, they should know about life insurance, lending, and every other product line to provide well-rounded customer service. “Using avatars to build sales capabilities and simulate real-life customer handling experiences for sales teams also enhances frontline sales productivity and staff’s ability to handle customers’ objections,” explains Gadgil. “This two-way role play is going to revolutionize the whole sales function in the financial services sector and unlock revenue from digital customer acquisitions at scale.”

Scaling beyond demand like never before

Less than a year after its launch, SimpliFi has evolved drastically from an informational interface to a platform for enriched customer journeys, with contextual responses, proactive nudges, and other emerging functionalities. “Especially when it comes to generative AI, we’ve been the first movers to leverage many cutting-edge solutions that are available on Azure,” says Gadgil.

Aditya Birla Capital’s confidence moving forward is based on the knowledge that if it suddenly gets more traffic, its platforms have the necessary stability, speed, and scalability using Azure app, data, and AI services to support and serve every financial need of every customer across their different life cycles.
