XP Inc. is one of the largest financial institutions in Brazil, with more than BRL 1 trillion in total assets under custody for its over 4 million customers, according to the latest financial results release for the second quarter of 2024. The company employs more than 7,000 people and has been working for over 20 years to transform the financial market and improve people's lives.

With the advent of generative AI and the goal of optimizing internal processes to offer the best products and services to their customers, XP Inc. saw the implementation of Microsoft 365 Copilot as an opportunity to transform productivity, inclusion, and accessibility in the workplace – all while maintaining its cutting-edge culture.

Early adopters of Microsoft 365 Copilot

XP Inc. was one of the first 10 Brazilian companies to adopt Microsoft 365 Copilot. With its disruptive culture and extensive use of the Microsoft platform, the company saw the launch of this tool as an opportunity to innovate and boost productivity with entirely new solutions. These solutions ranged from automating tasks with the help of generative AI to enhancing inclusion and accessibility. According to Adriano Espósito, IT executive and leader in Enterprise Architecture and Engineering Platforms at XP Inc., "Initial adoption took between three and four months, during which XP structured and distributed the licenses, in addition to conducting workshops and mentoring with the support of Microsoft."

During the process, XP Inc. implemented intensive training to help employees adapt to the new tools, understand the possibilities and advantages of the new technology, and align expectations for different use cases. These initial challenges were overcome through a structured approach and strong support from Microsoft.


After adopting generative AI, the XP Inc. team, with the support of Avanade, a partner and technology specialist, led the Copilot expansion project. This initiative identified numerous use cases in more than 10% of the business areas, resulting in measured productivity gains and boosting the use of the tool within the organization.

According to Felipe Almeida, Client Solutions Lead, Avanade Brazil, "Through the Copilot 365 Value Program, we integrate a culture of Artificial Intelligence into the day-to-day work of different business areas through M365 Copilot, redesigning the way employees work, developing forms of measurement and defining robust value indicators that prove productivity and collaboration."


Reinventing productivity with Microsoft 365 Copilot

Among the 9,000 hours saved through the adoption of Copilot in activities such as meetings and the creation of minutes, the internal audit team stands out, having experienced a 30% increase in efficiency. This resulted in significant time savings. Inclusion and accessibility with Microsoft 365 Copilot

Today, AI is capable of fluent, human-like conversations. But what if it can also take on everyday customer interactions on behalf of businesses? This is the vision driving Virbe, a Polish startup. Virbe’s AI-powered avatars can engage customers through voice interactions across websites, mobile apps, and even virtual worlds, providing a seamless, accessible, and personalized customer experience.

Krzysztof Wróbel, the Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Virbe recalls, “Before generative AI went mainstream, people were very skeptical about the technology we offer. Generative AI changed everything. Now, people immediately see the possibilities our product opens up.”

Partner for sustainable growth

From the start, Wróbel pursued various startup accelerator programs with the goal of achieving sustainable growth, ultimately finding the most value with Microsoft. "The support and mentorship we’ve received from Microsoft were unmatched," Wróbel notes. “We were connected with experts early on who helped us navigate the startup landscape.”

Microsoft Azure quickly became Virbe’s go-to platform. “None of the other cloud providers offered the variety of services in one platform,” recalls Wróbel. Virbe could deploy its product directly on customers’ Azure accounts, giving them full control over their data and enabling them to meet local legal requirements for data privacy and security. 

Virbe introduced Azure OpenAI Service to power the conversational flow, allowing the avatar to engage naturally. It then used Azure AI Search to pull up relevant company-specific information. This enables customers to configure every aspect of the avatar, including appearance and knowledge base. “Our product uses large language models, embeddings, and other solutions. We’re able to glue all these components together within the Azure ecosystem to make them act in a way that aligns with business goals and solves end-user issues,” adds Wróbel.

But the biggest win came when Virbe chose Azure AI Services to make the avatar sound natural and inviting. "Azure’s neural voice cloning remains the most reliable, secure, and the most scalable solution on the market," Wróbel says. “Microsoft takes the most cautious approach to the matter, requiring early access approval and verbal consent from the person whose voice you intend to clone. Azure’s solution is also about eight times cheaper than its alternatives, making it one of the key features that helped us sell licenses and scale.”

More reach, bigger impact

Finally, with encouragement and guidance from Microsoft, Virbe introduced its product to the Azure Marketplace as a transactable application to increase its reach. "Once we had our product on the Azure Marketplace, enterprise customers knew that our product had passed through the rigorous Microsoft compliance process and it’s safe to use in their day-to-day operations," explains Wróbel. The global reach of the Azure Marketplace also enabled Virbe to close deals with customers in countries like India, Japan, and Canada, expanding its footprint without a physical presence.

Through Microsoft’s mentorship and guidance, Virbe also found a way to lower barriers for potential customers. "Digital avatars are a new technology, and people can sometimes struggle to realize its potential. The decision to offer a free demo on Azure Marketplace made it easier for people to test Virbe and see its ease-of-use firsthand," Wróbel explains. 

While Virbe can be used in any industry, its customers have already found innovative ways to integrate digital avatars into their operations. In banks, avatars placed on digital signage screens can act as guides. "When a person walks into a bank branch, the AI avatar can help them check their balance, for example," explains Wróbel. 

In retail environments, avatars assist customers with finding products, answering in-depth product questions, and even providing tailored advice. For instance, as winter approaches, the avatar might suggest warmer jogging clothes as an upsell. If a person isn’t a buyer, the AI still captures valuable insights from these conversations, helping businesses understand common questions and needs and improve their service. "This kind of personalized experience is difficult to scale with human staff alone, especially in mass-market retail. But virtual avatars allow retailers to maintain a high level of service without adding personnel costs," Wróbel notes. 

The avatars are already attracting eyeballs. “A major retailer in Poland saw a 25% engagement rate using our product. Engaging a quarter of customers provides valuable insights to the retailer," adds Wróbel. At conferences, Virbe's AI avatars help businesses stand out in crowded settings. The AI avatar proactively detects when someone approaches, engaging people passing by. "With Azure OpenAI, one customer reported a 10x increase in leads," says Wróbel. “It’s still early days so this number will likely change but it’s good to know that the solution is making a difference.”

The flexibility of Virbe’s platform allows customers to configure the avatar's role. "The digital avatar can act as a virtual sales rep or it can just be a helpful interaction," Wróbel explains. Businesses can choose whether the avatar collects information like emails or keeps the conversation completely anonymous in alignment with local data protection regulations.

The power of persistence

As AI technology evolves, Virbe advances with it. “We’re particularly excited about Azure’s “personal voice” feature, which could allow voice cloning in 30 seconds. It’s in limited access now, but once it’s broadly available, it will be even easier to deploy Virbe’s solution securely and at scale with Azure’s offerings,” shares Wróbel.

Wróbel reflects on the Virbe’s journey. "The key factor in our success so far has been persistence," he says. Navigating a market where conversational AI wasn't mainstream required dedication. "I believed it had potential, but sometimes it’s hard to keep your business operational until the market aligns with your vision," Wróbel adds. Support and mentorship programs, like Microsoft’s, were instrumental in Virbe overcoming challenges. "Success stories only reveal the tip of the iceberg, while the invisible majority is filled with struggle. But if you’re persistent in your vision and effort, and you have the support of a partner like Microsoft, you can overcome anything,” concludes Wróbel.

Expanding the “infinite possibilities of communication”

NTT Communications envisions a world where everyone can work in their own way, “giving shape to the infinite possibilities of communication.” The Japanese telecom underpins its reputation on innovation, leadership, and global reach. Unsurprisingly, global businesses rely on NTT Communications for the networks, cybersecurity, datacenters, AI, 5G and IoT technologies, and more. Its network spans more than 190 areas worldwide.

Daily exposure to threats, coupled with a shortage of skilled security personnel, sparked NTT Communications’s search for a connected, proactive, and productivity-enhancing security platform for its global estate.

Turning to Microsoft Security solutions

As a longtime customer, NTT Communications trusted Microsoft. Security is built into Microsoft productivity and security applications, so NTT Communications knew it could unify its security posture while amplifying analyst effectiveness. The company created an interoperable cybersecurity foundation by using Defender XDR and Microsoft Sentinel together as its security information and event management (SIEM) system. “With Defender XDR, it’s easy to understand variable alert context,” says Ken Ito, Vice President of Security Operations Division. “This has greatly improved SOC team responsiveness.”

NTT Communications aggregates threat data into Microsoft Sentinel from Defender XDR and related Defender solutions, such as Defender for Endpoint. Microsoft Sentinel natively connects to Azure Logic Apps, an Azure cloud service, for AI-enriched threat intelligence. “By ingesting logs and alerts from our security solutions into Microsoft Sentinel, we can correlate threat analysis from multiple sources,” explains Masaki Onishi, Director of Security Operations Division. This includes activity arising from Microsoft 365 E5 applications, Defender for Endpoint, Defender for Cloud Apps, Entra ID, and more. “This automation saves valuable time to resolve incidents,” adds Onishi.

Supercharging a dedicated SOC team with Security Copilot

Despite the scarcity of highly trained SOC analysts, NTT Communications can upskill a more diverse talent pool faster while helping senior analysts work more efficiently than ever with Microsoft Security Copilot. It shortens the learning curve for Kusto Query Language (KQL) for effective threat hunting. “With KQL natural language ability, even a junior analyst can create an effective query,” reports Rikiya Sakuma, Manager of Digital Innovation. “Inexperienced analysts use the high-quality summaries and recommendations that Security Copilot provides to improve their security response skills."

According to Onishi, “Our analysts use the script analysis feature in Security Copilot to analyze PowerShell and other types of scripts quickly. This has significantly increased our analysts’ productivity.”

Previously, analysts had to verify the scripts with the person who reported the attempted compromise. “The summary and recommendations for remediation generated by the script analysis feature in Security Copilot allows SOC teams to skip that step and make the right decisions quickly," he adds.

Realizing a matrix of benefits

Less than a year after implementing Security Copilot, NTT Communications has achieved significant efficiencies. “Since introducing Microsoft Security Copilot, we’ve automated identification, prevention, detection, response, and recovery, improving security operations efficiency without increasing labor costs,” says Tsuyoshi Toyoshima, General Manager of the Information Systems Division of the Digital Transformation Promotion Department at NTT Communications.

“We can also automatically invoke Security Copilot in Logic Apps for alerts ingested into Microsoft Sentinel, and circulate a summary of the incidents generated by Security Copilot.”

NTT Communications relies on this cost-effective efficiency and visibility over its vast estate to keep data safer in the face of increasing threats. “We believe that using Security Copilot will provide us with valuable information about threats and mitigation plans,” adds Toyoshima. “Even now, our most junior staff are performing at a much higher level than before.” 

Greater efficiency on the cybersecurity front translates into other cherished NTT Communications goals. “The operational efficiencies we gain with Security Copilot help reduce our environmental impact,” concludes Toyoshima. “That’s critical to the prosperous and sustainable society we want to help create.”

Established in 2015 under the Education Act, the Education Authority of Northern Ireland (EANI) is a regional body responsible for delivering education and youth services to approximately 1,200 schools, 21,000 teachers, and 380,000 students across the region. Their goal is to challenge, inspire, and empower students from pre-school through post-primary education.

Achieving this goal requires removing learning barriers, which range from ability and cultural background differences to limited resources and geographic isolation faced by the country’s sizable rural population. EANI is focused on fostering equity to ensure every child in Northern Ireland is equipped with the necessary tools and resources to thrive in a modern classroom.

“For us in education, it's about the impact for children,” explains Cynthia Currie, Director of Education at the Education Authority. “I see education as a passport to a child’s future, and we can really make a difference if we get that right in the early stages of an individual's career.”

Tapping into the power of Microsoft Copilot

To meet the unique needs of the education system, EANI launched Northern Ireland’s Education Information Solutions (EdIS) program. Designed to modernize hardware and software across schools, EdIS links the entire educational community within one unified digital system. This initiative is transforming digital technology across EA schools, in hopes of closing learning gaps and improving access to quality education.  

Educators faced mounting administrative burdens that took away valuable time from focused instruction. They needed tools that could streamline their workload, support the creation of engaging and effective lessons, and offer tailored support to meet the diverse individual needs of students, regardless of their circumstances or location.


What EANI realized they needed was Microsoft Copilot.


“What we saw in Copilot was the opportunity to reduce teacher workload and to prepare lessons in a much faster but more meaningful way,” says Damian Harvey, Interim Head of EA C2K (Classroom 2000), a service within EANI that oversees education technology resources needed by schools. “And for us, that's a real game changer.”

EANI chose Microsoft and Copilot for the responsible AI approach and information governance standards, ensuring data security while minimizing exposure of sensitive student information. EANI further proved their commitment to ethical AI use in three key areas: promoting safe and secure use of AI, assessing its impact on children and young people (specifically avoiding bias), and building educator confidence in integrating the new technology.  


“We needed to know that AI would help young people gain the best experiences and outcomes,” says Currie, “and that there was a closed network to ensure that information governance was secure.”

Increasing productivity to maximize learning time

Northern Ireland’s education system benefits from a centralized structure with a dedicated core team that directly supports schools and builds trust through ongoing, personalized interactions. This team plays a critical role in introducing and scaling AI initiatives like Copilot by creating communities of practice and ensuring data security, effectively addressing educators’ concerns about new technology. 


EANI initially rolled out AI-powered learning tools on a small scale, selecting key innovative educators to pilot the free version of Copilot in their classrooms. These educators immediately recognized its potential to save time—a critical need given increasing demands and educator shortages. However, some educators expressed concerns about the tool’s scope, particularly regarding its widespread use in the classroom.  

To address these concerns, EANI introduced training sessions focused on effective prompt writing, showcasing Microsoft 365 Copilot’s capabilities. Educators quickly discovered the practical benefits of upgrading to Microsoft 365 Copilot for tasks like creating PowerPoint presentations, generating questions in Microsoft Forms, and developing differentiated classroom resources. The substantial time savings and enhanced ability to meet diverse student needs drove widespread staff adoption and growing enthusiasm.


“Any trepidation that my staff had quickly disappeared when they saw for themselves how Copilot could actually help us with our teaching and learning,” says Helen Doherty, Vice Principal of St. Coleman's College in Newry, Northern Ireland. “It saves considerable time from tedious paperwork and allows educators to incorporate more activities involving group work, critical thinking, and problem-solving.” 


With the introduction of Microsoft 365 Copilot, educators could easily distribute differentiated resources and conduct digital assessments.

Using Teams integrations to streamline workloads and provide individualized learning

As part of its move to adopt the latest in learning technology and further embrace AI, EANI began exploring integrating AI into Microsoft Teams to support educators with providing personalized and efficient feedback. The solution learns from educators’ responses to suggest relevant comments in future assessments, reducing administrative workloads.


“In terms of supporting curriculum development and the various interventions that can support children, we were looking for best-in-breed technology to help every child succeed in the classroom,” explains Damian. “Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot 365 came forward as something that could help us to achieve our aims. It supports us in assessing how a child is progressing and providing salient, impactful feedback that will support learning opportunities going forward. It gives us the ability to integrate with Teams to support the assessment of classroom work and to give more meaningful feedback to each individual child.”

Using Copilot to transform approaches to inclusivity

In Northern Ireland, the increasing complexity of special educational needs requires tailored approaches in classrooms. Educators need to manage multiple personalized learning pathways, a challenging task that is made easier with AI-powered tools like Copilot.    


Clifton Special School in Bangor, Northern Ireland, embraces this inclusive approach by providing a high-quality education that prepares pupils to lead rich and rewarding lives. They serve students aged 3 to 19 with a range of complex healthcare needs, behavioral challenges, and learning difficulties. Clifton focuses on supporting each student’s unique needs, seeing them as strengths instead of difficulties. 


Vice Principal Brenda Mullan believes Copilot is transformative in supporting this diversity. “The opportunity to personalize learning is huge,” she says. “Now every child can utilize the resources they need to move them forward academically.”

Clifton empowers students by promoting their independence and ensuring they have agency in their education. Historically, students with learning difficulties were often treated passively, but Clifton aims to change that by aligning the curriculum with the unique interests and passions of students. Using Copilot, an educator can incorporate students’ interests to inform lesson planning, making learning more engaging and customized rather than a one-size-fits-all model.

Looking ahead, there is excitement about integrating Microsoft Copilot 365 to streamline tasks like lesson planning and data analysis, giving educators more time to interact with their students.

“With these accessibility tools, a young person who doesn't have the ability to click a mouse or touch a touch screen can make the choice with their eyes,” Mullan explains. “These kinds of things will open opportunities for young people with disabilities. It's about removing barriers to learning so that our young people can experience and achieve success on their own. And we're really keen on working with Microsoft to explore how that could happen.” 


For an art class project, students chose options based on their likes and interests. Educators then used Copilot to create a prompt reflecting these preferences, enabling students to create their own artwork with minimal assistance. This approach aligns with Northern Ireland’s Special Educational Needs and Disability Act, which emphasizes valuing young people’s voices in decisions that affect them.


“The very fact that the young person has been the architect of their own work based on their likes, dislikes, and choices, the pride that they show—the ownership of that— has raised their self-esteem,” Brenda says. “It’s all informed through Copilot. Our young people are much happier, invested, and valued.”


EANI plans to expand the use of Microsoft 365 Copilot in schools across Northern Ireland, supported by a research study to measure its impact. This research will independently verify the tool’s influence on student outcomes, sharing success stories to inspire the wider educational community.

Collaborating with Microsoft for enhanced customer experience

Crediclub, a Mexican financial services company with a strong social commitment, offers credit, savings, and investment services for individuals and SMEs. Their goal is to empower Mexicans with fair and accessible financial services. With over 150 branches, Crediclub needed to enhance operational management to maintain the quality of its processes. Daily meetings were crucial for discussing issues like delinquencies and daily goals. However, their audit model required changes. "We wanted to work with Microsoft to reduce costs and offer better prices to our customers," says Luis Ernesto López de Rivera Muñoz, Data Scientist and Analytics at Crediclub.

Kicking off the digital era of audits 

To optimize the audit process and reduce costs, Crediclub made a significant leap in its digital transformation by implementing an AI-based solution. With Microsoft's support, the company developed an innovative system on the Microsoft Azure infrastructure in 2023, integrating services such as Microsoft Azure AI, Microsoft Azure Cosmos DB, and Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service.

This system, named “The Watcher,” is designed to enhance scalability and efficiency by automating the capture, storage, and analysis of meeting data in real time. Each call is automatically recorded, transcribed, and stored in Microsoft SharePoint and Cosmos DB.

The collected data is then analyzed using GPT language models in Azure, which extract key topics, identify relevant points, and generate automatic evaluations based on predefined metrics, such as attendee engagement and decision-making.

950 beneficiaries and 96% monthly savings 

The adoption of "The Watcher" has yielded impressive results in terms of efficiency and savings. Before its implementation, the audit team could only review about 20 meetings daily. Now, the system can analyze 150 meetings in about an hour, representing a 650% increase in review capacity. This significant boost in productivity also drastically reduced operational costs, as the system can scale to evaluate more meetings without needing additional staff.

"Thanks to this project, 800 sales advisors and 150 branch managers now have an additional 1,600 hours per day to interact directly with customers, without the need to travel," says Gabriel Ruelas, Director of Operations and Co-founder of Crediclub. Financially, the credit institution reduced its monthly audit expenses from approximately $40,668 USD to just $1,597 USD, a 96.1% decrease due to process automation. Additionally, the ability to evaluate meetings on the same day they occur allows the company to take immediate corrective action.

Inclusive financing with Crediclub Activa


At Crediclub, promoting equal opportunities for everyone is a fundamental mission. One of its key products, Crediclub Activa, is specifically designed to finance women entrepreneurs. Through group credits, each consisting of five or more women, a leader acts as a mentor to the other participants, fostering an environment of support and collaboration.

Since its inception, Crediclub Activa has served over 800,000 customers, granting more than three million productive loans. This represents a total disbursement exceeding $3.8 billion USD, aimed at growing and sustaining women-led businesses. These loans not only boost businesses but also significantly impact the beneficiary families. It is estimated that these loans contribute to generating more than $850 million USD in annual income for these families, many of whom lack access to traditional bank financing.

Previously, an internal team would analyze credit applications within 48 hours. Today, thanks to Microsoft's services, these analyses are performed automatically in seconds, allowing customers to receive immediate credit approval. This automation clearly determines the amount to be granted and the applicable conditions. "This approach allows us to lend to unbanked people who otherwise wouldn't have access to financing, even if they don't have high credit scores," says Gabriel Ruelas proudly.

Getting closer to people and promoting education 

"With technology, we achieve greater closeness with our clients, treating each case individually and acting as a key facilitator of financing," says the co-founder. But Crediclub does not stop here. The company plans to continue expanding The Watcher's capabilities with more advanced AI functionalities, such as emotion and conflict detection, and predictive analytics to correlate meeting results with key business indicators. The goal is to further refine the system to improve the accuracy of assessments and generate even more valuable insights that drive branch performance.

"Companies that use this technology will be more inclusive by offering credit services to those who did not have access," concludes Luis López de Rivera. The financial sector in Mexico is undergoing a transformation, with the adoption of technology and digitalization as key elements to stay competitive. Crediclub understood the importance of differentiating itself, especially from traditional banks, and its track record shows how innovation can be a factor in positioning itself in a competitive market.

Greece’s Ministry of Digital Governance oversees digitizing public services for citizens and businesses. The Ministry optimizes and digitizes all sorts of processes, everything from shipping to paying fines. For example, it leverages artificial intelligence (AI) to spot traffic violations or analyze satellite data and catch issues like wildfires and floods. “We aim to create a society that no longer wastes time on paperwork, queuing, or being held up by red tape," shares Konstantinos Kyranakis, Deputy Minister of Digital Governance in Greece. “Our vision is to harness the potential of AI to transform the public sector, making it more efficient in serving citizens.”

One manual, time-consuming process that the Ministry decided to streamline was land purchases. Traditionally, a person intending to buy a house had to go to the local registry office with a large stack of documents. A Ministry employee would have to read through 300 pages of paperwork, make notes, and provide an assessment. Another employee would later have to re-read and input everything into an outdated system. “The legal review, certificate verification, and data entry were all manual. Previously, when you bought a house, you might need to wait months or even years to be officially recognized as the owner,” shares Kyranakis.

Aiming to eliminate these delays, the Ministry established Hellenic Cadastre, a unified and constantly updated property records system for citizens and the state. Hellenic Cadastre allows Cadastre employees to retrieve transactions, assess them, sign them digitally, and request assistance. It integrates seamlessly with the ecosystem of lawyers, notaries, and other officials who file new transactions on behalf of citizens.

To streamline the process even further, Hellenic Cadastre introduced AI into the property buying process. "Using Azure OpenAI Service, we've built a system that understands property contracts in natural language. It automatically classifies the contracts into categories such as buying or inheriting property and applies the relevant legal rules," shares Kyranakis. As a result, the system generates a ready-made assessment of each document, enabling the registry director to approve or reject an application.

Additionally, Hellenic Cadastre developed a digital assistant using Azure OpenAI Service to answer citizens' questions. “The chatbot reduces the workload of the local land registry offices, which used to handle many questions in person,” adds Kyranakis. “Every week, we gather more complex questions that require detailed answers, and we update the chatbot’s knowledge base so that everyone across Greece gets consistent and accurate information.”

Upskilling staff with AI

The Ministry introduced these changes carefully and gradually across its offices. "Upskilling staff for AI is the biggest challenge for the public sector," reflects Kyranakis. "There are about 150 people with approving authority in our system, and most of them are not necessarily very comfortable with technology," he explains. Though collaborating with stakeholders helped with buy-in, many in the local offices were still skeptical. However, as employees received training and began using the new system, their engagement grew. "When they saw what the AI system could do and how quick it was, they were very thankful," notes Kyranakis. Soon, the Ministry started receiving daily feedback from public servants on how to make the system even faster and better.

Enhanced transparency to inform resource allocation

Today, 90% of transactions across all local land registry offices are processed online. This gives the Ministry complete transparency. “We can see the current status of every case, something that was impossible with the old paper-based system,” shares Kyranakis. Power BI reports offer leaderboards and real-time performance data on all local offices, enabling the Ministry to monitor performance and allocate resources more efficiently. “We also share this real-time data to other authorities, giving them clarity on the volume of real estate transactions. This helps them plan the national budget,” adds Kyranakis. “For the first time, we have predictive tools to support financial planning. It’s revolutionary.”

The system also tracks the cost per assessment. "Right now, the cost of each contract assessment is 0.11 euros, down from 15 euros before adopting Azure OpenAI," he notes. “This level of transparency enables us to justify this innovation to taxpayers, who now know they're paying much less than they did before.”

But the most important benefit is speed. “Previously, contract assessments could take up to three hours. Now, it takes less than 10 minutes. The entire transaction can be validated in days rather than months. With Azure OpenAI, we're saving a massive amount of time," highlights Kyranakis.

This rapid validation allows property owners, banks, and state-owned property managers to proceed without lengthy delays. "With faster transactions, more transactions can be completed within a financial year, so the Greek economy will also grow, and the state will receive more taxes," notes Kyranakis. “This signals to investors that the Greek real-estate market is reliable, with clear rules and fast, secure digital processes for property transactions, which further boosts economic growth.”

Much of the work was made possible with strong support from the local Microsoft team. "Microsoft was always available to support us. We still have weekly meetings to discuss opportunities or possible issues,” shares Kyranakis. “We feel like we have a real partner in Microsoft, not a faceless provider somewhere halfway across the world."

Digitizing a billion paper documents

Inspired by the newfound efficiency, Hellenic Cadastre has embarked on an ambitious project to digitize its vast archive. “By 2025, we aim to have a fully digitized archive of 1 billion pages and a digital map of Greece where every piece of land corresponds to a registry code. All of this data—about 8 petabytes—will be hosted and accessed via Azure technologies, with Microsoft’s support.” This will completely eliminate the need for physical visits to complete transactions.

Transforming public service with AI

Taking in its success, the Ministry is confident in its strategy. “With AI, we can completely transform the public sector and empower citizens with the right services at the right time. Public services will become much faster and cheaper, ultimately lowering taxes and improving citizen journeys," Kyranakis concludes.

Properstar, a leading real estate platform since 2018, has over three million listings worldwide and uses innovative technology to simplify and safeguard the process of buying and renting properties. Thanks to personalized search features and intelligent data analytics, Properstar connects buyers, tenants, and agents to deliver a smooth, customized real estate experience. Headquartered in Switzerland and with a global outlook, Properstar provides reliable support through all stages of each transaction. By next year, it will have a footprint in 65 countries.

The vision of Properstar's founders was to create an innovative real estate platform that gave buyers and tenants greater flexibility and a wider range of filters. However, it soon became clear that two main obstacles first had to be overcome. First, real estate agency data was often incomplete or inaccurate. Important information was usually only available in the free-text descriptions of properties, not in the structured CRM data. To enable more comprehensive and accurate property searches, it was therefore also necessary to integrate the unstructured data.

The second obstacle was that conventional filter systems did not meet the requirements for nuanced property searches. Properstar thus set itself the ambitious goal of developing a completely new and dynamic filter system that would not only provide exact matches, but would also display properties that, although different in some ways, might still be suitable overall. This would ensure that no relevant offer would be overlooked in the future.

Properstar's founders recognized that using AI was the key to quickly and efficiently realizing their vision. Having already established a successful strategic partnership with Microsoft, the company decided to sign up to the FastTrack for Azure program. “Our partnership with Microsoft has been the engine of our innovation,” notes Gérard Paratte, CEO of Properstar. “The extensive Azure ecosystem allowed us to access cutting-edge AI tools and slot them easily into our solution. This in turn enabled us to very rapidly develop the most innovative real estate platform on the market.”

More detail and better matches: Properstar relies on Azure AI technologies

Using Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service is at the heart of Properstar's technological solution. AI analyzes unstructured property descriptions in a variety of languages and extracts relevant details such as the presence of a swimming pool, a garage, or barrier-free access. Doing so significantly enlarges the data set, as around 40% more information is collected for each property. All this data lays the foundation for more comprehensive and accurate property searches.

Using Azure AI Search, the developers then created a flexible filter system that lets users distinguish between mandatory and optional features. Now, users can keep an eye on properties that may not meet all their criteria but could still be a generally good fit. For example, if a user is looking for a property with a swimming pool, properties that do not yet have a pool but offer the option of building one are also considered. “We pushed the limits of what Azure AI Search could do and tested numerous approaches,” Ivan Torreblanca, CTO of Properstar, recalls. “In the end, our efforts paid off. By combining Azure OpenAI and Azure AI Search, we now achieve a 98% match rate, which means that almost every suitable property is covered.”

Leveraging big data for market analysis

The rich diversity of the Microsoft Azure ecosystem opens up still further innovative possibilities for Properstar. By harnessing leading-edge big data tools such as Azure Synapse Analytics, Azure Databricks, and Power BI in Azure, the company can now perform comprehensive market price analyses and process massive amounts of data from millions of real estate listings and search queries. Armed with this data, Properstar can analyze global market price trends in detail and present them transparently. The result? Buyers and investors have a powerful tool with which to make informed decisions based on accurate price trends. In other words, comprehensive data analysis gives users a significant competitive advantage, while further cementing Properstar's position as a leading player in the field of data-driven real estate markets.

Scalability, security, and agility thanks to Microsoft Azure

At the same time, the Microsoft Azure infrastructure allows Properstar to scale up globally while ensuring the platform's high performance and security at all times. “Microsoft Azure gives us the flexibility to respond to changes in the market,” Paratte stresses. “The cloud infrastructure gives us the agility and security we need to expand our business globally and provide our users with the best possible experience.” Meanwhile, Microsoft Defender for Cloud and the implementation of standardized security protocols guarantees comprehensive data protection and regulatory compliance. This boosts user confidence and protects the platform from security threats, while minimizing the risk of data breaches and/or penalties for non-compliance.

Another crucial aspect is the use of Azure Databricks and Azure Data Factory to automate data collection and transformation. These tools enable Properstar to roll out new AI features and capabilities faster, resulting in shorter innovation cycles and a faster time to market for platform enhancements.

The development team has also been able to optimize processes and automate repetitive tasks using Azure DevOps and the GitHub Copilot. Collaboration thus becomes easier, while developers are more productive and happier with their jobs as teams are free to focus more on creative problem solving and innovation.

AI-powered user experience: Properstar shapes the real estate world of tomorrow

Properstar remains focused on innovation and AI-based solutions in order to continuously develop its platform. For example, it has developed a communication platform based on Microsoft Azure that greatly simplifies interaction between buyers, tenants, and agents. On this basis, it is much easier to coordinate viewing appointments and even conduct virtual viewings. An AI-based translation tool also enables real-time conversations between people who speak different languages.

A central component of Properstar’s future concept includes plans for an AI concierge—an intelligent assistant that supports buyers and tenants in their search for real estate and walks them through the entire purchase process. This AI concierge will not only make personalized property suggestions; it will also help manage viewing appointments and documents. There are further plans to make the concierge available as a voice assistant, allowing users to submit spoken requests. “Our goal is to make the user experience as enjoyable and efficient as possible,” Paratte points out. “The AI concierge adds a personal touch to digital interaction, helping users find the right property faster and simplifying the entire process.”

Building on Microsoft Azure, Properstar wants to further step up the pace of innovation, setting new standards and continually redefining what is possible with a data-driven real estate platform—all for the benefit of users who can now find their dream property even more easily.

São Paulo hosts Brazil’s largest education system, with over 3.7 million students across more than five thousand schools. Basic education is mandatory, free, and inclusive, with specialized support for students requiring learning assistance.

SEDUC—which translates to "State Secretariat for Education and Quality of Education"—is the governmental body responsible for the formulation, supervision, coordination, execution, and evaluation of educational policy in São Paulo. As Brazil’s largest education network, it manages the implementation of programs across the state.

Overcoming hesitation and resistance to AI

SEDUC advises state schools across Brazil in developing, implementing, and evaluating educational programs and pedagogical innovations. As part of its mission to enhance teaching and learning, the organization sought to integrate AI and digital tools into its operations, catering to the diverse needs of students, including those with special educational needs. Some educators and students were initially hesitant, fearing AI could replace educators or pose ethical dilemmas. SEDUC addressed these concerns through training and guidance, as well as deepening its partnership with Microsoft.

Microsoft has been an important, long-standing partner for SEDUC as they value the integration capabilities of Microsoft solutions, and the company’s commitment to customer success. After researching all of its options for AI solutions, SEDUC chose Azure OpenAI Service as the best solution for its educators and students’ diverse needs.

SEDUC is rolling out Microsoft 365 A5 licenses to all employees, educators, and 3.5 million students to enhance security governance and provide improved support. The phased adoption of Microsoft Copilot has also begun, with 1,000 licenses currently in use to upskill and integrate new technologies among faculty, staff, and students.

Initial implementation prioritized administrative tasks—such as generating legal documents and handling administrative inquiries—and has expanded to include AI usage with students and teachers, including personalized learning to cater to individual student needs and help them recover from learning losses during the pandemic.

Its partnership with Microsoft emphasizes SEDUC’s commitment to data security and privacy by spearheading robust measures to protect sensitive information. Moving forward, the education network is carefully considering the ethical implications of AI, ensuring it is used responsibly and equitably, while championing transparency to gain trust in the process.

“The idea was to have a very strong partner on this journey because nobody knows the implications of what we are working towards, and we need to protect and support children in the best way possible,” says Luzia Sarno, IT Director at SEDUC. “We had a lot of data and now we want to explore this data for, for instance, ‘Why is one school performing better than another?' ‘Why is this teacher performing better than another?’ So, everything that we are doing, we try to have measures and then apply that intelligence. We need somebody that understands our needs and that’s Microsoft.”

AI-powered personalization to enhance student feedback

After addressing initial hesitation, SEDUC moved forward with its AI-powered implementation journey, starting with the use of Azure OpenAI Service to help provide personalized feedback on student essays. The sheer volume of essays made manual grading impractical. Azure OpenAI Service analyzes millions of essays, offering personalized, tailored feedback to educators so they can help students improve their writing skills and understanding of the subject matter. This technology saves educators thousands of hours, freeing them to focus on instruction.

“A typical teacher in São Paulo may have about six different classes,” says Daniel Barros, Pedagogical Director at SEDUC. “And if you have about 40 students in each of these classes, we are talking about 240 students. Our expectation is that students write an essay every month for eight consecutive months. That process resulted in nearly 10 million essays since the beginning of the school year in February! So how can you expect them to correct all of these essays in a few weeks or in a month? They simply can’t without help. Now, with AI, educators receive meaningful feedback and can easily customize it to that very student. And this feedback is multidimensional.”

Streamlining administrative tasks for efficiency

Building on the success of personalized student feedback, SEDUC is exploring new ways to harness AI across its entire education system, including streamlining content creation for educators and curriculum developers, leading to greater efficiency. Azure OpenAI Service has helped with curating academic materials, generating questions, developing quizzes, building activities, and assessing student knowledge. These automated processes streamline content development, improve material quality, and free up educators for one-on-one student interactions and instruction.

“We’ve also been trying hard to improve the content that we produce for every single class,” explains Barros. “Now we have digital materials available that support each teacher. We have 150,000 teachers in our schools and a large team that produces and updates this content, so we’ve been using AI to great effect to improve that.”

Through collaboration with Microsoft, SEDUC has also been using AI tools to streamline development processes and enhance the efficiency of administration systems. These AI-driven solutions have automated tasks such as payroll processing, student registration, and even legal document analysis. As a result, payroll issues have dropped from 35,000 to 400 cases, with response times shrinking from months to a matter of days.This automation allows administrators to shift their focus to more strategic initiatives, driving greater impact across the organization.

“What I'm trying to do is get SEDUC to be more efficient,” says Vinicius Neiva, Secretary of Education, State of São Paulo. “In Brazil, we have a regulation mandating that at least 25% of the total revenue of the state must be invested in education. So, as we become leaner and more efficient, all of this money that we save can directly support students. We have a lot of very decentralized services that were not very efficient. We are working to concentrate that control and make services more efficient, using AI-powered services. And the results have so far proved dramatic.”

Prioritizing security, privacy, and ethical AI use

While streamlining administrative tasks has increased efficiency, SEDUC remains focused on ensuring that these advancements are supported by robust security measures and ethical AI use. Although achieving previously insurmountable learning milestones is important, SEDUC also realizes the importance of responsible AI development. This includes addressing concerns about data privacy, security, compliance, and potential biases in AI algorithms. SEDUC, with Microsoft support, is committed to prioritizing ethical considerations and mitigating security risks throughout its AI implementation.

“Security is a huge concern for us, especially with required Brazilian security laws,” Neiva explains. “So, we have a strategic plan for responding to data issues and classifying that data to keep it safe. There is a lot of work for us to do. But security is a very huge issue for us, so we are working hard to improve that.”

Empowering all: Training and upskilling for AI integration

Neiva also emphasizes the need for ongoing training, upskilling, and support of faculty, staff, and students to ensure successful adoption of new technologies. For an extensive organization like SEDUC, having a clear strategy for training and rollout plans beyond initial licenses is critical to guiding future actions and decisions.

“We are working to change the misconception amongst many educators—and even some students—that whenever students use AI, they are somehow cheating, rather than viewing it as a tool that can enhance learning, adds Barros. “So, we're thinking about how we can encourage the use of AI-powered activities and tools as part of their learning journey. But educators need to have a good idea of how to do this. They need training. They need orientation. They need suggestions. So, this will be a focus for SEDUC in the near future.”

Moving forward: Expanding AI’s role in education

With ongoing training in place for their AI-powered solution for personalized feedback on student essays, SEDUC is now looking ahead to further expand AI’s role in education. Integrating AI into existing systems and workflows has been key to SEDUC’s success. To address specific needs of its diverse student population, SEDUC developed internal tools, including a grammar checker and one for generating open-ended questions to enrich student learning. Currently in the testing phase, the AI system has already processed hundreds of thousands of open-ended questions, and the feedback has been invaluable for students.

“With just one grade, we had hundreds of thousands of these open questions corrected,” Barros notes. “The feedback is then given back to the students. It’s incredible. We wouldn't be able to do this without AI.”

Looking ahead, SEDUC plans to further integrate AI into curriculum development, virtual tutoring, personalized learning paths, and other student support systems, while continuing to empower educators and students to develop greater AI literacy.

SEDUC is also exploring new opportunities by expanding its use of Dynamics 365 and Power Platform, focusing on new technologies like chatbots and Power Pages, signifying a significant upgrade in the network’s technological infrastructure. It is also working to leverage AI to gain insights from data and make more informed decisions.

SEDUC’s mission is to provide a robust educational framework that supports the success of every student. This includes actively fostering collaboration with other educational institutions and technology providers to share best practices, advance AI in education throughout Brazil, and stay current with AI innovations to adapt inclusive learning strategies for long-term success.

By leveraging Microsoft AI-powered solutions and committing to responsible AI practices, SEDUC has improved student outcomes, enhanced efficiency, and addressed key educational challenges. As AI continues to evolve, SEDUC’s proactive approach to integrating these technologies positions it as a leader not just in Brazil but globally. By balancing innovation with responsibility, SEDUC is setting a global standard for education systems.

“Microsoft AI solutions support our pedagogical side, our administrative side, and our technical foundation,” says Sarno. “We want to meaningfully contribute to society. And all of our Microsoft AI tools provide more and better solutions for teachers, faculty, and—of course—our students to help prepare them for a bright future. These tools can help them to be better students, better people, and better employees and entrepreneurs.”

Story Content:
Universitas Terbuka (UT), Indonesia’s largest public university by enrollment, makes education accessible to all Indonesians, regardless of their location anywhere in the world. In recent years, the convenience and low cost of its open distance model, plus growing student comfort with remote learning, have driven exploding enrollment. More than 525,000 active students—a number projected to reach 750,000 before 2025—have strained the university’s resources.

Providing timely, effective, and personalized tutor support has been particularly difficult on such a large scale. Many of the university’s educators are responsible for hundreds of students in up to a dozen different classes. Each semester, UT sets up online tutorials for each, creating tens of thousands of virtual tutorial classes that involve up to 2.3 million student interactions in total over the term. It could take instructors as long as a week to reply to student questions or assignments submitted through UT’s online learning management system (LMS). The challenge was especially frustrating and time-consuming for educators tasked with repeatedly answering similar questions. This situation affected student engagement, progression toward degrees, and ultimately student retention. To improve student satisfaction, achieve its mission, and continue to grow, UT needed a new approach.

Supporting educators and students with AI

To continue providing quality education without overburdening educators, Universitas Terbuka turned to generative AI and Microsoft Azure AI, data, and app services solutions. UT uses a hybrid application infrastructure, shifting workloads between on-premises hosting for inactive courses and a microservices architecture on Azure. Cloud hosting delivers the scale needed for active courses with peaks of up to 60,000 concurrent users. That ability to scale made Azure AI the obvious choice for a university anticipating 1 million active students before 2027.

"We needed a solution that is scalable and stable enough to handle the number of students. Azure OpenAI Service provided that scalability,” says Dimas Agung Prasetyo, M.S., currently Head of the Undergraduate Program in Data Science for Universitas Terbuka. Previously Director of Information Systems, he initiated the AI project to enhance learning services for students.

In 2023, the university used Azure AI Foundry to build an AI tutor accessed through the school’s customized Moodle LMS, which students use for discussions and assignments. The AI tutor uses Azure OpenAI Service for the latest GPT series models, and Azure AI Foundry enables parallel testing of each model. Prasetyo says, “We used Azure AI Foundry as our integrated development environment.”

Ensuring accurate response quality

Course lecturer materials and grading rubrics for five core classes, including Indonesian Language and Civic Education, were indexed. Source documents were scanned efficiently with the help of Azure AI Document Intelligence, part of Azure AI services. The results were stored in object storage using Azure Blob Storage or as vectors using Azure Cosmos DB to streamline information management.

“The indexing went faster than we expected,” notes Prasetyo, who says the resulting knowledge base is also easy to update. Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with Azure Cosmos DB helps ensure accurate tutor responses aligned with instructors’ curricula. Although the AI tutor can access external knowledge bases, its responses rely primarily on the internal knowledge base. Prasetyo says replacing the university’s traditional MongoDB services with Azure Cosmos DB also accelerated development and AI response generation. Finally, Azure Cosmos DB works with the university’s PostgreSQL database that manages general LMS data storage and caching.

 

This architecture reliably and automatically accommodates high-volume, concurrent interactions with students and the generative AI model. Meanwhile, Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) and Azure App Service support several key academic services apps, which track students’ class registrations and degree progress.

“Azure Kubernetes Service lets us deploy in a microservices architecture in the easiest way—automatically and with less pain,” Prasetyo says. “And Azure App Service makes deployments faster, too. We don’t have to do much fine-tuning. We trust that Azure is fine-tuning for us.” UT’s modernized Azure infrastructure also reduces IT workloads by minimizing maintenance of its on-premises datacenters.

Making education more flexible and inclusive

Because students need both answers to questions and feedback on completed assignments, UT also needed the optical character recognition (OCR) capabilities of Azure AI Vision, another of the Azure AI services. This solution enables students to submit text-based work for assessment, either by entering answers online or by uploading Microsoft Word or PDF documents.

The resulting tutor is awake and working nonstop, making education more available, flexible, and inclusive. Students can learn and progress more quickly because they receive quick answers and other support. For instance, the AI tutor directs students to additional information in course reading materials and suggests ways to improve future assignments.

In the initial pilot, the AI tutor answered student questions for about 500 students enrolled in one section each of five core classes. The pilot validated the system architecture, integration, and operational costs. A second phase expanded the AI tutor to some 100,000 students, demonstrating scalability. Prasetyo hopes to double the number of classes involved to 1,000 soon. Ultimately, the AI tutor will aid students in all UT classes.

Improving student grades 24 hours a day

The always-on availability of the AI tutor has made UT education even more flexible and increased student engagement and productivity. Students’ questions receive more comprehensive answers, and they can follow up for interactive learning. This enhances knowledge retention, academic performance, and student retention.

“Students who have the AI tutor in their classes have the ability to get better grades than students who don’t,” says Prasetyo. “That’s good news.” Specifically, research data from four courses involving nearly 38,000 students indicated that those with the AI tutor participated more in discussions and earned better scores on assignments. These results were statistically significant.

The AI tutor has reduced the workload of lecturers, who act as moderators. Prasetyo notes, “We don’t have to answer student posts one at a time. We can just curate the AI responses.” The AI tutor also speeds the creation of assignments from days of work to just one or two. As a result, educators can focus on more impactful activities such as curriculum enhancement, research, and personalized student support.

UT is currently testing an AI tutor enhancement for working with mathematical problems, including the ability to recognize handwritten solutions. This new capability is expected to go live soon. It will enhance the educational experience for many more students and classes.

Prasetyo says, “As our student load is increasing, the AI tutor gives better service to our students by giving more responsive, more elaborate answers while also reducing tutor workloads and optimizing resources to help keep tuition costs low. It’s enabling Universitas Terbuka to continue to grow as an education innovator.”

Story Content:
In today’s rapidly evolving retail landscape, staying ahead of market trends is critical for businesses aiming to enhance customer engagement and drive growth. Since 1922, Canadian Tire Corporation (CTC) has been providing Canadians with the products they need for the jobs and joys of life by continuously seeking to revolutionize the customer experience. Through the power of generative AI, the company is now poised to redefine productivity, efficiency, and business growth as it works to deliver on its brand purpose to “make life in Canada better.”

AI-driven transformation

Several years ago, CTC made a commitment to strategically invest in the Microsoft Azure AI platform, ensuring a robust foundation for generative AI. By moving a significant amount of its data from on-premises systems to Azure, the company matured its data governance capabilities to gain deeper insights from its data.

“There is no question that AI can help us provide cost efficiencies and enhance our customers’ experiences, online and in-store,” says Susan O’Brien, Executive Vice President & Chief Brand & Customer Officer at Canadian Tire Corporation.

A key initiative in this transformation was using Azure OpenAI Service to develop its own assistant, named ChatCTC. The platform, used regularly by more than 3,000 corporate employees, has become an integral part of the company’s daily operations. Employees use the digital assistant for a wide variety of tasks, including training and skills development, building job descriptions, and generating product descriptions.

“Thanks to ChatCTC, our corporate employees save 30 to 60 minutes a day, which is helping them focus on higher-value tasks like driving innovation for our customers—in turn, helping us grow our business,” says Cari Covent, Head of AI and Emerging Technology at Canadian Tire Corporation.

In addition to building ChatCTC to boost employee productivity, CTC also used Azure OpenAI Service to develop CeeTee, an AI-powered shopping assistant that simplifies the complicated tire buying process for customers. Built with scale in mind, CeeTee has already demonstrated a significant impact on conversion rates during the recent spring tire buying season. Plans are currently underway to expand CeeTee further to improve CTC’s customer shopping experience.

Data quality, trust, and innovation

In addition to boosting employee productivity, the implementation of AI has led to significant improvements in data quality and trust. Through building a process framework for data ingestion into its Azure Data Lake, CTC ensures that data quality issues are identified and addressed at the source. This enables the company to provide self-service access to data for both business and technology workers, fostering a data-driven culture across the organization. “We are enabling our employees access to the right data, at the right time, for the right purpose,” says Covent.

Promising prospects

As CTC continues to expand its AI capabilities, the company is focused on using AI to solve system-wide problems rather than just point solutions. This approach aims to generate significant value by addressing horizontal processes and constraints across the organization, ultimately enhancing productivity and the customer experience. “We are using Azure AI to create solutions that will disrupt and transform how we operate,” says Rex Lee, Chief Information and Technology Officer at Canadian Tire Corporation. “In addition to simplifying the tire shopping process for customers through our CeeTee shopping assistant, the company is realizing increased revenue from online sales conversions and improved competitive differentiation."

“Customer expectations are evolving in unpredictable ways,” says Lee. “Our technology must adapt and shift as our customers’ needs and expectations change.” He concludes, “With leading AI technologies from Microsoft, we are creating practical applications that are setting new benchmarks for engaging our customers across Canada.”

A new data strategy

To grow smartly and sustainably, businesses must have a profound understanding of customers—and this begins with data. International hygiene, baby, and beauty consumer goods company PZ Cussons is dedicated to the wellbeing of people, and to better serve them, the company needed to know customers more completely. Facing data and analytics challenges, PZ Cussons explored technologies to eliminate data silos, improve data quality, and move teams from reliance on manual processes and offline reports to a centralized data platform.

“Companies talk about digital transformation, but there is no digital without data. We began with a blank sheet of paper when we created our digital vision and strategy, and step one was to figure out our data,” says Jawaz Illavia, Chief Information Officer at PZ Cussons.

A bold, pioneering solution

PZ Cussons has a strong relationship with Microsoft and is an early adopter for Microsoft solutions. The company began evaluating Microsoft Fabric as a robust and scalable solution to ground its decision-making processes in data.

“We have a long history of being bold and pioneering, and our size means we can do things more quickly than our larger competitors. We’re using Microsoft technology to tackle today’s challenges with tomorrow’s thinking,” Illavia adds.

Deploying Microsoft Fabric as the front-end experience and Azure Databricks as the back-end architecture, PZ Cussons is ingesting and harmonizing data from various sources, providing accurate sales, market share, and price data for an initial use case, Revenue Growth Management(RGM).

“We’re using Azure Databricks as the data transformation and storage engine for the data platform,” says Richard Sharkey, Head of Data Analytics and AI at PZ Cussons. “Azure Databricks prepares the data to load into Fabric for downstream consumption in various experiences within Fabric, as we look to meet the users at their needs in terms of democratization and tooling.”

The new data platform is delivering important insights. “Every consumer goods company needs to understand pricing strategy,” says Sharkey. “We’re exploring the effects of price changes and competitor pricing, alternate promotions, and more. Data and analytics drive the answers to those questions.”

PZ Cussons is taking the lessons learned from the initial use case to optimize its business units for growth and develop consistent frameworks to understand its brands at a global level.

“Microsoft Fabric is a very user-focused platform that’s helping break down the barriers between business users and technology data teams. It’s also speeding up what took days managing segments with different systems and multiple spreadsheets,” says Sharkey.

The company plans to fully adopt all Microsoft Fabric experiences, with Azure Data Factory bringing in data from various sources and OneLake serving as a scalable and efficient lakehouse. Also, PZ Cussons is using Fabric Copilot, bringing AI capabilities to analytics and reporting.

“We’re using Copilot to create executive summaries for our board, which is part of our adoption and maturity strategy. Producing analysis and recommendations at an executive level, demonstrating we know our data, and taking steps to better use the full power of Copilot is making our lives easier,” says Illavia.

The right products for the job

The deployment of Microsoft technologies has had a transformative impact on PZ Cussons’s business, employees, and customers. “With Fabric, we have easy-to-use tools that eliminate data silos and let teams focus on impactful work rather than data processing,” says Gurpreet Bhinder, Global Revenue Growth Management Director at PZ Cussons. “We’ve seen great employee adoption because the Fabric solution offers single sign-on for most systems, facilitates improved decision-making, and increases efficiency.”

“Fabric is one of the only data and analytics products that can deliver a consistent experience,” adds Sharkey. “No matter the role, we’re all working from the same version of truth. We’re pursuing AI readiness, so when each new use case emerges, we’ve already been thinking about it, and we’re ready to get started.”

The integrated, scalable Fabric-based data platform has enhanced operational efficiency and ensured PZ Cussons is future-ready, building increasingly personalized experiences and ensuring brand loyalty.
